Magnitudes are in the unit system of the analysis (see describe_analysis, case.unitSystem; N-mm-t-s: N, MPa and gravity 9810 mm/s^2). loadCase groups loads solved together; category limit | ultimate drives later margin factors. A moment (kind moment, vector = [mx, my, mz], optional referencePoint) is applied in the CalculiX deck as a statically equivalent couple of nodal forces on the target face / edge nodes (no rigid coupling) and in the Nastran BDF export as a MOMENT on an RBE3 reference node. The target is given as points near the topology (see add_fea_constraint).

analysisId.description: Id of the analysis (affected[0] of create_analysis, e.g. an-1.1).

distribution.description: force only: "total" (default) spreads the vector over the target; "per_node" applies it at every target node.

kind.description: Load type.

loadCase.description: Load case name this load belongs to: 1-40 letters, digits or underscores (e.g. "LC1", "landing_2"). Default "LC1".

magnitude.description: pressure only: positive pushes INTO the material (compressive), negative pulls (in the case unitSystem: N-mm-t-s -> N, MPa, mm/s^2 (9.81 m/s^2 = 9810); N-m-kg-s -> N, Pa, m/s^2; lbf-in-slinch-s -> lbf, psi, in/s^2).

name.description: Display name, e.g. "tip load".

referencePoint.description: moment only: point [x, y, z] in document units the moment acts about; the Nastran BDF export puts an RBE3 reference node there. Default: the centroid of the target nodes. The CalculiX deck applies a pure couple, which has no reference point, so it ignores this.

target.description: force / pressure / moment: the faces (edges, points for force) the load acts on. A moment needs a face, an edge or at least three points. Not for gravity.

edgesNear.description: Points identifying edges: each resolves to the nearest edge.

items.description: A point [x, y, z] in document units lying on (or very near) the intended edge.

entityId.description: Id of the analysed 3D entity (it must be a part of the analysis: set_part_idealization).

facesNear.description: Points identifying faces: each resolves to the NEAREST face of the entity at meshing time.

items.description: A point [x, y, z] in document units lying on (or very near) the intended face.

intersectPlane.description: Optional: restrict the target to the curve where the faces meet this plane.

normal.description: Plane normal (need not be unit length).

pointsNear.description: Points identifying vertices / locations: each resolves to the nearest vertex or node.

items.description: A point [x, y, z] in document units lying on (or very near) the intended vertex or location.

vector.description: force / gravity: direction and magnitude [x, y, z]; moment: the moment vector [mx, my, mz] by the right-hand rule in force x length of the unit system (N-mm-t-s: N.mm, N-m-kg-s: N.m, lbf-in-slinch-s: lbf.in) (in the case unitSystem: N-mm-t-s -> N, MPa, mm/s^2 (9.81 m/s^2 = 9810); N-m-kg-s -> N, Pa, m/s^2; lbf-in-slinch-s -> lbf, psi, in/s^2). Not for pressure.

name: add_fea_load

description: Create an exact signed-distance primitive as an implicit FIELD node (negative inside, millimetres in a mm document); it has no mesh until create_implicit_body. Shapes and the dimensions they need: sphere (radius), box (size [x,y,z] full extents; optional rounding), cylinder (radius, height; axis +Z, centred), capsule (radius, height = distance between the two cap centres; axis +Z, centred), torus (ringRadius, tubeRadius; ring in the XY plane, tubeRadius < ringRadius), cone (radius at the base z=0, height to the apex), plane (normal, offset: the half-space normal.p < offset is inside). position places the shape centre (cone: base centre), rotation is Euler XYZ in radians. Use combine_fields to unite / cut / blend fields.

height.description: cylinder / cone height, or the distance between the capsule cap centres, in document units (> 0).

name.description: Optional label for the field node.

normal.description: plane normal [x, y, z] (non-zero; normalised for you). The side opposite the normal is inside.

offset.description: plane offset along the unit normal, in document units: the plane is normal.p = offset. Default 0.

position.description: Placement [x, y, z] in document units. Default [0, 0, 0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

radius.description: sphere / cylinder / capsule / cone radius, in document units (> 0).

ringRadius.description: torus ring (major) radius in document units (> 0).

rotation.description: Euler XYZ rotation in radians. Default [0, 0, 0].

rounding.description: box edge rounding radius in document units (>= 0, < half the smallest size). Boxes only. Default 0.

shape.description: Primitive kind; see the command description for each kind's dimensions.

size.description: box full extents [x, y, z] in document units (each > 0).

tubeRadius.description: torus tube (minor) radius in document units (> 0, < ringRadius).

name: add_field_primitive

description: Add an edge flange (a bend plus a flat leg) to a sheet-metal part on a straight outline edge picked by a world point `edge.near` (any point within one thickness of the edge). angle is the angle bent THROUGH in degrees (90 = right angle; a closed 45-degree angle is a 135-degree bend); direction up bends towards the flat's +normal face. length is measured from the bend to the free end along the flange: to the outside mold line (virtual sharp of the outer faces, default for drawings), the inside mold line, or the bend tangent line. position says where the picked edge sits: 'material_outside' = the edge is the bend tangent line (the bend grows outside the profile), 'material_inside' = the edge is the outside mold line (the flat is trimmed back by the outside setback), 'bend_outside' = the edge is the extreme of the outer bend surface. insideRadius defaults to the rule radius. widthStart / widthEnd inset the bend from the edge ends. All lengths are in the document length unit. Refusals: FTR_PART_NOT_FOUND, FTR_BEND_ANGLE_OUT_OF_RANGE, FTR_SHARP_BEND_FORBIDDEN (R = 0), FTR_EDGE_NOT_STRAIGHT (no edge at edge.near), FTR_EDGE_OCCUPIED, FTR_FLANGE_TOO_SHORT. Next: add_relief, add_sheet_cutout, flat_pattern, check_sheet_metal.

angle.description: Bend angle in degrees: the angle bent THROUGH (0 = flat, 90 = right angle). 0 < angle <= 180; 180 only with lengthReference tangent.

autoRelief.description: Default true: when the rule defines a rectangular relief, cut it automatically at each end of the new bend that stops short of the edge end (width = widthRatio x thickness, depth = inside radius + thickness + depthExtra, all in the document length unit; the result's data.reliefs names the defaulted values). false = leave the bend ends unrelieved (check_sheet_metal then warns FTR_RELIEF_MISSING).

direction.description: Bend towards the flat's +normal face ('up', default) or the -normal face ('down').

near.description: World point [x, y, z] on or within one thickness of the straight edge that receives the flange (document length unit).

id.description: Sheet-metal part id (returned by add_sheet_metal_base).

insideRadius.description: Inside bend radius in the document length unit; default the rule radius; >= 0.

length.description: Flange length in the document length unit, measured as lengthReference says; must leave a flat leg > 0.

lengthReference.description: Where `length` ends at the bend: 'outside_mold_line', 'inside_mold_line' or 'tangent' (the bend tangent line).

position.description: Where the picked edge sits relative to the bend: 'material_outside', 'material_inside' or 'bend_outside'.

widthEnd.description: Inset of the flange from the edge end, in the document length unit (>= 0, default 0).

widthStart.description: Inset of the flange from the edge start, in the document length unit (>= 0, default 0).

name: add_flange

description: Add a flanged (lightening) hole to ONE flat of a sheet-metal part: a hole with a lip bent up or down around it, as on stiffened ribs. The flat is picked by the world point `face.near`; `center` is the hole axis point [x, y, z] (projected onto the flat). holeDiameter is the bore diameter of the lip where the bend starts; flangeHeight is the rise of the free end of the lip above the flat face on the lip side; flangeAngle is the angle bent through in degrees (0 < angle <= 90; 90 = cylindrical lip); lipRadius is the inside radius of the bend between flat and lip. The physical hole in the flat has radius holeDiameter/2 + thickness + lipRadius (data.cutRadius). In the flat pattern the hole is DEVELOPED to a smaller circle (data.flatCutDiameter) flagged approximate and unverified (stretch flange): do not cut it without a trial. All lengths are in the document length unit. The hole and its lip must lie wholly inside the flat, clear of its edges, bends, cutouts and beads. Refusals: FTR_PART_NOT_FOUND, FTR_FACE_NOT_FOUND, FTR_FORM_INVALID, FTR_CUTOUT_INVALID. Next: flat_pattern, check_sheet_metal.

center.description: World point [x, y, z] of the hole axis (document length unit); projected onto the flat plane.

direction.description: Lip towards the flat's +normal face ('up', default) or the -normal face ('down').

near.description: World point [x, y, z] on or near the flat that gets the hole (document length unit).

flangeAngle.description: Angle the lip is bent through, in degrees: 0 < angle <= 90 (90 = cylindrical lip).

flangeHeight.description: Rise of the lip free end above the flat face on the lip side, in the document length unit; must exceed lipRadius*(1-cos(angle)).

holeDiameter.description: Bore diameter of the lip where the bend starts, in the document length unit; > 0.

id.description: Sheet-metal part id (returned by add_sheet_metal_base).

lipRadius.description: Inside (concave) radius of the bend between flat and lip, in the document length unit; > 0.

name: add_flanged_hole

description: Add concrete pad footings with default sizes (to size and reinforce them from the loads, run design_footings afterwards; to verify them, check_foundations): one at a plan location, or (underColumns: true) one under every steel and concrete column foot of the level (underColumns wins over location). With underColumns, feet that already carry a footing on the level (within 10 mm) are skipped and the command is refused when none is left; an explicit location that already carries a footing on the level (within 10 mm) is refused. Top of footing at level + topOffset (default −300 mm); default 1500 × 1500 × 600 mm.

length.description: Size along Y, in document units. Default = width.

levelId.description: Level id. Default: the active level (a "Level 0" is created if none).

thickness.description: Depth of the pad, in document units. Default 600 mm.

topOffset.description: Top of footing relative to the level, in document units. Default −300 mm.

underColumns.description: Place one under each steel or concrete column foot of the level (ignores location).

width.description: Size along X, in document units. Default 1500 mm.

name: add_footing

description: Couple two physics joints (add_body_joint) rigidly, like meshing gears, a belt or a chain: speed(driven) = ratio × speed(driver), enforced by the physics engine, so each side feels the other's inertia and load. ratio = -teeth(driver)/teeth(driven) for an external spur mesh (opposite rotation), +teeth(driver)/teeth(driven) for a belt or an internal ring gear. Planetary with fixed ring, sun → carrier: ratio = sunTeeth / (sunTeeth + ringTeeth). Planets relative to the carrier: -ringTeeth / planetTeeth (driver = carrier joint). Kinematic-only equivalent for add_joint joints: add_drive_relation. Returns the coupling id in affected[0].

driven.description: Joint id that follows (e.g. the propeller joint).

driver.description: Joint id whose speed drives the other (e.g. the crankshaft joint).

efficiency.description: Mesh efficiency in (0, 1] (FR-FPR-74): the transmitted torque is reduced by (1 - efficiency) on the driven shaft, against its rotation. Real spur meshes are above 0.98 with peaks 0.993-0.999 [NASA TM 81426]; 0.99 is the usual value. Omitted = ideal gear (1, no loss).

id.description: Optional explicit coupling id.

ratio.description: speed(driven) / speed(driver); negative reverses the direction. Give this OR `teeth`; with both they must agree.

reverseRotation.description: With `teeth`: true for an external spur mesh (the driven shaft turns the other way, ratio negative). Default false.

teeth.description: Tooth counts [driver, driven]: ratio = driverTeeth / drivenTeeth, exact (Rotax 912 reduction 21/51 pinion on the crank: [21, 51] gives 2388.24 rpm from 5800 rpm), negated by `reverseRotation`.

name: add_gear_coupling

description: Add a feature control frame (geometric tolerance) to a 3D solid: characteristic (straightness, flatness, roundness, cylindricity, profile_line, profile_surface, angularity, perpendicularity, parallelism, position, concentricity, coaxiality, symmetry, circular_runout, total_runout), zone, optional material condition (MMC / LMC, only on a feature of size), zone modifiers (free_state, tangent_plane, statistical, separate_requirement, all_around / all_over for profiles ...) and up to 3 ordered datum references. Target ONE of: entityId + facesNear (a face set), targetPmiId (a size dimension, so MMC applies to its size), or compositeOf (the lower segment of a composite FCF: it inherits the upper frame's target, takes the same position / profile characteristic and a zone no larger than the upper one). Form tolerances (straightness, flatness, roundness, cylindricity) take no datums. Needs the OCC kernel. Refusals carry a GDT_* code: GDT_DATUM_UNDEFINED, GDT_DATUM_REPEATED, GDT_DATUM_TOO_MANY, GDT_ZONE_NON_POSITIVE, GDT_MC_ON_NON_FOS, GDT_DIAMETRAL_ON_PLANE, GDT_FORM_WITH_DATUM, GDT_MODIFIER_NOT_APPLICABLE, GDT_COMPOSITE_INVALID, GDT_PMI_UNKNOWN. Review required.

compositeOf.description: Id of the upper position / profile FCF this is the lower segment of; target is inherited.

datums.description: Ordered datum references, primary first, at most 3; default none.

items.description: One datum reference.

boundary.description: Datum boundary modifier: MMB (maximum material boundary) or LMB.

label.description: Datum letter(s) of an existing datum feature on the same solid.

entityId.description: Solid id; with facesNear, targets a face set.

facesNear.description: World points, one per face of the feature (document units). The faces are re-found from these points at every replay, so PMI follows its face through parametric edits. A pattern of equal holes takes one point on each hole. Use inspect_faces to find points on faces.

items.description: One world point [x, y, z] ON the face (document units), e.g. a point from inspect_faces centroid or samples.

materialCondition.description: Material condition of the tolerance; default RFS (no symbol).

placement.description: Optional explicit annotation placement; omit for the automatic plane (recomputed when the model changes). An explicit placement is kept.

leaderTo.description: Optional leader attachment point on the feature [x, y, z].

normal.description: Annotation plane unit normal [x, y, z].

origin.description: Annotation plane origin [x, y, z], document units.

position.description: Frame centre in plane coordinates [u, v], document units.

xDir.description: Annotation plane x direction [x, y, z] (unit, perpendicular to normal).

targetPmiId.description: Id of a size dimension (add_size_dimension) the frame applies to, e.g. "$holeSize".

zone.description: The tolerance zone: { value, diametral?, spherical?, projectedLength?, unequallyDisposed?, maxValue? }.

diametral.description: true = cylindrical zone, shown Ø. Not for planar features.

maxValue.description: Maximum value of the tolerance (per-unit-area style limit), document units.

projectedLength.description: Projected tolerance zone length (Ⓟ), document units; must be > 0.

unequallyDisposed.description: Profile unequally disposed zone value (UZ), document units, within [0, value].

value.description: Tolerance zone width or diameter, document length units; must be > 0.

name: add_geometric_tolerance

description: Create a graph (beam) lattice as an implicit FIELD from sketched curves: lines, polylines, arcs, circles, ellipses, rectangles, splines (2D sketch entities) and nurbs_curve entities in the document. Straight pieces become one beam each; curved pieces are sampled into chords of at most `chord` document units. Nodes closer than mergeTolerance are merged; zero-length and duplicate beams are dropped and counted in data.dropped. The beam radius varies linearly along each source curve from radiusStart to radiusEnd (document units); cap "sphere" puts a ball of the end radius on every beam end (a rounded joint), "butt" leaves flat ends. The sources must stay as they are while a body depends on this node (IMP_SOURCE_IN_USE). region (a field id) clips the graph. Next: create_implicit_body (the field is bounded by the beams), lattice_properties, export_3mf beamLattice.

cap.description: End caps: sphere (default, rounded joints) or butt (flat).

chord.description: Largest chord of the beams that approximate curved pieces, document units (> 0). Default 1.

mergeTolerance.description: Nodes closer than this are one node, document units (>= 0). Default 1e-6.

name.description: Optional label for the node.

radiusEnd.description: Beam radius at the end of each source curve in document units (> 0). Default: radiusStart (constant).

radiusStart.description: Beam radius at the start of each source curve in document units (> 0; 2 * radius is the strut diameter).

region.description: Id of a field that clips the graph (kept where that field is negative).

sourceIds.description: Ids of the curve entities (lines, polylines, arcs, circles, ellipses, rectangles, splines, nurbs_curve) that carry the beams.

name: add_graph_lattice

description: Frame beams along the structural grid (add_grid_line): along every listed grid line, one beam per bay between consecutive intersections with the other lines (so it frames column to column when add_grid_columns was run first). The beam top sits at the level FFL + topOffset (reference "ffl", default) or at the level top (FFL + level height) + topOffset (reference "levelTop"). Bays that already hold a beam with the same end points and a top of steel within 100 mm are skipped (any section). Mark SB, role beam.

axes.description: Grid line labels to frame along (e.g. ["A","B"]). Default: every grid line.

endJoint.description: Joint at each beam end: "pinned" (default) or "rigid".

levelId.description: Level id: the beams sit at its finished floor level. Default: the active level.

reference.description: Datum of topOffset: "levelTop" = level elevation + level height (underside of the next floor), "ffl" = level finished floor elevation. The same reference and topOffset put add_beam and add_grid_beams at the same absolute elevation. Default differs by domain and is kept so existing documents replay unchanged: add_beam "levelTop" (concrete beam under the next slab), add_grid_beams "ffl" (steel framing referenced to finished floor). Pass reference explicitly to be unambiguous; the summary states the resolved elevation.

startJoint.description: Joint at each beam start: "pinned" (default) or "rigid" (moment connection).

topOffset.description: Top of steel relative to the level FFL, in DOCUMENT UNITS (not necessarily mm). Default 0 (top of steel at FFL); negative puts it below the FFL, e.g. minus the grating thickness.

name: add_grid_beams

description: Add vertical bracing in one bay of one grid line for one storey: the bay lies in the plane of grid line axis between the crossing lines from and to. pattern "x" gives two crossing diagonals, "diagonal" one from bottom at from to top at to. Bottom nodes sit at the base level FFL + bottomOffset, top nodes at the next storey FFL (base elevation + level height) + topOffset. Mark BR, role brace.

axis.description: Label of the grid line the bracing lies in, e.g. "A".

bottomOffset.description: Bottom node height relative to the base level FFL, in DOCUMENT UNITS (not necessarily mm). Default 0 (at the FFL).

from.description: Label of the grid line crossing axis that bounds the bay at one side, e.g. "1".

levelId.description: Storey base level id: bracing starts at its FFL and rises one level height. Default: the active level.

pattern.description: "x" (default): two crossing diagonals; "diagonal": one, from bottom at from to top at to.

to.description: Label of the grid line crossing axis that bounds the bay at the other side, e.g. "2".

topOffset.description: Top node height relative to the NEXT storey FFL (base elevation + level height), in DOCUMENT UNITS (not necessarily mm). Default 0 (at the next FFL); negative puts the node under the floor beams.

name: add_grid_bracing

description: Place one vertical STEEL column (profile section) at every intersection of the structural grid (add_grid_line); for concrete columns, single or per grid intersection, use add_column: the way to start framing a building. The column runs from the base level FFL up to topLevelId (a continuous column through intermediate floors) or, by default, to the top of the base level. Restrict with axes (both crossing lines must be listed) and exclude. Intersections that already hold a column on that level, or a continuous column from a lower level passing through it, are skipped. Mark SC, role column; follow with add_grid_beams / add_grid_bracing.

axes.description: Grid line labels (e.g. ["A","B","1","2"]); an intersection is used only when BOTH its lines are listed. Default: all grid lines.

baseFixity.description: "pinned" (default) or "fixed": the column foot restrains rotation in check_steel_members.

exclude.description: Intersections to skip, written "A/1" (the order of the two labels does not matter).

levelId.description: Base level id: columns start at its finished floor level. Default: the active level.

roll.description: Section rotation about the vertical axis, radians. Default 0.

topLevelId.description: Level id whose FFL is the column top; must be above the base level. Default: base level elevation + base level height.

name: add_grid_columns

description: Add one structural grid axis from start to end (plan [x, y]) with a labelled bubble at each end, on layer S-GRID. Label defaults to the next free number. Refused if an axis with the same end points exists.

end.description: Axis end [x, y].

label.description: Bubble label, e.g. "A" or "3". Must be unique.

start.description: Axis start [x, y].

name: add_grid_line

description: Add a flat triangle mesh grid in the plane z = position[2], centred on `position` (x, y), `size` [sx, sy] long, `cells` [nx, ny] cells (two triangles per cell, +Z normal, open mesh). The patch to sculpt on (sculpt_mesh) or to test smoothing on. Reports triangles, vertices, the cell size and the area (document units). Refusals: CMD_INVALID_PARAMS, MESH_PARAM_INVALID (over one million vertices), MESH_ASSET_UNAVAILABLE (no asset store for a result above the inline cap).

position.description: Centre [x, y, z] of the grid (document units). Default [0, 0, 0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

name: add_grid_mesh

description: Lay out a rectangular structural grid. Numbered axes 1, 2, 3… run parallel to Y and are spaced along X by xSpacings; lettered axes A, B, C… (I and O skipped) run parallel to X, spaced along Y by ySpacings. E.g. xSpacings [6000, 6000] gives axes 1–3 six metres apart. Refused when every axis of the new grid already exists; otherwise labels continue after the existing ones.

extension.description: How far axes overrun the outer grid lines (document units). Default 1500 mm.

origin.description: Intersection of axis 1 and axis A [x, y]. Default [0, 0].

xSpacings.description: Bay widths along X between consecutive numbered axes (each > 0, at most 100).

ySpacings.description: Bay widths along Y between consecutive lettered axes (each > 0, at most 100).

name: add_grid_system

description: Create an exact helix (cylindrical, conical or with a variable pitch) or a planar spiral as a NURBS curve that remembers its definition: the sweep along it is built from the exact helix by the exact kernel (springs, threads, screws, coils, worm gears). The helix starts at position + radius along a reference direction ⟂ axis, and winds about axis (default +Z) right-handed (counter-clockwise rising, default) or left-handed. Give exactly two of pitch (axial advance per turn), turns and height (total axial length), or pitchLaw (a law of the turn fraction t in 0..1, e.g. a table: closed end turns and a wider middle) together with turns. radius is the start radius; endRadius or taperDeg (half angle, degrees, positive narrows along the axis) makes it conical. type "spiral" winds in the plane ⟂ axis from radius to endRadius, or by pitch (radial advance per turn) over turns. Lengths in document units, angles in radians (startAngleRad) except taperDeg. Returns data { length, curvatureRadiusMin, torsion, turns, pitch, height, fitDeviation, unit }. Next: sweep_profile with pathId (a round wire; for a flat thread section use orientation axis_plane), or add_coil for a ready spring.

axis.description: Direction [x, y, z] of the helix axis (non-zero). Default [0, 0, 1].

color.description: Hex color string #rrggbb, e.g. "#c8553d". Defaults to "#2a7ab0".

endRadius.description: Radius at the end (> 0): conical helix or spiral. Do not combine with taperDeg. Omit for a cylinder.

handedness.description: "right" (default, counter-clockwise seen against the axis while rising) or "left".

height.description: Total axial length of the helix, document units (> 0).

layerId.description: Layer id to assign the entity to. Defaults to the document default layer.

name.description: Optional display name for the entity (shown in the scene tree).

pitch.description: Axial advance per turn (helix) or radial advance per turn (spiral), document units, > 0. Give two of pitch, turns, height.

pitchLaw.description: Axial advance per turn (> 0, document units). A law over t in [0, 1] (the fraction of the turns): { type: "linear", start, end } | "s_curve" (smoothstep) | "constant" { value } | "table" { points } | "expression" { expression }.

end.description: linear / s_curve: value at the path end (t = 1).

endSlope.description: table: optional derivative at t = 1 (default: a shape-preserving one-sided estimate from the last points).

expression.description: expression: formula of t (t in [0, 1] (the fraction of the turns)) in document length units advanced per turn, e.g. "10 + 2*t".

points.description: table: [t, value] pairs (t t in [0, 1] (the fraction of the turns); value in document length units advanced per turn), t strictly increasing from 0 to the end; a smooth shape-preserving cubic (no overshoot) passes through them.

start.description: linear / s_curve: value at the path start (t = 0).

startSlope.description: table: optional derivative at t = 0 (default: a shape-preserving one-sided estimate from the first points).

type.description: Law kind: constant, linear, s_curve (smoothstep), table or expression.

value.description: constant: the value, in document length units advanced per turn.

position.description: Origin [x, y, z] of the curve in document units; the poles are relative to it. Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

radius.description: Radius at the start of the helix, document units (> 0).

startAngleRad.description: Start angle about the axis, radians, measured from the reference direction. Default 0.

taperDeg.description: Cone half angle in degrees (helix only): the radius changes by -height * tan(taperDeg); positive narrows. Do not combine with endRadius.

tolerance.description: Largest distance between the NURBS poles and the exact helix, document units. Default 1e-6 × the larger radius.

turns.description: Number of turns, 0 < turns <= 200, fractions allowed.

type.description: "helix" (default) rises along the axis; "spiral" stays in the plane ⟂ axis.

name: add_helix

description: Add a 180-degree hem (a flat folded back over itself along a straight edge) to a sheet-metal part: a 180-degree bend followed by a straight return leg. The edge is picked by the world point `edge.near` (within one thickness of the edge) and is the bend tangent line. hemType 'closed' = no gap (inside radius 0, the return leg lies against the flat; allowed even when the rule forbids sharp bends); 'open' = a gap between the flat and the return leg (inside radius = gap/2, gap required). length is the straight return leg after the bend, from the bend tangent line to the free edge. All lengths are in the document length unit. The developed length of the hem (flat_pattern data.hems[]) is pi*(gap/2 + K*T) + length with the rule K at that radius: the neutral-surface model extended to 180 degrees, flagged UNVERIFIED (not checked against a published hem table). The teardrop hem is not supported. Refusals: FTR_PART_NOT_FOUND, FTR_PARAM_INVALID, FTR_FLANGE_TOO_SHORT, FTR_EDGE_NOT_STRAIGHT, FTR_EDGE_OCCUPIED. Next: flat_pattern, check_sheet_metal.

direction.description: Fold towards the flat's +normal face ('up', default) or the -normal face ('down').

near.description: World point [x, y, z] on or within one thickness of the straight edge that gets the hem (document length unit).

gap.description: Clear gap between the flat and the return leg in the document length unit; required and > 0 for an open hem, omitted for a closed hem. Inside radius = gap/2.

hemType.description: 'closed' = zero gap (inside radius 0); 'open' = gap between flat and return leg.

id.description: Sheet-metal part id (returned by add_sheet_metal_base).

length.description: Straight return leg length after the bend in the document length unit; > 0.

widthEnd.description: Inset of the hem from the edge end, in the document length unit (>= 0, default 0).

widthStart.description: Inset of the hem from the edge start, in the document length unit (>= 0, default 0).

name: add_hem

description: Cut holes into a planar face of a 3D solid: simple, counterbore, countersink or counterdrill (countersink cone, then counterbore, then bore); through the whole part (through_all), through the first wall only (up_to_next), up to the plane of a parallel face below (up_to_face, extent.face.near) or blind with a drill point (default 118 degrees, reported as defaulted; drillPointAngle 0 = flat bottom). The face is picked by a world point on it (face.near); the holes go INTO the material, along the opposite of the face outward normal. All lengths are in the document length unit, all angles in degrees. points: [u, v] in the face frame (origin = the world origin projected on the face plane, u = world X (or Y) projected on it, v = normal x u), or pointsFrame "world_xy" ([x, y] world, the point is moved along Z onto the face), or "world" ([x, y, z] projected onto the face). All positions are validated first: if one is bad nothing is cut. hole.thread is a cosmetic attribute (geometry unchanged) unless thread.modelled is true (a real helical groove). hole.fastener takes the clearance diameter from the document fastener catalogue. Consumes target and creates one mesh entity (exact B-rep with an exact kernel). Refusals carry error.code: FTR_FACE_NOT_FOUND, FTR_FACE_NOT_PLANAR, FTR_HOLE_POINT_OUTSIDE_FACE, FTR_HOLE_DIAMETERS_INCONSISTENT, FTR_CSK_ANGLE_OUT_OF_RANGE, FTR_BLIND_DEPTH_INVALID, FTR_DRILL_POINT_ANGLE_OUT_OF_RANGE, FTR_THREAD_DESIGNATION_INVALID, FTR_FASTENER_CATALOG_UNAVAILABLE, FTR_UP_TO_TARGET_INVALID, FTR_FEATURE_BUILD_FAILED. Next: check_machining, hole_table, recognize_features.

depth.description: Blind only: cylindrical depth from the face, in document length units (drill point excluded). Must be inside the stock.

drillPointAngle.description: Blind only: drill point included angle in degrees in (0, 180); 0 = flat bottom. Omitted = 118 (named as defaulted).

face.description: up_to_face only: the planar target face the hole stops at, picked by a world point.

near.description: World point [x, y, z] on the planar target face, in document length units.

kind.description: "through_all" cuts through the whole part along the axis; "blind" stops at depth; "up_to_next" cuts through the first wall only (until the axis leaves the material, measured per hole: refined on the exact faces of the kernel when it has them (OpenCascade), else on the display mesh, which is only accurate to the tessellation on curved exit walls; the summary says which); "up_to_face" stops at the plane of the planar face picked by face.near, which must be parallel to the hole face and below it.

face.description: The planar face to drill into, picked by a world point.

near.description: World point [x, y, z] on (or within 0.1% of the part size of) the planar face, in document length units.

hole.description: Hole definition: kind, diameters, optional thread (cosmetic, or a modelled helical groove) and fastener reference.

cboreDepth.description: Counterbore (or counterdrill) depth from the face, in document length units; a counterdrill needs it below the cone.

cboreDiameter.description: Counterbore (or counterdrill) diameter, in document length units; must exceed diameter.

cskAngle.description: Countersink included angle in degrees, in (0, 180), e.g. 82, 90, 100.

cskDepth.description: Countersink cone depth from the face, in document length units. Alternative to cskDiameter (D = d + 2*depth*tan(angle/2)).

cskDiameter.description: Countersink diameter at the face, in document length units; must exceed diameter (counterdrill: must exceed cboreDiameter). Alternative to cskDepth.

diameter.description: Bore diameter, in document length units. Required unless fastener gives it from the catalogue.

fastener.description: Standard fastener this hole is for: its clearance hole diameter comes from the document fastener catalogue.

fit.description: Optional fit label recorded with the hole (no geometric effect).

partNumber.description: Part number; its dash token selects the catalogue size, whose hole diameter is used.

kind.description: "simple" (plain bore), "counterbore" (needs cboreDiameter, cboreDepth), "countersink" (needs cskAngle and cskDiameter or cskDepth) or "counterdrill" (a countersink cone from the face down to the counterbore, then the counterbore, then the bore: needs cboreDiameter, cboreDepth, cskAngle and cskDiameter or cskDepth; cskDiameter > cboreDiameter > diameter).

thread.description: Thread attribute of the hole: cosmetic by default, a real helical groove when modelled is true.

depth.description: Threaded depth, in document length units. Omit for the full hole depth.

designation.description: Thread designation, e.g. "MJ6x1-4H5H", ".1900-32 UNJF-3B", "M6x1-6H", "1/4-20 UNC-2B". Cosmetic unless modelled is true.

family.description: Thread family (UNJ, MJ, UN, M, other). Omit to infer it from the designation.

modelled.description: true cuts a real helical thread groove (basic 60 degree internal ISO 68-1 profile; M / MJ / UN / UNJ designations with an explicit pitch, e.g. "M6x1"; MJ / UNJ root radius not applied, unverified) into the hole: the bore diameter must be about the minor diameter (D - 1.0825 P) and below the major diameter; needs a geometry kernel; changes the geometry and the shape recipe key. Omit or false = cosmetic, no geometry.

items.description: One centre: [u, v], [x, y] or [x, y, z] in document length units.

anyOf.description: Hole centres taken from a 2D sketch placed on the target face plane (the sketch plane must coincide with the face plane; a point off the plane is refused). Give sketchEntityIds, pointRefs or both.

pointRefs.description: Single vertices of sketch entities (see vertex), for when only some vertices of a polyline should be drilled.

id.description: Id of the sketch entity.

vertex.description: Vertex index in that entity (dimensionless): polyline point index; line 0 = start, 1 = end; rectangle 0..3 counter-clockwise from the lower-left corner; circle / arc / point 0.

sketchEntityIds.description: Ids of 2D sketch entities whose points become hole centres: a point entity gives its position; a polyline gives ALL its vertices; a line its two ends; a rectangle its four corners; a circle or arc its centre.

points.description: Hole centres. Either a list in document length units: [u, v] (pointsFrame face), [x, y] (world_xy) or [x, y, z] (world), at least one; OR { sketchEntityIds?, pointRefs? } taking the centres from 2D sketch points (point entities, polyline vertices...) lying on the face plane (pointsFrame is then ignored; a sketch point off the face plane is refused).

pointsFrame.description: Coordinates of points: "face" (default), "world_xy" or "world". See the command description.

target.description: Id of the 3D solid to drill (a primitive or a kernel result).

name: add_hole

description: Add a closed triangle mesh icosphere: a regular icosahedron projected onto the sphere of `radius`, subdivided `level` times (level 0 = 20 triangles, each level x4, 0..7), outward wound, all vertices exactly on the sphere. A mesh entity for sculpt_mesh, remesh_mesh, decimate_mesh or mesh_to_brep, not a primitive solid (use add_sphere for a parametric one). Reports triangles, vertices, the polyhedral volume and area (document units). Refusals: CMD_INVALID_PARAMS, MESH_ASSET_UNAVAILABLE (result above the inline cap and no asset store).

position.description: Centre [x, y, z] (document units). Default [0, 0, 0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

radius.description: Sphere radius (document units).

name: add_icosphere_mesh

description: Place a raster image (a scanned drawing, a photo of a sketch) on a 2D work plane as a semi-transparent underlay to trace over. The lower-left corner of the image sits at `position`; size it with `width` (document units) OR `pixelSize` (document units per pixel, e.g. 1.5 for 1.5 mm/px); with neither, 1 unit per pixel. Then use calibrate_underlay (two pixel points + their real distance) to fix the scale, origin and orientation, and image_to_world to convert pixel coordinates read off the picture into model coordinates for draw_polyline / extrude_profile / revolve_profile. Accepts PNG or JPEG base64 data URLs up to 8000000 characters.

dataUrl.description: The image as a base64 data URL: "data:image/png;base64,…" or "data:image/jpeg;base64,…".

locked.description: true: the viewport never picks/selects it while tracing. Defaults to false.

name.description: Optional display name for the entity (shown in the scene tree).

opacity.description: Opacity in [0, 1] (0 = invisible, 1 = opaque). Defaults to 0.5.

pixelSize.description: Document units per image pixel (> 0), e.g. 1.5 for a 1.5 mm/px scan. Excludes width.

position.description: World position [x, y, z] of the image lower-left corner (work-plane origin). Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

rotation.description: three.js intrinsic XYZ Euler angles in RADIANS [rx, ry, rz] (equivalent to rotating about world Z first, then world Y, then world X) of the work plane. Defaults to [0, 0, 0].

width.description: Placed image width in document units (> 0); height follows the aspect ratio.

name: add_image_underlay

description: Prescribe the motion of one translational dof (x, y or z) of the nodes of a part face or near points in an explicit_dynamics case (llull_explicit): kind velocity gives v(t), kind displacement gives the displacement u(t) from the start position; the curve is [[time s, value], ...] (piecewise linear, constant outside its range) in `unit` (mm/s, m/s for velocity; mm, m for displacement). The target is a part of the case with points near a box face (all its nodes on that plane) or near nodes. A dof can carry one motion. Returns the motion id in affected[1].

analysisId.description: Id of the analysis (affected[0] of create_analysis, e.g. an-1.1).

kind.description: What the curve gives; default velocity.

name.description: Name, e.g. "punch".

target.description: Where the motion acts (give facesNear and / or pointsNear).

entityId.description: Id of a part of the case.

facesNear.description: Faces: all the part nodes on the nearest box face plane.

items.description: A point [x, y, z] in document units on (or near) a box face of the part.

pointsNear.description: Nodes: the part node nearest each point.

items.description: A point [x, y, z] in document units.

unit.description: Unit of the curve values: a velocity (mm/s, m/s) or a length (mm, m) for displacement.

name: add_imposed_motion

description: Create an internal (ring) involute gear: a cylindrical rim whose bore carries inward-pointing teeth, as ONE closed mesh solid built without booleans. Same tooth convention as add_spur_gear (addendum 1·module, dedendum 1.25·module), tooth spaces widened by 0.05·module backlash so an external gear of the same module and pressure angle meshes without interference. The ring is centred on its axis (+Z, z from 0 to faceWidth) at `position`; tooth pitch diameter = module * teeth. Pair with add_spur_gear: centre distance = module * (ringTeeth - pinionTeeth) / 2. For a complete sun/planet/ring set use add_planetary_gearset (it phases the teeth for you). The result is a world-space mesh entity (position/rotation are baked in).

color.description: Hex color. Default "#8892a0".

name.description: Optional display name for the entity (shown in the scene tree).

outerRadius.description: Radius of the cylindrical rim (outside of the ring). Must be >= pitchRadius + 2.25 * module so that material remains behind the tooth spaces.

position.description: World-space location of the anchor point [x, y, z] in document units. Right-handed frame, +Z up. Centre of the ring on its axis (z = bottom face). Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

pressureAngle.description: Pressure angle in RADIANS, in (0, π/2). Default 0.3491 (20°).

rotation.description: three.js intrinsic XYZ Euler angles in RADIANS [rx, ry, rz] (equivalent to rotating about world Z first, then world Y, then world X). Matches rotate_entity convention. Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. If non-finite or not length-3 the rotation is ignored and [0,0,0] is used.

teeth.description: Number of internal teeth, integer >= 12 and <= 1000. Typical ring gears have 40-120.

name: add_internal_gear

description: Add a joggle (two reverse bends of angle phi that offset the rest of a flat by `offset`) across the full width of one flat of a sheet-metal part. The flat is picked by the world point `face.near`; `line` is the start tangent line of the first bend as two [x, y] points in the flat's own plane coordinates (for the base flat these are the profile coordinates); the line is extended to the flat's outline. The piece on the RIGHT of line[0] -> line[1] keeps the flat (for a flat that is attached through a bend the side attached to the bend is kept automatically); an inclined flat of length s and the offset piece are inserted on the LEFT. offset (the offset between the two flat faces), angle (degrees, 0 < angle <= 90) and insideRadius are in document length unit / degrees. Inclined straight s = (offset - 2*(R+T/2)*(1-cos(angle)))/sin(angle) must be > 0, else FTR_JOGGLE_OFFSET_TOO_SMALL (increase the offset to more than 2*(R+T/2)*(1-cos(angle)), or reduce R or angle). Other refusals: FTR_PART_NOT_FOUND, FTR_FACE_NOT_FOUND, FTR_BEND_ANGLE_OUT_OF_RANGE, FTR_SHARP_BEND_FORBIDDEN, FTR_JOGGLE_LINE_INVALID. flat_pattern then reports the joggle allowance and run.

angle.description: Joggle bend angle phi in degrees; 0 < angle <= 90.

near.description: World point [x, y, z] on or near the flat to joggle (document length unit).

id.description: Sheet-metal part id (returned by add_sheet_metal_base).

insideRadius.description: Inside bend radius of both bends in the document length unit; default the rule radius; >= 0.

line.description: Start tangent line of the first joggle bend, as two [x, y] points in the picked flat's plane coordinates (document length unit).

items.description: Start of the line [x, y] in the flat plane coordinates (document length unit).

offset.description: Offset between the two flat faces in the document length unit; > 0.

side.description: Direction of the offset: 'up' moves the offset piece towards the flat's +normal side, 'down' towards -normal.

name: add_joggle

description: Add a kinematic joint between two InstanceEntity frames to model a mechanism (poses only, no forces; for rigid-body physics with masses and forces use add_body_joint + simulate_motion instead). Kinds: "revolute": rotation about axis (hinge, 1 DOF: angle rad). "prismatic": slide along axis (1 DOF: displacement). "rigid": b is welded to a (0 DOF). "cylindrical": rotate AND slide along the same axis (2 DOF: [angle, displacement]). "pin_slot": a pin rotating about axis that also slides along slotAxis (2 DOF: [angle, displacement]). "planar": two slides in the plane normal to axis plus a rotation about it (3 DOF: [u, v, angle]; u,v = right-handed basis of the plane, for axis z: x then y). "ball": three rotations about the pivot (3 DOF: Euler XYZ angles). "cam": follower b slides along axis by an amount read from the closed profile entity profileId as joint camJoint (a revolute) turns (0 DOF, derived). "a" and "b" are MateRef objects { instanceId, frame? }; b moves relative to a about pivot (default: a's origin; give pivot to put the pin elsewhere, e.g. the far end of a link). "axis" is "x"|"y"|"z" or a [x,y,z] vector. Closed loops (four-bar, slider-crank): add every joint, mark the joints whose value should be SOLVED passive:true, drive the others with set_joint_value; evaluate_motion then solves the loop (Levenberg-Marquardt) and refuse when it cannot close. "values" are initial DOF values (default 0; for passive joints the initial guess, which picks the assembly branch); "limits" one {min,max} per DOF. Use set_joint_value to drive the joint; evaluate_motion (apply=true to move the instances) applies it. For gear/belt ratios between kinematic joints use add_drive_relation (add_gear_coupling is the physics equivalent). Returns the new joint id in affected[0].

a.description: First instance frame reference (the fixed/anchor frame). { instanceId: "<id>", frame?: "origin"|"axis-x"|"axis-y"|"axis-z" }. instanceId must be an existing InstanceEntity. frame defaults to "origin".

frame.description: Frame selector: origin (default), axis-x, axis-y, or axis-z.

axis.description: Rotation / slide axis (planar: plane normal; cam: follower slide axis). "x", "y", "z" or a [x,y,z] vector.

b.description: Second instance frame reference (the moving frame). { instanceId: "<id>", frame?: "origin"|"axis-x"|"axis-y"|"axis-z" }. instanceId must be an existing InstanceEntity. frame defaults to "origin".

frame.description: Frame selector: origin (default), axis-x, axis-y, or axis-z.

camJoint.description: cam only: id of the revolute joint whose angle drives the follower.

id.description: Optional explicit joint id. When omitted a unique id is generated. If the id already exists in doc.joints the command is a no-op.

kind.description: Joint type; see the command description.

limits.description: Travel limit per DOF, same order as values: { min?, max? } in radians / document units. Values are clamped into it.

max.description: Upper bound (radians or document units). Omit for none.

min.description: Lower bound (radians or document units). Omit for none.

passive.description: True when the joint value is an unknown of a closed loop: it is solved so the loop closes. Default false.

pivot.description: Optional world point [x,y,z] (rest pose) the joint acts about. Default: the origin of instance a.

profileId.description: cam only: id of the 2D profile entity (closed polyline, circle or rectangle) whose local XY origin is the cam rotation centre. Its boundary radius along the follower direction gives the follower lift.

slotAxis.description: pin_slot only: direction the pin slides along ("x"|"y"|"z" or [x,y,z]).

values.description: Initial DOF values in kind order (radians / document units). Default all 0. Not for rigid and cam.

name: add_joint

description: Create a round shaft along +Z (z from 0 to length) with a rectangular keyway (pocket) on its +X side, built as one closed mesh solid without booleans. Keyway width b, groove depth t1 (from the shaft surface to the groove floor) and the optional key height h default to the DIN 6885 form A values for the shaft diameter (e.g. d=40 -> b=12, t1=5, h=8). The pocket spans keyLength starting keyOffset above the bottom end (defaults: keyLength = 60% of length, centred); keyOffset 0 or reaching the top gives an open-ended keyway. includeKey=true also creates the matching parallel key as a separate mesh solid seated in the groove (affected = [shaft, key]). Result is world-space mesh entities.

color.description: Shaft hex color. Default "#9aa3ad".

includeKey.description: Also create the parallel key part. Default false.

keyDepth.description: Groove depth t1 measured from the shaft surface. Default from DIN 6885.

keyHeight.description: Key height h (only used when includeKey is true). Default from DIN 6885.

keyLength.description: Keyway length along the shaft, > 0 and <= length. Default 60% of length.

keyOffset.description: Distance from the shaft bottom end (z = 0) to the keyway start, >= 0. Default centred.

keyWidth.description: Keyway width b. Default from DIN 6885 for the diameter.

name.description: Optional display name for the shaft.

position.description: World-space location of the anchor point [x, y, z] in document units. Right-handed frame, +Z up. Centre of the shaft bottom face. Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

rotation.description: three.js intrinsic XYZ Euler angles in RADIANS [rx, ry, rz] (equivalent to rotating about world Z first, then world Y, then world X). Matches rotate_entity convention. Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. If non-finite or not length-3 the rotation is ignored and [0,0,0] is used.

name: add_keyed_shaft

description: Mark a cylindrical face of a solid as knurled (cosmetic, like a cosmetic thread: a PMI note, no geometry): pattern straight (axial teeth), diagonal (one helix direction) or diamond (crossed helices), with the circular `pitch` you ask for in document units. The teeth must close round the circumference, so the count is round(pi d / pitch) and the pitch actually used is pi d / teeth; when that differs from your request the result carries the warning WRP_KNURL_PITCH_ADJUSTED (data.warnings, the pitch used is data.pitch). Diagonal and diamond patterns take `helixAngleDeg` from the axis (default 30, a named default, not a standard: no DIN 82 / ISO 13444 table is shipped). Returns data { knurlId, teeth, pitch, requestedPitch, diameter, pattern, helixAngleDeg?, pitchAdjusted, warnings, reviewRequired: true }. The note is review-required PMI (drawings and STEP AP242 carry it). With model 'geometry' (straight pattern only) the grooves are CUT: the solid is replaced by one with N V-grooves along the axis (tooth angle `toothAngleDeg`, default 90 included; depth `depth`, default the one that leaves a flat land of 10 % of the pitch between grooves; both named defaults, not standards); data.expectedVolumeDelta is the closed-form volume removed (N x length x groove area) and no PMI note is added (add_pmi_note if the drawing needs one). Diagonal and diamond geometry refuses with WRP_KNURL_GEOMETRY_UNSUPPORTED (helical grooves are not built: use the cosmetic model). A face that is not a cylinder refuses with WRP_KNURL_FACE_NOT_CYLINDER. Needs the exact (native) kernel. Next: check_pmi, accept_pmi_review, mass_properties, render_view.

depth.description: geometry only: groove depth below the surface, document units, > 0. Default: the depth that leaves a flat land of 10 % of the pitch.

face.description: The face to work on: give faceNear (a point on the face), or faceIndex, or faceName. The command records the face name so a later edit of the model finds the same face (REF_LOST when it is gone).

faceIndex.description: Unique face index of the solid (inspect_faces / inspect_topology list them).

faceName.description: Persistent face name recorded by an earlier run of this command; wins over faceIndex and faceNear.

faceNear.description: A point on or near the intended face [x, y, z] in world document units; the face nearest to it is taken.

helixAngleDeg.description: Helix angle from the axis, degrees in (0, 90), for diagonal and diamond patterns. Default 30 (named default).

id.description: Id of the solid.

model.description: cosmetic (default): a PMI note only. geometry: cut V-grooves into the solid (straight pattern only).

pattern.description: straight: teeth parallel to the axis; diagonal: one helix; diamond: two crossed helices.

pitch.description: Circular pitch asked for, document units, > 0. The pitch used is adjusted so a whole number of teeth closes (data.pitch).

toothAngleDeg.description: geometry only: included angle of the V groove, degrees in (0, 180). Default 90 (named default).

name: add_knurl

description: Create a new layer with the given name and append it to the layer order. Returns the new layer id in affected. The layer starts visible and unlocked.

color.description: Optional hex color string #rrggbb for the layer, e.g. "#ff0000"; any other format is rejected. Used by the UI to tint layer contents. Omit to leave unset.

name.description: Human-readable name for the new layer, e.g. "Walls". Must be non-empty.

name: add_layer

description: Add a building level (storey). Elevation is the finished-floor height; height is floor-to-floor. Defaults: elevation = top of the highest existing level (or 0), height = 3000 mm. Building elements (walls, slabs, columns…) are placed relative to their level.

elevation.description: Finished-floor elevation in document units. Default: stacks on the top level.

height.description: Floor-to-floor height in document units (> 0). Default 3000 mm.

makeActive.description: Make it the active level for new elements. Default true.

name.description: Level name, e.g. "Ground floor", "Level 1".

name: add_level

description: Add a location dimension between two features of one 3D solid: the distance between parallel planes, between parallel hole axes, or from a hole axis to a plane, or the angle (degrees) between normals / axes. Each side is named by facesNear points on ONE plane or ONE hole. The value is measured from the exact B-rep. Omit tolerance for a basic (theoretically exact, boxed) dimension, the usual base of a position tolerance. Needs the OCC kernel. Refusals: GDT_LOCATION_AMBIGUOUS, GDT_LOCATION_INVALID, GDT_LOCATION_SAME_FEATURE, GDT_LIMITS_INVERTED, GDT_POINT_NOT_ON_FACE. Review required.

entityId.description: Id of the 3D solid.

from.description: Points on the first feature (one plane or one hole).

items.description: World point [x, y, z] on the first feature.

measure.description: distance in document length units, or angle in degrees.

placement.description: Optional explicit annotation placement; omit for the automatic plane (recomputed when the model changes). An explicit placement is kept.

leaderTo.description: Optional leader attachment point on the feature [x, y, z].

normal.description: Annotation plane unit normal [x, y, z].

origin.description: Annotation plane origin [x, y, z], document units.

position.description: Frame centre in plane coordinates [u, v], document units.

xDir.description: Annotation plane x direction [x, y, z] (unit, perpendicular to normal).

to.description: Points on the second feature (one plane or one hole).

items.description: World point [x, y, z] on the second feature.

lower.description: Lower deviation (<= upper), e.g. 0 or -0.05. Document length units (degrees for an angle).

type.description: Deviations from the measured nominal.

upper.description: Upper deviation (>= lower), e.g. 0.021. Document length units (degrees for an angle).

lower.description: Lower limit of size, e.g. 6.6. Document length units (degrees for an angle).

type.description: Absolute limits of size.

upper.description: Upper limit of size (>= lower), e.g. 6.9. Document length units (degrees for an angle).

lower.description: Lower deviation from the nominal for that code. Document length units (degrees for an angle).

type.description: ISO fit class code as text with its explicit deviations (no ISO 286 table is shipped).

upper.description: Upper deviation from the nominal for that code. Document length units (degrees for an angle).

type.description: Theoretically exact dimension, shown boxed, no tolerance.

tolerance.description: Optional tolerance; omitted = basic dimension.

description: Add a drainage manhole / inspection chamber / outfall at a plan position. Give `invertElevation` and either `rimElevation` or a `surfaceId` (rim = ground level there). Optional catchment (area in ha, runoff coefficient), point inflow and `entryTimeMin` (inlet time, default 5 min) feed the network check. Connect manholes with add_drainage_pipe.

catchmentAreaHa.description: Contributing catchment area in hectares (> 0) for the rational method.

diameter.description: Chamber internal diameter in document units (> 0). Default 1200 mm.

entryTimeMin.description: Inlet (entry) time in minutes (> 0) of this manhole's catchment for the time of concentration. Default 5.

inflowLps.description: Additional point inflow in litres per second (>= 0).

invertElevation.description: Invert (lowest internal) elevation of the chamber.

location.description: Plan position [x, y] of the chamber centre, document units.

name.description: Display name. Default "MH<n>".

rimElevation.description: Rim (cover level) elevation; must be above the invert. Overrides `surfaceId`.

runoffCoefficient.description: Runoff coefficient C, 0 to 1. Default 0.9 when a catchment area is given.

surfaceId.description: Surface id; when `rimElevation` is omitted the rim is the ground level there.

description: Attach a constitutive or durability law to a material (create_material first): linear elasticity (isotropic, orthotropic, transversely isotropic, anisotropic), J2 plasticity with isotropic and kinematic hardening, Ramberg-Osgood, hyperelasticity (Neo-Hooke, Mooney-Rivlin, polynomial, Yeoh, Ogden, Arruda-Boyce), Prony viscoelasticity, Norton / Garofalo creep, Johnson-Cook / Cowper-Symonds rate laws, and the fatigue / crack-growth variants. Parameters carry units; conventions are stated, never guessed (linear hardening needs modulusKind plastic or tangent, curves need their measure, Ogden needs its convention, Ramberg-Osgood its form); llull stores the canonical form and records the conversion. Elastic stiffness must be positive definite and a hyperelastic law Drucker-stable inside its declared stretch validity. The parameter hash is recomputed. Next: define_constitutive_set, then material_point_response and check_material_models.

basis.description: A | B | S, typical, supplier_unstated, company, unspecified (typical / unstated / unspecified ⇒ unverified).

fit.description: Fit record exactly as returned by fit_material_model (never hand-written).

id.description: Model id, unique on the material, e.g. "elastic", "plastic.iso", "treloar.yeoh".

material.description: Material id: the name given to create_material.

model.description: The law, by kind. ELASTIC: elastic_isotropic {E, nu}; elastic_orthotropic {E1,E2,E3,nu12,nu13,nu23,G12,G13,G23}; elastic_transversely_isotropic {isotropyPlane '12'|'23', Ep, Et, nuP, nuPT, Gt}; elastic_anisotropic {stiffness: 21 numbers, upper triangle row-wise in Voigt order 11 22 33 12 13 23 (engineering shear), unit}. PLASTIC: j2_plasticity {isotropic: perfect {yieldStress} | linear {yieldStress, modulus, modulusKind plastic|tangent REQUIRED} | multilinear {stressUnit, curves [{temperature?, points [[stress, plasticStrain]…]}], inputMeasure {stress true|engineering, strain plastic|total, strainKind true|engineering, youngModulus? for total} REQUIRED} | voce {yieldStress, Q, b} | johnson_cook {A, B, n, m, meltTemperature, transitionTemperature}; kinematic: none | linear {C} | chaboche {backstresses [{C, gamma}…]}}; ramberg_osgood {form 'calculix' {E, nu, sigma0, alpha, n} | 'engineering' {E, nu, sigma02, n} REQUIRED}; hill48_plasticity {isotropic: as j2 (the reference flow stress), form 'stress_ratios' {anisotropy {R11,R22,R33,R12,R13,R23}} | 'r_values' {anisotropy {r0,r45,r90}} | 'coefficients' {anisotropy {F,G,H,L,M,N}} REQUIRED, material axes 1-2-3, stored as F,G,H,L,M,N; needs elastic_isotropic or elastic_orthotropic; no CalculiX / Nastran card}. HYPERELASTIC (stress parameters {value, unit}, D in 1/stress, D1 > 0 compressible: W = W_dev + Σ (1/D_i)(J − 1)^2i, Arruda-Boyce (1/D)((J² − 1)/2 − ln J); D = 0 incompressible): hyper_neo_hooke {C10, D1}; hyper_mooney_rivlin {C10, C01, D1}; hyper_polynomial {order, C {C10…}, D[], stressUnit}; hyper_reduced_polynomial {order, Ci0[], D[], stressUnit}; hyper_yeoh {C10, C20, C30, D[3], compliance}; hyper_ogden {convention 'calculix'|'ogden1972' REQUIRED, terms [{mu, alpha}] (1-3), D[], stressUnit}; hyper_arruda_boyce {mu, lambdaM, D}. TIME: visco_prony {shear [{g, tau}], bulk?, shift? wlf|arrhenius}; creep_norton {A, n, m, stressUnit, timeUnit, hardening}; creep_garofalo {A, alpha, n, activationEnergy}; rate_johnson_cook {C, referenceRate}; rate_cowper_symonds {D, q}. DURABILITY (stored and validated structurally, never in a set): sn_basquin, sn_power_law, sn_table, sn_equivalent_stress, en_coffin_manson, cyclic_ramberg_osgood, haigh_table, da_dn_paris, da_dn_walker, da_dn_forman, da_dn_nasgro, da_dn_table, fracture_toughness. A stress-like parameter is {value, unit} or {propertyModelId} (a define_property_model model of the same material, e.g. E(T)).

preferred.description: Mark as THE model of its kind on the material (one per kind).

replace.description: Replace an existing model with the same id (default false: refused with MATL_MODEL_EXISTS).

source.description: Provenance of the parameters (required).

locator.description: Table / page / figure in the source.

sourceId.description: Registered source id, when one exists.

validity.description: Ranges the law is valid in (T, equivalentPlasticStrain, strainRate, time, stretch): REQUIRED for exports, advised for every constitutive law.

data.description: [min, max] of the data the parameters were derived from.

equation.description: [min, max] the source allows (⊇ data; default = data).

unit.description: Unit of the bounds, e.g. 'K', '1/s', '1'.

variable.description: State variable the range applies to: T, strainRate, time, equivalentPlasticStrain, stretch …

name: add_material_model

description: Detail the portal frame moment connections: a bolted end plate at every rafter-to-column joint (eaves, with a haunch under the rafter) and a pair of end plates at every rafter-to-rafter joint (apex), for the given rafters or every rafter of the level. Sized from the rafter section (plate 20/25 mm, M20 bolts, haunch = 1/5 of the rafter plan length). Follows the rafter; plate, haunch and bolt quantities feed the takeoff and the connection schedule.

apexHaunchLength.description: Apex haunch length along each of the two rafters meeting at the ridge, in document units. Default none.

boltDiameter.description: Bolt diameter, in document units. Default 20 mm (M20).

haunchLength.description: Eaves haunch length along the rafter. Default 1/5 of its plan length.

levelId.description: Level id. Default: the active level.

plateThickness.description: End plate thickness, in document units. Default 20 / 25 mm.

rafterIds.description: Rafter member ids. Default: every rafter of the level.

name: add_moment_connections

description: Drive a joint for simulate_motion. kind "torque_curve" = an engine or electric motor: torque (N·m) vs shaft speed (rpm) at full throttle, e.g. curve [[0, 300], [2000, 420], [2800, 400], [3200, 0]], times `throttle` (0..1). A single constant torque: `torque: 50` (same as a one-point curve). The speed then rises until the load (propeller, friction, damping) absorbs the torque — the physically settled operating point. kind "speed" = a governed drive that holds `rpm` using at most `maxTorque` N·m (a test rig / constant-speed prop governor). Torque acts in the joint's positive direction (right-hand rule about the joint axis). Returns the motor id in affected[0].

curve.description: torque_curve: [[rpm, torque N·m], …] with increasing rpm; linear between points, held flat outside them.

id.description: Optional explicit motor id.

joint.description: Joint id to drive (e.g. the crankshaft joint).

kind.description: "torque_curve" = engine (torque vs rpm); "speed" = holds a set rpm.

rpm.description: speed: target shaft speed in rpm.

throttle.description: torque_curve: fraction of the curve torque, 0..1. Default 1.

torque.description: torque_curve shortcut: one constant torque in N·m (instead of curve).

name: add_motor

description: Add a flanged nozzle to an equipment (vessel from add_vessel, or any add_equipment block). Identify the equipment by tag or id. `mark` is unique per equipment (N1, M1 ...); the connection port is "<tag>:<mark>", e.g. "V-101:N1". Size by dn or nps, rating CL150 / PN16 ..., facing RF / FF / RTJ. location: { on: "shell", elevation (vertical vessel, above the bottom tangent line) or station (horizontal vessel, from the left tangent line), orientationDeg } | { on: "head", head: top | bottom | left | right, radialOffset, orientationDeg } | { on: "free", position, direction } in the equipment frame (blocks, pumps). projection = distance from the vessel AXIS to the flange face (shell nozzles) or from the TANGENT LINE to the face (head nozzles), document units. Angles use angleConvention (north_cw default: vertical 0 = plant north growing clockwise; horizontal 0 = top). The flange comes from the piping catalogue (placeholder warning when no row). Returns portId, world position and unit direction of the flange face (what route_pipe / routing connect to), flange, warnings, angleConvention. Refusals: EQP_NOT_FOUND, EQP_NOZZLE_MARK_DUPLICATE, EQP_NOZZLE_OFF_BODY, EQP_NOZZLE_PROJECTION_TOO_SHORT, EQP_RATING_UNKNOWN, EQP_PARAM_INVALID.

angleConvention.description: How angles in this call are read and reported. north_cw (default): vertical equipment 0 = plant north (+Y), growing clockwise seen from above (90 = east, +X); horizontal equipment 0 = top (+Z), 90 = the +Y side; a plan rotation grows clockwise. east_ccw: CAD maths, 0 = east (+X), growing counter-clockwise; horizontal equipment 0 = +Y, 90 = top; a plan rotation grows counter-clockwise. Every result names the convention.

dn.description: Nominal size DN (15..600 of the EN 10220 series). Give dn OR nps.

equipment.description: Equipment tag (e.g. "V-101", the element mark) or element id (e.g. "equipment-3").

location.description: Where the nozzle sits. Only the fields of the chosen `on` are read.

direction.description: free: outward direction of the nozzle axis [dx, dy, dz] in the equipment frame; normalised.

elevation.description: shell, vertical vessel: height above the bottom tangent line, 0..tangentLength.

head.description: head: top / bottom for a vertical vessel, left / right for a horizontal one.

on.description: shell: on the cylinder (vertical vessel: elevation; horizontal vessel: station). head: on a formed head (top / bottom or left / right) at radialOffset. free: any equipment, including plain add_equipment blocks and pumps: position + direction in the equipment frame.

orientationDeg.description: shell / head: angle around the vessel axis in degrees, read with angleConvention. Default 0 (north / top).

position.description: free: flange face centre [x, y, z] in the equipment frame (origin = plan location at the level elevation, +Z up).

radialOffset.description: head: distance of the nozzle axis from the vessel axis, 0 = on the axis (default), below the inside radius.

station.description: shell, horizontal vessel: distance from the left tangent line, 0..tangentLength.

mark.description: Nozzle mark, unique on this equipment: N1, M1, S1 ...

nps.description: Nominal pipe size in inches, e.g. 6 or "2-1/2"; converted to DN. Give dn OR nps.

projection.description: Distance to the flange FACE: shell nozzles from the vessel axis, head nozzles from the tangent line, free nozzles the neck length behind position. Document units.

rating.description: Flange rating: CL150, CL300, CL600 ... or PN16, PN40 ...
