thickness.description: flat only: plate thickness in document units (not used by volumes).

type.description: Head type. ellipsoidal: needs ratio (2 = 2:1 semi-ellipsoidal, depth = D/4). torispherical: needs standard OR crownRadius + knuckleRadius. hemispherical: depth = D/2. flat: depth 0. conical: needs halfAngleDeg (apex half-angle from the axis, 0..90 exclusive).

insideDiameter.description: Inside diameter of the shell, document units.

levelId.description: Level id. Default: the active level (a "Level 0" is created if none).

location.description: Plan position [x, y] of the vessel axis (document units).

name.description: Descriptive name, e.g. "HP separator". Default: the tag.

planRotationDeg.description: Plan rotation of the equipment frame about +Z in degrees, read with angleConvention. Default 0.

platformClips.description: Platform support clips on the shell (read by the structures plugin for platform layout).

depth.description: Radial projection of the clip. Default 100 mm.

elevation.description: Clip elevation above the bottom tangent line, document units.

fromDeg.description: Start angle of the clip arc around the column, read with angleConvention.

height.description: Clip height. Default 100 mm.

toDeg.description: End angle of the clip arc; the arc runs from fromDeg to toDeg in the direction the convention grows.

shellThickness.description: Nominal shell wall thickness (corrosion allowance included), document units.

support.description: Support of the vessel; only the fields of the chosen type are read.

axisElevation.description: saddles: height of the vessel axis above the level; must exceed the shell outside radius.

baseElevation.description: none: elevation of the lowest shell point (horizontal) or bottom tangent line (vertical) above the level. Default 0.

baseRingWidth.description: skirt: width of the base ring outside the skirt. Default 0 (no ring).

count.description: legs: number of legs, at least 3, spread evenly (none on the north axis).

height.description: skirt / legs: height from the level (floor) to the bottom tangent line, document units.

legWidth.description: legs: side of the square leg section. Default: 5 % of the shell outside diameter.

pitchDiameter.description: legs: diameter of the circle through the leg centres. Default: the shell outside diameter.

stations.description: saddles: positions along the vessel from the left tangent line, each inside 0..tangentLength.

thickness.description: skirt: wall thickness. Default: the shell thickness (reported in defaulted).

type.description: skirt (vertical): needs height. legs (vertical): needs count >= 3 and height. saddles (horizontal): needs stations, width and axisElevation. none: needs nothing (baseElevation optional).

width.description: saddles: width of each saddle along the vessel axis.

tag.description: Equipment tag, unique in the document, e.g. "V-101". It is the element mark and the first half of the port ids.

tangentLength.description: Tangent-to-tangent length of the cylindrical shell, document units (heads excluded).

trays.description: Tray stack. Tray i is at firstElevation + (i - 1) x spacing above the bottom tangent line and must not exceed tangentLength.

firstElevation.description: Elevation of the first tray above the bottom tangent line, document units.

type.description: Tray type label, e.g. "sieve", "valve". Informational.

name: add_process_column

description: Load a revolute joint with a propeller's aerodynamics for simulate_motion (static / take-off condition by default). With n = rev/s and D = diameter (m): thrust T = Ct·ρ·n²·D⁴ (pushes the spinning body along thrustDirection), shaft power P = Cp·ρ·n³·D⁵, drag torque Q = P/(2πn) against the rotation. Ct, Cp come from propeller test data (static): typical fixed-pitch wooden / composite props Ct 0.08–0.14, Cp 0.04–0.08 (larger pitch → larger Cp). Use the PROPELLER joint (after any reduction gear). Forward flight (FR-FPR-75): give `table` (measured [J, Ct, Cp] rows, J = V/(n·D), strictly increasing from 0, with a source: monotone cubic interpolation, held at the ends) and `airspeedMps`; Ct, Cp then follow the table whenever J > 0 (J = 0 keeps the static pair) and a run beyond the last J warns FPR_OUTSIDE_VALIDATED_RANGE. No propeller table ships with llull: use measured data (NACA TR-640 class curves are about 1 % repeatable, applicability to your propeller is not validated). `inertiaKgM2` declares the shaft inertia when the propeller is not a rigid body (plausibility-checked against the Rotax 912 limit 0.15-0.60 kg·m²). Returns the propeller id in affected[0].

airspeedMps.description: Forward speed of the air relative to the propeller, m/s (>= 0). Needs `table`. Default 0 (static).

id.description: Optional explicit propeller id.

inertiaKgM2.description: Propeller moment of inertia about its shaft, kg·m² (when it is not a rigid body).

joint.description: Revolute joint the propeller turns on.

table.description: Measured Ct(J), Cp(J) replacing the static pair when J > 0.

grade.description: Source grade: A measured / verified, B published curve, C reconstructed or unchecked. Default C.

points.description: [[J, Ct, Cp], ...]: advance ratio J = V/(n·D) strictly increasing, first J >= 0.

source.description: Where the table comes from (report, figure, test); required.

thrustDirection.description: World direction of the thrust on the propeller (the pull direction), e.g. [0, 1, 0].

name: add_propeller

description: Create a pyramid solid with a rectangular base and a single apex. Right-handed world frame, +Z up. The base extends ±baseWidth/2 in X and ±baseDepth/2 in Y from the anchor point. The apex is at base-center + [0, 0, height]. All three dimensions must be > 0. anchor controls which point the position refers to: "base-center" (default) = center of the rectangular base; apex at position+[0,0,height]; "center" = geometric center of the AABB; "min" = min-XYZ corner of the AABB. The anchor offset is applied in the local UNROTATED frame; rotation is then applied by the viewport about the stored origin.

anchor.description: Which point on the pyramid the position refers to. "base-center" (default): center of the rectangular base; apex at position+[0,0,height]. "center": geometric center of the AABB (mid X/Y/Z). "min": min-XYZ corner of the AABB. Unknown values fall back to "base-center". Offset is applied in the local UNROTATED frame; viewport rotates about the stored origin.

baseDepth.description: Full depth of the rectangular base along Y in document units. Must be > 0.

baseWidth.description: Full width of the rectangular base along X in document units. Must be > 0.

color.description: Hex color string #rrggbb, e.g. "#c8553d". Defaults to "#6b8f9c".

height.description: Height from the base center to the apex along the local +Z axis in document units. Must be > 0.

position.description: World-space location of the anchor point [x, y, z] in document units. Right-handed frame, +Z up. Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

rotation.description: three.js intrinsic XYZ Euler angles in RADIANS [rx, ry, rz] (equivalent to rotating about world Z first, then world Y, then world X). Matches rotate_entity convention. Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. If non-finite or not length-3 the rotation is ignored and [0,0,0] is used.

name: add_pyramid

description: Store measured or datasheet data an engine model is validated against (FR-FPR-77); compare_to_reference runs the model at each point and reports S (simulated), D (reference), E = S - D, E/D, the validation uncertainty and pass / fail against the band. Give a `preset` for the shipped public curves: "rotax_912uls_full_throttle" (brake torque 2500-5800 rpm, digitised from the OM-912 graph, +-1 N·m), "rotax_912is_power_table" (brake power kW, 5 points), "o320a_full_throttle" and "o320b_full_throttle" (Lycoming brake power kW, 2200-2800 rpm), "rotax_912_static_rpm_window" (fixed-pitch static full-throttle rpm 5100-5800); any field you add overrides the preset. Or give your own: `quantity` (brake_torque_Nm, brake_power_kW, bmep_bar, static_rpm, propeller_rpm, bsfc_g_per_kWh), `points`, `source` (required), `grade`. `calibrationRpm` lists the points you calibrate the model on (default practice: the rated point only; presets name theirs): those get origin "calibrated", are shown as information and never count as pass evidence; every other point is a hold-out prediction. `bandRel` is the relative pass band, default 0.05 [GT-Power calibration practice]. Returns the reference id in affected[0].

altitudeM.description: Altitude of the measurement, m (default 0). llull does not model altitude: a non-zero value is reported as a warning.

calibrationRpm.description: Speeds (rpm) of the points the model is calibrated on; they must be point speeds.

digitised.description: The points were read off a graph (the uncertainty is then the reading error). Default false.

grade.description: Source grade: A measured / verified, B manufacturer data or digitised graph, C reconstructed. Default C.

id.description: Optional explicit reference id.

note.description: Free note on the condition (fuel, ignition, propeller).

points.description: Reference points; at least one. Required without a preset.

max.description: Upper bound of a window point.

min.description: Lower bound of a window point (e.g. the static rpm window): the model passes when inside min..max.

rpm.description: Crank speed of the point, rpm (omit for a quantity that does not depend on speed).

uncertainty.description: Reading / measurement uncertainty of `value`, same unit (digitised graphs: the reading error). Omit = unknown.

value.description: Measured / datasheet value in the unit of the quantity; for a window point the window centre.

preset.description: Shipped public data set; its id is the preset name unless `id` is given.

quantity.description: What the points are: brake_torque_Nm, brake_power_kW, bmep_bar, static_rpm, propeller_rpm or bsfc_g_per_kWh.

source.description: REQUIRED without a preset: document, figure or test the data comes from.

throttle.description: Operating condition: "full" throttle (default) or along the "propeller_curve".

name: add_reference_data

description: Add a rectangular bend relief to a sheet-metal part: a notch cut into the parent flat beside one end of a bend, so the bend can form without tearing. bend is the bend node id (listed in flat_pattern data.bends[].id), end 'start' or 'end' is the end of the bend line (the end the flange stops short of the edge end). width (along the bend line, beyond its end) and depth (into the parent flat from the bend tangent line) are in the document length unit; when omitted they come from the rule's relief (width = widthRatio x thickness, depth = inside radius + thickness + depthExtra) and the summary says so. The notch must fit on the free stretch of the edge. Refusals: FTR_PART_NOT_FOUND, FTR_PARAM_INVALID, FTR_RELIEF_INVALID. Next: check_sheet_metal (FTR_RELIEF_MISSING), flat_pattern.

bend.description: Bend node id inside the part (e.g. "b1"), see flat_pattern data.bends[].id.

depth.description: Relief depth into the parent flat in the document length unit; > 0. Default inside radius + thickness + depthExtra from the rule relief.

end.description: Which end of the bend line gets the relief: 'start' or 'end' (the flange is narrower than the edge at that end).

id.description: Sheet-metal part id (returned by add_sheet_metal_base).

width.description: Relief width along the bend line in the document length unit; > 0. Default from the rule relief (widthRatio x thickness).

name: add_relief

description: Add a result probe to an analysis: a point (document units) at which a quantity is read from the solved results (the nearest node is used). quantity: temperature (thermal / thermo-mechanical cases, in the case temperature scale), heat_flux, u_mag / u_x / u_y / u_z (displacement), von_mises, s_xx / s_yy / s_zz (stress), and the cylindrical components s_hoop / s_radial / s_axial / u_radial about an axis (axisPoint + axisDirection; default: the z axis through the centre of the mesh bounding box, so a quarter / half model needs the real axis; hoop / radial are null on the axis). Dynamic cases: random_response probes read a_x / a_y / a_z (absolute acceleration rms, g), u_x_rel / u_y_rel / u_z_rel (displacement relative to the base) and s_xx / s_yy / s_zz; frequency_response probes read u_x / u_y / u_z and s_xx / s_yy / s_zz (complex response peaks). Returns the probe id in affected[0].

analysisId.description: Id of the analysis (affected[0] of create_analysis, e.g. an-1.1).

axisDirection.description: Only for s_hoop / s_radial / s_axial / u_radial.

axisPoint.description: Only for s_hoop / s_radial / s_axial / u_radial.

name.description: Display name, e.g. "hot spot".

point.description: Probe location [x, y, z] in document units; it should lie on or inside a part.

quantity.description: Quantity to read at the point.

name: add_result_probe

description: Grow a rib from a planar face of a 3D solid: an OPEN polyline path (>= 2 points) is thickened by thickness (centred on the path when symmetric, else on its left), raised along the plane normal and fused to the part. plane = { origin: a point on the supporting face, normal: the OUTWARD normal of that face, which is the direction the rib rises }; the path lies on that plane in [u, v] face coordinates (origin = the world origin projected on the plane, u = world X (or Y) projected on it, v = normal x u) or, with pointsFrame "world_xy", world [x, y]. Give exactly one of height (rib height above the plane) or upToFace (stop at the plane of a parallel planar face above it). All lengths are in the document length unit. The rib must stand entirely on the face: otherwise it is refused. Consumes target, creates one mesh entity. Refusals carry error.code: FTR_FACE_NOT_FOUND (no such target), FTR_FACE_NOT_PLANAR, FTR_RIB_PATH_NOT_SUPPORTED, FTR_PROFILE_NOT_CLOSED (bad path), FTR_PARAM_INVALID, FTR_UP_TO_TARGET_INVALID, FTR_FEATURE_BUILD_FAILED. Next: check_machining, inspect_topology.

height.description: Rib height above the plane, in document length units. Omit with upToFace.

path.description: Open polyline of the rib, >= 2 vertices [u, v] (pointsFrame), in document length units; consecutive vertices distinct, no self-crossing.

plane.description: The supporting plane the rib stands on and its rise direction.

normal.description: Outward normal [x, y, z] of the supporting face = the direction the rib rises; any non-zero length (normalised).

origin.description: World point [x, y, z] on the supporting planar face, in document length units.

pointsFrame.description: Coordinates of path: "face" (default), "world_xy" or "world" ([x, y, z]).

symmetric.description: true (default) = the rib is centred on the path; false = the thickness lies on the left of the path direction (in u, v).

target.description: Id of the 3D solid to add the rib to (a primitive or a kernel result).

thickness.description: Rib thickness measured across the path, in document length units; must be > 0.

upToFace.description: Raise the rib up to the plane of this planar face, which must be parallel to the plane and above it. Omit height.

near.description: World point [x, y, z] on the planar target face, in document length units.

name: add_rib

description: Make a set of 3D entities move together as ONE rigid body for physics simulation (simulate_motion). Mass, centre of mass and inertia are computed from the entities' real geometry: each entity uses its assigned material (density model, else plain density), else `density` (kg/m³, default 7850 steel; aluminium 2700, wood 600, CFRP 1550; or pass densityUnit, e.g. { density: 7.85, densityUnit: "g/cm^3" }: the same densityUnit option as create_material, whose bare density is g/(document unit)³ instead). Give `massKg` when the real part mass is known (hollow parts): the distribution is scaled to it. Give `inertiaKgM2` when the inertia is known (a point mass on a rod, a measured part): it replaces the inertia computed from the geometry (the centre of mass still comes from the geometry). `fixed: true` welds the body to the ground (engine block, frame, stand). A non-fixed body with no joint is a free body that falls under gravity. Next: connect bodies with add_body_joint. Returns the body id in affected[0] and its mass / centre of mass in the summary.

density.description: Density for entities without a material: kg/m³ unless densityUnit is given. Default 7850 (steel).

densityUnit.description: Optional unit of `density`, e.g. "kg/m^3" (default), "g/cm^3", "lb/in^3"; converted to kg/m³ (the stored unit).

entityIds.description: Ids of the 3D entities forming the body (e.g. a propeller: hub + 3 blades + spinner).

fixed.description: true = welded to the ground (never moves). Default false.

id.description: Optional explicit body id (shares the id space of all dynamics records).

inertiaKgM2.description: Known inertia tensor in kg·m² about the centre of mass, world axes at the modelled pose: [Ixx, Iyy, Izz, Ixy, Ixz, Iyz] (tensor components, so Ixy = -∫xy dm; zeros for principal axes along x, y, z). Replaces the geometry inertia. A point mass m at distance r from its pivot: give a tiny value such as m·1e-6 on each axis.

massKg.description: Known real mass in kg; the computed mass distribution is scaled to it.

name.description: Display name, e.g. "propeller", "crankshaft".

name: add_rigid_body

description: Add a fixed, frictionless planar rigid wall to an explicit_dynamics case: `point` on the plane (document units) and `normal` pointing toward the model. Nodes are not allowed to cross the plane; the wall force history is reported by analysis_report. Returns the wall id in affected[1].

analysisId.description: Id of the analysis (affected[0] of create_analysis, e.g. an-1.1).

name.description: Unique wall name, e.g. "anvil".

normal.description: Plane normal toward the model, non-zero.

point.description: A point of the plane [x, y, z], document units.

name: add_rigid_wall

description: Define a room (space) with a name and number from a plan boundary polygon, or from wallIds forming a closed loop (the room then follows the inner wall faces). Draws the outline and an area tag; rooms feed the room schedule and IFC spaces. Refused if a room with the same outline already exists on the level.

levelId.description: Level id. Default: the active level (a "Level 0" is created if none).

name.description: Room name, e.g. "Kitchen".

number.description: Room number. Default: level index × 100 + n (e.g. "101").

wallIds.description: Alternative to boundary: ids of walls enclosing the room (closed loop).

name: add_room

description: Add a section view to a drawing sheet: the model is cut by a plane and seen from `direction` with the cut faces hatched (hidden lines omitted). `offset` is the world coordinate of the cutting plane on the axis the view looks along (x for left/right, y for front/back, z for top/bottom); material between the plane and the viewer is removed. Pass `parentViewId` to draw the cutting-plane line with arrows and the letter on that view (the parent must show the plane edge-on, i.e. be perpendicular to `direction`, e.g. parent "front" with direction "right"). Labelled "SECTION A-A" with the next free letter. Returns the view id.

direction.description: Side the section is seen from; the cutting plane is perpendicular to this direction. No iso.

entityIds.description: Ids of the 3D solids to draw. Omit to draw every visible 3D solid of the document (the usual choice).

offset.description: World coordinate of the cutting plane on the viewing axis (document units), e.g. 0 for the middle of a centred part.

paperPosition.description: Centre of the view on the paper in millimetres. Omit for automatic layout.

parentViewId.description: View on the same sheet that gets the cutting-plane line. Its entities are reused.

scale.description: Own scale denominator N of 1:N. Omit to use the sheet scale.

name: add_section_view

description: Cut a hole through ONE flat of a sheet-metal part. Give the shape ONE of three ways: `profileId` (a closed rectangle / closed polyline / circle drawn earlier on a plane PARALLEL to the flat), or `circle` { center, radius }, or `polygon` { points } given directly as WORLD points [x, y, z] that are projected normal onto the flat (no drawing needed; this is the way to cut a flange, whose plane is vertical or tilted: e.g. on a flange standing on the y = 0 edge of a part, with face.near [100, 0, 20], circle center [100, 0, 20] radius 4 cuts a hole 20 above the bend). A drawn profile on a flange needs its plane rotated onto the flange (rotate_entity, radians); circle/polygon avoid that. The cut is normal to the flat: the shape is projected onto the flat picked by the world point `face.near` (any point on or within one thickness of the flat), stored in the flat's own coordinates and appears as a cutout (CIRCLE for a circle) in flat_pattern and the DXF. The profile must lie wholly inside that flat and not touch other cutouts. All lengths are in the document length unit. Refusals: FTR_PART_NOT_FOUND, FTR_PROFILE_NOT_CLOSED, FTR_FACE_NOT_FOUND, FTR_CUTOUT_INVALID. Next: check_sheet_metal (hole-to-bend and hole-to-edge distances), flat_pattern.

circle.description: Round hole in world coordinates, projected normal onto the picked flat. Use instead of profileId.

center.description: World point [x, y, z] of the hole axis (document length unit); projected onto the flat plane.

radius.description: Hole radius in the document length unit; > 0.

near.description: World point [x, y, z] on or near the flat to cut (document length unit).

id.description: Sheet-metal part id (returned by add_sheet_metal_base).

polygon.description: Closed polygon (3+ vertices, any winding) in world coordinates, projected normal onto the picked flat. Use instead of profileId.

points.description: Polygon vertices as world points [x, y, z] (3 or more).

items.description: World point [x, y, z] of a vertex (document length unit); projected onto the flat plane.

profileId.description: Id of a closed 2D profile entity (rectangle, closed polyline or circle) on a plane parallel to the flat. Omit when giving circle or polygon.

name: add_sheet_cutout

description: Create a sheet-metal part from a closed 2D profile (rectangle or closed polyline drawn with draw_rectangle / draw_polyline) and a rule from create_sheet_metal_rule. The profile becomes the base flat of the rule's thickness on its work plane (side up = material on the +normal side, down = on the -normal side, mid = centred). Returns the part id (also the id of the derived, read-only folded solid). Lengths are in the document length unit. Refusals: FTR_RULE_NOT_FOUND, FTR_PROFILE_NOT_CLOSED (open, self-intersecting, or not a rectangle/closed polyline). Next: add_flange, add_sheet_cutout, flat_pattern, check_sheet_metal.

profileId.description: Id of a closed 2D profile entity (rectangle or closed polyline). It stays in the document.

rule.description: Name of a rule created with create_sheet_metal_rule; it supplies thickness, radius and K-factor.

side.description: Where the material lies relative to the profile plane: 'up' (+normal), 'down' (-normal) or 'mid' (centred).

name: add_sheet_metal_base

description: Add a size dimension with tolerance on a feature of size of a 3D solid: a cylinder (hole / shaft, sizeKind diameter or radius), two opposite parallel planes (width of a slot or tab), or a sphere (spherical_diameter), named by facesNear points. The nominal is measured from the exact B-rep (never typed); a pattern of equal holes (one point per hole) gives nX = the number of holes. Tolerance: plusMinus deviations, absolute limits, a fit code with explicit deviations, or basic. Optional ISO 14405 sizeModifiers (E envelope, LP, GG ...). Needs the OCC kernel. Refusals: GDT_NOT_FOS (a plane alone), GDT_SIZE_MIXED, GDT_SIZE_KIND_MISMATCH, GDT_LIMITS_INVERTED, GDT_POINT_NOT_ON_FACE, GDT_KERNEL_NO_TOPOLOGY. Review required. The pmi id in affected can be the target of add_geometric_tolerance (targetPmiId) and a stack-up contributor (pmiId).

entityId.description: Id of the 3D solid.

facesNear.description: World points, one per face of the feature (document units). The faces are re-found from these points at every replay, so PMI follows its face through parametric edits. A pattern of equal holes takes one point on each hole. Use inspect_faces to find points on faces.

items.description: One world point [x, y, z] ON the face (document units), e.g. a point from inspect_faces centroid or samples.

placement.description: Optional explicit annotation placement; omit for the automatic plane (recomputed when the model changes). An explicit placement is kept.

leaderTo.description: Optional leader attachment point on the feature [x, y, z].

normal.description: Annotation plane unit normal [x, y, z].

origin.description: Annotation plane origin [x, y, z], document units.

position.description: Frame centre in plane coordinates [u, v], document units.

xDir.description: Annotation plane x direction [x, y, z] (unit, perpendicular to normal).

sizeKind.description: Kind of size; decides which faces are valid (see the description).

sizeModifiers.description: ISO 14405-1 size modifier codes, stored and shown with the dimension. E = envelope.

lower.description: Lower deviation (<= upper), e.g. 0 or -0.05. Document length units (degrees for an angle).

type.description: Deviations from the measured nominal.

upper.description: Upper deviation (>= lower), e.g. 0.021. Document length units (degrees for an angle).

lower.description: Lower limit of size, e.g. 6.6. Document length units (degrees for an angle).

type.description: Absolute limits of size.

upper.description: Upper limit of size (>= lower), e.g. 6.9. Document length units (degrees for an angle).

lower.description: Lower deviation from the nominal for that code. Document length units (degrees for an angle).

type.description: ISO fit class code as text with its explicit deviations (no ISO 286 table is shipped).

upper.description: Upper deviation from the nominal for that code. Document length units (degrees for an angle).

type.description: Theoretically exact dimension, shown boxed, no tolerance.

tolerance.description: Tolerance as { type: "plusMinus", upper, lower } deviations, { type: "limits", upper, lower } absolute limits, { type: "fit", code, upper, lower } or { type: "basic" }.

name: add_size_dimension

description: Add a floor, roof or foundation slab whose TOP sits at the level elevation + offset. Give either a plan boundary polygon or wallIds forming a closed loop (edge at the wall centerlines by default, see wallFace). Refused if a slab with the same outline, offset and role already exists on the level.

levelId.description: Level id. Default: the active level (a "Level 0" is created if none).

offset.description: Top-of-slab offset from the level elevation. Default 0 (roof: put it on the level above).

role.description: Slab role used in schedules and IFC. Default floor.

thickness.description: Slab thickness (> 0), in document units. Default 200 mm.

wallFace.description: With wallIds: slab edge at the outer wall faces, the wall centerlines (default — the slab bears into the walls), or the inner faces.

wallIds.description: Alternative to boundary: wall ids forming a closed loop.

name: add_slab

description: Cut a void through a slab (stair well, lift or service shaft). Give a plan boundary polygon, or a stairId to cut its well (footprint + margin) in the floor slab of the level above — slabId is then found automatically. Openings are deducted from quantities and exported as IFC openings.

boundary.description: Opening polygon [[x, y], …], strictly inside the slab.

margin.description: With stairId: clearance around the stair footprint, in document units. Default 100 mm.

slabId.description: Slab element id, e.g. "slab-2". Optional with stairId.

stairId.description: Alternative to boundary: cut the well of this stair.

name: add_slab_opening

description: Create a sphere solid. Right-handed world frame, +Z up. radius must be > 0. rotation is accepted and stored for uniformity but is geometrically moot. anchor controls which point the position refers to: "center" (default) = geometric center; "min" = min-XYZ corner of the AABB; "base-center" = center of the bottom face (mid X/Y, min Z). The anchor offset is applied in the local UNROTATED frame; rotation is then applied by the viewport about the stored origin.

anchor.description: Which point on the sphere the position refers to. "center" (default): geometric center. "min": min-XYZ corner of the AABB. "base-center": center of the bottom face (mid X/Y, min Z). Unknown values fall back to "center". Offset is applied in the local UNROTATED frame; viewport rotates about the stored origin.

color.description: Hex color string #rrggbb, e.g. "#c8553d". Defaults to "#6b8f9c".

position.description: World-space location of the anchor point [x, y, z] in document units. Right-handed frame, +Z up. Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

radius.description: Radius of the sphere in document units. Must be > 0.

rotation.description: three.js intrinsic XYZ Euler angles in RADIANS [rx, ry, rz] (equivalent to rotating about world Z first, then world Y, then world X). Stored for uniformity; geometrically moot for a sphere. Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. If non-finite or not length-3 the rotation is ignored and [0,0,0] is used.

name: add_sphere

description: Create an involute spline shaft in the style of DIN 5480 (e.g. W200x5x38 = referenceDiameter 200, module 5, 38 teeth) as one extrusion along +Z (z from 0 to length). Tooth count follows DIN 5480: teeth = referenceDiameter/module - 2 (override with `teeth`). Flanks are involutes of the generating circle (module*teeth/2) at the 30° pressure angle; the nominal tooth thickness on the reference circle is half the pitch; tip radius = referenceDiameter/2 - 0.1*module, tooth depth 0.9*module (approximation of the DIN tolerances). Tooth flanks are sampled coarsely (7 points) to keep STEP/boolean cost low.

color.description: Hex color. Default "#9aa3ad".

name.description: Optional display name for the entity (shown in the scene tree).

position.description: World-space location of the anchor point [x, y, z] in document units. Right-handed frame, +Z up. Centre of the bottom face. Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

pressureAngle.description: Flank pressure angle in RADIANS, in (0, π/2). Default 0.5236 (30°, DIN 5480).

referenceDiameter.description: DIN 5480 reference diameter dB, > 0 (e.g. 200 for W200x5x38).

rotation.description: three.js intrinsic XYZ Euler angles in RADIANS [rx, ry, rz] (equivalent to rotating about world Z first, then world Y, then world X). Matches rotate_entity convention. Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. If non-finite or not length-3 the rotation is ignored and [0,0,0] is used.

name: add_spline_shaft

description: Add a spring-damper force element (physics, for simulate_motion; NOT the add_coil solid geometry) between a point on one rigid body and a point on another body or the ground, for simulate_motion (a coil spring, a gas strut, a bungee, an engine-valve spring). Force along the line joining the two points: F = stiffness · (length - freeLength) + damping · d(length)/dt, positive = pulling the ends together; it works in any direction and for any joint arrangement (a rocker, a four-bar link, a falling body). `pointA` / `pointB` are WORLD points in DOCUMENT units at the pose the bodies are modelled in (where the spring physically attaches); each then rides on its body. With pointFrame "body" they are instead OFFSETS from each body's centre of mass (world axes, document units; a ground end stays a world point), e.g. [0, 0, 50] = 50 units above it. `bodyA` / `bodyB` are rigid body ids (add_rigid_body) or "ground". Stiffness in N/m (1 N/mm = 1000 N/m), damping in N·s/m. The spring is relaxed at `freeLengthMm` (mm); by default that is the distance between the points at the modelled pose (no force at the start). `preloadN` instead sets the tension force at the modelled pose (positive = stretched, pulling together; negative = compressed, pushing apart), which fixes the free length = distance - preloadN / stiffness; give at most one of the two. Spring energy is part of the potential energy of simulate_motion (energy: true), and simulate_motion reports each spring's length range and force (data.springs); render_motion draws it as a zig-zag. Mass on a spring: period 2π·sqrt(m/k), static deflection m·g/k. Remove with delete_dynamics_item (also removed when either body is). Returns the spring id in affected[0].

bodyA.description: Rigid body id carrying the first end, or "ground".

bodyB.description: Rigid body id carrying the second end, or "ground".

damping.description: Viscous damping along the spring in N·s/m. Default 0.

freeLengthMm.description: Length in mm at which the spring force is zero. Default: the distance between pointA and pointB (relaxed at the start).

id.description: Optional explicit spring id (shares the id space of all dynamics records).

pointA.description: World point of the first end at the modelled pose, document units.

pointB.description: World point of the second end at the modelled pose, document units. Must differ from pointA.

pointFrame.description: "world" (default): pointA / pointB are world points. "body": each is an offset from its body's centre of mass, world axes, document units (a ground end stays a world point).

preloadN.description: Alternative to freeLengthMm: tension force in N at the modelled pose (positive = stretched, pulling together; negative = compressed). Default 0.

stiffness.description: Spring rate in N/m (1 N/mm = 1000 N/m). Must be > 0.

name: add_spring

description: Create a parametric involute spur gear solid (extrusion with exact Bézier/arc tooth curves; mesh when bore > 0). Computes the full closed 2D tooth profile from module, tooth count, and pressure angle, then extrudes it by faceWidth along +Z. module (metric) sets the tooth scale: pitchDiameter = module * teeth. pressureAngle is in RADIANS; standard value is 0.3491 rad (20 degrees = Math.PI/9). faceWidth is the gear thickness along Z. bore is a central hole radius; if > 0 the gear is emitted as a closed mesh solid with a through hole (no boolean needed). position is [x, y, z] of the gear axis at its bottom face (the gear spans z..z+faceWidth, not centred on z); rotation is three.js intrinsic XYZ Euler angles in radians (about world Z, then Y, then X). Right-handed frame, +Z up.

bore.description: Central bore hole radius in document units. >= 0 and < pitch radius. Default 0 (solid hub, extrusion entity). When > 0 the result is a mesh solid with a through hole.

color.description: Hex color string #rrggbb, e.g. "#c8553d". Defaults to "#7a9cbb".

faceWidth.description: Gear face width (thickness along Z) in document units. Must be > 0. Typical: 8–12× module for spur gears.

module.description: Gear module (metric). Controls tooth scale: pitchDiameter = module * teeth. Must be > 0. Common values: 1 (small), 2 (medium), 4 (large).

name.description: Optional display name for the entity (shown in the scene tree).

position.description: World-space position [x, y, z] of the gear axis at its BOTTOM face: the gear axis passes through [x, y] and the gear spans z..z+faceWidth (it is not centred on z). Right-handed frame, +Z up. Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

pressureAngle.description: Pressure angle in RADIANS. Must be in (0, π/2). Standard value: 0.3491 rad (20°). Omit to use the 20° default.

rotation.description: three.js intrinsic XYZ Euler angles in RADIANS [rx, ry, rz] (equivalent to rotating about world Z first, then world Y, then world X). Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. If non-finite or not length-3 the rotation is ignored and [0,0,0] is used.

teeth.description: Number of teeth. Must be an integer >= 3. Below ~17 teeth undercut occurs; the profile is approximated by clamping the involute to the root circle.

name: add_spur_gear

description: Add a reinforced-concrete-style stair climbing one full level, modelled as a waist slab (sloping slab, waistThickness) with the steps on top; the last riser lands on the upper floor, so N risers give N-1 treads (N-2 treads + the landing when a landing is used) and every stair rises from the base of its level. Riser count defaults to the level height ÷ 175 mm (rounded up), so risers are equal; tread default 280 mm. By default it is ONE straight flight of N-1 treads, run (N-1) x tread. INTERMEDIATE LANDING: pass landingAt (riser number after which a horizontal landing slab, as thick as the waist, sits; integer 2 to N-2) and/or shape. shape "straight" (default) puts the landing in line between two flights; "quarter_turn" is an L: the second flight leaves sideways from the far end of the landing; "half_turn" is a dog-leg: the second flight doubles back beside the first, flightGap apart (default 100 mm), sharing the landing. turn "left" (default) or "right" is the side the second flight goes to (quarter_turn, half_turn). Shapes quarter_turn / half_turn without landingAt put the landing at half the risers. landingLength is the landing depth along the first flight (default = width). The start point and angle are those of the FIRST flight (middle of its first riser); the second flight is placed from the landing, and the stair is one element (one id, one mark, one takeoff line; flights and landing are separate entities stair-1:flight-1, :flight-2, :landing). The summary reports the Blondel rule (2R + G, comfortable between 600 and 650 mm) and, for a landing, a WARNING when landingLength < width plus the headroom between the landing and the floor above; add_slab_opening { stairId } cuts a well covering every flight and the landing. Refused above 200 risers, with a landing on fewer than 4 risers, or if a stair with the same start and angle already exists on the level.

angle.description: Run direction of the first flight in radians, counter-clockwise from +X. Default 0 (climbs toward +X).

flightGap.description: half_turn only: clear gap between the two flights, in document units (>= 0). Default 100 mm.

landingAt.description: Number of risers climbed before the intermediate landing (integer, 2 to riserCount - 2): flight 1 has landingAt risers, the last one arriving on the landing; flight 2 the remaining ones. Omit for no landing (unless shape is quarter_turn / half_turn, which default it to half the risers).

landingLength.description: Landing depth along the first flight direction, in document units (> 0). Default = stair width. Below the width gives a warning. Needs a landing.

levelId.description: Level id. Default: the active level (a "Level 0" is created if none).

riserCount.description: Total number of risers over both flights (integer, 2 to 200). Default: level height ÷ 175 mm, rounded up.

shape.description: Plan layout around the landing: "straight" (default, in line), "quarter_turn" (L, 90 degrees) or "half_turn" (dog-leg, 180 degrees, two flights side by side).

start.description: Plan point [x, y] at the middle of the first riser of the first flight.

treadDepth.description: Tread (going) depth, in document units. Default 280 mm.

turn.description: Side the second flight departs to for quarter_turn / half_turn, seen walking up the first flight. Default left.

waistThickness.description: Thickness of the sloping waist slab under the steps, perpendicular to the flight, in document units (> 0). Also the thickness of the landing slab. Default 175 mm.

width.description: Stair width (each flight), in document units. Default 1000 mm.

name: add_stair

description: Add a steel member with a catalogue section (e.g. "HEA300", "IPE400", "CHS76.1x3.6") between two 3D points [x, y, z] (z above the level). Role sets the layer, mark and IFC class: column, rafter, beam, brace, purlin, rail (side rail / girt) or crane (runway beam). Section depth points up for beams and along +X for vertical columns (roll π/2 turns it along +Y); roll (radians) turns it about the axis. Beams may declare startJoint / endJoint "rigid" (moment connection to the column they frame into; default pinned) and columns baseFixity "fixed" (column foot restrains rotation; default pinned or the base plate fixity): check_steel_members analyses rigidly connected beams and columns as planar moment frames. Refused if an identical member (section, role, roll, end points in either direction) already exists on the level.

baseFixity.description: Columns only: "pinned" (default; or the fixity of its base plate) or "fixed" (the foot restrains rotation in check_steel_members).

end.description: Axis end [x, y, z]; [x, y] means z = 0.

endJoint.description: Beams only: joint at the end end: "pinned" (default) or "rigid".

levelId.description: Level id. Default: the active level (a "Level 0" is created if none).

note.description: Note carried to the member schedule.

roll.description: Section rotation about the axis, radians. Default 0.

start.description: Axis start [x, y, z], z relative to the level; [x, y] means z = 0.

startJoint.description: Beams only: joint at the start end: "pinned" (default) or "rigid" (moment connection to the column it frames into).

name: add_steel_member

description: Create a periodic strut (beam) lattice as an implicit FIELD: cubic (3 edges per cell), bcc (8 half body diagonals), fcc (6 face diagonals), octet (24 bonds, stretch-dominated), diamond (diamond cubic, 16 bonds), kelvin (bitruncated cubic honeycomb, 24 bonds), bccz (bcc + vertical z edges), fccz (fcc + vertical z edges) or reentrant (auxetic: corner nodes + six face nodes pushed a quarter cell inward, 24 struts). Struts are round with the given radius (a number, or a scalar field id to grade it: create_scalar_field); the radius must stay below half the shortest strut. Pass region (a bounded field id, e.g. a box primitive) to clip the lattice to a body. Next: create_implicit_body for a mesh, lattice_properties for strut counts, length, relative density and the Maxwell count, export_3mf beamLattice for a slicer-native beam file.

anyOf.description: Cell size per axis [x, y, z].

cellSize.description: Unit-cell size in document units: one number (cubic cell) or [x, y, z]. Every size > 0.

name.description: Optional label for the node.

nodeRadius.description: Optional ball radius at every node in document units; only larger than radius has an effect (constant radius only).

origin.description: Lattice origin [x, y, z] (a lattice node) in document units. Default [0, 0, 0].

radius.description: Strut radius in document units: a number (> 0, and 2 * radius < the shortest strut length of the cell) or a scalar field id (graded; its range must satisfy the same bound where known).

region.description: Id of a field that clips the lattice (kept where that field is negative).

rotation.description: Lattice Euler XYZ rotation in radians about origin. Default [0, 0, 0].

name: add_strut_lattice

description: Create a freeform solid (or, with `boundary`, an open surface) as a Catmull-Clark subdivision surface over a coarse polygon control cage — for organic shapes no primitive gives (saddles, shifter hoods, grips, dropouts, fairings, handles). Start from a `box` cage (size + segments per axis) or a `cylinder` cage (radius, height, sides, segments along Z), both centred on `position`, or give a custom closed cage (`vertices` local to `position` + `faces` as vertex-index loops wound counter-clockwise seen from outside). Then shape it with edit_subdivision_cage (move / scale regions of cage vertices, with soft falloff; crease edges). The surface stays inside the cage and is smooth (2-3 levels); creased edges stay sharp. Semi-sharp creases: `edgeSharpness` / `vertexSharpness` (0..10). Returns data { vertexCount, faceCount, vertices, vertexIds, faceIds } (cage vertices in world coordinates, by index, with their stable element ids) to aim later edits. A closed solid: booleans, blend_union, measurement and export all work. With the OCC kernel a smooth solid (levels >= 1) is an exact B-spline solid — one bicubic face per refined cage quad, exactly the limit surface away from extraordinary vertices and creases (close to it there) — so STEP export and booleans are exact; levels 0 stays faceted.

boundary.description: Accept an OPEN custom cage (some edges border one face, e.g. a sheet, a bowl, a cage with a hole): its boundary edges stay infinitely sharp. "edge_and_corner" also pins the corner vertices (boundary vertices of a single face); "edge_only" keeps them as smooth crease points. Absent = the cage must be closed. An open cage has no volume.

segments.description: Cage faces along x, y, z (1..32; default [1, 1, 1]).

size.description: Cage size [x, y, z] (> 0); the smooth surface sits inside it.

color.description: Hex color string #rrggbb, e.g. "#c8553d". Defaults to "#6b8f9c".

creaseMethod.description: How sharpness decays per level: uniform (default, minus 1) or chaikin (smoothed).

creases.description: Cage edges kept sharp, as [vertexIndex, vertexIndex] pairs (each must be an edge of a face).

cylinder.description: Cylinder (n-gon prism) cage along Z centred on position.

height.description: Cage height along Z (> 0).

radius.description: Cage circumradius (> 0).

sides.description: Sides of the cage polygon (3..64; default 8).

edgeSharpness.description: Semi-sharp cage edges (OpenSubdiv creases). Use creases for infinitely sharp ones.

a.description: Cage vertex index of one end.

b.description: Cage vertex index of the other end.

s.description: Sharpness 0 < s <= 10: the edge stays crisp for about s subdivision levels (10 = infinite).

faces.description: Custom cage faces (use with vertices); the cage must be closed.

items.description: Vertex indices of one face, counter-clockwise from outside.

id.description: Optional explicit entity id. If omitted a unique id is generated.

layerId.description: Layer id to assign the entity to. Defaults to the document default layer.

levels.description: Subdivision levels 0..4 (0 = the faceted cage itself; 2-3 is smooth; each level quadruples the face count).

name.description: Optional display name for the entity (shown in the scene tree).

position.description: World position of the cage origin. Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

rotation.description: three.js intrinsic XYZ Euler angles in RADIANS [rx, ry, rz] (equivalent to rotating about world Z first, then world Y, then world X). Matches rotate_entity convention. Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. If non-finite or not length-3 the rotation is ignored and [0,0,0] is used.

vertexSharpness.description: Semi-sharp cage corners: the vertex stays a point for about s levels.

items.description: Cage vertex [x, y, z], local to position.

name: add_subdivision_solid

description: Add a surface texture requirement (roughness) on faces of a 3D solid: parameter (Ra, Rz, Rq, Rsk, Rku, Rmax, Sa, Sz), value > 0 in micrometres (unit um, default) or microinches (uin), optional lay symbol text and process text (e.g. "ground"). Faces are named by facesNear points. Needs the OCC kernel. Refusals: GDT_SURFACE_PARAMETER_UNKNOWN, GDT_ZONE_NON_POSITIVE, GDT_POINT_NOT_ON_FACE. Review required.

entityId.description: Id of the 3D solid.

facesNear.description: World points, one per face of the feature (document units). The faces are re-found from these points at every replay, so PMI follows its face through parametric edits. A pattern of equal holes takes one point on each hole. Use inspect_faces to find points on faces.

items.description: One world point [x, y, z] ON the face (document units), e.g. a point from inspect_faces centroid or samples.

parameter.description: Roughness parameter: Ra, Rz, Rq, Rsk, Rku, Rmax, Sa or Sz.

placement.description: Optional explicit annotation placement; omit for the automatic plane (recomputed when the model changes). An explicit placement is kept.

leaderTo.description: Optional leader attachment point on the feature [x, y, z].

normal.description: Annotation plane unit normal [x, y, z].

origin.description: Annotation plane origin [x, y, z], document units.

position.description: Frame centre in plane coordinates [u, v], document units.

xDir.description: Annotation plane x direction [x, y, z] (unit, perpendicular to normal).

unit.description: um = micrometres (default), uin = microinches.

value.description: Requirement value, > 0, in the unit below.

name: add_surface_texture

description: Drill ISO metric TAPPED holes (modelled internal thread) into a planar face of a 3D solid: a bore at the basic minor diameter d1 = d - 1.082532 P plus a real helical thread groove of the ISO 68-1 basic profile (H = 0.866025 P, pitch diameter d2 = d - 0.649519 P). size is "M8" (coarse pitch of ISO 261: M3 0.5, M4 0.7, M5 0.8, M6 1, M8 1.25, M10 1.5, M12 1.75, M14 2, M16 2, M18 2.5, M20 2.5, M22 2.5, M24 3, M27 3, M30 3.5, M33 3.5, M36 4, M39 4, M42 4.5, M45 4.5, M48 5, M52 5, M56 5.5, M60 5.5, M64 6) or "M8x1" (explicit/fine pitch); only M3-M64 are supported (anything else is refused). The face, points (including points taken from sketch points) and extent work exactly as in add_hole (through_all or blind; a blind thread length defaults to the full depth, thread.depth shortens it). Sizes are in mm in the designation; the geometry is created in the document unit. The result and refusals are those of add_hole (codes FTR_*); data = { designation, pitch, majorDiameter, pitchDiameter, minorDiameter } in document units.

depth.description: Blind only: cylindrical depth from the face, in document length units (drill point excluded). Must be inside the stock.

drillPointAngle.description: Blind only: drill point included angle in degrees in (0, 180); 0 = flat bottom. Omitted = 118 (named as defaulted).

face.description: up_to_face only: the planar target face the hole stops at, picked by a world point.

near.description: World point [x, y, z] on the planar target face, in document length units.

kind.description: "through_all" cuts through the whole part along the axis; "blind" stops at depth; "up_to_next" cuts through the first wall only (until the axis leaves the material, measured per hole: refined on the exact faces of the kernel when it has them (OpenCascade), else on the display mesh, which is only accurate to the tessellation on curved exit walls; the summary says which); "up_to_face" stops at the plane of the planar face picked by face.near, which must be parallel to the hole face and below it.

face.description: The planar face to drill into, picked by a world point.

near.description: World point [x, y, z] on (or within 0.1% of the part size of) the planar face, in document length units.

anyOf.description: Hole centres taken from a 2D sketch placed on the target face plane (the sketch plane must coincide with the face plane; a point off the plane is refused). Give sketchEntityIds, pointRefs or both.

pointRefs.description: Single vertices of sketch entities (see vertex), for when only some vertices of a polyline should be drilled.

id.description: Id of the sketch entity.

vertex.description: Vertex index in that entity (dimensionless): polyline point index; line 0 = start, 1 = end; rectangle 0..3 counter-clockwise from the lower-left corner; circle / arc / point 0.

sketchEntityIds.description: Ids of 2D sketch entities whose points become hole centres: a point entity gives its position; a polyline gives ALL its vertices; a line its two ends; a rectangle its four corners; a circle or arc its centre.

points.description: Hole centres: a list ([u, v] face frame by default, see pointsFrame) or { sketchEntityIds?, pointRefs? } from sketch points, as in add_hole.

pointsFrame.description: Coordinates of a points list: "face" (default), "world_xy" or "world" (see add_hole).

size.description: ISO metric size: "M8" (coarse pitch) or "M8x1" (explicit pitch). M3-M64 only.

target.description: Id of the 3D solid to tap (a primitive or a kernel result).

threadDepth.description: Threaded depth from the face, in document length units. Omit for the full hole depth.

name: add_tapped_hole

description: Attach an operating temperature limit to a part (entityId) or to faces / points (target) of a heat_* analysis; returns the limit id in affected[0]. Give max and/or min as { value, unit } (degC | K | degF). `source` is MANDATORY: where the limit comes from (component datasheet, company rule, material record); llull ships no limit tables and never defaults one. check_temperature_limits then reports margin, PASS / MARGINAL / FAIL per bound; an exceeded limit is dispositioned only by a human (dispose_thermal_limit).

analysisId.description: Id of the analysis (affected[0] of create_analysis, e.g. an-1.1).

entityId.description: Scope: id of an analysed part; the limit applies to the whole part. Exclusive with target.

unit.description: Unit text of the 08 grammar, e.g. 'degC', 'K', 'W/(m^2*K)', 'W'.
Unit text of the 08 grammar, e.g. 'degC', 'K', 'W/(m^2*K)', 'W'.

name.description: Display name, e.g. "board max junction".

source.description: REQUIRED: citation (and locator) of the limit.

citation.description: Where the value comes from: datasheet, correlation, company rule, owner statement.

locator.description: Page, table or clause inside the citation.

target.description: Scope: faces / edges / points of a part. Exclusive with entityId.

edgesNear.description: Points identifying edges: each resolves to the nearest edge.

items.description: A point [x, y, z] in document units lying on (or very near) the intended edge.

entityId.description: Id of the analysed 3D entity (it must be a part of the analysis: set_part_idealization).

facesNear.description: Points identifying faces: each resolves to the NEAREST face of the entity at meshing time.

items.description: A point [x, y, z] in document units lying on (or very near) the intended face.

intersectPlane.description: Optional: restrict the target to the curve where the faces meet this plane.

normal.description: Plane normal (need not be unit length).

pointsNear.description: Points identifying vertices / locations: each resolves to the nearest vertex or node.

items.description: A point [x, y, z] in document units lying on (or very near) the intended vertex or location.

name: add_temperature_limit

description: Place an annotation text label in the document. `content` is the text string (must not be empty). `position` is the world-space anchor [x, y, z] — for 2D annotations use z=0 (the default work plane). `height` is the cap-height in model units (must be > 0). Optional `rotation` is Euler angles [rx, ry, rz] in radians that orient the work plane (default [0,0,0]). Optional `anchor` controls horizontal alignment: 'left' (default) — position is left edge; 'center' — position is horizontal midpoint; 'right' — position is right edge. Optional `color` is a hex string (e.g. "#333333"). Optional `layer` is the target layer id. Optional `font` (a font id from import_font / list_fonts, or the family of a bundled font such as "Fira Sans") turns the text into a closed outline profile that text_outline, extrude_profile, wrap_to_face and emboss_on_face accept; `height` is then the exact cap height. With a font, `verticalAnchor` (baseline | cap_middle | cap_top), `letterSpacing` (document units after each glyph), `kerning` and `lineSpacing` (newline breaks lines) apply. A single-line font (family "LLULL Single Line", bundled) draws open strokes for engraving: wrap_to_face wraps them as curves and emboss_on_face mode engrave cuts a groove along them. `onCurve` { curveId, offset?, reverse? } bends a font text along a line / arc / circle / polyline / spline of the same sketch plane (the baseline follows the curve, glyphs stand on its left; anchor left / center / right aligns the text to the start / middle / end of the curve, `offset` shifts it along; refused when the text is longer than the curve). Without `font` the text stays an annotation. Characters the font lacks are reported in data.warnings (WRP_GLYPH_MISSING).

anchor.description: Horizontal alignment of the text relative to position. 'left' (default): position is the left edge of the first glyph. 'center': position is the horizontal midpoint. 'right': position is the right edge of the last glyph.

color.description: Hex color string, e.g. "#333333". Defaults to "#333333".

content.description: The text string to display. Must not be empty.

font.description: Font of the outline text: a font id (import_font, list_fonts) or a bundled family name such as "Fira Sans" (embedded in the document on first use).

height.description: Cap-height of the text in model units. Must be greater than 0.

kerning.description: Font text only: apply the font kern pairs. Default true.

layer.description: Layer id to assign the entity to. Defaults to the document default layer.

letterSpacing.description: Font text only: extra distance in document units added after each glyph. Default 0.

lineSpacing.description: Font text only: line pitch as a multiple of the font line height (ascender - descender + line gap). Default 1.

onCurve.description: Font text only: bend the text along this curve.

curveId.description: Id of a 2D curve entity (line, arc, circle, ellipse, polyline, spline) in the same plane as the text (same rotation).

offset.description: Arc length added to the anchor position along the curve, document units. Default 0.

reverse.description: Run along the curve from its end to its start (the text then stands on the other side). Default false.

position.description: World-space anchor position [x, y, z] of the text. For 2D drafting use z=0. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

rotation.description: Euler rotation angles [rx, ry, rz] in radians that orient the work plane. Defaults to [0,0,0].

verticalAnchor.description: Font text only: baseline (default) puts position on the baseline, cap_middle at half the cap height, cap_top on the cap line.

name: add_text

description: Add a thermal boundary condition or load to a heat_steady / heat_transient analysis; returns the BC id in affected[0]. kind: temperature (value+unit degC | K, on faces / edges / points), surface_flux (W/m^2, positive INTO the part, on faces), heat_generation (W/m^3, or total W with mode "total" spread over the part volume, on a part via entityId), concentrated_flux (W at points), film (filmCoefficient W/(m^2*K), or filmTable { points: [[T, h], ...] } for h(T) of the face temperature in heat_steady cases, and sinkTemperature), radiation (emissivity 0-1 and sinkTemperature; evaluated on absolute temperature). Film coefficients and emissivities are NEVER defaulted: pass `source` with a citation. Faces are given as points near them (facesNear, document units). amplitude names a define_amplitude curve that scales the value (sink temperature for film / radiation) over time. Refuses emissivity outside [0, 1], h <= 0, a wrong unit dimension or a non-thermal case. Next: set_thermal_step (transient), set_mesh_controls, check_thermal, then the host runs fea_mesh and fea_solve.

amplitude.description: Optional amplitude id or name (define_amplitude): the BC value (sink temperature for film / radiation) is multiplied by f(t).

analysisId.description: Id of the analysis (affected[0] of create_analysis, e.g. an-1.1).

emissivity.description: radiation only: hemispherical emissivity, 0 to 1. Never defaulted: needs `source` (PHY-15 emissivityIr is not built).

entityId.description: heat_generation only: id of the analysed part (solid) that generates heat.

filmCoefficient.description: film only: constant h as { value, unit } in W/(m^2*K); > 0. Never defaulted: needs `source`. Alternative: filmTable.

unit.description: Unit text of the 08 grammar, e.g. 'degC', 'K', 'W/(m^2*K)', 'W'.

filmTable.description: film only: h(T) of the FACE temperature T instead of filmCoefficient (heat_steady cases only, no amplitude): points [[T on the case scale, h in W/(m^2*K)], ...], at least 2, strictly increasing T, h > 0; end values are held outside the rows. Needs `source`.

points.description: Rows [surface temperature on the case temperature scale, h in W/(m^2*K)]: at least 2, strictly increasing temperature, h > 0.

kind.description: temperature | surface_flux | heat_generation | concentrated_flux | film | radiation.

mode.description: heat_generation only: value is W/m^3 ("density", default) or total power W spread over the part volume ("total").

name.description: Display name, e.g. "hot face film".

sinkTemperature.description: film / radiation: temperature of the environment as { value, unit } (degC | K | degF). Radiation uses absolute temperature.

description: Record a thermal contact conductance between a master face and a slave face of two different parts (bolted interface on a cold plate); returns the contact id in affected[0]. conductance: { value, unit "W/(m^2*K)" } or { points: [[W/(m^2*K), pressureMPa, T], ...] }. The deck ties the two faces thermally (CalculiX tied *CONTACT PAIR with *GAP CONDUCTANCE); the parts are meshed separately, so the two face meshes need not match. A table is evaluated at the mean temperature of the two faces (temperature on the case scale) and at zero contact pressure, so give the pressure column 0 unless it varies nothing. Check the result with analysis_report. Change it later with update_thermal_contact, remove it with delete_analysis_item.

description: Add a piping connection point (tie-in or battery limit) that runs start or end at: world position, outward face direction (pointing from the connection face toward the pipe), nominal size DN and end type. Lengths in document units (mm in plant documents). Returns the tie-in id (affected[0]) to pass as { portId } to route_pipe / route_problem / auto_route_pipe. Equipment nozzles (add_nozzle) are ports too: "<tag>:<mark>". Refusals: RTE_INVALID_PORT, RTE_DUPLICATE_TAG. Next: create_pipeline, then route_pipe (compass legs) or auto_route_pipe.

direction.description: Outward face direction [dx, dy, dz] (toward the pipe); normalised. Auto-routing needs an axis direction.

endType.description: End type: BW butt weld, FL flanged, SW socket weld, SC screwed, PL plain, WAF wafer, LUG lug. A SW or SC port joins a socket-weld (plain-end pipe) or threaded spec; the pipe goes in by the depth of the spec own socket / thread fittings of that size.

kind.description: Point kind (default 'tie_in').

position.description: World position [x, y, z] of the connection face centre. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

description: Create a torus (donut) solid. Right-handed world frame, +Z up. ringRadius is the distance from the torus center to the tube center (major radius); tubeRadius is the radius of the tube cross-section (minor radius). Both must be > 0; tubeRadius < ringRadius for a non-self-intersecting torus. anchor controls which point the position refers to: "center" (default) = geometric center of the torus; "min" = min-XYZ corner of the AABB; "base-center" = center of the bottom face (mid X/Y, min Z). The anchor offset is applied in the local UNROTATED frame; rotation is then applied by the viewport about the stored origin. Orientation: pass EITHER rotation (Euler radians) OR axis [dx,dy,dz] = direction the local +Z (symmetry) axis should point in world space; axis wins when both are given and Euler angles are derived and stored.

anchor.description: Which point on the torus the position refers to. "center" (default): geometric center. "min": min-XYZ corner of the AABB. "base-center": center of the bottom face (mid X/Y, min Z). Unknown values fall back to "center". Offset is applied in the local UNROTATED frame; viewport rotates about the stored origin.

axis.description: Optional direction [dx, dy, dz] (any non-zero length, normalized) that the primitive local +Z axis (its symmetry axis) points along in world space, e.g. [1, 0, 0] lays it along +X. When given it OVERRIDES rotation (the rotation param is ignored and the resolved Euler angles are stored). A zero-length or malformed axis is rejected as a no-op.

color.description: Hex color string #rrggbb, e.g. "#c8553d". Defaults to "#6b8f9c".

position.description: World-space location of the anchor point [x, y, z] in document units. Right-handed frame, +Z up. The ring lies in the XY plane. Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

ringRadius.description: Distance from the torus center to the center of the tube (major radius) in document units. Must be > 0.

rotation.description: three.js intrinsic XYZ Euler angles in RADIANS [rx, ry, rz] (equivalent to rotating about world Z first, then world Y, then world X). Matches rotate_entity convention. Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. If non-finite or not length-3 the rotation is ignored and [0,0,0] is used.

tubeRadius.description: Radius of the circular tube cross-section (minor radius) in document units. Must be > 0. Should be less than ringRadius for a non-self-intersecting torus.

description: Create a triply periodic minimal surface lattice (gyroid, schwarz_p, diamond, neovius, iwp, lidinoid, fischer_koch_s, split_p) as an implicit FIELD. form "sheet" is a wall around the surface F=0, "network" is the solid side {F <= level}. Give EXACTLY ONE control: thickness (sheet wall in document units; with normalize "gradient", the default, the wall is this thickness to first order; with normalize "none" it is the raw half-width t of {|F| <= t} in F units), level (network level in F units, 0 = half of the volume for gyroid / P / diamond / Neovius / Fischer-Koch S) or relativeDensity (0..1 solid fraction of the cell, solved once for you). thickness and level accept a scalar field id (create_scalar_field) to GRADE the lattice. Sheet thickness must be < half the smallest cell. The lattice is infinite: pass region (a bounded field id) to clip it, e.g. a box primitive, or create_implicit_body needs bounds. Next: create_implicit_body, then lattice_properties / check_implicit.

anyOf.description: Cell size per axis [x, y, z].

cellSize.description: Unit-cell size in document units: one number (cubic cell) or [x, y, z]. Every size > 0.

form.description: sheet: wall of the given thickness around F=0; network: solid {F <= level}.

kind.description: TPMS family (equations in the llull spec: Schoen, Lidin & Larsson, Fischer & Koch, Al-Ketan & Abu Al-Rub).

level.description: Network control: level in F units (gyroid |level| < 1.5, P < 3, diamond < 1); 0 gives half the volume; a number or a scalar field id. Network only.

axis.description: Axis direction [x, y, z] (non-zero).

cellsAround.description: Whole cells per full turn (an integer >= 1; a fraction makes the lattice jump at the seam: IMP_MAP_SEAM).

kind.description: Wrap the cells around an axis.

origin.description: A point on the axis [x, y, z] in document units.

radialCellSize.description: Cell size along the radius in document units (> 0). The axial cell size is cellSize[2].

cellsAround.description: Whole cells per turn of longitude (an integer >= 1, else IMP_MAP_SEAM).

cellsPolar.description: Whole cells over the half turn of colatitude pole to pole (an integer >= 1, else IMP_MAP_SEAM).

kind.description: Wrap the cells around a point: longitude x colatitude x radius.

origin.description: Centre of the sphere [x, y, z] in document units.

radialCellSize.description: Cell size along the radius in document units (> 0).

map.description: Conformal cell map (replaces origin / rotation). cylindrical: sleeves and tubes. spherical: shells; the cells collapse at the poles (warning IMP_MAP_POLE). Normalised walls stay uniform away from the singularities.

name.description: Optional label for the node.

normalize.description: gradient (default): divide F by its physical gradient so walls have uniform thickness; none: raw F.

origin.description: Lattice origin [x, y, z] in document units. Default [0, 0, 0].

region.description: Id of a field that clips the lattice (the lattice is kept where that field is negative).

relativeDensity.description: Control by target solid fraction of the cell, strictly between 0 and 1.

rotation.description: Lattice Euler XYZ rotation in radians about origin. Default [0, 0, 0].

thickness.description: Sheet control: wall thickness in document units (normalised) or raw half-width in F units (normalize "none"); a number or a scalar field id (graded). Sheet only.

description: Create a parametric pressure vessel (equipment element with a tag): cylindrical shell with two formed heads (ellipsoidal 2:1, torispherical by standard or radii, hemispherical, flat, conical), a support (skirt, legs, saddles or none) and optional design data. Dimensions are INSIDE diameter and tangent-to-tangent length in document units; thicknesses are nominal and include the corrosion allowance. Vertical vessels: heads {top, bottom}, support skirt / legs (height = floor to the bottom tangent line). Horizontal vessels: heads {left, right}, support saddles { stations from the left tangent line, width, axisElevation } or none. The geometry is derived (exact revolutions) and the legacy size / shape / weight fields are re-derived so clash checks, floor loads and schedules keep working. The tag must be unique. Next: add_nozzle for connections (their ports are "<tag>:<mark>"), vessel_volume for volumes, update_equipment_parameters to revise. Returns elementId, tag, bottom / top tangent elevations (vertical) or axisElevation (horizontal), defaulted[] (named defaults used), weightKg, angleConvention.

angleConvention.description: How angles in this call are read and reported. north_cw (default): vertical equipment 0 = plant north (+Y), growing clockwise seen from above (90 = east, +X); horizontal equipment 0 = top (+Z), 90 = the +Y side; a plan rotation grows clockwise. east_ccw: CAD maths, 0 = east (+X), growing counter-clockwise; horizontal equipment 0 = +Y, 90 = top; a plan rotation grows counter-clockwise. Every result names the convention.

description: Create a stochastic (Voronoi) strut lattice as an implicit FIELD: a seeded random point set with `density` seeds per document unit^3 fills the bounding box of `region`, and the beams run along the edges of its Voronoi diagram (about 13 beams per seed), cut to that box and clipped by the region field. The same seed gives the same lattice on every machine. Beams have a constant radius; cap "sphere" rounds the joints. At most 5000 beams (about 330 seeds): lower the density or shrink the region otherwise. Next: create_implicit_body (voxel well below radius), export_3mf beamLattice for printers that read beams.

cap.description: End caps: sphere (default, rounded joints) or butt (flat).

density.description: Seeds per document unit^3 (> 0). The mean cell diameter is about density^(-1/3).

name.description: Optional label for the node.

radius.description: Beam radius in document units (> 0).

region.description: Id of a field with finite bounds (e.g. a box primitive or field_from_solid): its bounding box is filled and the lattice is clipped by it.

seed.description: Non-negative integer seed of the point process; the same seed gives the same lattice.

name: add_voronoi_lattice

description: Create a wedge solid — a right-triangular prism (ramp shape). Right-handed world frame, +Z up. size is [width, height, depth]: width = X extent; height = full height of the front face; depth = Z extent (ramp direction). The slope cuts the top-rear corner: front face is a full rectangle, back edge tapers to zero height. All size components must be > 0. anchor controls which point the position refers to: "min" (default) = lower-front-left corner of the bounding box (min-XYZ); "center" = geometric center of the AABB; "base-center" = center of the bottom face (mid X/Y, min Z). The anchor offset is applied in the local UNROTATED frame; rotation is then applied by the viewport about the stored origin.

anchor.description: Which point on the wedge the position refers to. "min" (default): lower-front-left corner of the bounding box (min-XYZ). "center": geometric center of the AABB. "base-center": center of the bottom face (mid X/Y, min Z). Unknown values fall back to "min". Offset is applied in the local UNROTATED frame; viewport rotates about the stored origin.

color.description: Hex color string #rrggbb, e.g. "#c8553d". Defaults to "#6b8f9c".

position.description: World-space location of the anchor point [x, y, z] in document units. Right-handed frame, +Z up. Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

rotation.description: three.js intrinsic XYZ Euler angles in RADIANS [rx, ry, rz] (equivalent to rotating about world Z first, then world Y, then world X). Matches rotate_entity convention. Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. If non-finite or not length-3 the rotation is ignored and [0,0,0] is used.

size.description: [width, height, depth] in document units. width=X extent; height=full height at front face; depth=Z extent (ramp direction). All must be > 0.

description: Insert a window into a wall: cuts the wall between sill and head and adds the glazing. The summary warns when the opening overlaps a column in the wall line. Refused if it does not fit in the wall or overlaps another opening.

at.description: Alternative to offset: a plan point [x, y] projected onto the wall to place the opening center. Ignored when offset is given.

height.description: Opening height in document units (> 0). Default 1200 mm, limited to the wall height.

mark.description: Schedule mark, unique among windows. Default next WNn.

offset.description: Distance along the wall from its start to the opening CENTER, in document units (arc length on a curved wall). Takes precedence over at. Default: wall midpoint.

sillHeight.description: Height of the opening bottom above the wall base, in document units (>= 0). Default 900 mm.

wallId.description: Host wall element id: a straight ("wall-1") or curved ("curvedWall-1") wall.

width.description: Opening width in document units (> 0). Default 1200 mm.
