description: Create a NACA airfoil section as an exact cubic NURBS curve through the section ordinates (NACA Report 824 equations): 4-digit ("0012", "2412") or 230-series 5-digit ("23012"; other 5-digit mean lines are not supported). The section is chord-normalised: chord 1, leading edge at the origin, chord along +x, thickness along +y, drawn from the upper trailing edge round the leading edge to the lower one. `trailingEdge` "open" (default, the original definition, blunt 0.00252 chord for t = 12 %) or "closed" (sharp, a4 = 0.1036). `points` is the total ordinate count, odd, 21..801 (default 161 = 81 cosine stations per surface); `spacing` "cosine" (default) or "uniform". Returns the airfoil id (use it in create_wing / airfoil_properties) and the curve id. Place several airfoils with `position`. `chord` (default 1) scales the section to document units and `incidenceDeg` (default 0) rotates it nose-up about the leading edge. `as` "nurbs" (default) makes the exact curve plus the airfoil id; `as` "polyline" instead draws one plain closed 2D polyline (no airfoil id; affected[0] is the polyline) for analyze_airfoil { entityId }, extrude_profile or loft_sections.

as.description: "nurbs" (default): exact NURBS curve + airfoil id; "polyline": one closed 2D polyline, no airfoil id.

chord.description: Chord length in document units, > 0. Default 1 (chord-normalised).

designation.description: NACA designation: 4 digits ("0012", "2412") or the 230-series 5-digit "23012"; an optional "NACA " prefix is accepted.

incidenceDeg.description: Nose-up rotation about the leading edge in degrees. Default 0.

points.description: Total number of ordinates, an odd integer 21..801. Default 161.

position.description: Where to place the curve [x, y, z] in document units (the section stays in the local XY plane). Default [0, 0, 0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

spacing.description: Chordwise station spacing: "cosine" (default, dense at the nose) or "uniform".

trailingEdge.description: "open" (default): blunt trailing edge as originally defined; "closed": sharp trailing edge.

name: airfoil_from_naca

description: Read-only section metrics of an airfoil made with airfoil_from_naca / import_airfoil, computed from its exact curve and chord-normalised (unit "chord", areas in chord^2): maximum thickness tMax at xTMax, maximum camber (signed) at xCamberMax, leading-edge radius from the curve curvature, trailing-edge thickness and wedge angle in degrees, section area and centroid. `unverified` is true when the input has no pinned source. NACA 0012 reference: tMax 0.12 at 0.30, LE radius 0.0159, area 0.0822.
name: airfoil_properties

description: Move every entity in targetIds so that its bounding-box edge (or center) along the specified axis matches the reference entity's. edge values: "min-x", "min-y", "min-z", "max-x", "max-y", "max-z", "center-x", "center-y", "center-z". The reference entity is not moved. Returns affected: targetIds.

edge.description: Which bounding-box face or center to align along: "min-x"|"min-y"|"min-z"|"max-x"|"max-y"|"max-z"|"center-x"|"center-y"|"center-z".

referenceId.description: Id of the entity whose bounding-box edge is the alignment target. Not moved.

targetIds.description: Ids of entities to move. Must all exist in the document.

name: align

description: Station-by-station report of an alignment (metres): x, y, ground, design, cut/fill (design - ground, + = fill), cross-section cut / fill areas (m2, need profile + road section + surface), cumulative cut / fill volumes (m3, average-end-area method) and the mass-haul ordinate (cum. cut - cum. fill, no bulking). Also `data.csv`. With `designSpeedKmh` it checks horizontal curve radii against R = V^2 / (127 (e + f)) with e = the set_superelevation maxRate (0 plus a warning when none is set) and f from a simple speed table (0.28 at 30 .. 0.09 at 120 km/h), and vertical curve K against minimum crest / sag K (AASHTO-style stopping sight distance table), plus grade breaks over 0.5 % without a vertical curve; failures are listed.

designSpeedKmh.description: Design speed (km/h, > 0) to enable the geometric checks.

interval.description: Row spacing, document units. Default: the alignment station interval.

name: alignment_report

description: Declare that two parts are MEANT to overlap (a press fit, a thread, a weld, or an overlap by design), so check_assembly reports the pair as FPR_PAIR_ALLOWED (pass, with your reason shown) instead of FPR_PAIR_HARD. Welds, threads and press fits also count as rigid connections when check_assembly decides whether a part is attached (FPR_PART_FLOATING). The declaration is stored in the document, is never applied silently and is listed in every check. Refused when a = b, an id is unknown or 2D, the reason is empty, or the pair already has an intent (delete_interference_intent first). Returns the intent id (fit-<step>.<k>) in affected[0]. Next: check_assembly.

a.description: Entity or instance id of the first part.

b.description: Entity or instance id of the second part (different from a).

kind.description: "press_fit", "thread", "weld" (rigid connections) or "overlap_by_design" (overlap only).

reason.description: Why the overlap is intended, e.g. "pin pressed into piston boss, 0.02 mm interference". Must be non-empty.

name: allow_interference

description: Read the RESULTS of an analysis (describe_analysis reads its set-up and ids). Every number is recomputed from the artifact store; a stale result must be re-run, "missing" and "untrusted" (FEA_SUMMARY_MISMATCH) states withhold numbers. The view follows the analysis type. status (static, modal, buckling, nonlinear_static, thermo_static, coupled_temperature_displacement): data { state: unmeshed | meshed | solved | stale | missing | untrusted, unitSystem, mesh (node and element counts, quality, warnings), results (per load case max von Mises and max displacement with positions and units, or the thermal summary), eigen (modal: modes [{ mode, frequencyHz, participation, effectiveMass, fractionOfModelMass }], totalEffectiveMass, rigidBodyModes; buckling: factors, criticalFactor, criticalMode; null otherwise), problem, probes [{ probeId, quantity, unit, nodeId, nodeDistance, values }] at the nearest mesh node }. thermal (heat_steady, heat_transient; view "thermal" also on coupled_temperature_displacement): maxT / minT {value, at, entityId, timeS}, maxHeatFlux, bcHeatFlows [{ bcId, timeS, valueW }] (positive INTO the part), heatBalance {inW, outW, storedW, residualRel, tolerance, withinTolerance} (check it before reporting a result as final), probes, heatFluxProbes, physicalConstants, propertyRangeExceeded, unverified; params timeS (seconds, nearest result time for bcHeatFlows, default last) and probes (probe ids) apply; end with check_thermal. explicit (explicit_dynamics): state, controls with named defaults, initial velocities, rigid walls and, when solved, termination, cycles, energies and energy error, hourglass and added-mass ratios, max von Mises and plastic strain with location, failed elements, per-wall peak force and impulse, energy and wall-force histories; param maxPoints (2 to 500, default 200) applies. dynamic (frequency_response, random_response): summary { modesKept, massParticipation, dampingPerMode, probes (frf peaks / random rms and 3-sigma peak), nodalMax, unverified }; param probes (probe names) applies. Set view to read a case in another view (e.g. status on a heat_* case). thermal, explicit and dynamic results are reviewRequired: report them as "computed by llull, not approved". Topology studies are read with topology_report.

analysisId.description: Id of the analysis (affected[0] of create_analysis, e.g. an-1.1).

maxPoints.description: explicit view only: most samples per history, 2 to 500. Default 200.

probes.description: thermal view: only these probe ids (default all temperature and heat_flux probes); dynamic view: only these probe names (default all).

timeS.description: thermal view only: report the per-BC heat flows at the result time nearest to this (seconds). Default: the last.

view.description: Which report. Default from the analysis type: heat_* thermal, explicit_dynamics explicit, frequency_response / random_response dynamic, else status.

name: analysis_report

description: Read-only inviscid analysis of a 2D airfoil section: linear-strength vortex panel method with the Kutta condition (Kuethe & Chow), giving lift cl, pitching moment cm about `momentReference` (fraction of chord, default 0.25) and the pressure distribution Cp; plus thin-airfoil theory (zero-lift angle, cm c/4) for NACA sections. Give `naca` ("2412") or `entityId` of a closed 2D polyline (chord along its local x; any size). `alphasDeg` angles of attack in degrees (default [0, 5]); lift slope and zero-lift angle are fitted from them. Inviscid: no drag, no stall, no Reynolds effect — real sections reach about 85-95 % of the inviscid lift slope below stall (NACA 0012 measured 0.106/deg vs 0.1195 here). `includeSurface` returns Cp per panel. Next: analyze_wing with the section lift slope and zero-lift angle.

alphasDeg.description: Angles of attack in degrees, each within -20..20, at most 41. Default [0, 5].

closedTrailingEdge.description: NACA only: sharp closed trailing edge (default true).

entityId.description: Id of a closed 2D polyline airfoil (e.g. from airfoil_from_naca as "polyline"). Give this or naca.

includeSurface.description: Return x/c, y/c, Cp, V/V∞ per panel for every angle. Default false.

momentReference.description: Moment reference point as a fraction of chord. Default 0.25.

naca.description: NACA designation, e.g. "0012", "2412", "23012". Give this or entityId.

panelsPerSide.description: NACA only: panels per surface, 20..400. Default 100.

name: analyze_airfoil

description: Read-only curvature analysis of a nurbs_curve: at `samples` equally spaced parameters (default 21, 2..1000) or at explicit `parameters`, return the point (entity-local), unit tangent, curvature (1/document unit), radius of curvature, rate of change of curvature d(curvature)/ds, torsion, arc length from the start and the curvature-comb tip (`comb` = point - normal * curvature * combScale, pointing away from the centre of curvature). Planar curves also report the signed curvature (positive counter-clockwise about planeNormal) and the number of inflections. Summary: min / max curvature, max |d(curvature)/ds|, curve length. Samples where the speed is zero are flagged `degenerate`.

combScale.description: Length of a comb tooth per unit curvature, in document units. Default 1.

id.description: Id of a nurbs_curve entity.

parameters.description: Explicit curve parameters to sample (each inside the knot domain, see inspect_nurbs `domain`), at most 1000.

samples.description: Number of equally spaced sample parameters, integer 2..1000. Default 21. Ignored when `parameters` is given.

name: analyze_curve_curvature

description: Report how a deformation command (twist_body, taper_body, stretch_body, bend_body, scale_nonuniform) moved a body, as numbers instead of a visual judgement. data: law (kind and parameters, angles in radians), frame (origin, axis, reference), region, path ("exact" or "mesh"), jacobian {min, max, minAt, bound} (det J of the map: 1 = volume kept, <= 0 = folded; bound is the closed form over the whole body), volume {source, predicted, driftRel and the result volume} (predicted = integral of det J over the source, independent of the result surface; the result volume is read from the kernel or the mesh; document units^3), maxDisplacement (document units), approximation {maxError, tolerance, facesConverted, facesSplit} (on the exact path the largest deviation of the fitted B-spline faces from the deformed source, SAMPLED at the fit grid and at cell middles, not a proven bound; on the mesh path the largest chordal deviation; document units), topology {before, after} (exact path: faces / edges / vertices of the source and of the result), regionCrease (per region end, the angle in radians between the faces inside and outside a linear ramp; 0 for a smooth ramp), fibres {neutral, inner, outer} (bend: fibre lengths in document units), unverified (an input mesh has no pinned source hash) and provenance; compareTo (optional analytic reference torus / cylinder / cone / spheroid) adds data.compareTo.maxDeviation. Read-only. Refuses an entity that was not deformed (DEF_NOT_DEFORMED).

compareTo.description: Optional analytic reference (torus, cylinder, cone, spheroid): data.compareTo.maxDeviation is the largest distance of the result surface vertices to it, document units. Fields needed: torus majorRadius, minorRadius, center, axis; cylinder radius, point, axis; cone apex, axis, halfAngleDeg; spheroid center, semiAxes.

apex.description: cone: apex point, world document units.

axis.description: torus / cylinder / cone: axis direction, unitless (normalised); for a cone it points from the apex toward the wide end.

center.description: torus / spheroid: centre point, world document units.

halfAngleDeg.description: cone: half opening angle, degrees, 0 < angle < 90.

kind.description: Analytic reference surface the result should coincide with.

majorRadius.description: torus: distance from the torus axis to the tube centre circle, document units, > 0.

point.description: cylinder: a point on the axis, world document units.

radius.description: cylinder: radius, document units, > 0.

semiAxes.description: spheroid: semi-axes along world x, y, z, document units, each > 0.

id.description: Id of the deformed mesh entity to analyse (the id a deformation command returned in affected).

name: analyze_deformation

description: Read-only draft analysis against a mould pull direction. `id` is a nurbs_surface (sampled on a `grid` x `grid` patch grid) or a 3D solid (every facet of its tessellation; the exact kernel is not needed). The draft angle of a face is asin(n . pull) in degrees, n the outward unit normal: 0 = parallel to the pull, positive = the face leans away so the part releases, negative = an undercut. A cone with the pull along its axis and base radius 5, top radius 3, height 10 has a lateral draft of atan(0.2) = 11.31 degrees. Returns min / max draft, the area below `minDraftDeg` (default 0 = undercuts only) and the undercut area, with `pass` true when no face is below the minimum. A sheet has no inside: set `flip` true when its normal (S_u x S_v) points into the part. Samples are listed up to 2000 (thinned evenly).

flip.description: Reverse the normal of a nurbs_surface (S_u x S_v) before measuring. Default false; ignored for solids.

grid.description: Samples per direction for a nurbs_surface, integer 2..200. Default 20. Ignored for solids.

id.description: Id of a nurbs_surface or a 3D solid entity.

minDraftDeg.description: Smallest acceptable draft angle in degrees (-90..90). Default 0.

pullDirection.description: Direction [x, y, z] the part is pulled out of the mould (any non-zero length), e.g. [0, 0, 1].

name: analyze_draft

description: Classical Laminate Theory of a stack: reduced stiffness Q of the first ply material, A (N/mm), B (N), D (N*mm), the 6x6 ABD inverse, engineering constants Ex, Ey, Gxy (MPa) and nuxy reported as membrane constants (A inverse), in-plane constants with bending unrestrained ("free bending", from the ABD inverse; equal to membrane when symmetric) and flexural constants (constantsFlexural, from D inverse: E = 12 / (h^3 d)). Stacking runs bottom (tool side) to top, +z along the laminate normal, engineering shear strain, N-mm-MPa (thickness converted from document units). Give EITHER `part` + `point` (the stack of the part at that world point, see core_sample) OR `angles` (degrees, bottom to top) / `laminate` (stacking string, e.g. "[0/+-45/90]s") + `material`. With `environment` (deltaT, deltaMoisture) it adds the hygrothermal resultants and free laminate strains, effective expansion per kelvin and residual ply stresses. With `loads` (Nx, Ny, Nxy in N/mm; Mx, My, Mxy in N*mm/mm) it adds mid-plane strains, ply stresses at the bottom and top of every ply in material axes and the first-ply failure strength ratio R (load multiplier to failure) for each criterion (max_stress, tsai_hill, tsai_wu; default all) with the critical ply: R below 1 means failure. Tsai-Wu uses F12* = -0.5 unless the material gives one (reported under defaults). Results from "mean" / "unknown" material data are flagged unverified; failure results are flagged reviewRequired (computed by llull, not approved). Refused: missing strengths when loads are given. Read-only.

angles.description: Ply angles bottom to top, degrees (with `material`).

items.description: Ply angle, degrees.

criteria.description: Failure criteria to evaluate; default max_stress, tsai_hill and tsai_wu. "larc03" is a LaRC04-style plane-stress criterion (Mohr-Coulomb matrix compression, fibre kinking; no in-situ strengths, unverified) and needs GIc and GIIc on the material.

environment.description: Hygrothermal state: free thermal and moisture strains of every ply (alpha dT + beta dM). Adds laminate resultants, curvature and residual ply stresses; strength ratios then mean the multiplier of the mechanical loads on top of that state (0: the state alone fails).

deltaMoisture.description: Moisture content change, mass fraction (0.01 = 1%); needs beta1 and beta2 on the material.

deltaT.description: Temperature change from the stress-free (cure) state, kelvin; needs alpha1 and alpha2 on the material.

loads.description: Resultant loads per unit width; omitted components are 0.

point.description: World point [x, y, z] on the part, document units (with `part`).

name: analyze_laminate

description: Numeric health report of a mesh (or the triangles of any 3D solid): vertex / edge / face counts, Euler characteristic and genus, closed and manifold flags, orientation consistency, boundary loops (edges, length, centroid), non-manifold edges, shells (faces, volume, genus each), degenerate and duplicate faces, crossing triangle pairs, area, volume and centroid (closed shells), edge-length and triangle-quality (aspect ratio, min angle) statistics. Vertices within weldTolerance are welded first (default 1e-6 x bounding-box diagonal, reported as a named default). Lengths in document units, areas in units^2, volumes in units^3. Next: check_mesh for a pass / fail verdict. Refusals carry error.code MESH_ENTITY_NOT_FOUND, MESH_NOT_A_MESH, MESH_ENGINE_CAP_EXCEEDED.

id.description: Id of the mesh (or other 3D solid) to analyse.

maxListed.description: Longest list returned (loops, shells, pairs, non-manifold edges); totals are always exact. Default 20.

selfIntersections.description: Search for crossing triangle pairs (counts transversal crossings; touching contacts are not counted). Default true up to 200000 triangles.

weldTolerance.description: Vertices closer than this (document units) are merged. Default: 1e-6 x bounding-box diagonal.

name: analyze_mesh

description: Read-only tolerance stack-up of named contributors (each nominal with signed upper / lower limits, normal or uniform): y = expression(contributors) or a linear stack y = Σ sensitivity_i x_i. Reports the nominal and mean of y, worst case (linearised) and exact corners, RSS, σ_y, P(y < lowerSpecLimit) / P(y > upperSpecLimit) (exact normal CDF, or exact uniform-sum CDF), per-contributor % of WC and RSS, and with methods ["monteCarlo"] a seeded deterministic Monte Carlo (Philox4x32-10, up to 2e6 samples; above, use the native stackup_monte_carlo tool which draws the same samples). Defaults (σ = half tolerance / 3, seed, samples) are named in the result. Contributors with verified: false are listed in data.unverified. A qualified engineer must review the result.

contributors.description: Contributors (1..64), each with nominal and signed limits; the mean is nominal + (upper + lower)/2.

distribution.description: normal (default: σ = half tolerance / sigmaPerHalfTolerance) or uniform over the limits (σ = t/√3).

lower.description: Lower deviation from the nominal, signed (e.g. -0.1); lower <= upper. Required unless pmiId is given.

name.description: Identifier used in `expression` (letters, digits, underscore; not starting with a digit), unique.

nominal.description: Nominal value in document length units (degrees for angles). Required unless pmiId is given (then measured from the PMI item).

pmiId.description: Id of a PMI size or location dimension whose measured nominal and tolerance feed this contributor (limits become deviations); the stack follows the PMI.

sensitivity.description: Linear stack only: coefficient a_i of this contributor (y = Σ a_i x_i). Give it on every contributor, or use expression.

unit.description: length (default, document unit) or deg for an angle (reported only).

upper.description: Upper deviation from the nominal, signed (e.g. +0.1, or -0.007 for a shaft). Required unless pmiId is given.

verified.description: false marks a hand-typed value not confirmed against its source: it is listed in data.unverified (never hidden).

expression.description: y = f(contributors), e.g. "H - (A + B + C + D)" or "L * sin(theta * pi / 180)" (an optional "gap = " prefix is ignored). Grammar: + - * / ( ), numbers, pi, tau, sin cos tan asin acos atan atan2 sqrt abs exp ln log10 pow hypot min max floor ceil round trunc sign mod. Sensitivities come from exact automatic differentiation. Give either expression or a sensitivity on every contributor.

lowerSpecLimit.description: Lower specification limit L of y: reports P(y < L).

methods.description: Methods to report. Default ["worstCase", "rss"]; add "monteCarlo" for sampling (seeded, deterministic).

name.description: Display name of the stack, e.g. "housing gap".

samples.description: Monte Carlo samples, >= 1000. Default 100000; analyze_stackup caps at 2000000 (above: the native stackup_monte_carlo tool).

seed.description: Monte Carlo seed, integer 0..2^53-1 (Philox4x32-10 key). Default 1 (reported as defaulted).

sigmaPerHalfTolerance.description: k in σ = half tolerance / k for normal contributors, > 0. Default 3 (±3σ = the limits), reported as defaulted.

upperSpecLimit.description: Upper specification limit U of y: reports P(y > U).

name: analyze_stackup

description: Read-only curvature analysis of a nurbs_surface (made by loft_surface, surface_from_points, fill_surface, loft_fuselage ...): at a `grid` of [nu, nv] equally spaced parameter points (each 2..200, default [11, 11]) or at explicit `samples` [u, v] (inside the domain, see inspect_nurbs), return the world point, unit normal, principal curvatures k1 >= k2, Gaussian curvature K = k1*k2 and mean curvature H = (k1+k2)/2 (1/document unit, signed about the normal). The summary reports min / max K and H and where they occur (flat spots: K ~ 0, bumps and dents: large |K|). `data.samples` is listed up to 2500 samples; larger grids return only the statistics and `extremes`. Samples on a singular point (a collapsed edge, a pole) are flagged `degenerate` and excluded from the statistics.

grid.description: [nu, nv]: number of sample parameters along u and along v, integers 2..200 each. Default [11, 11]. Ignored when `samples` is given.

id.description: Id of a nurbs_surface entity.

samples.description: Explicit [u, v] parameter pairs inside the surface domain, at most 10000.

name: analyze_surface_curvature

description: Read-only vortex-lattice (horseshoe VLM) analysis of one or more lifting surfaces — wing, horizontal tail, canard, fin — for swept, tapered, twisted, dihedral and multi-surface configurations. Each surface comes from a loft_sections solid (loftId: one section per ring) or from explicit sections (leading edge, chord, incidence) root to tip, mirrored about y = 0 by default. Frame: x downstream, y spanwise, z up. Returns CL, induced drag CDi (Trefftz plane), Cm about referencePoint, span efficiency, lift and moment slopes, the neutral point x and the static margin with the CG at referencePoint, and the span loading. Camber enters as a zero-lift angle (naca or zeroLiftAngleDeg). Inviscid and incompressible: no stall or viscous drag (see drag_buildup). Up to 1000 panels (both sides); larger lattices run natively with the vortex_lattice_solve tool (same data).

alphasDeg.description: Angles of attack in degrees within -20..20, at most 31. Default [0, 5].

referenceArea.description: Reference area S. Default: planform area of the first surface (both sides).

referenceChord.description: Reference chord for Cm. Default: mean aerodynamic chord of the first surface.

referencePoint.description: Moment reference point = centre of gravity [x, y, z] (static margin measured from it). Default [0, 0, 0].

surfaces.description: Lifting surfaces (1..8): wing, tails, canards; each from loftId or sections. The first is the main wing (reference).

loftId.description: Id of a loft_sections solid: each ring is a section (leading edge = least x, trailing edge = largest x, world frame).

mirror.description: Add the mirror image about y = 0 (a half wing given root to tip). Default true, except false for a surface on y = 0 (fin) or one already spanning both sides (full-span loft).

naca.description: Section NACA designation: its thin-airfoil zero-lift angle is applied as a camber incidence.

name.description: Surface name, e.g. "wing", "htail".

sections.description: Explicit sections root to tip (alternative to loftId), at least 2.

chord.description: Chord length, >= 0 (0 only at a pointed tip, e.g. an elliptic planform).

incidenceDeg.description: Section incidence (twist), degrees, nose up positive. Default 0.

leadingEdge.description: Leading-edge point [x, y, z] (x downstream, y spanwise, z up), same length unit everywhere.

spacing.description: Spanwise spacing: cosine (default, clustered at the tips) or uniform.

zeroLiftAngleDeg.description: Section zero-lift angle, degrees (overrides naca). Default 0 (flat plate).

name: analyze_vortex_lattice

description: Read-only finite-wing aerodynamics by Prandtl lifting-line theory (Glauert Fourier series, symmetric loading): lift coefficient CL, induced drag CDi, span efficiency e (Oswald factor of induced drag), lift slope and the spanwise lift distribution. Planform `trapezoidal` (rootChord, tipChord; rectangular when equal) or `elliptical` (rootChord = centre chord); `twistDeg` = linear twist root -> tip (negative = washout). Section: `naca` gives the thin-airfoil zero-lift angle (lift slope 2π), or set `sectionLiftSlopePerRad` (default 2π, flagged defaulted; use analyze_airfoil or test data) and `zeroLiftAngleDeg`. Lengths are in any one unit (metres when forces are wanted). With `speed` + air state (altitudeM or densityKgM3) it returns lift and induced drag in N. Valid for unswept wings of aspect ratio above about 4, attached flow, low Mach (no compressibility, no stall).

alphasDeg.description: Root angles of attack in degrees within -15..15, at most 31. Default [0, 5].

altitudeM.description: Geometric altitude in m for the U.S. Standard Atmosphere 1976 (-5000..86000). Default 0 (sea level) unless densityKgM3 is given.

densityKgM3.description: Air density in kg/m³ (> 0) instead of the standard atmosphere, e.g. a measured value.

naca.description: Section NACA designation: zero-lift angle from thin-airfoil theory.

rootChord.description: Root chord (centre chord of an elliptical wing), > 0, same unit as span.

sectionLiftSlopePerRad.description: Section lift slope a0 per radian. Default 2π (thin-airfoil theory, flagged defaulted).

span.description: Wing span b tip to tip, > 0 (metres when forces are wanted).

speed.description: Speed (air speed for aircraft, ground speed for road vehicles) in speedUnit, >= 0.

speedUnit.description: Unit of speed: m/s (default), km/h, kn (knot, 1852 m/h) or mph.

temperatureOffsetK.description: ISA temperature deviation ΔT in K at the standard pressure (e.g. 15 for ISA+15). Default 0.

terms.description: Number of odd Fourier terms, 2..80. Default 40.

tipChord.description: Tip chord of a trapezoidal wing, 0 < tip <= root. Default = rootChord (rectangular).

twistDeg.description: Linear geometric twist at the tip relative to the root, degrees (washout < 0). Default 0.

viscosityPaS.description: Dynamic viscosity in Pa·s with densityKgM3; default Sutherland at 288.15 K + temperatureOffsetK (1.7894e-5 Pa·s).

zeroLiftAngleDeg.description: Section zero-lift angle in degrees (overrides the naca value). Default 0.

name: analyze_wing

description: Attach a motion clip to an entity or group. mode 'spin' = constant velocity: speed is angular velocity in rad/s for the rotation channel (e.g. 6.283 = 1 revolution/s) or linear velocity in document units/s for the position channel. mode 'oscillate' = sinusoidal motion sin(2π·frequency·t) · amplitude: amplitude is the peak displacement (radians for rotation, document units for position) and frequency is in Hz; both must be > 0. axis is the world-space direction vector ([0,1,0] = Y axis); it need not be unit-length — the viewport normalizes it. pivot is the world-space rotation pivot point; when omitted, the player defaults to the target entity/group position. trigger 'auto' runs the animation under the global Play button; 'click' toggles it when the user clicks the part in the viewport.

amplitude.description: oscillate: peak displacement, radians for the rotation channel or document units for the position channel. Must be > 0.

axis.description: World-space direction vector [x, y, z] the motion acts along. For rotation this is the axle; for position this is the translation direction. Need not be unit-length. Defaults to [0, 1, 0] (Y axis).

channel.description: Transform channel to drive: 'rotation' (default) turns / rocks the part; 'position' translates / slides it.

frequency.description: oscillate: complete cycles per second (Hz), > 0. Example: 0.5 = one full back-and-forth every 2 seconds.

mode.description: 'spin' = constant velocity (give speed); 'oscillate' = back-and-forth sine motion (give amplitude and frequency).

pivot.description: World-space pivot point [x, y, z] for the rotation axis. Only meaningful for the rotation channel. When omitted the player uses the target entity/group position as the pivot.

speed.description: spin: constant velocity, rad/s for the rotation channel (e.g. 6.283 ≈ 1 rev/s) or document units/s for the position channel.

targetId.description: Id of the entity or group to animate. Must exist in the document.

trigger.description: When to run the animation: 'auto' (default) starts under the global Play button; 'click' toggles the animation on/off when the user clicks the animated part in the viewport.

name: animate

description: Rebuild the model from a feature trace (LLULL_TRACE) recorded by running llull-generated CadQuery or build123d code — normally called for you by the import_code tool. Parameters are set first, then each traced feature runs as its llull command, keeping parameter expressions in the feature history. mode "replace" (default) swaps the current solids/parameters/history for the trace; "append" adds to them.

mode.description: "replace" (default) or "append".

trace.description: The trace: { parameters: [{ name, expression }], features: [{ command, params, ref?, name? }] }. Numbers in params may be { value, expression? } terms; solids are referenced as { ref: "f3" }.

name: apply_code_trace

description: Build the model from a .lld design: one line per feature (`<command> <alias> key=value …`, any registered command), `param` defaults, anchors (face=base.top, on=base.top align=back), loops (for i in 0..n-1 { … }) and `check` lines. The design becomes the document's recipe: ONE feature step holding the source, re-run on every regeneration (set_parameter w=100 rebuilds it). A document has one design; applying again replaces it. Fails with the line number on the first failing line (document unchanged). data: { aliases, checks[] } — checks report, they never fail it (check_design gates). Language: describe_design_syntax.

description: Add many semantic PMI items to one 3D solid in one step: datum features, feature control frames (characteristic, zone, datum labels), size and location dimensions with tolerances. Each item names its faces by facesNear points (document units, one point ON each face; inspect_faces lists them), exactly as add_datum_feature / add_geometric_tolerance / add_size_dimension / add_location_dimension do, and is re-found at every replay. This is the import path of AP242 PMI (import_step_exact calls it per body) and the bulk path for an agent that already holds a PMI list. Items are taken as found: no rule is enforced (check_pmi reports them); a feature that resolves to no face is kept with faceIndices [] and counted (doc.pmi.import.unresolved), a nominal the B-rep disagrees with is flagged unverified. Every item is review-required; only a signed human accept_pmi_review clears it. Needs the OCC kernel. Refusals: GDT_ENTITY_NOT_SOLID, GDT_KERNEL_NO_TOPOLOGY, GDT_DATUM_DUPLICATE, GDT_LIMITS_INVERTED. Returns data { created, unresolved, unverified }.

description: Build a colour profile that tints pipes by service from ASME A13.1 (scheme "asme_a13_1") or ISO 14726 ("iso_14726"): serviceMap maps each service text of the model (e.g. "cooling water") to a category of the scheme (e.g. "water"; ISO: the medium, e.g. "sea water"; see list_service_colour_schemes). YOU decide the mapping: llull never guesses a hazard class from text. One rule per mapped service, in map order, first match wins; the pipe is tinted with the row field / main colour from the default palette (approximate display hex). data { profileId, mapped, unmapped[] (services in the model absent from the map: they keep their own colour), reviewRequired: true }. The profile is flagged reviewRequired: a qualified reviewer must approve the mapping before the colours are used on a deliverable. Follow with colour_by_rule_report and check_display. Re-running with the same profileId replaces it. Errors: VIS_SCHEME_UNKNOWN, VIS_SCHEME_CATEGORY_UNKNOWN. Does not change geometry or add a feature step.

description: Create a 3D NURBS curve that approximates ordered points within `tolerance` using as few poles as possible (least squares; first and last point are interpolated, interior points are fitted). Use it for dense or noisy data (scans, digitised airfoils, 400-point ordinates) where interpolate_curve would give a pole per point and wiggles. Chord-length parameters; the pole count is searched upwards (per degree between `degreeMin` and `degreeMax`, the lowest degree wins ties) until the largest point-to-curve distance is within `tolerance`. Returns the curve id, pole count, degree, and the real max / rms deviation. Refuses (no curve) when `tolerance` cannot be reached with at most `maxPoles` poles. For an exact pass-through use interpolate_curve.

color.description: Hex color string #rrggbb, e.g. "#c8553d". Defaults to "#2a7ab0".

degreeMax.description: Highest degree tried, integer >= degreeMin and <= 25. Default equal to degreeMin.

layerId.description: Layer id to assign the entity to. Defaults to the document default layer.

maxPoles.description: Pole budget, integer 3..10000. Default 10000 (never more than the point count).

name.description: Optional display name for the entity (shown in the scene tree).

points.description: 3..10000 ordered points.

items.description: Ordered data point [x, y, z] in document units, relative to `position`.

position.description: Origin [x, y, z] of the curve in document units; the poles are relative to it. Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

tolerance.description: Largest allowed distance from any point to the curve, document units (> 0).

name: approximate_curve

description: Duplicate an entity into a linear pattern. Creates count-1 new copies spaced by offset (a world-space vector [dx,dy,dz]). The original stays at instance 0; copy k is placed at original.position + k*offset (k = 1..count-1). count must be an integer >= 2.

count.description: Total number of instances including the original. Must be an integer >= 2.

id.description: Id of the entity to array.

offset.description: World-space translation vector [dx, dy, dz] between consecutive instances. All components must be finite numbers.

name: array_linear

description: Duplicate an entity into a polar (circular) pattern about an axis line through center. The original counts as instance 0; count-1 new copies are created. Copy k is the original rigidly rotated by k*(angle/count) radians about the axis: its position orbits the axis line and its orientation is composed with the same rotation (R_axis(k*step) applied after the existing rotation), so already-rotated parts (e.g. radial cylinders) stay correctly oriented. axis defaults to [0, 0, 1] (world Z; then center only uses cx, cy and Z position is unchanged). angle defaults to 2*PI (full circle). count must be >= 2.

angle.description: Total sweep angle in radians over which instances are distributed. Defaults to 2*PI (full 360-degree circle). A partial angle (e.g. PI) fans the instances over that arc.

axis.description: Optional rotation axis direction [dx, dy, dz] (any non-zero length, normalized). Defaults to [0, 0, 1]. Right-hand rule gives the positive angle direction.

center.description: World-space point [cx, cy, cz] the rotation axis passes through. With the default Z axis only cx and cy matter.

count.description: Total number of instances including the original. Must be an integer >= 2.

id.description: Id of the entity to array.

name: array_polar

description: Number the characteristics (balloons) of the drawing for AS9102 Form 3: every size / location dimension, geometric tolerance (feature control frame), surface texture and, with includeNotes, note among the PMI items (03 GD&T) gets a stable characteristic number in doc.plm.characteristics, keyed by its PMI id. Existing numbers never change, retired numbers are never reused, so regenerating the model keeps every balloon. Datums are references and are not numbered. The stored requirement text is what the drawing prints. export_sheet_svg then draws the number in a balloon next to the callout. sheetId limits the numbering to items an explicit view of that sheet shows (or any item for an automatic-PMI sheet) and records that sheet; designators sets a customer key / critical flag per PMI id. Changes only the PLM record, never the definition.

description: Assign a named material to one or more entities. The material must already exist in the document (create it first with create_material), or be one of the sourced catalogue names "al_4032" (piston alloy, 2680 kg/m³ [Smiths datasheet]) and "steel_4340" (7850 kg/m³ [AISI 4340 sheet]), which are created with their cited source and grade on first use. Once assigned, mass_properties uses the material's density for that entity (mass = volume × material.density), overriding the caller-supplied density param. The material may be a record (define_material_record or a library record: use its id); an unresolved private record can be assigned, but mass_properties answers MAT_LIBRARY_UNRESOLVED until resolve_material_libraries. Multiple entity ids can be assigned in a single call; unknown ids are skipped with a note. Pattern copies (array_linear, array_polar, pattern_along_path) of a target that still share its previous material follow it, even when the pattern was made first. Assigning a material is a replayable document edit recorded in featureHistory.

entityIds.description: List of entity ids to assign the material to. Must contain at least one id. Unknown ids are skipped and reported in the summary; valid ids are updated. To assign to a single entity, pass a one-element array, e.g. ["e-abc123"].

materialName.description: Name of the material to assign. Must exactly match a material created with create_material (case-sensitive). Example: "steel", "aluminium_6061".

name: assign_material

description: Attach a mesh stored in this machine's content-addressed mesh asset store (made by `llull mesh import <file> --units mm`, or by a mesh command on a large mesh) as a mesh entity. The document keeps a display level of detail (about 50 000 triangles) and the asset key; analyze_mesh, repair_mesh, decimate_mesh, the exports and every other mesh command read the full-resolution triangles from the store. Meshes of at most 100000 triangles are copied inline instead. The entity is `unverified` unless the importer pinned the source sha256. Refusals: MESH_ASSET_UNAVAILABLE (no store here), MESH_ASSET_MISSING (key unknown on this machine: re-import the source file).

description: Attach an imported point cloud to the document by its asset key (printed by `llull scan import <file>`). The document stores a reference (key, name, placement transform, display settings), never the points, so it stays small and replays without the scan. placement "grid" places a georeferenced cloud (projected metres) next to the local model through the civil site calibration (set_site_calibration). `transform` (asset -> document, metres) overrides the placement. Then use describe_point_cloud, query_cloud_points, slice_cloud, fit_primitive, extract_pipes, compute_registration, cloud_to_model_deviation, check_asbuilt_clash and check_point_clouds.

description: Route several pipe lines automatically in one transaction, in an automatic order, each routed run an obstacle for the next. order auto (default): DN descending, then straight-line distance descending, then request position; when a line cannot be routed because earlier lines are in the way, the first line that fails is promoted to the front and the pass is repeated, up to maxAttempts passes (default 4, at most 12). order given: exactly the request order (or only the lines of sequence, in that order; run ids still follow the request position), one pass (the native transport uses it with solutions, one per line, each validated against the problem of its turn). With sequence the lines left out are skipped by request and do not count: all-or-nothing is about the sequenced lines. Default all-or-nothing: if any line cannot be routed in any tried order nothing changes and RTE_AUTOROUTE_LINES_FAILED names every line and why; partial: true keeps the lines that routed (the pass that routed most) and reports the others. Each line is routed as auto_route_pipe does (spec fittings, clash-body obstacles, rack elevations) and becomes an ordinary run. data = { order (routing order of the committed pass), attempts: [{ order, routed, lines }], lines: [{ lineId, status routed|failed|skipped, runId, bends, centrelineToPiLengthMm, cost, engine, code, message }], routed, failed, complete }. Run ids are minted once per request position, so any order and any retry gives the same ids. In-process search is capped per first-move candidate (maxExpansions); for large grids use llull auto_route with lines (native router). Refusals: RTE_AUTOROUTE_LINES_INVALID, RTE_AUTOROUTE_LINES_FAILED.

description: Route a pipe line automatically between two ports and add it as a pipe run: orthogonal legs on a lattice, fewest bends and shortest length for the bend cost, clear of every 3D entity, existing run (its pipe, insulation, flanges, valve operators, branches) and keep-out by pipe radius + insulation + clearance, rack elevations preferred. With solution (from llull auto_route) it checks the problem hash, every leg and the length / bends / cost before committing. The run is an ordinary run: it derives the same parts as route_pipe (cut pipe pieces, spec elbows, flange sets) and is refused if they do not derive. data = { runId, pis, centrelineToPiLengthMm, bends, cost, optimal, expansions, engine, problemHash, unverified, unverifiedReasons, parts, totalPipeMm }. description: Bend a straight region of a 3D solid or mesh onto a circular arc (a bar becomes an arc, a cylinder a torus segment). Give exactly TWO of: radius (document units, of the neutral fibre), angleDeg (degrees, 0 < angle <= 360, how far the region turns; exactly 360 on the whole body closes a ring and needs the native exact kernel) and length (document units, the straight region length; or region.start and region.end, which gives the same). The neutral fibre is the plane through frame.origin perpendicular to frame.reference: its length is kept (radius x angle = length); material toward the centre of curvature (frame.reference direction) is shortened by (R - y)/R and material away from it is lengthened. The bend axis is perpendicular to both the frame axis and frame.reference and passes through the point radius away from the origin along frame.reference; the bend direction is set by frame.reference (it points toward the centre of curvature). The frame origin defaults to the centre of the face where the body starts along the axis, the axis to the longest bounding-box direction and the reference to the next longest. The part of the body past the region follows the bent end rigidly. symmetric true keeps the middle of the region in place and bends both halves away from it. Volume changes by Pappus: V x (1 - mean offset / R). The result replaces the entity as a mesh entity that keeps the construction (brep recipe). Refuses radius <= the distance from the neutral fibre to the body on the centre side (DEF_BEND_RADIUS_TOO_SMALL), more than 360 degrees, 360 with a straight part left or without the exact kernel, or a straight part that would hit the bent body (DEF_SELF_INTERSECTION) and not exactly two of radius / angleDeg / length (DEF_BEND_UNDERDETERMINED / DEF_BEND_OVERDETERMINED). Then call analyze_deformation (fibre lengths) and check_deformation.

angleDeg.description: Angle the region turns, degrees, > 0 and at most 360 (360 only for the whole body, on the exact kernel: the two end faces are sewn into a ring).

frame.description: Bend frame; every field defaults from the body bounds and the defaults used are reported in data.frame.

axis.description: Direction the straight region runs along, unitless (normalised). Default: the longest bounding-box direction.

origin.description: A point of the neutral fibre, world document units. Default: the centre of the face where the body starts along the axis (the neutral fibre passes through the body centre line).

reference.description: Direction toward the centre of curvature, unitless; its component perpendicular to the axis is used and the bend turns toward it. Default: the next longest bounding-box direction.

id.description: Id of the 3D solid or mesh entity to deform (describe_scene lists ids). It is replaced by the deformed mesh entity (keepSource keeps it).

ids.description: Ids of several 3D solids or meshes to deform with the same parameters (one feature step; every body gets its own frame and region defaults from its own bounds). Use this or id.

keepSource.description: true: keep the original entity(ies) next to the deformed one(s) instead of replacing them. Default false.

length.description: Length of the bent region along the axis, document units, > 0 (the neutral fibre length). The region starts at region.start, default where the body starts.

output.description: How the result is computed: kernel choice and mesh tolerance.

mode.description: "auto" (default): the exact kernel builds the result when it can evaluate this deformation (the native kernel does for every law: the faces become B-splines fitted within output.tolerance), else the mesh path runs and the summary says so; "exact": refuse (DEF_EXACT_UNAVAILABLE) unless the exact kernel built it; "mesh": force the faceted mesh path.

preserveAnalytic.description: Recognise cylinders, cones and planes in an exact result (needs the exact warp of a later milestone; true is refused today).

tolerance.description: Largest deviation of the result from the true deformed surface, document units, > 0: the chordal deviation of the mesh path, or the fit error of the B-spline faces and edges on the exact path (a smaller value costs control points, not accuracy). Default: 1e-5 times the body bounding-box diagonal, clamped to [1e-6, 0.01].

radius.description: Bend radius of the neutral fibre, document units, > 0 (must exceed the body extent on the centre side).

region.description: Bent region along the axis; giving both start and end counts as giving length.

end.description: Where the bend ends along the axis, document units from the frame origin; with start this fixes the length.

start.description: Where the bend starts along the axis, document units from the frame origin. Default: where the body starts.

symmetric.description: true: keep the middle of the region in place and bend both halves away from it. Default false (the region start stays).

name: bend_body

description: Bevel edges of a subdivision cage: each edge is replaced by a strip of `segments` quads, set back by `width` (a fraction 0 < width < 0.5 of the length of the adjacent edges) on both sides. A chamfer of a cage: the smooth surface gets a rounded edge where it was crisp, or with `sharp` a crisp chamfer. `edges` are ids ("e:<idA>|<idB>") or [a, b] vertex index pairs; the edges must not share a vertex (bevel the others in another call) and must border two faces. A symmetric cage bevels the mirror edges too. Refuses width >= 0.5 (DIR_BEVEL_TOO_WIDE), edges sharing a vertex (DIR_BEVEL_ADJACENT) and boundary edges (DIR_BEVEL_BOUNDARY). Returns data { vertexCount, faceCount, vertices, vertexIds, faceIds, newVertices, newFaces }. Next: set_cage_crease, edit_subdivision_cage, check_subdivision.

edges.description: Edges to bevel: ids "e:<idA>|<idB>" or [a, b] vertex index pairs; no two may share a vertex.

items.description: A cage edge: id "e:<vertexIdA>|<vertexIdB>" (stable) or a [vertexIndex, vertexIndex] pair.

id.description: Id of the subdivision solid.

segments.description: Quads across the strip, 1..16 (default 1: a flat chamfer).

sharp.description: Sharpness 0..10 given to the two long edges of the strip (default 0 = smooth; 10 = infinitely crisp).

width.description: Setback as a fraction of the adjacent edge length, 0 < width < 0.5 (0.25 on a 2-unit cube edge = 0.5 document units).

name: bevel_cage_edges

description: Generate a bill of materials (BOM) from all InstanceEntity objects in the document. Groups instances by componentId; reports count per component and a breakdown of child entity kinds (perEntityKindCounts). Instances whose componentId is absent from doc.components are reported as orphan rows (componentName: "(missing)", orphan: true) — no error is thrown. Returns the unchanged document, affected:[], and data: { rows: BomRow[], totalInstances: number, distinctComponents: number, totalMassKg: number, rowsWithoutDensity: string[] }. A BomRow has: { componentId, componentName, count, perEntityKindCounts, orphan?, unitMassKg, totalMassKg, massSources?, massUnverified?, massReason? }; mass = solid volume (instance scale applied) x material density (same resolution as mass_properties), totalMassKg = sum over the row's instances; a row with a solid lacking a material/density has unitMassKg and totalMassKg null (massReason) and is listed in rowsWithoutDensity and excluded from data.totalMassKg. The summary ends the rows with "total mass X kg (N rows without density)". Standard parts (components with a partRef, e.g. fasteners inserted by insert_fastener_stack) are also grouped by part number in data.standardParts: { partNumber, family, description?, count, componentIds, unitMass?, totalMass?, representative? } (no mass for placeholder geometry). With includeMaterials, data.materials lists per assigned material { materialId, solidCount, totalVolume, volumeUnit, totalMass (g), totalMassKg, volumeMethod, densitySource, unverified, unverifiedReasons } plus data.unassignedSolidCount.

includeMaterials.description: Add data.materials: volume and mass (g) per assigned material over all solids, with unverified flags. Default false.

includeStandardParts.description: Add data.standardParts (instances grouped by part number). Default true when any component has a partRef, else the section is omitted.

name: bill_of_materials

description: Bind a component of this assembly (doc.components) to a managed item of another document: part number, revision, lifecycle state and, for a released / superseded / obsolete child, its release content hash (64 hex). HUMAN GATE. The signer attests these facts; llull cannot read the child document from here, and an agent can never declare a child released. Re-binding the same part number replaces its record (e.g. a new revision). Allowed only while this assembly revision is in_work. Needs `confirmation` (plm_act_payload): an agent gets PLM_HUMAN_GATE and hands over.

at.description: When the act happened: ISO-8601 UTC, e.g. 2026-11-02T09:30:00Z. The host (UI / llull CLI) fills it; commands never read a clock.

by.description: Ignored: the binding is recorded under the signer of the confirmation.

componentId.description: Id of a component of this document (doc.components); its instances are the quantity in the EBOM.

confirmation.description: HUMAN SIGNATURE, required: { alg: "Ed25519", keyId, publicKey, signature, nonce } made by a human with a TRUSTED signing key over this exact act (get the bytes with plm_act_payload, sign them in the desktop app or `llull exec ... --confirm-key KEYID`). An agent has no trusted key: it prepares the act and hands over (PLM_HUMAN_GATE).

contentHash.description: Release content hash (64 lowercase hex) of that child revision; required when state is released, superseded or obsolete.

name.description: Item name; default = the component name.

partNumber.description: Part number of the managed item this component is (A-Z 0-9 . _ - /, at most 64 characters).

revision.description: Revision label of the child that this assembly uses, e.g. "B".

state.description: Lifecycle state of that child revision, as the signer attests it.

name: bind_component_item

description: Create a blend sheet that bridges the gap between one boundary edge of nurbs_surface `a` and one of nurbs_surface `b` with tangent (G1) or curvature (G2) continuity at both ends. `continuity` "G1": the blend leaves each sheet in its tangent plane (cubic across); "G2": it also matches the normal curvature across each edge (quintic across). `factor` scales the end tangents (fraction of the gap, default 1: larger bulges more). The edges are matched point to point (each station of the first edge goes to its foot point on the second), so they should face each other: the sheets must leave their edges towards the other one (otherwise SRF_BLEND_FOLD). The blend is a new sheet (the inputs are kept; sew_surfaces or check_continuity next). The result reports the MEASURED continuity of both joints (g0Gap, g1AngleRad, g2Gap, order): the match is exact at the stations and approximate (interpolation) between them, so read `order` rather than assuming it. Reference: two pieces of the parabolic cylinder z = x^2 / 2 at x in [0, 1] and [2, 3] blend with G2.

a.description: First sheet and its edge.

id.description: Id of the first nurbs_surface.

side.description: Boundary edge of the sheet to blend from: "u0" / "u1" = the edge at the lowest / highest u, "v0" / "v1" likewise for v. Omit to detect the closest pair.

b.description: Second sheet and its edge.

id.description: Id of the second nurbs_surface.

side.description: Boundary edge of the sheet to blend from: "u0" / "u1" = the edge at the lowest / highest u, "v0" / "v1" likewise for v. Omit to detect the closest pair.

color.description: Hex color string #rrggbb, e.g. "#c8553d". Defaults to "#9fb4c7".

continuity.description: "G1" tangent-plane continuity (default) or "G2" curvature continuity across both edges.

factor.description: End tangent length as a fraction of the gap between the edges, 0.05..3. Default 1.

layerId.description: Layer id to assign the entity to. Defaults to the document default layer.

name.description: Optional display name for the entity (shown in the scene tree).

position.description: Origin [x, y, z] of the surface in document units; the poles are relative to it. Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

stations.description: Stations along the edge used to build the blend, integer 5..129. Default 33.

name: blend_surfaces

description: Weld 2+ solids into ONE exact solid and round every joint where they meet with a fillet: the one-piece frame operation (bike frame tubes, lugs and dropouts; pipe tees; brackets welded to plates; organic joints between swept or lofted parts). All intersection curves created by the union are filleted with `radius` (for a radius that varies along one edge, use fillet_edge radiusEnd on the result). The operands are consumed and replaced by one mesh entity that keeps the exact construction (STEP export, further fillets and booleans see true faces). Needs the exact kernel (check kernel_info): the OCC kernel (the desktop default; LLULL_KERNEL=occt-native or occt for the CLI and server); with the mesh kernel it cannot fillet and no-ops (use boolean op union there). If the kernel refuses, try another radius: a blend must fit inside the smallest wall it touches, and a crotch where three solids meet can reject specific radii.

ids.description: Ids of the 3D solids to weld (>= 2, distinct). The first one styles the result.

radius.description: Joint fillet radius in document units (> 0).

name: blend_union

description: Combine two 3D solid entities with a CSG operation into a single mesh entity: op "union" merges them, "subtract" removes the volume of b from a (order matters: result = a minus b), "intersect" keeps only the volume shared by both. Both operand entities are consumed (removed) and replaced by the result mesh. The kernel path requires a geometry kernel to be injected (available after app initialization); the mesh path needs only a mesh engine. Triangle-only operands (imported meshes, mesh results with no exact shape) are always combined by the mesh engine under engine "auto" (default; decided from the operands alone, so replay does not depend on the host): the result stays a plain mesh with guaranteed-manifold output and no polyhedral B-rep; engine "kernel" forces the B-rep kernel, engine "mesh" forces the mesh engine (refuses MESH_ENGINE_UNSUPPORTED without one; non-manifold operands refuse MESH_NON_MANIFOLD). Both operands must be 3D solids (any solid kind: box, cylinder, sphere, cone, torus, wedge, pyramid, extrusion, revolution, mesh); 2D shapes are rejected.

a.description: Id of the first 3D solid operand (the base solid for subtract).

b.description: Id of the second 3D solid operand (the tool solid for subtract), or a list of tool ids for union / subtract: the tools are unioned as a balanced tree and applied in ONE boolean — use a list for patterned cuts (coolant channels, bolt holes) instead of hundreds of sequential booleans, which nest the recipe deeper each step and slow down quadratically.

engine.description: "auto" (default): the mesh engine for triangle-only operands, else the kernel. "kernel": always the B-rep kernel. "mesh": always the mesh engine (B-rep operands are tessellated).

name: boolean

description: Break the link of projected sketch geometry: the project_edges_to_sketch step that made the entity is rewritten with its current plane-local geometry frozen, so later edits of the solid no longer move or fail it. All entities of that step are unlinked.

id.description: Id of a linked sketch entity (doc.sketchLinks).

name: break_sketch_link

description: Bridge two regions of a subdivision cage with a tube of quads (a handle, a tunnel, a loop): side A is `facesA` (an edge-connected face region that is removed; ids or indices) or `loopA` (one boundary edge of an existing hole of an open cage), likewise side B. The two boundary loops need the same number of vertices (DIR_BRIDGE_COUNT_MISMATCH); they are paired by the rotation that minimises the summed distance, shifted by `twist` whole vertices, and `segments` layers of quads are laid between them. With `otherId` side B is taken from another subdivision solid, which is merged into this one (placed by its own position / rotation) and removed. Within one closed solid the genus grows by 1 (a handle); with `otherId` two bodies are joined into one (no handle). Refuses a side that is not a single loop (DIR_BRIDGE_REGION), sides that share a vertex (DIR_BRIDGE_SAME) and different loop sizes. Returns data { vertexCount, faceCount, vertices, vertexIds, faceIds, newVertices, newFaces, loopSize, pairing, merged }. Next: edit_subdivision_cage to shape the tube, set_cage_crease, check_subdivision.

facesA.description: Side A as faces (one edge-connected region, removed). Give facesA or loopA.

items.description: A cage face: element id ("f-1.2", stable across topology edits) or current index.

facesB.description: Side B as faces (one edge-connected region, removed); with otherId they belong to that solid. Give facesB or loopB.

items.description: A cage face: element id ("f-1.2", stable across topology edits) or current index.

id.description: Id of the subdivision solid.

loopA.description: Side A as one boundary edge of a hole of the open cage. Give facesA or loopA.

loopB.description: Side B as one boundary edge of a hole (of otherId when given). Give facesB or loopB.

otherId.description: Id of a second subdivision solid that supplies side B; it is merged into `id` and removed.

segments.description: Layers of quads along the tube, 1..16 (default 1).

twist.description: Rotates the pairing of the loops by this many vertices (default 0 = the closest pairing).

name: bridge_cage_faces

description: Apply an ordered list of command actions as one project. Each action is one of: (1) { command, params, as? } — plain action; (2) { repeat: { count, as? }, step: { command, params } } — run step N times; count may be a number or expression string. Each iteration exposes $i (0-based) in params expressions. (3) { for_each: { values, as }, step: { command, params } } — iterate over values array (or expression). $as is the current element, $i the index. (4) NESTABLE LOOPS (preferred): { repeat: { count, as? }, actions: [ ...actions ] } runs the body count times with loop variable `as` (default "i", 0-based); { for: { var, from, to, step? }, actions: [...] } runs var from..to inclusive. count/from/to/step are numbers or "=expr" strings (count must be a non-negative integer; at most 1000 iterations per plan); bodies may contain loops. Use the loop variable and document parameters in any "=expr", e.g. "position": ["=r*cos(2*pi*i/n)", "=r*sin(2*pi*i/n)", 80] with parameters n and r. Expressions support + - * / ( ), pi, sin cos tan asin acos atan atan2 sqrt abs floor ceil round trunc sign exp ln log10 pow hypot mod min max. Aliases inside loops interpolate {expr}: "as": "piston{i}" binds $piston0, $piston1, ... (usable later, and as "$piston{i}" in the same body). A top-level loop is recorded as ONE history step that re-expands on replay, so set_parameter on n/r (even the count) regenerates it; entities made by later steps that reference loop-made ids by position may break if the count shrinks. Validation reports issues by path ("step 4 › iter 2 › step 1"). A step may bind its result to an alias with "as"; later steps reference it as "$alias" or "$alias[N]". params values starting with "=" are evaluated as arithmetic expressions against doc.parameters plus $i/$as. onError="abort" (default) rolls the whole document back on the first failing step; "continue" applies what it can. validate=true performs a dry run without changing the document.

actions.description: Ordered list of actions. Each item is { command, params?, as? } OR { repeat: { count, as? }, step: { command, params? } } OR { for_each: { values, as }, step: { command, params? } } OR nestable { repeat: { count, as? } | for: { var, from, to, step? }, actions: [ ...actions ] }. Params values may be "$alias" references or "=expr" arithmetic expressions.

onError.description: Failure policy: "abort" (default, full rollback on first failure) or "continue".

validate.description: When true, dry-run only: validate every step without modifying the document.

name: build_project

description: Read-only BUILDING schedule table (like Revit schedules; not a mechanical BOM: see bill_of_materials) for one element category: wall, door, window, room, slab, column, beam, stair, member (steel cut list), footing, panel, equipment, pipe (line list), tray, plate, connection or support (pipe supports: mark, line, pipe, type, steel it bears on, position, hanger rod length, attached / UNATTACHED) — one row per element with mark, level, dimensions, material and quantities. Column and beam rows give the NET volume (same rule as quantity_takeoff: slab > column > beam, overlaps counted once) in "Volume (m³)" and the raw prism in "Gross volume (m³)". data.csv is spreadsheet-ready.

kind.description: Which schedule to produce.

name: building_schedule

description: Set an image underlay to true scale from a known dimension: two points in IMAGE PIXEL coordinates and the real distance between them (document units). The scale becomes distance / pixel distance units per pixel (uniform). By default pixelA keeps its world position; pass `origin` to pin a pixel to a world point instead (e.g. the drawing datum to [0, 0, 0]). Pass `align` "x" or "y" to rotate the image in its plane (by the smallest angle) so the A→B segment runs along that axis — this also de-skews a crooked scan. Image pixel coordinates [px, py]: origin at the TOP-left corner of the picture, +px right, +py DOWN (as read off the image); fractional values are fine.

align.description: Rotate in-plane so A→B lies along the work-plane "x" or "y" axis. Default "none".

distance.description: Real distance between pixelA and pixelB, in document units (> 0).

id.description: Id of the image underlay to calibrate.

origin.description: Optional: pin an image pixel to a world point. Defaults to pixelA staying where it is.

pixel.description: Image pixel [px, py] to pin (same convention as pixelA).

world.description: World point [x, y, z] that pixel maps to after calibration.

pixelA.description: First reference point. Image pixel coordinates [px, py]: origin at the TOP-left corner of the picture, +px right, +py DOWN (as read off the image); fractional values are fine.

pixelB.description: Second reference point, same pixel convention as pixelA.

name: calibrate_underlay

description: Read-only report of the recorded flow result of a case: forces and coefficients (Cd, Cl, Cs, Cm, CdA), per-body forces, pressure and speed peaks with positions, convergence (steps, averaging, drag history), probe values and provenance (solver, device, precision, wall time, what is not modelled, named defaults). `stale: true` with the warning CFD_RESULT_STALE when the case or the geometry changed since the solve; `trusted: false` when the recorded summary cannot be re-verified against the stored bundle on this machine. `include` picks the sections (default all). Refused with CFD_NO_RESULT before any cfd_solve.
name: cfd_report

description: Bevel a single vertex of a polyline with a straight chamfer at the given distance. The polyline entity is updated: the vertex at vertexIndex is replaced by two points located distance back from the vertex along each adjacent segment, and a new line entity is added connecting those two points (the bevel face). vertexIndex is 0-based; for an open polyline valid range is 1 to N-2 (interior vertices only); for a closed polyline any vertex 0 to N-1 is valid. No-op if distance is too large for the adjacent segment lengths.

distance.description: Chamfer setback distance from the vertex along each adjacent segment. Must be > 0.

id.description: Id of the polyline entity to chamfer.

vertexIndex.description: 0-based index of the polyline vertex to chamfer. For open polylines: valid range is 1 to N-2. For closed polylines: valid range is 0 to N-1.

name: chamfer_2d

description: Bevel (chamfer) exact B-rep edges of a 3D solid entity and replace it with a new mesh entity that keeps the exact construction (its brep recipe). The source entity is consumed. Select edges with edgeIndices (indices from inspect_topology) and/or edgesNear (points near the edges, robust to parametric edits); with neither, ALL edges are chamfered. distance alone is a symmetric chamfer (equal legs on both faces). Asymmetric: add distance2 (second leg, document units) OR angleDeg (degrees, 0..90 exclusive, measured on the side1 face between that face and the chamfer; on a right-angle edge the second leg is distance * tan(angle)), together with side1Near (a point on the face that carries distance) or side1Name (persistent face name); for each selected edge the one of its two faces nearest to the point is side 1. Needs the exact kernel (check kernel_info): the OCC kernel (the desktop default; LLULL_KERNEL=occt-native or occt for the CLI and server); with the mesh kernel it no-ops. Target must be a 3D solid (box, cylinder, sphere, cone, torus, wedge, pyramid, extrusion, revolution, or mesh — including boolean results).

angleDeg.description: Chamfer angle in degrees, strictly between 0 and 90, measured on the side1 face from that face to the chamfer (distance-angle chamfer). Needs side1Near or side1Name. Exclusive with distance2.

distance.description: Chamfer distance in document units. Must be > 0. With distance2 or angleDeg it is the leg on the side1 face; alone it is the leg on both faces.

distance2.description: Second leg in document units (> 0), on the face that is not side 1 (distance-distance chamfer). Needs side1Near or side1Name. Exclusive with angleDeg.

edgeIndices.description: 0-based indices of the unique B-rep edges to chamfer, as listed by inspect_topology on the same entity (each edge counted once). Pass [] or omit (with no edgesNear) to chamfer ALL edges.

edgeNames.description: Persistent edge names (inspect_topology lists them on the native kernel): recorded automatically from the first pick and used on regeneration, so the same edge is rounded after an upstream edit; a name that is gone or split refuses the step (REF_LOST / REF_SPLIT). Wins over edgeIndices / edgesNear.

edgesNear.description: Select edges by location: each point picks the roundable edge nearest to it (distance to the edge curve, so any point on an edge, e.g. its visible corner on a drawing, selects it). Prefer this in parametric models: the feature history keeps the points, so the same edge is re-selected after an upstream edit renumbers edges. Combines with edgeIndices.

items.description: A point [x, y, z] in document units near the edge to chamfer (e.g. its mid point from inspect_topology).

id.description: Id of the 3D solid entity to chamfer. Must exist and be a 3D solid kind.

side1Name.description: Persistent face name of side 1 (inspect_topology lists face names on the native kernel); alternative to side1Near.

side1Near.description: A point [x, y, z] in document units on the face that carries distance (side 1) when distance2 or angleDeg is given.

name: chamfer_edge

description: Check access means of the BUILDING model against the access rules (ISO 14122, OSHA 29 CFR 1910) and list findings with stable STA_* codes, measured value, limit, clause, source and a one-line fix. M1 covers existing concrete stairs (add_stair: Blondel 2h+g, riser, tread, pitch angle, width, flight rise) and slab open edges (add_slab). Only grade A rules fail; grade B rules warn and add STA_RULE_UNVERIFIED; the result always has reviewRequired: true (a qualified person signs access means). Lengths in the answer are millimetres and angles degrees, whatever the document units. Open edges need edgeDropThresholdMm (no graded rule exists, so there is no default): without it the edge check is skipped with the warning STA_EDGE_RULE_UNSET. The drop is measured from the slab top to the next surface below (another slab, else the lowest level elevation); an edge is protected when the drop is within the threshold or a wall of the slab level reaching at least 1100 mm above the slab top covers it. Read-only; see list_access_rules for the rows.

edgeDropSource.description: Where edgeDropThresholdMm comes from (project document, clause); echoed in the findings.

edgeDropThresholdMm.description: Open-edge check only: a drop above this height (millimetres, whatever the document units) needs protection. No default: it has no graded source.

ids.description: Building element ids (stairs, slabs) to check. Default: every stair and slab. Other element kinds are listed under `skipped`.

include.description: Which checks to run: "stairs" (concrete stairs) and/or "edges" (slab open edges). Default both.

rulesets.description: Rulesets to evaluate: "iso_14122" (ISO 14122-2/3/4:2016) and/or "osha_1910" (OSHA 29 CFR 1910.23/25/28/29). No default: choose the site standard.

name: check_access

description: Check a finite-element analysis end to end and return data { status: pass | warn | fail, state, items [{ code, severity: error | warning, ids, message, remediation }], reviewRequired: true }: parts exist and are solids with a material, elastic E / nu (static, thermo_static, coupled) or thermal properties (heat), supports (static needs at least one: FEA_NO_CONSTRAINTS), loads, thermal / thermo-mechanical set-up, mesh recorded and not stale or inverted, results recorded and not stale, and every recorded summary matching its artifact in the artifact store (a differing one is FEA_SUMMARY_MISMATCH, state untrusted; no store or artifact is FEA_MESH_MISSING / FEA_RESULTS_MISSING, state missing). Run it before fea_mesh / fea_solve (readiness) and after the solve. Modal / buckling: supports, rigid-body modes, buckling-factor guards; any structural case: supports that remove all six rigid-body motions (FEA_UNDERCONSTRAINED) and mesh adequacy (FEA_MESH_ADEQUACY); solved static / thermo_static cases with allowables: the margin rows (FEA_MS_NEGATIVE, FEA_MARGINAL_BAND_UNSET, FEA_DISPOSITION_PENDING). It is not a certification: reviewRequired is always true and a qualified person must review the model, mesh and results.

analysisId.description: Id of the analysis (affected[0] of create_analysis, e.g. an-1.1).

name: check_analysis

description: Read-only design-vs-scan clash: for each design entity, scan points inside it (hard) or within `clearance` of it, grouped in clusters (voxels of 2 x the point spacing, 26-connected); a cluster counts only with >= minPointsInVolume points (named default 10, so rain or people in the scan are noise). Per entity: status hard | clearance | clear, minGap (negative = penetration), location, points, clusters, and the sampling bound (spacing / 2). An as-built run committed from this cloud ignores its own surface points. reviewRequired is always true: a clear result from a scan is not proof of absence. device "gpu" (RS-4) prunes far points on the GPU with a conservative bound and re-checks the rest in f64 on the CPU: same result.

clearance.description: Required clearance in document units, e.g. 75 (mm).

cloudId.description: Id of an attached cloud (affected[0] of attach_point_cloud, e.g. "cloud-1.1").

device.description: cpu (default): the recorded Rust-CPU path. gpu: the wgpu fast path (RS-4); see the command for what it changes.

entityIds.description: Design entity ids: pipe runs (add_pipe_run ids), cylinders, boxes, spheres or any 3D solid.

excludeExtractionsOf.description: Ignore an as-built run's own scan points (default true).

minPointsInVolume.description: Noise threshold: points a cluster needs (default 10, named).

searchDistance.description: Reach for the gap of a clear entity in document units (default 1 m).

name: check_asbuilt_clash

description: Buildability gate of the 3D parts (solids and component instances): is every part a valid closed single-lump solid, do parts overlap (FPR_PAIR_HARD with overlap volume mm3, FPR_PAIR_CONTAINED), touch (info) or sit closer than the required clearance, is every part attached to something grounded (FPR_PART_FLOATING, FPR_PART_RESTING_ONLY), are walls thick enough for a manufacturing process (FPR_WALL_THIN), and is each revolute dynamics joint physically realised by a pin in a bore (OCC only; clearance and engagement in mm). Read-only. Every item has a stable FPR_ code, ids, values with unit suffixes (mm, mm2, mm3), a threshold with its source and a remediation. status is the worst item (fail > not_run > warn > pass); not_run means the installed kernel cannot verify it, never a pass. Scope: no selector = all parts; ids = only those entities/instances; body = the entities of a rigid body (pairs inside it are then checked too); component = every instance of that component. Next: fix fails; declare intended overlaps (press fit, thread, weld) with allow_interference; mark world-fixed parts with set_part_grounded; then simulate_motion. Computed by llull, not approved: a qualified engineer must review.

body.description: Rigid body id (dynamics): check its entities, including pairs inside the body.

clearanceMm.description: Required clearance between parts in millimetres; closer pairs give FPR_PAIR_CLEARANCE. Default 0 (no clearance check).

component.description: Component id: check every instance of it.

ids.description: Check only these entity / instance ids. Mutually exclusive with body and component.

includeJoints.description: Also check that each revolute dynamics joint has a coaxial pin and bore. Default true.

minWallMm.description: Minimum wall thickness in millimetres; overrides process.

process.description: Manufacturing process whose sourced minimum wall (vendor guidance, grade B) is the wall threshold.

raysPerPart.description: Thickness samples per part. Default 2000; parts × samples must stay under 200000.

thickness.description: "ray" measures wall thickness by inward rays (default when process or minWallMm is given), "off" skips it.

touchToleranceMm.description: Distance in millimetres at or below which parts count as touching. Default 0.001 document units.

name: check_assembly

description: Read-only continuity check of the fillets of solids (every solid with a fillet when `ids` is omitted). For each edge fillet the exact kernel measures, at `samples` points along each contact line where the blend meets a support face: the gap between the faces (g0Gap, document units), the angle between the outward normals (g1AngleRad, radians), and the normal-curvature jump (g2Gap in 1/unit, g2Rel relative: 1 for a plane against a circular fillet) with the order reached (G0 = not tangent, G1, G2). Findings carry stable codes: BLD_CHECK_G1_ANGLE (fail), BLD_CHECK_G2_JUMP (fail when require is G2, else info), BLD_CHECK_G0_GAP, BLD_CHECK_INVALID (fail), BLD_CHECK_UNVERIFIED_PICK (warn: kernel keeps no names), BLD_CHECK_UNVERIFIED_CONTACT (warn: a blend face has no measurable contact line, so nothing is claimed), and with purpose "release" BLD_CHECK_TOLERANCE_DEFAULTED (warn) and BLD_CHECK_REVIEW (info; reviewRequired true). tolerances names every limit with `defaulted`. Needs the exact native kernel (check kernel_info); without it, or with no filleted solid, status is "not_run". Does not modify the document.

g0.description: Largest allowed gap between the blend and a support face, document units (> 0). Default 1e-6 x the bounding-box diagonal.

g1AngleRad.description: Largest allowed angle between the outward normals at a contact, radians (> 0). Default 0.01.

g2Rel.description: Largest relative normal-curvature jump still counted as G2, dimensionless (> 0). Default 0.1.

ids.description: Ids of solids to check. Default: every solid whose recipe contains a fillet.
