name.description: Display name of the case.

notch.description: Optional notch: the nominal stress is scaled by Kf = 1 + q (Kt - 1) (Neuber on the cyclic curve for strain-life).

feIncludesKt.description: true when the stress already contains the concentration (no extra Kf); false: Kf scales the nominal stress.

q.description: Notch sensitivity q in [0, 1]: Kf = 1 + q (Kt - 1).

blocksPerUnit.description: Blocks of the history per flight or hour (flights / hours only).

unit.description: Unit of the required life; flights / hours need blocksPerUnit.

name: create_fatigue_case

description: Realise an implicit FIELD as a closed triangle mesh solid (derived and read-only: change the field nodes and run this again). voxel is the grid spacing in document units: error is second order (volume error ~ 0.6 (voxel/smallest feature radius)^2). Bounds default to the field's support box (primitives, clipped lattices); a bare lattice or plane needs `bounds` or a region. Budgets are checked before sampling: a grid above the engine limit is refused with IMP_GRID_BUDGET (use a coarser voxel or the native engine), and a mesh above maxTriangles (default 5000000; 20000000 with the native engine when the host keeps big meshes in its mesh asset store) with IMP_TRIANGLE_BUDGET. hideSource moves the listed solids (e.g. the part the field came from) to a hidden layer. Next: implicit_properties, lattice_properties, check_implicit, export_3mf / export_stl.

bounds.description: Box to realise. Default: the support box of the field. The grid is padded by 2 voxels so the surface closes.

max.description: Upper corner [x, y, z] in document units.

min.description: Lower corner [x, y, z] in document units.

color.description: Optional hex colour of the body, e.g. "#d9b26f".

field.description: Id of the field node to realise.

hideSource.description: Ids of solids to move to a hidden layer once the body exists (kept, not deleted).

maxTriangles.description: Refuse a mesh with more triangles than this. Default 5000000 (more when the host stores big meshes as assets).

mesher.description: tetra (default): marching tetrahedra, always closed and manifold, cuts sharp edges and corners by up to a voxel. dual_contouring: one vertex per surface cell placed by a quadratic error fit on exact edge crossings and gradients, so box corners, clipped edges and blend creases stay sharp (volume error far below the tetrahedra on faceted bodies); the TS engine meshes it (up to its grid limit); when the result is not closed and manifold the body falls back to tetra and data.mesherFallback says so.

name.description: Optional name of the body.

voxel.description: Grid spacing in document units (> 0). Halve it for 4x smaller error and 8x more samples.

name: create_implicit_body

description: Create or replace a composite lamina material record (the input of laminate analysis, zones and plies). Elastic constants E1 (fibre), E2 (transverse), G12 (in-plane shear) in MPa (or in `stressUnit`, e.g. psi / ksi in inch documents: stored converted to MPa), nu12 (major Poisson ratio, dimensionless); optional strengths Xt, Xc (fibre tension / compression), Yt, Yc (transverse), S (in-plane shear), all MPa and positive magnitudes: failure criteria are refused when one is missing (no default exists). plyThickness is the cured ply thickness in document length units; density is mass per unit^3 (needed by laminate_mass). basis states what the numbers are: "mean" / "unknown" values or an empty source make every result computed from this material UNVERIFIED; use "b_basis" / "a_basis" only for cited allowables (e.g. NCAMP). source is the free-text citation. lockingAngle / warningShear (degrees) are fabric shear limits for drape; tsaiWuF12Star in [-1, 0] overrides the Tsai-Wu default -0.5. Refused: non-positive values, nu12^2 >= E1/E2 (CMP_MATERIAL_NOT_POSITIVE_DEFINITE). Next: define_rosette, create_composite_part, analyze_laminate.

E1.description: Longitudinal (fibre direction) modulus, MPa; must be > 0.

G12.description: In-plane shear modulus, MPa; must be > 0.

G13.description: Optional out-of-plane shear modulus 1-3, MPa; must be > 0.

G23.description: Optional out-of-plane shear modulus 2-3, MPa; must be > 0.

GIIc.description: Mode II fracture toughness, N/mm (for the LaRC03 matrix-tension criterion); must be > 0.

GIc.description: Mode I fracture toughness, N/mm (for the LaRC03 matrix-tension criterion); must be > 0.

S.description: In-plane shear strength, MPa; must be > 0.

Xc.description: Fibre-direction compressive strength, MPa (give the magnitude, positive); must be > 0.

Xt.description: Fibre-direction tensile strength, MPa (positive); must be > 0.

Yc.description: Transverse compressive strength, MPa (magnitude); must be > 0.

Yt.description: Transverse tensile strength, MPa; must be > 0.

alpha1.description: Coefficient of thermal expansion along the fibre, 1/K (may be slightly negative for carbon).

alpha2.description: Coefficient of thermal expansion across the fibre, 1/K.

beta1.description: Moisture swelling strain along the fibre per unit moisture content (mass fraction, dimensionless).

beta2.description: Moisture swelling strain across the fibre per unit moisture content (mass fraction, dimensionless).

density.description: Lamina density, mass per unit^3 of the document (e.g. g/mm^3 in a mm document); must be > 0.

form.description: Material form: unidirectional tape, woven fabric or a core.

lockingAngle.description: Fabric shear locking angle, degrees (drape limit, no default).

name.description: Unique material name, e.g. "T300_5208"; reused names replace the record.

nu12.description: Major Poisson ratio (dimensionless); nu12^2 must stay below E1/E2.

plyThickness.description: Cured ply thickness, document length units (mm in mm documents); must be > 0.

source.description: Citation of the data (standard, report, supplier datasheet). Empty = unverified.

stressUnit.description: Unit of E1, E2, G12, G13, G23, Xt, Xc, Yt, Yc and S: Pa, kPa, MPa (default), GPa, psi, ksi or Msi. The record is stored in MPa; use psi / ksi / Msi for data given in US customary units (inch documents).

tsaiWuF12Star.description: Tsai-Wu interaction factor F12* in [-1, 0]; default -0.5 when omitted (reported as a default).

name: create_lamina_material

description: Store the laminate of a composite part as shell sections for structural analysis: one section per zone (the stack laid where that zone governs; one section for the whole part when it has no zones), each with its plies from the tool side up: material name (the lamina record in the composites materials), cured thickness in document units, angle in degrees from the part rosette 0-degree direction, and the total thickness. The analysis plugin reads doc.composites.sections to write PCOMP / composite shell sections; re-run after changing plies or zones (earlier sections of the part are replaced). Returns the section ids. Refused when the part has no plies.
name: create_laminate_sections

description: Define or replace a named material in the document material library. A material carries a physical density (used by mass_properties for mass = volume × density) and PBR visual properties (color, metalness, roughness) used by the 3D viewport renderer. If a material with the same name already exists it is replaced (its property models are kept). Records made with define_material_record keep their record; records imported from a library are read-only (MAT_RECORD_READONLY). UNIT TRAP: a bare `density` is in GRAMS per (document unit)³, NOT kg/m³. mm document: steel 0.00785 (g/mm³), aluminium 0.0027, PLA 0.00124. Metre document: steel is 7 850 000 g/m³; passing 7850 meaning kg/m³ makes every mass ~1000× too light. Safest: always pass densityUnit, e.g. { density: 7850, densityUnit: "kg/m^3" } or { density: 7.85, densityUnit: "g/cm^3" } in any document (add_rigid_body takes the same densityUnit; its bare density is kg/m³). A density outside 0.01–25 g/cm³ (0.0005–25 with an explicit densityUnit) is still stored but returns a WARNING in the summary and data.warnings naming the likely intended unit; the summary always prints the density in g/cm³ and kg/m³ — check it. Assign the material to entities with assign_material.

clearcoat.description: Clear lacquer over the finish in [0, 1] (glossy carbon, painted parts). Default 0.

color.description: Diffuse/albedo color as a 6-digit CSS hex string, e.g. "#b0b0b0" for grey steel. Must match the pattern #rrggbb (exactly 6 hex digits after the #). Used by the 3D viewport PBR renderer. Default: the replaced material's color, else "#b0b0b0".

color2.description: Secondary #rrggbb colour of the finish (crossing tows, checker squares).

density.description: Density; must be > 0 and finite. Without densityUnit it is GRAMS per (document-length-unit)³ (not kg/m³): for a mm document g/mm³ — steel ≈ 0.00785, aluminium ≈ 0.0027, PLA ≈ 0.00124, titanium ≈ 0.00445, copper ≈ 0.00893; for a metre document steel = 7850000 (g/m³) — or pass 7850 with densityUnit "kg/m^3". This value is used by mass_properties when the material is assigned to an entity.

densityUnit.description: Optional unit of `density`, e.g. "g/cm^3", "kg/m^3", "lb/in^3". When given, density is converted to g/(document-unit)³ (the stored unit). Omit it to give density directly in g/(document-unit)³.

finish.description: Optional procedural surface texture (albedo + normal + roughness maps, box-projected, shown in the viewport and embedded in export_gltf): carbon_twill (2×2 twill carbon weave), carbon_plain (plain weave), brushed (brushed metal), knurl (diamond knurling), checker. Carbon fibre: color "#16181b", metalness 0.2, roughness 0.35, finish "carbon_twill", clearcoat 1.

finishScale.description: Size of one texture tile in document units (> 0; a carbon tile holds 8 tows). Default 24.

metalness.description: PBR metalness factor in [0, 1]. 0 = fully dielectric (plastic, wood, ceramic), 1 = fully metallic (aluminium, steel, copper). Non-metallic coatings are typically 0. Default: the replaced material's value, else 0.

name.description: Human-readable material name used as the lookup key, e.g. "steel", "aluminium_6061". Must be a non-empty string. Case-sensitive. Used with assign_material to reference this material.

normalStrength.description: Relief depth of the finish normal map in [0, 2]. Default 1.

roughness.description: PBR roughness factor in [0, 1]. 0 = mirror-smooth (polished metal), 1 = fully diffuse/matte (rough concrete, unfinished wood). Brushed aluminium ≈ 0.3, matte plastic ≈ 0.7. Default: the replaced material's value, else 0.5.

name: create_material

description: Derive and freeze the manufacturing BOM of a product baseline. Starts from the engineering BOM of the baseline (every member except the end item, at the baselined revision, with the quantity frozen at release) and applies: omit (design-only EBOM items, with a reason), quantities (a different build quantity, e.g. a kit, with a reason) and add (manufacturing-only lines: consumable, tooling, process-material or phantom, with a name, quantity and reason). Lines are sorted by part number and the record is sealed with a SHA-256. An agent may create one. Use it as the mbom of record_as_built; read it with manufacturing_bom.

kind.description: What the line is.

name.description: What it is, non-empty.

partNumber.description: Part number of the manufacturing-only item (A-Z 0-9 . _ - /), not already a line.

reason.description: Why, non-empty: it is kept in the MBOM (e.g. "supplied as a kit", "design-only item").

revision.description: Revision label when it has one; default "-".

at.description: When the act happened: ISO-8601 UTC, e.g. 2026-11-02T09:30:00Z. The host (UI / llull CLI) fills it; commands never read a clock.

baseline.description: Id of the product baseline (create_baseline) whose engineering BOM this derives from.

by.description: User id doing the act (the host fills it from the authenticated user; an agent cannot override it where the server has named users).

id.description: MBOM id; omitted = the next 'MBOM-nnnn'.

name.description: MBOM name (non-empty), e.g. "Hinge plant 2 build".

omit.description: EBOM items not built or not bought separately.

reason.description: Why, non-empty: it is kept in the MBOM (e.g. "supplied as a kit", "design-only item").

partNumber.description: EBOM part number whose build quantity differs.

reason.description: Why, non-empty: it is kept in the MBOM (e.g. "supplied as a kit", "design-only item").

name: create_mbom

description: Create a 3D NURBS curve (clamped B-spline, optionally rational) from its control polygon. `degree` 1..25 (3 = cubic), `poles` the control points (at least degree + 1, at most 10000). Omit `knots` for a clamped uniform knot vector on [0, 1]. To give them, either pass the FULL knot vector in `knots` (non-decreasing, length poles + degree + 1, e.g. [0,0,0,0,1,1,1,1] for a cubic Bezier) or pass the distinct knots in `knots` with their `multiplicities` (end multiplicities degree + 1, interior at most degree). `weights` (one > 0 per pole) make it rational: a quadratic with weights [1, w, 1] is a conic arc. The curve does not pass through the poles (use interpolate_curve for that). Next: inspect_nurbs, analyze_curve_curvature, edit_nurbs.

color.description: Hex color string #rrggbb, e.g. "#c8553d". Defaults to "#2a7ab0".

degree.description: Polynomial degree, an integer 1..25 (1 = polyline, 2 = quadratic, 3 = cubic).

knots.description: Optional knots: the full non-decreasing vector (length poles + degree + 1) when `multiplicities` is omitted, else the DISTINCT strictly increasing knots. Omit for clamped uniform.

layerId.description: Layer id to assign the entity to. Defaults to the document default layer.

multiplicities.description: Optional multiplicity of each distinct knot (first and last degree + 1, others 1..degree). Use with distinct `knots`.

name.description: Optional display name for the entity (shown in the scene tree).

items.description: Control point [x, y, z] in document units, relative to `position`.

position.description: Origin [x, y, z] of the curve in document units; the poles are relative to it. Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

weights.description: Optional rational weights, one finite number > 0 per pole. Omit for a non-rational curve.

name: create_nurbs_curve

description: Create a NURBS surface sheet (clamped tensor-product B-spline patch, optionally rational) from its control net. `poles` is a grid [i][j] of control points: i runs along u (the outer array), j along v (each inner array), all inner arrays the same length. `degreeU` / `degreeV` 1..25 (3 = bicubic), each direction needs at least degree + 1 poles. Omit the knots for clamped uniform vectors on [0, 1]; to give them, pass the full knot vector (`knotsU` / `knotsV` alone) or the distinct knots with `multiplicitiesU` / `multiplicitiesV`. `weights` (a grid like `poles`, every value > 0) make it rational (spheres, cylinders, tori are exact rational patches). The patch is a sheet: it has area but no volume. Next: inspect_nurbs, analyze_surface_curvature, check_continuity, thicken_surface.

color.description: Hex color string #rrggbb, e.g. "#c8553d". Defaults to "#9fb4c7".

knotsU.description: Optional u knots: the full non-decreasing vector, or the distinct knots when `multiplicitiesU` is given.

knotsV.description: Optional v knots: the full non-decreasing vector, or the distinct knots when `multiplicitiesV` is given.

layerId.description: Layer id to assign the entity to. Defaults to the document default layer.

multiplicitiesU.description: Optional multiplicity of each distinct u knot (ends degreeU + 1).

multiplicitiesV.description: Optional multiplicity of each distinct v knot (ends degreeV + 1).

name.description: Optional display name for the entity (shown in the scene tree).

poles.description: Control net: poles[i][j], i along u, j along v; a rectangular grid of at least 2 x 2.

items.description: Control point [x, y, z] in document units, relative to `position`.

position.description: Origin [x, y, z] of the surface in document units; the poles are relative to it. Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

weights.description: Optional rational weights, a grid with the shape of `poles`, every value finite and > 0.

name: create_nurbs_surface

description: Create an empty draft piping spec: only the header (id, dimensional standard ASME or EN, rating basis, corrosion allowance, size range, catalogues searched, optional service, materials, mill tolerance, design temperature limits). Nothing is defaulted: the dimensional standard, rating, corrosion allowance and size range must be named (safety data). Then add components and branch cells with edit_pipe_spec. Refuses an existing id (PSC_SPEC_CONFLICT). Next: edit_pipe_spec, then check_pipe_spec.

catalogs.description: Catalogue ids searched in order, optionally pinned as id@version (the bundled one is "llull-open-piping").

corrosionAllowance.description: Corrosion allowance { value, unit: "mm" | "in" }; stored in mm. Required: there is no default (AF-31).

unit.description: "mm" or "in".

designLimits.description: Design temperature limits of the spec in degC.

dimensionalStandard.description: Dimensional standard of the pipe and fittings: ASME (B36.10M / B16.9, NPS) or EN (EN 10220 / EN 10253, DN). No default: name it.

elbowAngles.description: Elbow angle rules consumed by routing (02 RTE).

bendRadiusD.description: Pipe bends: bend centreline radius in pipe outside diameters (5 = a 5D bend) for a turn no angle fits; butt-weld pipe only (flagged RTE_NONSTANDARD_FITTING). A run bendRadius (route_pipe) overrides it.

trimmedAllowed.description: Whether a cut-to-angle (trimmed) elbow is allowed: the spec 90 degree elbow cut to a turn up to 90 degrees (flagged RTE_NONSTANDARD_FITTING).

id.description: Spec id, 1 to 64 characters of A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ -, e.g. "CS150-A1".

materials.description: Material per product form, e.g. { pipe: "ASTM A106 Gr B", fittings: "ASTM A234 WPB" }.

millTolerance.description: Mill under-tolerance as a fraction of the wall (0.125 = 12.5 %).

provenance.description: Where the spec comes from: { author, citation, accessed }.

rating.description: Pressure rating basis of the spec: { system, class | pn, materialGroup }. check_pipe_spec compares design conditions with it.

materialGroup.description: Material group of the rating table, "1.1" for carbon steel.

ratingTableId.description: Id of an imported rating table (reserved).

system.description: Rating standard: "ASME B16.5" (bundled table for group 1.1), "EN 1092-1" or "company".

service.description: Service the spec covers, free text ("hydrocarbon process, non-toxic").

sizeRange.description: Size range of the spec: { fromNps, toNps } (inch designation or number) or { fromDn, toDn }.

fromNps.description: Smallest NPS of the range, inch designation ("2-1/2") or number (2.5). Give fromNps + toNps or fromDn + toDn.

name: create_pipe_spec

description: Create a pipe line (the line-list record runs belong to): service, sequence, spec name, DN; line number from the document template (default {dn}-{service}-{sequence}-{spec}[-{insulationCode}{insulationThickness}], change it with set_piping_settings) unless given. The spec must already be in the document (import_pipe_spec, with the catalogues it names via import_piping_catalog); its pipe row for the DN gives the OD and wall. insulation { code, thickness (mm or "fromSpec"), material? }: "fromSpec" reads the spec insulation table by code, DN and designTempC (the row is named in data.insulation); the envelope (OD + 2 x thickness, data.envelopeDiameterMm) is what check_clashes and the auto-router keep clear. slope { value, unit, fall } declares a gravity line: check_piping then reports legs rising against it (RTE_ADVERSE_SLOPE) and low / high points without drain / vent (RTE_POCKET). Returns the line id (affected[0]); data = { lineId, lineNumber, template { value, defaulted, applied }, lineNumberParse (explicit number only: how the template reads it, differences are reported, never corrected), spec: { id, revision, status }, pipe: { outsideDiameterMm, wallMm }, insulation, envelopeDiameterMm, slope, unverified }. Refusals: RTE_SPEC_UNKNOWN (spec or a catalogue it names not loaded), RTE_SPEC_NO_COMPONENT (no pipe row for the DN, no insulation row), RTE_DUPLICATE_LINE_NUMBER, RTE_SLOPE_INVALID. Next: add_tie_in_point (or add_nozzle on equipment), then route_pipe (compass legs) or auto_route_pipe.

designTempC.description: Design temperature, °C (picks the insulation table row for "fromSpec").

dn.description: Nominal size DN of the line (e.g. 100).

from.description: From tag text for the line list.

insulation.description: Insulation of the line (envelope OD + 2 x thickness).

code.description: Insulation code written in the line number, e.g. 'H' (hot).

material.description: Insulation material; default from the spec table row, else unnamed.

thickness.description: Thickness in mm, or "fromSpec" to read the spec insulation table (needs designTempC and a table row for the code, DN and temperature).

lineNumber.description: Explicit line number; default from the template.

slope.description: Declared slope of the whole line (a gravity drain): check_piping reports legs that rise against it (RTE_ADVERSE_SLOPE) and low / high points without a drain / vent (RTE_POCKET).

fall.description: true = the pipe descends along the flow (a drain); false = it rises along the flow.

unit.description: "percent" (1 = 1 %), "ratio" (drop / plan length, 0.01) or "deg".

value.description: Slope size, > 0: percent of the plan length (1 = 1 %), a ratio (0.01) or degrees, per unit. At most 45 degrees (100 %).

spec.description: Id of a piping spec already in the document (list_pipe_specs), e.g. 'CS150'.

to.description: To tag text for the line list.

name: create_pipeline

description: Create one triangle-mesh solid per ply piece of a composite part (split into more solids where the plies below it stop, so each solid sits at one height), offset along the tool-face normal by the cured ply thickness and stacked on the plies below it (a ply on a ramp sits on the plies that cover it; a core created with add_core lifts the plies above it). Each solid is a closed mesh entity named "<ply> piece <n>" on the tool layer, so export_stl (perEntity), export_obj / export_gltf and the mesh STEP path export them; mass_properties measures them. `plies` selects plies by id or name (default all). `maxEdge` (document length units, default the outline diagonal / 16) bounds the triangle edge on curved faces: smaller is smoother and heavier (at most 4 refinement levels). The solids are a snapshot of the model now: re-run after editing plies (delete the old ones first). The core itself is not meshed. On a plane, cylinder, cone or NURBS tool face without a core, each solid also carries its exact construction (the piece of the tool face lifted by the cured thickness): export_step_ap242 writes it as a true B-rep solid named "<ply> piece <n>" with the OCC kernel, and falls back to the mesh when the kernel cannot build it. Computed by llull, not approved.

maxEdge.description: Maximum triangle edge on curved faces, document length units, > 0; default outline diagonal / 16.

plies.description: Plies to mesh; default every ply of the part.

items.description: Ply id or name.

name: create_ply_solids

description: Open a model-review issue (a BCF topic): title, type (e.g. "Clash", "Issue", "Request"), priority, optional description, labels, the viewpoints that show it (save_viewpoint) and the entities it concerns. Returns the id (iss-<n>) in affected[0] and data { id, guid }. export_bcf writes the issues as a BCF 3.0 file with snapshots. Does not add a feature step. Errors: VIS_ISSUE_INVALID, VIS_VIEWPOINT_NOT_FOUND, VIS_ENTITY_NOT_FOUND.

entityIds.description: Entities the issue concerns (selected in the BCF viewpoints).

title.description: Short title, e.g. "Line 102 clashes with the cable tray".

type.description: BCF topic type, e.g. "Clash", "Issue", "Request". Default "Issue".

viewpointIds.description: Saved viewpoints showing the issue (the first is the BCF default viewpoint).

name: create_review_issue

description: Create a named saved view (for a BCF review camera used by issues, walkthroughs and render_view use save_viewpoint instead): a camera (a preset direction framing the scene, or an explicit camera), the set of PMI items shown in it, an optional entity filter and an optional section. Saved views are what a reviewer opens (activate_saved_view) and what AP242 exchange carries. Give direction (front, back, left, right, top, bottom, iso) OR camera. pmiIds default to none, so list the items to show (e.g. "$holeSize"). Refusals: GDT_VIEW_REF_UNKNOWN, GDT_FIELD_INVALID_FOR_KIND. Returns the saved view id in affected.

camera.description: Explicit camera { target, azimuth, polar, distance } (same fields as set_camera).

target.description: Orbit target [x, y, z], document units.

direction.description: Preset viewing direction framing the scene.

entityIds.description: Optional entity filter: only these solids are shown.

name.description: View name, e.g. "TOP - HOLE PATTERN".

pmiIds.description: Ids of the PMI items visible in this view. Default none.

section.description: Optional section: cutting plane for this view.

direction.description: Side the section is viewed from.

offset.description: World coordinate of the cutting plane on the axis the view looks along, document units.

name: create_saved_view

description: Create a SCALAR field (a number at every point of space) to grade a lattice: pass its id as thickness / level (add_tpms_lattice), radius (add_strut_lattice), thickness (shell_field), distance (offset_field) or blend radius (combine_fields) instead of a number. kind coordinate: the x, y or z coordinate (axis). kind distance: distance in document units to a point (toPoint), a plane (toPlane, signed, positive on the normal side), the closed solid of an entity (toEntity, signed, negative inside) or the value of another field (toField); give exactly one. kind ramp: maps an input scalar (input) from [inMin, inMax] to [outMin, outMax], clamped by default, easing linear or smoothstep (the nTop "ramp"). kind mix: a*(1-factor) + b*factor. kind arith: add, subtract, multiply, divide, min or max of a and b. kind noise: deterministic value noise in [0, 1) from seed, frequency (cells per document unit) and octaves 1..6. a, b, factor accept a number or a scalar field id. Next: add_tpms_lattice / add_strut_lattice with the id as the graded value; evaluate_field does not take scalars (probe them through the lattice).

a.description: mix / arith: first operand, a number or a scalar field id.

axis.description: coordinate: which coordinate.

b.description: mix / arith: second operand, a number or a scalar field id.

clamp.description: ramp: hold the output at its ends outside [inMin, inMax]. Default true (required for smoothstep).

factor.description: mix: blend factor (0 gives a, 1 gives b), a number or a scalar field id.

frequency.description: noise: noise cells per document unit (> 0).

inMax.description: ramp: input value that maps to outMax (must differ from inMin).

inMin.description: ramp: input value that maps to outMin.

input.description: ramp: id of the input scalar field.

kind.description: Scalar kind; see the command description for the parameters of each.

name.description: Optional label for the node.

octaves.description: noise: octaves 1..6 (default 1); each doubles the frequency and halves the amplitude.

operation.description: arith: the operation on a and b.

seed.description: noise: integer seed (default 0); the same seed gives the same field.

toEntity.description: distance: signed distance to the closed 3D solid with this entity id (negative inside).

toField.description: distance: the value of this field node (e.g. a body field) as the scalar.

toPlane.description: distance: signed distance to this plane.

normal.description: Plane normal [x, y, z] (non-zero); positive on this side.

origin.description: A point on the plane [x, y, z].

toPoint.description: distance: measure to this point [x, y, z] in document units.

description: Create a drawing sheet: ISO paper with a frame and title block that documents the 3D model as orthographic line views. Pass `views` (e.g. ["front","top","right"]) to add standard projection views in one call, laid out automatically per the first-angle (ISO default) or third-angle convention. Views are live: they reference the model, so after the model changes export_sheet_svg shows the new geometry without editing the sheet. Add more with create_drawing_view, add_section_view, add_detail_view. Returns the sheet id then the view ids in affected. Omit `scale` to auto-fit the largest standard scale.

date.description: Title block date text, e.g. "2026-03-14". Printed as given.

entityIds.description: Ids of the 3D solids to draw. Omit to draw every visible 3D solid of the document (the usual choice).

name.description: Sheet name, e.g. "Bracket". Default "Sheet N".

title.description: Title block title. Default: the sheet name.

views.description: Standard projection views to create now, e.g. ["front","top","right"] or ["front","top","right","iso"].

name: create_sheet

description: Define a sheet-metal rule: material/temper label, thickness T, default inside radius R and the K-factor (one dimensionless kFactor, or a kTable of r/T -> K rows with a source; interpolated linearly in r/T and clamped at both ends). All lengths are in the document length unit. Nothing is defaulted: kFactor/kTable and insideRadius must be given (refusal FTR_K_FACTOR_MISSING / FTR_K_FACTOR_OUT_OF_RANGE: ANSI 0 < K <= 0.5, DIN 0 < K <= 1, DIN K = 2 x ANSI K). Design-rule thresholds (hole-to-bend, hole-to-edge, minimum flange, minimum land, depth ratio) are optional and each needs a source; check_sheet_metal reports the ones that are missing. A table, threshold or radius row marked 'unverified' (the default) flags every result computed from it. Next: import_bend_radius_table, then add_sheet_metal_base.

allowSharpBends.description: Allow inside radius 0 (default false: add_flange refuses R = 0, FTR_SHARP_BEND_FORBIDDEN).

insideRadius.description: Default inside bend radius R in the document length unit; >= 0 (0 is a sharp bend, forbidden unless allowSharpBends).

kFactor.description: Single K-factor (dimensionless, neutral-axis offset / T). ANSI 0 < K <= 0.5; DIN 0 < K <= 1. Give this OR kTable.

kFactorStandard.description: Convention of kFactor / kTable K values (dimensionless): 'ansi' (default) or 'din' (K_din = 2 x K_ansi, converted when used).

kTable.description: K-factor table (dimensionless K versus r/T). Give this OR kFactor.

source.description: Where the table comes from (mandatory).

material.description: Material label (e.g. 2024); with temper it selects the minimum-radius row. Text, no unit.

name.description: Unique rule name, referenced by add_sheet_metal_base (e.g. "AL2024-T3 1.6").

relief.description: Relief the check expects where a bend ends at a free edge.

depthExtra.description: Extra relief depth beyond R + T in the document length unit; omitted = 0 (reported as a named default).

type.description: Relief shape asked for at free bend ends.

widthRatio.description: Relief width as a multiple of thickness T (dimensionless).

temper.description: Temper label (e.g. T3). Without it no radius-table row can match. Text, no unit.

thickness.description: Sheet thickness T in the document length unit; must be > 0.

thresholds.description: Sourced design-rule thresholds, one entry per rule kind; absent ones are reported by check_sheet_metal, never assumed.

kind.description: Which design rule: holeToBend (hole edge to bend tangent, document length unit), holeToEdge (hole edge to part edge, document length unit), minFlange (flange flat length, document length unit), minLand (countersink land, document length unit) or maxDepthRatio (hole depth / diameter, dimensionless).

source.description: Where the value comes from (standard, handbook or company rule with edition); mandatory.

value.description: Threshold value in the document length unit (ratio for maxDepthRatio); >= 0.

verification.description: 'verified' only after dual-review transcription from the cited source; default 'unverified'.

name: create_sheet_metal_rule

description: Create a named sketch plane: a world plane (plane: "xy" | "xz" | "yz") or a planar FACE of a solid (face: { id, faceIndex | faceNear | faceName }), moved offset along its normal and turned spin degrees about it. Place 2D entities on it with place_on_sketch_plane, project solid edges into it with project_edges_to_sketch. A face plane follows the face (by its persistent name) when the model regenerates. Returns data { id, frame }.

id.description: Id of the 3D solid that carries the face.

faceNames.description: Persistent name of the face (recorded automatically from the first pick; wins over face.faceIndex / faceNear on regeneration).

name.description: Display name. Default "Plane N".

offset.description: Distance along the plane normal, document units. Default 0.

plane.description: World base plane (xz faces -Y, yz faces +X). Give plane OR face.

description: Build an existing-ground terrain surface (Delaunay TIN) from survey point groups and/or extra [x, y, z] points, with minor and major contours (labelled with elevations in m). Optional plan `boundary` clips the TIN; `maxEdgeLength` drops long hull triangles on concave sites. Defaults: every point group, 1 m contour interval, every 5th contour major.

items.description: Boundary vertex [x, y].

majorEvery.description: Every n-th contour is major. Default 5.

maxEdgeLength.description: Drop triangles with a longer plan edge (> 0).

name.description: Surface name. Default "EG <n>" (existing ground).

pointGroupIds.description: Point groups to triangulate. Default: every point group.

name: create_surface

description: Create a topology optimization study on an existing analysis (create_analysis + set_part_idealization + add_fea_constraint + add_fea_load; force, pressure and gravity loads) and return the study id in affected[0]. `voxel` is the grid spacing in document length units (e.g. 1 for 1 mm voxels); `volumeFraction` is the share of the design domain that may stay solid (0.7 = 30 % lighter). `designDomain` lists solids that are parts of the analysis and share one material (E, nu and, for gravity, the density come from it). A 2D study (dimension 2) optimises a plane-stress layout on the grid of one plane (default XY) across the thickness of the domain; a 3D study uses voxels. The objective is min_compliance (default) or min_volume under a compliance limit (optimizer mma). Every setting starts at a named default (see the summary; change them with set_topology_settings: optimizer, projection, manufacturing constraints). Refuses non-solids and grids above the voxel cap. Next: set_topology_regions to protect bosses and interfaces, then run the topology_solve transport (it stores the result with record_topology_result), then topology_report, suggest_rebuild, compare_to_topology and check_topology.

analysisId.description: Id of the analysis (affected[0] of create_analysis, e.g. an-1.1).

designDomain.description: Ids of the 3D solids that may be reshaped. They must be parts of the analysis and share one material.

dimension.description: 2 = plane-stress layout on one plane (needs a plate-like domain); 3 = voxel solid.

name.description: Display name of the study, e.g. "bracket 30 % lighter".

description: Create a lofted wing from airfoil sections (airfoil_from_naca / import_airfoil ids). Wing frame: x aft along the root chord, y to the right (span), z up; lengths in document units. `sections` (2..40, `span` strictly increasing from the root) each give the `airfoilId`, `twistDeg` (nose-up, washout negative, about the chord fraction `twistLocation`, default 0.25) and `chord`. Instead of chords give a `planform`: exactly 3 independent values among semiSpan, rootChord, tipChord, taper, area, aspectRatio (area / aspectRatio refer to the complete two-sided wing) fix a trapezoid whose chord is interpolated linearly along the sections; its sweepDeg / sweepLocation / dihedralDeg apply to every panel unless `segments` (one per span interval: sweepDeg measured at chord fraction sweepLocation, dihedralDeg) says otherwise. The sections are lofted exactly (not resampled) with the trailing edge kept as an edge: `loft` "linear" (default, straight between sections, exact trapezoid) or "smooth". `mirror` adds the left half as a second solid. Every airfoil of a wing needs the same `points` count and trailing-edge type. The result lists the solids (right half first, then the left half): the wing id is the id of the right-half solid, so it also works with mass_properties, boolean and export_*; the exact kernel gets the sections unchanged. Next: wing_properties, mass_properties.

description: Cut a mesh (or the triangles of any 3D solid) with a plane and keep the positive side (the side the normal points to), the negative side, or both. Triangles are clipped exactly, so it works on open and dirty meshes and needs no B-rep kernel. `cap` (default true for a closed mesh) closes every section loop with a planar fill that respects holes (a hollowed shell gets a ring); the result of a closed mesh is closed and wound outward. keep "both" rewrites `id` as the positive half and adds the negative half as a new mesh (positive first). Reports data.volumes {positive, negative} (document units^3, closed results), capArea (units^2), section loops and the ids. Reference: the unit cube cut by x + y + z = 1.5 (normal [1,1,1]) keeps 0.5 below the plane with a hexagonal cap of area 1.299. Refusals: MESH_ENTITY_NOT_FOUND, MESH_NOT_A_MESH, MESH_PARAM_INVALID, MESH_CUT_MISSES.

description: Reduce the triangle count of a mesh (or the triangles of any 3D solid) by quadric-error edge collapse (Garland-Heckbert 1997). Give a stop rule: `targetTriangles`, or `ratio` (fraction of the triangles to keep, 0..1), and / or `maxDeviation` (document units): collapses that would move the surface farther than this from the original, in either direction, are rejected, so the result stays within it (re-measured and returned as data.deviation {forwardMax, backwardMax, hausdorff, mean, rms}). With only a target the quadric error decides what is lost: flat regions collapse first at zero cost. Boundary vertices are locked unless preserveBoundary is false (then a penalty keeps the boundary shape); preserveFeatureAngleDeg keeps edges sharper than that angle; lockedRegion freezes every vertex inside a sphere. When the deviation bound or the locked boundary stops the reduction first, the result is still applied and data.reachedTarget is false with a warning MESH_TARGET_UNREACHABLE; requireTarget true refuses instead. Needs a manifold, consistently wound mesh without degenerate faces (repair_mesh first). Reports trianglesBefore / trianglesAfter, collapses and the rejections by reason. Lengths in document units. Refusals: MESH_ENTITY_NOT_FOUND, MESH_NOT_A_MESH, MESH_PARAM_INVALID, MESH_NON_MANIFOLD, MESH_ORIENTATION_INCONSISTENT, MESH_DEGENERATE, MESH_TARGET_UNREACHABLE.

binding.description: What the variable stands for. Default { kind: "free" }.

citation.description: Source of the scatter. Strongly recommended: without it results carry PRB_SCATTER_UNSOURCED and unverified: true.

locator.description: Optional page, table or clause inside the source.

text.description: What the scatter is based on: test report, specification, tolerance drawing, handbook.

kind.description: Normal distribution N(mean, sd).

sd.description: Standard deviation, in the variable unit; must be > 0.

kind.description: Lognormal distribution given by its own mean and standard deviation (not those of ln X).

mean.description: Mean of X, in the variable unit; must be > 0.

sd.description: Standard deviation of X, in the variable unit; must be > 0.

kind.description: Uniform distribution on [min, max].
Two-parameter Weibull distribution (F = 1 - exp(-(x/scale)^shape), x >= 0).

scale.description: Scale parameter lambda, in the variable unit; must be > 0.

kind.description: Gumbel (type I largest-value) distribution, F = exp(-exp(-(x - location) / scale)).

scale.description: Scale parameter beta, in the variable unit; must be > 0.

name.description: Symbol of the variable: letters, digits and underscores, not starting with a digit (e.g. "R", "yield_strength").

unit.description: Unit of the variable's values, e.g. 'MPa', 'mm', '1'. Recorded for reports; values are not converted.

name: define_random_variable

description: Define a rosette: the reference frame that gives every ply angle its 0-degree direction. origin is a point [x, y, z] in document units, axis0 the 0-degree fibre direction and normal the laminate normal (both direction vectors, any length). axis0 is projected perpendicular to the normal. method "translational" (default) projects axis0 onto a plane tool face (the part frame x axis); "cylindrical" and "radial" measure 0 degrees along the axis / meridian of a cylinder or cone tool face (give `axis` for cylindrical); "edge" is reserved. Ply angles are degrees counter-clockwise about the face normal. Returns the rosette id; use it (or its name) in create_composite_part. Refused: zero vectors, axis0 parallel to the normal.

axis.description: Cylinder / cone axis [x, y, z] for method "cylindrical".

name.description: Unique rosette name, e.g. "R0".

normal.description: Laminate normal [x, y, z] (any non-zero length).

origin.description: Rosette origin [x, y, z] in document units; the part frame origin is its projection on the tool face.

name: define_rosette

description: Define a time history (s, value) for PHY-09 dynamics: an input to shock_response_spectrum by name, and (V1) to transient cases. unit: factor | N | N*mm | mm | g. Times strictly increasing, values finite, source { citation }. Fatigue and crack-growth load histories (id-keyed series or blocks of cycles, stress / load_factor / strain) are a different record: use define_load_history.

name.description: Unique name: 1-40 characters of a-z, 0-9 and _.

source.description: Where the history comes from (measurement, test specification).

citation.description: Where the values come from (standard, test specification, measurement); never empty.

grade.description: Source grade; anything but A leaves the entry unverified.

timeS.description: Sample times in s, strictly increasing.

unit.description: Unit of the values.

values.description: Sample values, same length as timeS.

name: define_time_history

description: Define a base-acceleration spectral density (ASD) for random_response cases and quick checks: either points [[fHz, level], ...] with unit g2/Hz (default; g = 9.80665 m/s^2) or (m/s2)2/Hz and source { citation, grade? }, or library 'gevs_component_qual' / 'gevs_component_accept' (GSFC-STD-7000B component levels as quoted by secondary sources: grade B, so every result driven by them is unverified until the standard is read). Levels are interpolated log-log between breakpoints. Returns the overall grms (exact segment integral).

library.description: Copy a sourced library spectrum instead of points.

name.description: Unique name: 1-40 characters of a-z, 0-9 and _.

points.description: Breakpoints [[fHz, level], ...], at least 2, strictly increasing fHz > 0, level > 0.

source.description: Required with points: where the breakpoints come from.

citation.description: Where the values come from (standard, test specification, measurement); never empty.

grade.description: Source grade; anything but A leaves the entry unverified.

unit.description: Unit of the levels; default g2/Hz.

name: define_vibration_spectrum

description: Define a laminate zone of a composite part: a closed polygon in the part frame (the developed tool-face frame, document units) with a stacking string listed bottom (tool side) to top, e.g. "[45/-45/0/90]s" (+-a pairs, a_n repeats, (group)_n, trailing s symmetric, Ns, T total, ~ unduplicated middle ply). `priority` orders overlapping zones (higher wins where zones overlap; the thickest nested zone normally has the highest). The boundary must be a simple polygon inside the part outline. Zones do not create plies: run generate_plies_from_zones. Returns the zone id and its expanded angles. Refused: unparsable stack (the token is named), boundary self-intersecting or outside the face.

boundary.description: Zone polygon in the part frame (the developed face frame, document units), at least 3 vertices, simple.

items.description: A vertex [x, y] in the part frame (document units).

laminate.description: Stacking string, bottom to top, e.g. "[0/+-45/90]s".

name.description: Zone name, unique in the part.

name: define_zone

description: Push the material of a 3D solid or mesh around a point: every point within radius of `point` moves along `direction` by distance x falloff(r), where r = (distance from `point`) / radius and the falloff is 1 at the point and 0 at and beyond radius (smooth_c2 = (1 - r^2)^3, curvature-continuous, the default; cubic = 1 - 3r^2 + 2r^3). Use it for local bumps, dents and fit adjustments. distance is signed (document units, positive moves along direction), radius is the support (document units); the push is a smooth space map, so a bump on a face rises and the material around it follows. The push folds the body once |distance| reaches radius / max|falloff slope| (smooth_c2: 0.5823 x radius; cubic: 0.6667 x radius): the call is then refused with the limit (DEF_FOLDOVER). Pushing along the normal of a flat face whose full disk of radius lies on the face changes the volume by distance x pi x radius^2 / 4. The result replaces the entity as a mesh entity that keeps the construction (brep recipe). Refuses distance 0 (DEF_NO_EFFECT), a non-positive radius (DEF_REGION_INVALID), a zero direction (DEF_FRAME_DEGENERATE) and a point whose support sphere misses the body (DEF_REGION_MISSES_BODY). Then call analyze_deformation and check_deformation.

direction.description: Direction of the push, unitless; any non-zero vector (normalised). For a bump on a face use its outward normal.

distance.description: Displacement at the centre along direction, document units; negative pushes the other way. Must be below the fold limit (see the description).

falloff.description: Profile of the push: "smooth_c2" (default, (1 - r^2)^3, C2 at the support boundary) or "cubic" (1 - 3r^2 + 2r^3, C1).

id.description: Id of the 3D solid or mesh entity to deform (describe_scene lists ids). It is replaced by the deformed mesh entity (keepSource keeps it).

ids.description: Ids of several 3D solids or meshes to deform with the same parameters (one feature step; every body gets its own frame and region defaults from its own bounds). Use this or id.

keepSource.description: true: keep the original entity(ies) next to the deformed one(s) instead of replacing them. Default false.

output.description: How the result is computed: kernel choice and mesh tolerance.

mode.description: "auto" (default): the exact kernel builds the result when it can evaluate this deformation (the native kernel does for every law: the faces become B-splines fitted within output.tolerance), else the mesh path runs and the summary says so; "exact": refuse (DEF_EXACT_UNAVAILABLE) unless the exact kernel built it; "mesh": force the faceted mesh path.

preserveAnalytic.description: Recognise cylinders, cones and planes in an exact result (needs the exact warp of a later milestone; true is refused today).

tolerance.description: Largest deviation of the result from the true deformed surface, document units, > 0: the chordal deviation of the mesh path, or the fit error of the B-spline faces and edges on the exact path (a smaller value costs control points, not accuracy). Default: 1e-5 times the body bounding-box diagonal, clamped to [1e-6, 0.01].

point.description: Centre of the push, a world point in document units (the displacement is largest here).

radius.description: Radius of the support sphere, document units, > 0: nothing moves at or beyond this distance from the point.

name: deform_by_point

description: Deform a 3D solid or mesh by dragging curves: each pair names an initial nurbs_curve (lying on or near the body) and the target nurbs_curve it must land on. The curves are sampled at equal fractions of their arc length (samples per curve), and a smooth displacement field (a triharmonic spline, C2, no folds for moderate moves) that carries the initial samples onto the target samples is applied to the whole body. A pair without targetId keeps its curve where it is (a constraint that holds a part of the body still), and fixedPoints hold single points. stiffness 0..1 relaxes the fit (0: the curves land exactly; larger: a stiffer body that only approaches the targets). data.landing reports the largest distance, document units, between the mapped initial curve and its target (checked between the samples), refused above landingTolerance (default 1 percent of the size of the constraints). The result replaces the entity as a mesh entity that keeps the construction (brep recipe). Refuses a missing or non-curve entity in a pair (DEF_CURVE_PAIR_INVALID), a residual above the tolerance (DEF_APPROX_TOLERANCE: more samples or a lower stiffness) and a field that folds the body (DEF_FOLDOVER). Then call analyze_deformation and check_deformation.

fixedPoints.description: Points of the body held still. Default none.

items.description: A world point that must not move, document units.

id.description: Id of the 3D solid or mesh entity to deform (describe_scene lists ids). It is replaced by the deformed mesh entity (keepSource keeps it).

ids.description: Ids of several 3D solids or meshes to deform with the same parameters (one feature step; every body gets its own frame and region defaults from its own bounds). Use this or id.

keepSource.description: true: keep the original entity(ies) next to the deformed one(s) instead of replacing them. Default false.

landingTolerance.description: Largest accepted distance between a mapped initial curve and its target, document units, > 0. Default: 1 percent of the diagonal of the constraint points.

output.description: How the result is computed: kernel choice and mesh tolerance.

mode.description: "auto" (default): the exact kernel builds the result when it can evaluate this deformation (the native kernel does for every law: the faces become B-splines fitted within output.tolerance), else the mesh path runs and the summary says so; "exact": refuse (DEF_EXACT_UNAVAILABLE) unless the exact kernel built it; "mesh": force the faceted mesh path.

preserveAnalytic.description: Recognise cylinders, cones and planes in an exact result (needs the exact warp of a later milestone; true is refused today).

tolerance.description: Largest deviation of the result from the true deformed surface, document units, > 0: the chordal deviation of the mesh path, or the fit error of the B-spline faces and edges on the exact path (a smaller value costs control points, not accuracy). Default: 1e-5 times the body bounding-box diagonal, clamped to [1e-6, 0.01].

pairs.description: Curve pairs; each initial curve is carried onto its target (matching points by arc-length fraction, so give them the same direction).

initialId.description: Id of the nurbs_curve to move (on or near the body).

targetId.description: Id of the nurbs_curve it must land on. Omit to hold the initial curve in place.

samples.description: Samples per curve, integer 4..200 (default 24); more samples follow wiggly curves closer.

stiffness.description: Relaxation of the fit, 0..1: 0 lands the curves exactly (default); larger values give a stiffer, smoother field.

name: deform_curve_to_curve

description: Free-form deformation of a 3D solid or mesh: a regular lattice of control points (degrees [l, m, n], l + 1 by m + 1 by n + 1 points, 1..8 per axis) fills a box in the frame; moving control points bends the space inside the box smoothly (Bernstein polynomials, Sederberg & Parry 1986) and the body with it. Use it for bottles, grips, organic bulges, cambered shapes. Control point (i, j, k) sits at box.min + (i / l, j / m, k / n) x box size; moves name it by index [i, j, k] or by near (a world point: the nearest control point of the undisplaced lattice) and give delta, a displacement in frame coordinates (document units). Without box the lattice fills the body bounds. Frame default: the world axes at the origin, so box and delta are in world coordinates. With no moves nothing changes; moving all points by one affine map applies that map exactly. Points outside the box do not move, so the layers of control points next to a box face that the body crosses are fixed (fixedLayers, default 1) to keep the body continuous. Higher degrees give local control but need more moves. The result replaces the entity as a mesh entity that keeps the construction (brep recipe). Refuses a degree outside 1..8 (DEF_LATTICE_DEGREE), an index outside the net (DEF_LATTICE_INDEX), a move of a fixed layer (DEF_LATTICE_FIXED_MOVED), a lattice that folds the body (DEF_FOLDOVER: det J <= 0; reduce the moves) and a box that misses the body (DEF_REGION_MISSES_BODY). Then call analyze_deformation (det J range and its Bernstein bound) and check_deformation.

max.description: Lattice box corner with the largest coordinates, frame coordinates, document units; every component must exceed min.

min.description: Lattice box corner with the smallest coordinates, frame coordinates, document units.

box.description: Box the lattice fills, in frame coordinates: {min, max}, or "bounds" (default) for the body bounds in the frame plus a margin of 1e-6 of the diagonal.

degrees.description: Lattice degrees [l, m, n] along the frame x, y, z axes, integers 1..8 (the lattice has (l + 1)(m + 1)(n + 1) control points).

fixedLayers.description: Layers of control points next to each box face the body crosses that must stay put, integer >= 0 (default 1: continuous; 2: tangent-continuous). Faces the body does not reach are free.

frame.description: Frame the box, moves and deltas are expressed in; default the world axes.

axis.description: Frame z axis, unitless (normalised). Default [0, 0, 1].

origin.description: Frame origin, a world point in document units. Default [0, 0, 0].

reference.description: Direction giving the frame x axis, unitless; must not be parallel to axis. Default: the first world axis not parallel to axis.

id.description: Id of the 3D solid or mesh entity to deform (describe_scene lists ids). It is replaced by the deformed mesh entity (keepSource keeps it).

ids.description: Ids of several 3D solids or meshes to deform with the same parameters (one feature step; every body gets its own frame and region defaults from its own bounds). Use this or id.

keepSource.description: true: keep the original entity(ies) next to the deformed one(s) instead of replacing them. Default false.

moves.description: Control point displacements; several moves of one point add up. Default: none (no change).

delta.description: Displacement added to the control point, frame coordinates, document units.

index.description: Control point [i, j, k] to move, integers 0..l, 0..m, 0..n. Give index or near, not both.

near.description: World point: the control point nearest to it (in the undisplaced lattice) is moved. Give index or near, not both.

output.description: How the result is computed: kernel choice and mesh tolerance.

mode.description: "auto" (default): the exact kernel builds the result when it can evaluate this deformation (the native kernel does for every law: the faces become B-splines fitted within output.tolerance), else the mesh path runs and the summary says so; "exact": refuse (DEF_EXACT_UNAVAILABLE) unless the exact kernel built it; "mesh": force the faceted mesh path.

preserveAnalytic.description: Recognise cylinders, cones and planes in an exact result (needs the exact warp of a later milestone; true is refused today).

tolerance.description: Largest deviation of the result from the true deformed surface, document units, > 0: the chordal deviation of the mesh path, or the fit error of the B-spline faces and edges on the exact path (a smaller value costs control points, not accuracy). Default: 1e-5 times the body bounding-box diagonal, clamped to [1e-6, 0.01].

name: deform_lattice

description: Delete an analysis case with all its parts, constraints, loads, mesh controls, probes and recorded mesh/result summaries. Refused while another analysis reads its results as a temperature field. The geometry is untouched.

analysisId.description: Id of the analysis (affected[0] of create_analysis, e.g. an-1.1).

name: delete_analysis

description: Remove one set-up record from an analysis by its id: a constraint (fc-), load (fl-), result probe (pr-), thermal BC (tb-), thermal contact (tc-), temperature limit (tl-, also drops its dispositions), thermal amplitude (am-, refused while a thermal BC uses it), explicit contact (ct-), imposed motion (im-) or rigid wall (rw-). The id is affected[0] of the add_* / define_* command that created it (affected[1] for explicit records). Results become stale; the recorded mesh stays. To remove the whole analysis use delete_analysis.

analysisId.description: Id of the analysis (affected[0] of create_analysis, e.g. an-1.1).

itemId.description: Id of the record to remove (fc-, fl-, pr-, tb-, tc-, tl-, am-, ct-, im- or rw- prefix, e.g. fl-3.1).

name: delete_analysis_item

description: Delete building elements by element id; use this instead of delete_entities for anything in the building model, because it cascades to hosted and dependent elements and re-trims joins (delete_entities would leave orphan building data) (walls, doors, windows, slabs, columns, beams, stairs, rooms, grid axes). Deleting a wall also deletes its doors and windows; joined walls are re-trimmed. Deleting a steel member re-attaches the pipe supports bearing on it to the nearest steel in reach, or leaves them unattached (the summary says which).
name: delete_building_element

description: Delete faces of a subdivision cage, leaving a hole: the cage becomes an open surface whose boundary edges stay infinitely sharp (a bowl, a sheet, an opening to bridge or to shape). Faces are ids ("f-1.2") or indices; vertices that no face uses disappear, every other element keeps its id; a symmetric cage deletes the mirror faces too. `boundary` picks the corner rule of the open cage (default "edge_and_corner"). An open cage has no volume (mass_properties refuses it); close it again with fill_cage_hole or join two holes with bridge_cage_faces. Refuses deleting every face (DIR_CAGE_EMPTY) and a deletion that pinches the surface at a vertex (DIR_CAGE_INVALID). Returns data { vertexCount, faceCount, vertices, vertexIds, faceIds, removedFaces, removedVertices, boundaryLoops }. Next: fill_cage_hole, bridge_cage_faces, check_subdivision.

boundary.description: Corner rule of the open cage: "edge_and_corner" (default; corners of a single face stay pinned) or "edge_only" (corners stay smooth).

faces.description: Faces to delete, as ids or indices.

items.description: A cage face: element id ("f-1.2", stable across topology edits) or current index.

id.description: Id of the subdivision solid.

name: delete_cage_faces

description: Delete a flow case and its recorded result summary from the document. The bodies (entities) are not touched.

caseId.description: Id of the case to delete.

name: delete_cfd_case

description: Delete a civil object by civil id (use this instead of delete_entities, which would leave the civil model pointing at removed geometry) (point group, surface, platform, alignment, manhole or pipe) and its generated geometry. Refused when other objects reference it unless `cascade` is true, which deletes those dependents too (e.g. the pipes of a manhole).

cascade.description: Also delete dependent objects. Default false.

id.description: Civil object id, e.g. "manhole-2".

name: delete_civil_object

description: Delete a colour profile (deactivates it when it was active). Error: VIS_PROFILE_NOT_FOUND. Does not add a feature step.
name: delete_colour_profile

id.description: Id of the constraint to remove. Must match an existing constraint id exactly. Use describe_scene or list the document constraints to find valid ids.

name: delete_constraint

description: Remove a contact set by id. Joints and instances are untouched.

id.description: Id of the contact set to remove.

name: delete_contact_set

name: delete_crack

description: Delete a crack-growth case (its crack and histories stay).
name: delete_crack_growth_case

decalId.description: Id of the decal to remove.

name: delete_decal

viewId.description: Id of the view to remove.

name: delete_drawing_view

id.description: Id of the drive relation to remove. Must match an existing entry in doc.driveRelations.

name: delete_drive_relation

description: Remove a rigid body, joint, gear coupling, motor, propeller, cylinder pressure or point spring (add_spring) from the physics model by id. Cascades: a body takes its joints and springs with it; a joint takes the gears, motors, propellers, cylinder pressures and engine losses (set_engine_losses) on it. Entities (geometry) are never deleted.

id.description: Id of the body / joint / gear / motor / propeller / cylinder / spring to remove.

ids.description: Entity ids to delete (non-empty, at most 10000). Missing ids are skipped.

name: delete_entities

description: Remove an exploded view by id (switches the explosion off if it was showing). Parts are untouched.

id.description: Exploded view id.

name: delete_exploded_view

description: Delete faces of a B-rep and heal the gap (defeaturing): a fillet or chamfer disappears and the edge is sharp again, a hole is filled, a boss or pocket vanishes - the neighbouring faces extend until they meet. Pick ALL faces of the feature (a fillet chain, a hole wall and its countersink) by faceIndices, facesNear or faceNames. Exact B-rep only (native OCC kernel; inputs must be solids); the source is consumed and the result must be one valid solid. Returns data { volumeBefore, volumeAfter, volumeUnit, faces }. Refuses what OCC cannot heal (DIR_DEFEATURE_FAILED, e.g. an unclosed gap or a face that has no neighbours to extend). Next: mass_properties, inspect_topology, move_faces.

faceNames.description: Persistent face names (inspect_topology on the native kernel): recorded automatically from the first pick and used on regeneration; a name that is gone or split refuses the step (REF_LOST / REF_SPLIT).

facesNear.description: Faces picked by location: each point takes the face nearest to it.

items.description: A point [x, y, z] on the face (its nearest face is taken).

id.description: Id of the 3D solid.

name: delete_faces

description: Delete fastener stacks by id: removes the stack record and its bolt/pin/rivet, washer and nut instances. The holes cut in the plates stay (undo restores them). stackIds.description: Ids of the stacks to delete (fst-…), as returned by insert_fastener_stack in data.stackId.

name: delete_fastener_stack

description: Delete a fatigue case (its histories and curves stay).
name: delete_fatigue_case

description: Delete an implicit field node. It is refused while another field node or an implicit body reads it (IMP_FIELD_IN_USE lists the referrers); with cascade true the node, every node that reads it and every body that depends on it are removed together (the body meshes leave the document; solids hidden by create_implicit_body hideSource stay on their hidden layer). description: Remove a named parameter from the document. The parameter record is deleted; any other parameters whose expressions reference this name are re-evaluated and will have their error field set to "unknown parameter: <name>" until they are updated. If the parameter does not exist, the document is left unchanged.

name.description: Name of the parameter to delete. Must match an existing parameter name exactly (case-sensitive). Example: "width", "wall_thickness".

name: delete_parameter

The pipe line and the ports stay. Deleting a branch run removes its branch point from the header, which is re-cut without the tee (an olet is removed). Refusals: RTE_UNKNOWN_RUN; RTE_HAS_BRANCHES when another run is attached to it (a branch, or a run that starts or ends at one of its ends): delete those first (ids in the result) or pass cascade: true to delete them with it. The pipe supports of the deleted runs (add_pipe_support runId) are deleted with them and listed in the summary (data.deletedSupports).

runId.description: Pipe run id (affected[0] of route_pipe / auto_route_pipe / add_branch).

name: delete_ply

description: Delete one PMI item by id. Deleting a size dimension also deletes the feature control frames that target it, and an upper composite frame its lower segments; the removed ids are listed in affected. A datum feature still referenced by frames or datum targets is refused (GDT_DATUM_REFERENCED) unless cascade is true, which deletes the referrers as well. Saved views drop the removed ids.

cascade.description: true = also delete the frames / targets that reference a datum being deleted. Default false.

pmiId.description: Id of the PMI item to delete.

name: delete_pmi

description: Remove one property model from a material. Refused while another model of the material is a ratioOf of it, or a material law reads it (PROP_MODEL_IN_USE).

modelId.description: Id of the model to remove.

description: Size and design the reinforced-concrete pad footings under the portal-frame columns of a level to EN 1992-1-1 (C25/30, B500) and store the plan size, thickness and bottom reinforcement on each footing, using the same base reactions, loads and soil parameters as check_foundations (deadLoad / snowLoad / windPressure / craneCapacity, soilBearing, thrustTie, soilModulus, clayLayer). Essential for fixed column bases (columnBase "fixed"), whose default pads are far too small. Sizing: plan B × L keeps the existing aspect ratio (square for the default pads) in 100 mm steps from the plate / column footprint + 2 × 100 mm up to 6 m, thickness h 300–1500 mm in 50 mm steps; the smallest concrete volume (ties: wider plan first) that passes ALL of: the check_foundations footing rows (soil bearing with eccentricity incl. base moments, overturning, uplift EQU, sliding, settlement, evaluated with the founding level dropping as h grows, topOffset kept) AND the reinforced mat below. Pads that already pass are not shrunk (only grown) unless allowShrink is true. The top level (topOffset) stays fixed. Mat: ULS net soil pressure (no self-weight) from 1.35G + 1.5S / wind / crane combinations with load eccentricity (trapezoidal or triangular pressure); bending at the face of the base plate (else the column profile), d = h − 50 mm cover − φ, z ≤ 0.95d with K ≤ 0.167, As,min = 0.26 fctm/fyk b d; the lightest bar φ12/16/20/25 at 100–250 mm spacing (same both ways) satisfying As, one-way shear VRd,c at d from the face (§6.2.2, CRd,c 0.12) and punching at every control perimeter a ≤ 2d from the face (§6.4.4, vRd,c·2d/a) with the soil pressure inside it deducted (§6.4). If no size within 6 × 6 × 1.5 m passes, the footing is reported as failed and left unchanged (size and reinforcement). The summary lists the size changes (e.g. "F1 1500×1500×400 → 2600×2600×700"); the takeoff reports concrete and `footing.rebar.kg` for the new sizes. Simplifications: bending in the frame plane (x) from the horizontal reaction and, for fixed column bases, the base moment (eccentric pressure), uniform pressure across the other side, no uplift (tension) design, bar anchorage not checked. Preliminary design, not a substitute for a structural engineer.

allowShrink.description: true = also reduce oversized pads that already pass to the smallest passing size. Default false (pads are only grown, never shrunk).

clayLayer.description: Optional compressible clay layer under the pads, adds primary consolidation settlement to the settlement rows. topDepth: depth of the layer top below the founding level, m (>= 0). thickness: m (> 0). compressionIndex: Cc (> 0). recompressionIndex: Cr (> 0, <= Cc; default Cc/5, used only with preconsolidationPressure). voidRatio: e0 (> 0). unitWeight: bulk kN/m³ (> 9.81, default 19; groundwater assumed at the founding level; σ′0 = 18 kN/m³ × founding depth + γ′·z). preconsolidationPressure: σ′p in kPa (> 0; omit for normally consolidated clay). Required: topDepth, thickness, compressionIndex, voidRatio.

preconsolidationPressure.description: Preconsolidation pressure σ'p in kPa (> 0). Default: normally consolidated.

recompressionIndex.description: Recompression index Cr (> 0, <= Cc). Default Cc/5.

thickness.description: Layer thickness, m (> 0).

topDepth.description: Layer top below founding level, m (>= 0).

craneCapacity.description: Crane capacity in tonnes for every runway on the level. Default: read from the runways (add_crane_runway capacity); 0 = ignore cranes.

craneSelfWeight.description: Crane self-weight Gc in kN (> 0, bridge + trolley; trolley = 0.2 Gc). Default 0.5 Q + 20 kN.

deadLoad.description: Roof dead load (build-up, purlins, services), kN/m². Default 0.5.

hoistingClass.description: EN 1991-3 hoisting class for the dynamic factor φ2 = φ2,min + β2 vh (HC1 1.05 + 0.17 vh, HC2 1.10 + 0.34 vh, HC3 1.15 + 0.51 vh, HC4 1.20 + 0.68 vh). Default HC2.

hoistingSpeed.description: Hoisting speed vh in m/s (>= 0) for φ2. Default 0.1.

levelId.description: Level id. Default: the active level.

minHookApproach.description: Minimum approach of the hook to a rail in m (>= 0): the trolley position that maximises the wheel load. Default 1.0.

soilBearing.description: Allowable (SLS) soil bearing pressure in kPa. Default 150. Must be > 0.

soilModulus.description: Soil elastic (Young) modulus Es in MPa for the settlement rows. Default 20. Must be > 0.

thrustTie.description: true = the frame thrust is carried by a tie (ground slab cast around the columns or tie bars): each frame's columns share the frame's net horizontal reaction for the sliding check and one tie-force row per frame is added. false = every pad resists its own horizontal reaction by friction. Default true when the level has a slab element, else false.

wheelBase.description: Wheel base a of a crane rail wheel group (distance between its two wheels) in mm (> 0), used for the transverse drive force HT = φ5 ξ M / a. Default 3000.

windPressure.description: Peak velocity pressure qp, kN/m² (EN 1991-1-4; e.g. 0.6–1.0). Default 0 = wind not applied. Coefficients: walls cpe +0.8 / −0.5, roof −0.6 (monopitch roofs, EN 1991-1-4 Tab. 7.3a zone H: −0.6 with wind on the low eaves, −0.8 on the high eaves), each with internal pressure cpi +0.2 and −0.3.

name: design_footings

description: Create a rocket thrust-chamber nozzle as a CAD solid: the wall cross-section is revolved about +Z (throat at `position`, exhaust towards +Z). Contour (Huzel & Huang NASA SP-125 §4; Rao 1958): cylindrical chamber (`chamberLength`, radius R_t √contractionRatio), conical convergent (`convergentHalfAngleDeg`, default 30) into an upstream throat arc 1.5 R_t, a downstream throat arc 0.382 R_t, then `shape` conical (`halfAngleDeg`, default 15) or bell (Rao thrust-optimised parabola: `lengthFraction` of the 15° cone, default 0.8; angles θn / θe from the Huzel & Huang 80 % chart for ε 5-50 unless `entranceAngleDeg` / `exitAngleDeg` are given). Lengths in document units: `throatRadius`, `wallThickness`. Returns the lengths, radii and (with `includeContour`) the inner contour. Pair with nozzle_performance (same ε) for thrust and Isp; mass_properties for the wall mass.

chamberLength.description: Cylindrical chamber length before the convergent, document units, >= 0. Default 0.

color.description: Hex colour "#rrggbb" of the nozzle solid, e.g. "#b87333". Default: the revolve_profile colour.

contractionRatio.description: Chamber / throat area ratio ε_c, 1.5..20. Default 3 (flagged).

convergentHalfAngleDeg.description: Convergent cone half-angle in degrees, 15..60. Default 30.

entranceAngleDeg.description: bell: initial wall angle θn in degrees (default from the 80 % chart).

exitAngleDeg.description: bell: exit wall angle θe in degrees (default from the 80 % chart).

halfAngleDeg.description: conical: divergent half-angle in degrees, 5..30. Default 15.

includeContour.description: Return the inner wall contour points (axial, radius, angle) in data. Default false.

lengthFraction.description: bell: length as a fraction of the 15° cone, 0.6..1. Default 0.8.

position.description: Throat centre [x, y, z] in document units. Default origin. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

segments.description: Circumferential segments of the revolution, 16..256. Default 96.

throatRadius.description: Throat radius R_t in document units, > 0.

wallThickness.description: Wall thickness in document units, > 0 and < 0.382 R_t.

name: design_nozzle

description: Preliminary design of the portal frames of a level with the same loads, combinations and checks as check_portal_frames (strength, buckling, sway stability, SLS deflections): repeatedly analyses the frames and up-sizes the rafter / column sections that exceed targetUtilisation (uniformly for all frames) — strength / buckling failures to the next heavier profile of the same family, sway and stability failures (column-stiffness driven) by up-sizing the columns only to the section whose inertia the sway ratio asks for, with fixed column bases tried when pinned bases cannot pass (allowFixedBases) — then sizes the bolt groups of the moment connections (bolt diameter M20–M30 and rows) per connection type for every combination. Reports every change and the final utilisations.

allowFixedBases.description: Default true: when sway (crane h/400, wind h/150, αcr) governs the pinned-base design, it is repeated with the base plates of the frame columns set to 'fixed' (fixed bases make the columns up to ~4x stiffer against sway) and the fixed design is kept if it passes where pinned does not, or weighs under 75 % of it (the footings then carry base moments: run design_footings). False keeps the base fixity as modelled.

craneCapacity.description: Crane capacity in tonnes for every runway on the level. Default: read from the runways (add_crane_runway capacity); 0 = ignore cranes.

craneSelfWeight.description: Crane self-weight Gc in kN (> 0, bridge + trolley; trolley = 0.2 Gc). Default 0.5 Q + 20 kN.

deadLoad.description: Roof dead load (build-up, purlins, services), kN/m². Default 0.5.

hoistingClass.description: EN 1991-3 hoisting class for the dynamic factor φ2 = φ2,min + β2 vh (HC1 1.05 + 0.17 vh, HC2 1.10 + 0.34 vh, HC3 1.15 + 0.51 vh, HC4 1.20 + 0.68 vh). Default HC2.

hoistingSpeed.description: Hoisting speed vh in m/s (>= 0) for φ2. Default 0.1.

levelId.description: Level id. Default: the active level.

minHookApproach.description: Minimum approach of the hook to a rail in m (>= 0): the trolley position that maximises the wheel load. Default 1.0.

wheelBase.description: Wheel base a of a crane rail wheel group (distance between its two wheels) in mm (> 0), used for the transverse drive force HT = φ5 ξ M / a. Default 3000.

windPressure.description: Peak velocity pressure qp, kN/m² (EN 1991-1-4; e.g. 0.6–1.0). Default 0 = wind not applied. Coefficients: walls cpe +0.8 / −0.5, roof −0.6 (monopitch roofs, EN 1991-1-4 Tab. 7.3a zone H: −0.6 with wind on the low eaves, −0.8 on the high eaves), each with internal pressure cpi +0.2 and −0.3.

name: design_portal_frames

description: Preliminary design of the roof purlins and side rails of a level with the same loads and checks as check_purlins: repeatedly runs the check and up-sizes every purlin / rail profile (all members of that role and profile on the level, so rows stay uniform) whose utilisation exceeds targetUtilisation to the next heavier cold-formed C section, then to IPE when the C range is exhausted (at most 15 iterations). Deeper members are re-seated: a purlin moves along the rafter normal and a rail outwards from the column by half the depth change. Reports every change and the final maximum utilisation; no change returns the document untouched. Bracing eaves struts are not sized (see check_bracing).

levelId.description: Level id. Default: the active level.

roofDeadLoad.description: Roof build-up dead load carried by the purlins (sheeting, insulation, services) per m² of roof, kN/m², >= 0. Purlin self-weight is added automatically. Default 0.3.

snowLoad.description: Roof snow load on plan, kN/m², >= 0. Default 0.8.

windPressure.description: Peak velocity pressure qp, kN/m² (EN 1991-1-4, e.g. 0.6-1.0), >= 0. Default 0.6. 0 = no wind.
