description: Record a qualified person's disposition (accepted, rejected, redesign) of one fit_at_temperature row, identified by its rowKey. HUMAN-ONLY. It is recorded only when the signature verifies against the signing port; an agent without a human signature always gets TMC_HUMAN_GATE and the document is unchanged, so do not retry: hand the row to the reviewer. inputsHash is the hash of the fit inputs the reviewer saw; pass currentInputsHash (hash of the recomputed inputs) so a changed fit is refused with TMC_FIT_INPUTS_CHANGED.

currentInputsHash.description: Hash of the fit inputs as recomputed now; when it differs from inputsHash the call is refused.

fitParams.description: The params of the fit_at_temperature call that produced the row. The command re-runs it and requires sha256 of the row (JCS) to equal inputsHash, so a fit that changed is refused TMC_FIT_INPUTS_CHANGED.

inputsHash.description: Hash of the fit inputs the reviewer examined (stored with the disposition).

justification.description: Reviewer's reason for the decision (required, non-empty).

rowKey.description: rowKey of the fit_at_temperature row being dispositioned.

signature.description: Human signature object produced by the signing system over the payload hash; verified by the host.

name: dispose_fit_result

description: Record a qualified reviewer's decision (accepted | rejected | redesign) on a FAIL or MARGINAL row of compute_margins (rowId "r4"; pass the same criterion / allowable / groupBy / loadCases / marginalBand you used there so the row ids match). HUMAN GATE. Only a human-held signature over the row verifies (09 PLM signing port): an agent has none and always gets FEA_HUMAN_GATE with the document unchanged. Do not retry or work around it: hand the row over to the reviewer, who dispositions it in the desktop app. The decision never turns a FAIL into a PASS (the row reads "FAIL (accepted)", status stays FAIL, check_analysis keeps FEA_MS_NEGATIVE) and ends when the analysis is solved again.

against.description: Which check the explicit allowable is used for: ultimate (default) or yield (limit load cases only).

unit.description: Stress unit, e.g. "MPa", "psi", "ksi".

allowable.description: "ftu" (ultimate check), "fty" (yield check), or { value, unit, against? }. Omit for both checks from the material models.

analysisId.description: Id of the analysis (affected[0] of create_analysis, e.g. an-1.1).

criterion.description: Applied stress: von_mises (default) or the largest magnitude of the normal component s_xx, s_yy or s_zz.

groupBy.description: part (default): one row per part; target: per constraint / load node set and part.

loadCases.description: Load case names to include (default: all load cases of the analysis).

marginalBand.description: MS value below which a passing row is MARGINAL (>= 0, in MS units). No default: without it no row is marginal.

rowId.description: Row id of compute_margins, e.g. "r4" (a FAIL or MARGINAL row).

signature.description: Human signature object from the signing port. Agents cannot produce one.

singularityNote.description: Mandatory (non-empty) engineering justification when singularityRadius is given; echoed in the result data.

singularityRadius.description: Override of the singularity exclusion radius, in DOCUMENT length units (>= 0; 0 = exclude nothing). Default: 2 x the mesh globalSize (llull default, reported as defaulted). REQUIRES singularityNote.

name: dispose_margin

description: Record a qualified reviewer's decision (accepted | rejected | redesign) on a FAIL or MARGINAL row of check_temperature_limits (rowId "<limitId>:max|min"). HUMAN GATE. Only a human-held signature over the payload verifies (09 PLM signing port): an agent has none and gets THM_HUMAN_GATE with the document unchanged. Do not try to work around it: hand the row over to the reviewer, who dispositions it in the desktop app. The disposition binds to the results hash and ends when the case is solved again.

analysisId.description: Id of the analysis (affected[0] of create_analysis, e.g. an-1.1).

signature.description: Human signature object from the signing port. Agents cannot produce one.

name: dispose_thermal_limit

description: Distribute 2 or more entities evenly along a single axis. mode="equal-spacing" (default): center-to-center step is uniform. mode="equal-gap": gap between AABBs is uniform. The first and last entity (by their current position along the axis) are the anchors and are not moved; all entities in between are repositioned. Returns affected: the ids of the entities that actually moved.

axis.description: Axis along which to distribute: "x", "y", or "z".

mode.description: "equal-spacing" (default): equal center-to-center distance. "equal-gap": equal gap between entity bounding boxes.

targetIds.description: Ids of entities to distribute. Must contain at least 2 existing entity ids.

name: distribute

description: Compute the content hash of the document definition: SHA-256 (lowercase hex) of its canonical JSON (RFC 8785 key order) after dropping view state (selection, camera), the PLM record and plugin-derived geometry. Equal definitions hash equally whatever the key order; any edit of entities, history, parameters, materials, drawings... changes it. Returns data { sha256, bytes, canonicalJson? }. Read-only.

includeCanonical.description: Also return the exact canonical text that was hashed (large). Default false.

name: document_content_hash

description: Draft (taper) faces of a 3D solid for mould release: each picked face is tilted by angle degrees about its intersection with the neutral plane so the part opens along pull. Pick faces by faceIndices, facesNear or faceNames. The neutral plane defaults to the plane normal to pull through the lowest point of the solid (the parting line at the bottom). Exact B-rep only (native OCC kernel); the source is consumed.

angle.description: Draft angle in degrees, 0 < |angle| <= 89 (positive opens the part along pull).

faceNames.description: Persistent face names (inspect_topology on the native kernel): recorded automatically from the first pick and used on regeneration; a name that is gone or split refuses the step (REF_LOST / REF_SPLIT).

facesNear.description: Faces picked by location: each point takes the face nearest to it.

items.description: A point [x, y, z] on the face (its nearest face is taken).

id.description: Id of the 3D solid.

neutralPlane.description: A plane by a point and its normal.

normal.description: Plane normal [x, y, z] (any length > 0).

origin.description: A point [x, y, z] on the plane.

pull.description: Pull (mould opening) direction [x, y, z]. Default [0, 0, 1].

name: draft_faces

description: Read-only parasite (zero-lift) drag build-up of an aircraft or vehicle by components, CD0 = Σ Cf·FF·Q·S_wet / S_ref (Raymer §12.5): per component the Reynolds number on its reference length, flat-plate skin friction Cf (Raymer 12.26 laminar / 12.27 turbulent with the Mach correction, optional laminar fraction), the form factor FF (lifting surfaces: raymer with (x/c)_m and sweep, torenbeek or hoerner from t/c; bodies: torenbeek or hoerner from the fineness ratio l/d) and the interference factor Q (an input: default 1, flagged). Returns the table, CD0, the drag in N at the speed and the formulas with their sources. Wetted areas: frontal_area returns them from the model. Not modelled: roughness cutoff Reynolds number, wave drag, excrescences (add them to the result by hand).

altitudeM.description: Geometric altitude in m for the U.S. Standard Atmosphere 1976 (-5000..86000). Default 0 (sea level) unless densityKgM3 is given.

formFactorModel.description: Form-factor correlation. Default raymer (lifting) / torenbeek (body); raymer is for lifting surfaces only.

interferenceFactor.description: Interference factor Q >= 1 from a configuration source. Default 1 (flagged).

kind.description: lifting (wing, tail, strut, pylon) or body (fuselage, nacelle, pod).

laminarFraction.description: Laminar share of the reference length in [0, 1). Default 0 (fully turbulent).

maxThicknessX.description: lifting + raymer: chordwise position of maximum thickness (x/c)_m in (0, 1).

name.description: Component name, e.g. "wing", "fuselage".

referenceLengthM.description: Length for the Reynolds number in m, > 0: mean chord (lifting) or body length.

sweepDeg.description: lifting + raymer: sweep of the maximum-thickness line in degrees, |Λ| < 80. Default 0.

densityKgM3.description: Air density in kg/m³ (> 0) instead of the standard atmosphere, e.g. a measured value.

referenceAreaM2.description: Reference area S_ref in m² (usually the wing planform area), > 0.

speedUnit.description: Unit of speed: m/s (default), km/h, kn or mph.

temperatureOffsetK.description: ISA temperature deviation ΔT in K at the standard pressure (e.g. 15 for ISA+15). Default 0.

viscosityPaS.description: Dynamic viscosity in Pa·s with densityKgM3; default Sutherland at 288.15 K + temperatureOffsetK (1.7894e-5 Pa·s).

name: drag_buildup

description: Manhole and pipe schedules as CSV: ids, names, coordinates, rim and invert levels, depth, diameter, length, slope and material (metres). Returns data { manholeCsv, pipeCsv, csv }.
name: drainage_schedule

description: Kinematic (fishnet, Mack & Taylor) drape of a ply on its tool face: a pin-jointed net of inextensible tows of step `stepLength` seeded at the ply seed (drape.seed, default the pole of a sphere cap / the centre of a NURBS sheet) with two geodesic generators, the warp along the fibre direction and the weft across it, filled outward. Works on every tool face kind (plane, cylinder, cone, sphere cap, nurbs_surface sheet). Each node reports its shear, the absolute deviation of the tow crossing angle from 90 degrees. Returns the maximum shear and where, the number of nodes over the warning and the locking angle (material lockingAngle / warningShear or the params), the area of the cells over the lock and the over-lock regions (largest first, with centroid). A ply cut by darts or splices (split_ply) is draped piece by piece. Chart distances of a sphere cap and a NURBS sheet are not metric away from the centre: lengths here are measured on the surface. `output` "nodes" adds the net nodes (page with `offset`). Purely kinematic: no fabric mechanics, friction or tool contact. Read-only; the result is computed by llull and not approved.

lockingAngle.description: Locking (maximum) shear, degrees in (0, 90]; default the material lockingAngle (no built-in default exists).

offset.description: With output "nodes": first node index of the page (integer, default 0); pages hold 5000 nodes.

part.description: Part id or name; needed only when `ply` is a name.

stepLength.description: Fishnet cell size, document length units; default the ply drape.stepLength, else the outline diagonal / 200; must be > 0.

warningShear.description: Warning shear, degrees; default the material warningShear.

name: drape_ply

description: Draw a circular arc or a full circle in the local 2D work plane, defined by center and radius (and start/end angles in radians for an arc). Angles are measured counter-clockwise from the +X axis. radius must be > 0. The arc sweeps CCW from startAngle to endAngle (endAngle < startAngle wraps around CCW); a sweep larger than 2π is wrapped into (0, 2π] and the summary says so. OMIT BOTH startAngle and endAngle to draw a full circle (a `circle` entity, id circ-*); give both for an `arc` entity (id arc-*).

center.description: Center point [x, y] of the arc in local 2D work-plane coordinates.

color.description: Hex color string #rrggbb, e.g. "#c8553d". Defaults to "#4a90d9".

endAngle.description: End angle in radians, measured counter-clockwise from the +X axis. Arc sweeps from startAngle to endAngle counter-clockwise. Omit together with startAngle for a full circle.

position.description: World-space position [x, y, z] of the work-plane origin. Defaults to [0,0,0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

radius.description: Arc radius. Must be greater than 0.

startAngle.description: Start angle in radians, measured counter-clockwise from the +X axis. E.g. 0 = rightmost point. Omit together with endAngle for a full circle.

name: draw_arc

description: Compute the closed centerline of a belt or chain wrapping ≥2 circular pulleys/sprockets and emit it as a single closed polyline entity. For each adjacent pair of pulleys the command computes the external common tangent (open-belt / same-direction rotation convention, CCW outer envelope), then samples the wrap arc on each pulley between the two tangent touch-points. The result is one `polyline` with `closed: true`. pulleys is an ordered array of {center:[x,y], radius} objects; the belt wraps them in that order and closes back to the first. arcSamples controls chord resolution per wrap arc (default 12, minimum 2). position/rotation place the entity in 3D world space (default [0,0,0]). Fails gracefully (no-op) when: fewer than 2 pulleys, non-positive or non-finite radius, non-finite center coordinates, coincident centers, or any pulley is contained inside another (no external tangent exists).

arcSamples.description: Integer number of chord segments used to approximate each pulley wrap arc. Must be >= 2. Default 12. Higher values give smoother arcs.

color.description: Hex color string #rrggbb, e.g. "#c8553d". Defaults to "#4a90d9".

name.description: Optional display name for the entity (shown in the scene tree).

position.description: World-space position [x, y, z] of the work-plane origin. Defaults to [0,0,0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

pulleys.description: Ordered list of pulleys the belt wraps around. Each entry is an object { center: [x, y], radius: number } where center is a 2D point in the work plane and radius is a finite positive number. The belt wraps them in the given order and closes back to the first. Minimum 2 pulleys.

rotation.description: three.js intrinsic XYZ Euler angles in RADIANS [rx, ry, rz] (equivalent to rotating about world Z first, then world Y, then world X) for the work plane. Defaults to [0,0,0].

name: draw_belt_around

description: Draw an axis-aligned ellipse in the local 2D work plane, defined by center and semi-axis radii. radiusX is the half-width along the local X axis; radiusY is the half-height along the local Y axis. Both must be > 0. position places the work-plane origin in 3D space (default [0,0,0]).

center.description: Center point [x, y] of the ellipse in local 2D work-plane coordinates.

color.description: Hex color string #rrggbb, e.g. "#c8553d". Defaults to "#4a90d9".

position.description: World-space position [x, y, z] of the work-plane origin. Defaults to [0,0,0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

radiusX.description: Semi-axis length along the local X axis (half-width). Must be greater than 0.

radiusY.description: Semi-axis length along the local Y axis (half-height). Must be greater than 0.

name: draw_ellipse

description: Draw an open 2D involute curve sampled as a polyline in the local work plane. The involute of a circle: x(t) = baseRadius*(cos t + t*sin t), y(t) = baseRadius*(sin t − t*cos t). baseRadius is the base circle radius (must be > 0). startAngle and endAngle are the involute parameter t at the curve start and end (endAngle must be > startAngle). samples is the number of points on the curve (minimum 2; default 24). At t=0 the curve originates at (baseRadius, 0); radial distance from origin at t is baseRadius*sqrt(1+t²). The curve is open (not closed) and can be fed to other commands or used standalone as a reference curve. position is [x,y,z] world-space placement of the work-plane origin (default [0,0,0]). rotation is three.js intrinsic XYZ Euler angles in radians (about world Z, then Y, then X; default [0,0,0]).

baseRadius.description: Base circle radius of the involute. Must be > 0. Controls the curvature: smaller baseRadius gives a more tightly wound curve.

color.description: Hex color string #rrggbb, e.g. "#c8553d". Defaults to "#4a90d9".

endAngle.description: Involute parameter t at the end of the curve, in radians. Must be > startAngle. The radial distance from origin at the endpoint is baseRadius*sqrt(1 + endAngle²).

name.description: Optional display name for the entity (shown in the scene tree).

position.description: World-space position [x, y, z] of the work-plane origin. Defaults to [0,0,0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

rotation.description: three.js intrinsic XYZ Euler angles in RADIANS [rx, ry, rz] (equivalent to rotating about world Z first, then world Y, then world X) for the work plane. Defaults to [0,0,0].

samples.description: Number of points sampled along the curve (inclusive of both endpoints). Minimum 2. Default 24. Higher values give a smoother polyline.

startAngle.description: Involute parameter t at the start of the curve, in radians. Defaults to 0. At t=0 the curve starts at (baseRadius, 0). Must be < endAngle.

name: draw_involute

description: Place a point marker at the given 3D world position. The point entity has no local 2D geometry — its position is the point location.

color.description: Hex color string #rrggbb, e.g. "#c8553d". Defaults to "#4a90d9".

position.description: World-space position [x, y, z] of the point. Defaults to [0,0,0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

name: draw_point

description: Draw a connected sequence of line segments through an ordered list of 2D points in the local work plane. Requires at least 2 points. When closed=true the last point connects back to the first. An OPEN series of exactly 2 points is a single straight segment and creates a `line` entity (id line-*); any other series creates a `polyline` entity (id poly-*). A closed polyline can be fed to extrude_profile (id/ids) to become a 3D solid.

closed.description: When true, the last point connects back to the first point, forming a closed loop. Defaults to false.

color.description: Hex color string #rrggbb, e.g. "#c8553d". Defaults to "#4a90d9".

points.description: Ordered list of [x, y] vertices in local 2D work-plane coordinates. Minimum 2 points required.

position.description: World-space position [x, y, z] of the work-plane origin. Defaults to [0,0,0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

name: draw_polyline

description: Draw an axis-aligned rectangle in the local 2D work plane. The origin is at the lower-left corner; width extends along +X, height along +Y. position places the work-plane origin in 3D space. Both width and height must be > 0. Drawn on the XY plane (parallel to z = position[2]); a profile for add_sheet_cutout on a flange must lie in the flange plane, so for flanges give add_sheet_cutout circle/polygon world points instead.

color.description: Hex color string #rrggbb, e.g. "#c8553d". Defaults to "#4a90d9".

height.description: Height of the rectangle along the local Y axis. Must be greater than 0.

position.description: World-space position [x, y, z] of the work-plane origin (lower-left corner). Defaults to [0,0,0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

width.description: Width of the rectangle along the local X axis. Must be greater than 0.

name: draw_rectangle

description: Draw a Catmull-Rom interpolating spline through an ordered list of 2D through-points in the local work plane. The curve passes through every point (not a control polygon). Requires at least 2 points. When closed=true the spline loops back from the last point to the first. Centripetal Catmull-Rom parameterization is used; tessellation is performed by the renderer.

closed.description: When true, the spline loops back from the last point to the first, forming a closed curve. Defaults to false.

color.description: Hex color string #rrggbb, e.g. "#c8553d". Defaults to "#4a90d9".

points.description: Ordered list of through-points in local 2D work-plane coordinates. Each point is [x, y]. Minimum 2 points required.

position.description: World-space position [x, y, z] of the work-plane origin. Defaults to [0,0,0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

name: draw_spline

description: Draw a chain of joined walls through plan points ([[x, y], …]); closed: true adds the closing wall (e.g. a building perimeter); two points make one straight wall. Walls meeting at endpoints (L/T/X corners) are joined automatically; doors and windows are then hosted with add_door / add_window. A segment that duplicates an existing wall (same end points either way, same base offset, same level) is skipped and reported, so adjacent rooms can each be drawn as a closed loop sharing an edge; refused only if every segment is a duplicate.

baseOffset.description: Base offset above the level elevation, in document units. Default 0.

closed.description: Close the loop back to the first point. Default false.

height.description: Wall height above its base (document units, > 0). Default: the level height.

levelId.description: Level to place the wall on. Default: active level (a "Level 0" is created if none).

material.description: Material name used by quantities/cost: concrete (default), masonry, brick, block, timber, steel, gypsum…

points.description: Centerline vertices [[x, y], …], 2 to 500.

thickness.description: Wall thickness (document units, > 0). Default 200 mm.

name: draw_walls

description: Drive a joint from its current value to a target value and store the value reached. With contactSetId the motion STOPS at the first contact of any pair in that contact set (create_contact_set), located by bisection to "tolerance"; closed loops with passive joints also stop where the loop can no longer close. The result data is { requested, reached, stopped, reason?, pair?, from }. Instance placements are not changed: run evaluate_motion with apply=true afterwards.

contactSetId.description: Contact set whose first contact stops the motion. Omit to drive freely (limits still clamp).

dof.description: Coordinate index for multi-DOF joints. Default 0.

jointId.description: Id of the joint to drive (doc.joints).

samples.description: Coarse samples scanned for the first contact before bisecting. Default 200.

target.description: Target value (radians / document units) or a parameter expression.

tolerance.description: Bisection tolerance on the joint value, in joint units. Default 1e-6.

name: drive_joint_to

description: Clone several entities in one step (one undo), placing each copy at original.position + offset. Group membership is not copied. Ids that do not exist are skipped and listed in the summary; if none exist nothing changes. Returns the new entity ids in affected, in the order of the (de-duplicated) input ids.

ids.description: Entity ids to duplicate (non-empty, at most 10000). Missing ids are skipped.

offset.description: Optional [dx, dy, dz] offset applied to every copy. Defaults to [0, 0, 0] (exact overlap).

name: duplicate_entities

description: Change parameters of an existing implicit field node by id (design intent: radii, sizes, cell size, laws, blend radius...) and re-derive every implicit body built on it, so the bodies follow the edit. `changes` holds only what changes, named exactly as the parameters of the creating command: add_field_primitive (radius, size, height, ringRadius, tubeRadius, normal, offset, rounding, position, rotation), combine_fields (op, a, b, blend), offset_field (field, distance), shell_field (field, thickness, side), transform_field (field, position, rotation, scale), add_tpms_lattice (kind, cellSize, form, thickness, level, relativeDensity, normalize, origin, rotation, map, region; thickness and level may be a scalar-field id: a graded law), add_strut_lattice (cell, cellSize, radius, nodeRadius, origin, rotation, region; radius may be a scalar-field id), add_graph_lattice (sourceIds, radiusStart, radiusEnd, cap, chord, mergeTolerance, region), add_voronoi_lattice (region, density, seed, radius, cap), field_from_solid (entityId), create_scalar_field (the parameters of its kind). null removes an optional value (region, blend, map, nodeRadius). The shape, kind or lattice family of a node cannot be switched into another operation: create a new node. The node is validated like a new one; an edit that would make the graph cyclic, or that a dependent body cannot realise, is refused with the document unchanged. Next: implicit_properties / check_implicit on the re-derived bodies.

changes.description: Parameters to change, as an object of the creating command's parameter names; unchanged parameters are kept.

id.description: Id of the field node to edit (from the command that created it).

name: edit_field

description: Edit a nurbs_curve in place. `operation`: "move_pole" (`index`, `to` [x,y,z]: moves one control point, changes the shape), "move_poles" (`indices`, `delta` [x,y,z] added to each, optional `falloff` { radius in poles, shape }: neighbours follow with a soft weight), "drag_point" (`u`, `displacement` [x,y,z]: the curve point C(u) moves by exactly that vector with the least-norm pole change; poles whose basis is 0 at u stay), "set_weight" (`index`, `weight` > 0: makes the curve rational, changes the shape), "insert_knot" (`u` strictly inside the domain, `times` default 1: adds control points WITHOUT changing the shape, for local editing), "elevate_degree" (`by` default 1: raises the degree WITHOUT changing the shape), "reverse" (flips the direction). The summary reports the measured shape change for the shape-preserving operations. Look at the current definition with inspect_nurbs first.

by.description: elevate_degree: how many degrees to add, default 1 (result at most 25).

delta.description: move_poles: translation [x, y, z] added to every selected pole (and, weighted, to the falloff neighbours), in the entity-local frame (before the entity rotation), document units.

displacement.description: drag_point: how far C(u) moves [x, y, z] in document units.

falloff.description: move_poles: soft selection around the selected poles, measured in pole indices.

radius.description: Falloff radius in pole-index units (0 = only the selected poles).

id.description: Id of a nurbs_curve entity.

indices.description: move_poles: the pole indices (0-based) moved by the full delta.

operation.description: Which edit to apply; the other params depend on it.

times.description: insert_knot: how many times to insert it, default 1 (total multiplicity may not exceed the degree).

to.description: move_pole: new pole position [x, y, z] in document units, relative to the entity position.

u.description: insert_knot: parameter to insert, strictly inside the knot domain (see inspect_nurbs). drag_point: the curve parameter to drag, inside the domain (ends allowed).

name: edit_nurbs

description: Edit a nurbs_surface in place. `operation`: "move_poles" (select poles with `poles` [[i, j]...], `rows` (all poles of those u-rows), `cols` or `rect` { i0, i1, j0, j1 } inclusive, then `delta` [x,y,z] is added to each; optional `falloff` { radiusU, radiusV, shape } in pole-index units gives neighbours a soft weight), "set_weight" (`i`, `j`, `weight` > 0: makes the surface rational), "drag_point" (`u`, `v`, `displacement` [x,y,z]: S(u, v) moves by exactly that vector with the least-norm pole change), "insert_knot" (`direction`, the parameter in `u` or `v`, `times` default 1: more poles for local editing, shape unchanged), "elevate_degree" (`direction`, `by` default 1: shape unchanged), "reverse" (`direction`: flips that parameter), "transpose" (swaps u and v). Pole indices: i runs along u (0..nU-1), j along v (0..nV-1); inspect_nurbs lists the grid. The summary reports the measured shape change of the preserving operations. Refuses a pole outside the grid (DIR_POLE_RANGE) and a point outside the knot domain (DIR_POINT_OUTSIDE_DOMAIN).

by.description: elevate_degree: how many degrees to add, default 1.

cols.description: move_poles: select every pole of these v-columns (second index j).

delta.description: move_poles: translation [x, y, z] added to each selected pole, in the entity-local frame (before the entity rotation), document units.

direction.description: insert_knot / elevate_degree / reverse: the parameter direction.

displacement.description: drag_point: how far S(u, v) moves [x, y, z] in document units.

falloff.description: move_poles: soft selection; distance is max(|di| / radiusU, |dj| / radiusV) to the nearest selected pole.

radiusU.description: Falloff radius along u in pole-index units (0 = no spread along u).

radiusV.description: Falloff radius along v in pole-index units (0 = no spread along v).

id.description: Id of a nurbs_surface entity.

operation.description: Which edit to apply; the other params depend on it.

poles.description: move_poles: selected poles as [i, j] index pairs.

rect.description: move_poles: select the block of poles i0..i1, j0..j1.

rows.description: move_poles: select every pole of these u-rows (first index i).

times.description: insert_knot: how many times to insert the knot, default 1.

u.description: drag_point: parameter along u. insert_knot with direction "u": the knot to insert (strictly inside the domain).

v.description: drag_point: parameter along v. insert_knot with direction "v": the knot to insert (strictly inside the domain).

name: edit_nurbs_surface

description: Edit a piping spec with ordered operations, all or nothing: addComponent, updateComponent (members to change; null removes one), removeComponent, setSizeRange, setBranchCell (header, branch, fitting T | RT | W | S | TH | SI | SIR), clearBranchCell, setInsulationRow (code, dnMax, tempMaxC, thicknessMm, material, conductivityWmK?: adds or replaces a row of the insulation table that create_pipeline insulation "fromSpec" reads), removeInsulationRow (code, dnMax, tempMaxC), setHeader (title, service, dimensionalStandard, rating, materials, corrosionAllowance, millTolerance, designLimits, catalogs, elbowAngles, provenance). Component sizes are fromNps / toNps (inch designation) or fromDn / toDn. A draft spec is edited in place; editing an approved spec creates a new draft revision. Pipe lines that took their insulation thickness from the table read it again (their line number, parts and clash envelope follow). The result is validated like an import (PSC_SPEC_INVALID with the path, e.g. ops.2.id; an unknown insulation row to remove is refused the same way); removing the pipe component that a bound pipe element needs is refused (PSC_SPEC_IN_USE). Next: check_pipe_spec, resolve_spec_component.

ops.description: Operations applied in order; each is { op, ... } (addComponent, updateComponent, removeComponent, setSizeRange, setBranchCell, clearBranchCell, setInsulationRow, removeInsulationRow, setHeader).

component.description: Component in file form: { id, type, fromNps/toNps or fromDn/toDn, catalogRef, ends?, facing?, class?, pn?, radius?, schedule? | scheduleFromPipe?, wallMm?, priority?, branchFromNps/branchToNps?, commodityCode?, description?, material? }.

op.description: Add a component to the spec.

changes.description: Members to set; a member set to null is removed. The id cannot change. Setting fromNps / toNps replaces fromDn / toDn and vice versa.

id.description: Id of the component to change.
Id of the component to remove.

sizeRange.description: New spec size range { fromNps, toNps } or { fromDn, toDn }.

fitting.description: T equal tee, RT reducing tee, W weldolet, S sockolet, TH threadolet, SI stub-in, SIR reinforced stub-in.

header.description: Header size key (NPS or DN, in the system of the spec size range).

op.description: Add or replace one row of the insulation thickness table.

row.description: Row in file form: { code, dnMax, tempMaxC, thicknessMm, material, conductivityWmK? }. A row with the same code, dnMax and tempMaxC is replaced, else the row is added.

op.description: Remove one row of the insulation thickness table.

fields.description: Header members to set (a member set to null is removed, except the required ones): title, service, dimensionalStandard, rating, materials, corrosionAllowance { value, unit }, millTolerance, designLimits, catalogs, elbowAngles ({ anglesDeg, toleranceDeg, trimmedAllowed, bendRadiusD? }), provenance.

op.description: Set header members of the spec.

name: edit_pipe_spec

description: Edit a ply of a composite part: its name, lamina material, orientation (degrees from the rosette 0-degree direction), sequence label or boundary (same forms as add_ply). Omitted fields are kept. The stacking position does not change; use reorder_plies.

kind.description: Discriminator: the whole tool face.

anyOf.description: Explicit regions in the part frame.

kind.description: Discriminator: explicit regions.

polygons.description: One or more simple polygons in the part frame (developed face frame, document units); the ply covers their union.

items.description: A vertex [x, y] in the part frame (document units).

boundary.description: Where the ply lies on the tool face: { kind: "whole_face" } or { kind: "polygon", polygons: [[[x, y], ...]] }.

name.description: New ply name.

name: edit_ply

description: Edit the route of a spec-driven pipe run (route_pipe / auto_route_pipe / add_branch) and re-derive it. Legs are [start, ...pis, end]; a point of intersection (PI) is run.pis[index] (0 = the first interior point); a leg index is the merged-leg index of route_pipe data.legs. ops: "move_pi" { index, delta [dx,dy,dz] | point [x,y,z], mode } moves PI `index`; mode "orthogonal" (default) is the orthogonal stretch: every leg keeps its direction (and slope), the part of the move along a neighbouring leg lengthens / shortens it and the rest is carried, perpendicular, to the next point (a connected end never moves; with no parallel leg left the move is refused RTE_STRETCH_FAILED); mode "free" moves exactly that point, the two legs at it turn (their elbows must still match the spec angles, else the derivation code refuses); "stretch_leg" { index, length } sets the length of leg `index` by moving its end point orthogonally (a leg ending at a port cannot; stretch an earlier leg); "insert_pi" { index, points [[x,y,z]...] } adds points of intersection into leg `index` (give all the points of a jog at once so every elbow is valid); "delete_pi" { index, count } removes `count` PIs from `index` (the legs between merge into one straight leg). Collinear points merge. Inline components and branches keep the distance from the end of their leg that did not move and are re-indexed when legs merge or split (data.remapped lists them); one on a leg the edit removes, or that would leave its leg, refuses the edit (move it first). Branch runs and runs continuing from this one are stretched with it; if one cannot follow the edit is refused. Works on a run broken by a moved port: the ends then follow their ports as part of the edit. Returns the run id (affected[0]) and the stretched dependents; data = { runId, op, pis, legs (index, direction, lengthMm, cutLengthsMm, dropMm / slopeDeg on sloped legs), legChanges, remapped, dependents, pipePieces, totalPipeMm, centrelineLengthMm, warnings, unverified }. Refusals: RTE_UNITS_UNSUPPORTED, RTE_UNKNOWN_RUN, RTE_EDIT_INVALID, RTE_STRETCH_FAILED, RTE_ZERO_LEG, RTE_PORT_DIRECTION and any derivation code (RTE_NO_FITTING_FOR_ANGLE, RTE_SEGMENT_TOO_SHORT, RTE_INLINE_DOES_NOT_FIT, RTE_BRANCH_ON_FITTING ...). Next: piping_takeoff, check_piping.

count.description: delete_pi: how many consecutive PIs to remove from index (default 1).

delta.description: move_pi: displacement [dx, dy, dz] of the PI, mm. Give this or point.

index.description: move_pi / delete_pi: index of the PI in run.pis (0 = first). stretch_leg / insert_pi: index of the leg (0 = first, route_pipe data.legs).

length.description: stretch_leg: the new length of the leg between its points of intersection, mm (> 0).

mode.description: move_pi: "orthogonal" (default) keeps every leg direction; "free" moves only that point and turns the two legs at it.

op.description: The edit: move_pi, stretch_leg, insert_pi or delete_pi.

point.description: move_pi: new position [x, y, z] of the PI, mm. Give this or delta. insert_pi: a single point to insert (or use points).

points.description: insert_pi: points of intersection to add into the leg, in order from its start, mm.

items.description: Point of intersection [x, y, z], mm.

runId.description: Pipe run id (affected[0] of route_pipe / auto_route_pipe / add_branch).

name: edit_route

description: Replace the params of a feature history step by its stepId, then regenerate the document by replaying featureHistory. Use to parametrically edit a past operation (e.g. change the size of a box created earlier).

params.description: New params object for the step. Must be compatible with the command named in the step (i.e. a valid params object for step.name). The document is regenerated after replacement.

stepId.description: Id of the FeatureStep whose params are to be replaced (from doc.featureHistory[*].id).

name: edit_step_params

description: Sculpt a subdivision solid (add_subdivision_solid) by editing its control cage: select cage vertices by `vertexIndices`, by element references `vertices` / `edges` (their end vertices) / `faces` (their corners) — ids such as "v-1.7" are stable across topology edits, indices are resolved and recorded as ids — or by a world-space `region` box (none = all). Add a soft-selection `falloff` (a radius, or { radius, shape, metric }) so neighbours follow smoothly, then `scale` about `pivot` (per axis of the solid), `rotate` ({ axis (world), angleDeg, pivot }) and/or `translate` (world vector); order scale, rotate, translate. `crease` true makes cage edges between selected vertices infinitely sharp, false makes them smooth (use set_cage_crease for semi-sharp values). A cage with symmetry (set_cage_symmetry) stays mirror-symmetric unless `symmetry` is "ignore". `levels` changes the refinement. Returns data { vertexCount, faceCount, vertices, vertexIds, faceIds, selected, selectedIds } (world cage vertices; fully selected vertices). Next: check_subdivision, evaluate_subdivision.

crease.description: true: make edges between selected vertices infinitely sharp; false: make them smooth.

edges.description: Cage edges to select (both end vertices), as ids or [a, b] index pairs.

items.description: A cage edge: id "e:<vertexIdA>|<vertexIdB>" (stable) or a [vertexIndex, vertexIndex] pair.

faces.description: Cage faces to select (all their vertices), as ids or indices.

items.description: A cage face: element id ("f-1.2", stable across topology edits) or current index.

metric.description: Distance to the selection: euclidean (straight line, default) or topological (along cage edges, "connected only").

radius.description: Soft-selection radius (>= 0, document units): vertices closer than this to the selection follow it partly.

shape.description: Weight curve: smooth (default, 3t^2-2t^3), linear, sharp (t^2), root, sphere, inverse_square or constant; t = 1 - distance / radius.

falloff.description: Soft selection: a radius (smooth, euclidean) or { radius, shape, metric }. Default: none.

id.description: Id of the subdivision solid.

levels.description: Subdivision levels 0..4 (0 = the faceted cage itself; 2-3 is smooth; each level quadruples the face count).

pivot.description: World-space centre of scale and rotation. Default: centre of the fully selected vertices.

region.description: Select the cage vertices inside this world-space box (alternative to element selection).

max.description: World-space maximum corner [x, y, z] of the selection box.

min.description: World-space minimum corner [x, y, z] of the selection box.

rotate.description: Rotate the selection about an axis through the pivot (soft weights scale the angle).

angleDeg.description: Rotation angle in degrees (right-handed about the axis).

axis.description: World-space rotation axis (any non-zero length).

pivot.description: World-space centre of rotation. Default: the shared pivot.

scale.description: Scale factors [sx, sy, sz] (> 0) along the solid axes about the pivot (e.g. [0.6, 0.6, 1] narrows).

symmetry.description: "keep" (default when the cage has symmetry): mirror the edit onto the mirror images; "ignore": edit only the selection (if that breaks the mirror the cage symmetry is cleared).

translate.description: World-space move [dx, dy, dz] of the selection.

vertexIndices.description: Cage vertex indices to select (from the data of add_subdivision_solid).

vertices.description: Cage vertices to select, as ids or indices.

items.description: A cage vertex: element id ("v-1.7", stable across topology edits) or current index.

name: edit_subdivision_cage

description: Edit a zone of a composite part: rename it, replace its boundary (part frame, document units), its stacking string (bottom to top, see define_zone) or its priority. Omitted fields are kept. Plies created earlier are not changed: re-run generate_plies_from_zones with replaceGenerated true afterwards.

boundary.description: Zone polygon in the part frame (the developed face frame, document units), at least 3 vertices, simple.

items.description: A vertex [x, y] in the part frame (document units).

laminate.description: New stacking string, bottom to top.

name.description: New zone name.

name: edit_zone

description: Emboss (raise), deboss (sink), scribe (split the face along) or engrave (cut a groove along) 2D profiles on a plane, cylinder, cone, sphere or torus face of a solid: the profiles are wrapped onto the face keeping every length (method develop on plane, cylinder, cone) or by the geodesic / parametric chart of a sphere or torus (stretch measured and held to maxLengthStrain), lifted along the face normal by `depth` (document units; emboss adds material outside the face, deboss removes it inside), and fused or cut exactly; the walls are normal to the face. `profileIds` are closed sketch shapes (rectangle, circle, ellipse, closed polyline / spline) or text created with a font (holes of O, B ... are kept). `placement` anchors a sketch point on a face point, turns and may mirror the sketch (see wrap_to_face). scribe needs no depth and keeps the volume: the face is only split along the profile outlines (faces + 1 per closed profile). engrave takes ANY profile (open curves, closed shapes, single-line text such as font "LLULL Single Line"): a flat tool of `toolWidth` with round ends is swept along the outline paths and the swept area is cut `depth` deep (a closed shape gets a groove along its contour, not a pocket). The result replaces the solid and reports data: volumeDelta (exact, document units cubed), expectedVolumeDelta (closed form: plane A d; cylinder A d (1 +- d / 2r); cone A d +- (d^2 / 2) cos(alpha) A_uv; sphere A (d +- d^2 / R + d^3 / 3R^2)), regionArea, regions, angularSpanRad, distortion, unverified (font not pinned) and provenance. A sketch wider than one turn refuses with WRP_WRAP_OVERLAP, a region leaving the face with WRP_OUTSIDE_FACE, a cut as deep as the radius with WRP_DEPTH_EXCEEDS_SOLID, an open profile (not engrave) with WRP_PROFILE_OPEN, a sphere or torus with method develop with WRP_FACE_NOT_DEVELOPABLE, a stretch above the limit with WRP_DISTORTION_EXCEEDED, a freeform face with WRP_METHOD_UNAVAILABLE. Needs the exact (native) kernel. Next: check_wrap, mass_properties, render_view.

depth.description: Height of the emboss or depth of the deboss / groove, document units, > 0. Not used by scribe.

face.description: The face to work on: give faceNear (a point on the face), or faceIndex, or faceName. The command records the face name so a later edit of the model finds the same face (REF_LOST when it is gone).

faceIndex.description: Unique face index of the solid (inspect_faces / inspect_topology list them).

faceName.description: Persistent face name recorded by an earlier run of this command; wins over faceIndex and faceNear.

faceNear.description: A point on or near the intended face [x, y, z] in world document units; the face nearest to it is taken.

fitTolerance.description: Largest deviation of a fitted pcurve from its exact image, document units. Default: 1e-6 x the solid diagonal (named default).

id.description: Id of the solid to emboss.

maxLengthStrain.description: Largest accepted relative length change of the wrap (1 = 100 %). Default 0.02 (named default); develop faces have none. Held to the measured stretch of a geodesic or parametric chart.

mode.description: emboss: material added outside the face; deboss: material removed inside it; scribe: the face is split along the outlines, no material change; engrave: a groove of width toolWidth is cut along the outline paths.

placement.description: Sketch-to-face placement. Chart axes: x follows the circumference (cylinder / cone: +azimuth about the axis from the face x direction; plane: the face x direction), y follows the axis (cone: away from the apex along the generator; plane: normal x x direction). Lengths and angles are kept (develop).

anchor.description: Where the sketch sits on the face: sketch point `chart` lands on face point `on`.

chart.description: Sketch point [x, y] (sketch plane document units) that lands on `on`. Default [0, 0].

on.description: Point [x, y, z] on the face where the sketch point lands. Default: the point of the face nearest to faceNear (else the face centroid).

angleDeg.description: Turn of the sketch in degrees, counter-clockwise seen from outside the face, from the face reference direction (cylinder / cone: around the axis, +azimuth; plane: the face x direction). Default 0.

method.description: How the sketch is carried onto the face. develop (default) keeps every length and angle and works on plane, cylinder and cone faces (Gaussian curvature 0). geodesic, parametric and project are not built yet (WRP_METHOD_UNAVAILABLE); a sphere or freeform face is WRP_FACE_NOT_DEVELOPABLE with develop.

mirror.description: Flip the sketch y axis (a wrap seen from inside). Default false.

profileIds.description: Ids of the 2D profiles (or font texts) to emboss. Closed shapes for emboss, deboss, scribe; any curve for engrave.

toolWidth.description: engrave only: width of the flat tool, document units, > 0 (the groove is this wide with round ends).

name: emboss_on_face

description: Sanity-check a slider-crank engine analytically in milliseconds, with no simulation: exact piston travel, rod angle, crank torque per newton of piston force, and with forceN the crank torque T = F·dx/dθ, rod force F/cos β and cylinder side thrust F·tan β at chosen crank angles; and the mean-torque / mean-effective-pressure / power relation (T = MEP·V_d/(4π) four-stroke, MEP·V_d/(2π) two-stroke; P = T·ω). Geometry comes from `cylinder` (an add_cylinder_pressure id: crank radius, rod length, bore and the pressure model; angles are then CYCLE angles, 0 = firing TDC, and the gas force at each angle is used) or from crankRadiusMm + rodLengthMm (+ optional offsetMm of the cylinder axis; angles are crank degrees from TDC). Units: lengths mm, force N, pressure bar, displacement cm³, speed rpm, torque N·m, power kW. Use it before simulate_motion to check the model against hand numbers: the simulated static torque and bearing forces must match these within 0.5 %. With a `cylinder` whose crank has set_engine_losses and an `rpm`, data.brake gives the friction (FMEP), BMEP = IMEP - FMEP, brake torque / power and mechanical efficiency at that speed. data.accuracy states for each number its band (null = "± ?"), basis and origin: "calibrated" at a speed the heat release was calibrated at (not validation evidence), "predicted" elsewhere, "input" for a pressure table or a MEP you give. Read-only; needs no kernel or physics engine.

crankRadiusMm.description: Crank radius (half the stroke), mm. Required without `cylinder`.

cycle.description: Cycle for the MEP relation. Default the cylinder's, else four_stroke.

cylinder.description: Id of a cylinder pressure (add_cylinder_pressure): geometry and pressure are taken from the model.

displacementCm3.description: Swept volume of the engine, cm³ (all cylinders), for the MEP relation. Default: the cylinder or 2·r·π·bore²/4 if known.

forceN.description: Constant force on the piston toward the crank, N: adds torque, rod force and side thrust per angle.

mepBar.description: Mean effective pressure, bar: gives the mean torque (needs displacementCm3 or a cylinder).

offsetMm.description: Lateral offset of the cylinder axis from the crank axis, mm (default 0).

rodLengthMm.description: Connecting-rod length between pin centres, mm. Required without `cylinder`.

rpm.description: Crank speed, rpm: adds power and piston speed.

name: engine_quick_check

description: Engineering bill of materials of the managed PLM assembly (by part number and revision; for a plain parts/mass count of any document use bill_of_materials, for building quantities quantity_takeoff): one row per bound sub-item { level, partNumber, revision, state, quantity } where quantity is the number of instances of its component placed in this document, the total, how many children are not released and the components with instances that no sub-item covers. Only level 1 is available from one document (a child's own structure is in its own document). For a released revision the structure frozen at release is returned. Extends bill_of_materials, which counts components and materials. Read-only.

levels.description: Levels wanted; only level 1 exists in one document (default "all" = 1).

revision.description: A released revision whose frozen structure to return; default = the live structure.

name: engineering_bom

description: Query: the connection ports of one equipment (tag or id) or of all equipment: for every nozzle, id "<tag>:<mark>", world position of the flange face centre and unit direction pointing away from the equipment (document units, level elevation included), DN, rating, facing, service, orientationDeg in the chosen angleConvention, and the flange (outsideDiameter, thickness, placeholder, catalogRef). `ports` is keyed by port id (also listed in `order`). Without `equipment` at most 500 ports are returned (truncated says so). Routing connects pipes to these ports. Refusal: EQP_NOT_FOUND. Does not modify the document.

angleConvention.description: How angles in this call are read and reported. north_cw (default): vertical equipment 0 = plant north (+Y), growing clockwise seen from above (90 = east, +X); horizontal equipment 0 = top (+Z), 90 = the +Y side; a plan rotation grows clockwise. east_ccw: CAD maths, 0 = east (+X), growing counter-clockwise; horizontal equipment 0 = +Y, 90 = top; a plan rotation grows counter-clockwise. Every result names the convention.

equipment.description: Equipment tag (e.g. "V-101", the element mark) or element id (e.g. "equipment-3").

name: equipment_ports

description: Turn a random_response acceleration into a quasi-static load: adds a gravity load (acceleration vector = peakFactor x rms g along the probe axis, in the unit system of the static target case) to load case loadCase of targetAnalysisId, from a probe (an a_x / a_y / a_z probe name) or nodalMax: true (the largest nodal rms of the base-direction acceleration). peakFactor defaults to 3 (Gaussian 3-sigma, a named default stated in the result); give peakFactor and peakFactorSource for another value. The source results must be solved and current. basis 'miles' is refused: Miles' equation is a quick check, never an equivalent load. Apply the load with both signs when the sign matters. Next: fea_mesh / fea_solve the static case and compute_margins.

analysisId.description: Id of the solved random_response case.

basis.description: Basis of the acceleration; only 'random_response' is accepted.

loadCase.description: Load case name in the target (1-40 letters, digits or underscores).

nodalMax.description: true: use the largest nodal rms of the base-direction acceleration instead of a probe.

peakFactor.description: Peak factor (multiple of the rms); default 3 (named default).

peakFactorSource.description: Where a non-default peak factor comes from.

probe.description: Name of an acceleration probe (a_x / a_y / a_z) of the random case.

targetAnalysisId.description: Id of the static analysis that receives the load.

name: equivalent_static_load_case

description: Read-only priced bill of quantities: multiplies each quantity_takeoff line by its unit rate (stored rates from set_cost_rates, overridden by the rates param) and totals the estimate. Lines without a rate are listed as unpriced.

currency.description: Currency label. Default: the stored currency or EUR.

rates.description: Optional extra / overriding rates, same keys as set_cost_rates.

description: Sample an implicit FIELD: signed value (negative inside, in document units; exact only if distanceQuality is "exact", otherwise a bound or approximation), optionally the gradient, at up to 10000 points or on a plane grid (up to 200x200). Use it to probe a thickness, check a blend tangent point or read a lattice law instead of rendering. Give exactly one of points or grid. data: values[], gradients[] (when gradient is true), distanceQuality, lipschitz, nonFiniteSamples.

field.description: Id of the field node to sample.

gradient.description: Also return the gradient (3 numbers per sample). Default false.

grid.description: Alternative to points: a regular grid on an axis-aligned plane (row-major, u fastest).

min.description: Lower corner [u, v] in the plane axes (XY: x,y; XZ: x,z; YZ: y,z).

offset.description: Coordinate of the plane along its normal, in document units.

points.description: Up to 10000 points [x, y, z].

items.description: Sample point [x, y, z] in document units.

name: evaluate_field

description: Compute the result of applying all kinematic joints (add_joint, set_joint_value) and drive relations (add_drive_relation) between component instances. Use this for poses without forces; use add_body_joint + simulate_motion for rigid-body physics (masses, forces, time). Drive relations are walked in topological order: driven_value = driver_value * ratio + offset. Then each joint is applied: revolute rotates instance b around instance a's origin along the axis; prismatic translates instance b along the axis from instance a's origin. Closed loops with passive joints are solved first (Levenberg-Marquardt). apply=false (default) is a read-only query: the document is returned unchanged with affected:[]. apply=true WRITES the resulting position and rotation into the affected instances (undoable; affected[] lists the moved instance ids) and refuses with the document unchanged when the loop cannot close (e.g. a four-bar past its Grashof limit). Returns data: { resolvedJoints: Record<jointId, number>,   resolvedValues: Record<jointId, number[]> (all DOFs),   instancePositions: Record<instanceId, Vec3>,   instanceRotations: Record<instanceId, Vec3>,     loop?: { closed, residual, message, loops, passive } when joints form a closed loop (passive joints are solved; closed=false means it cannot close) }.

apply.description: false (default): only compute and report, the document is unchanged. true: write the computed position/rotation into the instances.

name: evaluate_motion

description: Evaluate a material property (k, cp, E, cte, thermalStrain …) at an operating point. Give every variable the model needs with its unit, e.g. at.T = {value: 77, unit: 'K'} or {value: -196, unit: 'degC'}. Returns value + unit, range status (in_data_range, or in_equation_range_only = unverified with PROP_OUTSIDE_DATA_RANGE), basis, source and `unverified`. Refuses outside the model's valid range (PROP_OUT_OF_RANGE) and never extrapolates. cte is derived as s'(T)/(1 + s(T)) when only a thermalStrain model exists. Use sample_property for tables, integrals and solver tables; use check_property_models before handing a result to the owner.

allowConstant.description: Allow the scalar density for a temperature-dependent query (reported as a named default).

unit.description: Unit, e.g. 'K', 'degC', 'degF', '1/s'.

at.description: Operating point: every variable the model needs (T, strainRate, time, exposureTime, pressure, equivalentPlasticStrain), each { value, unit }, e.g. { T: { value: 77, unit: 'K' } }.

band.description: Also return the uncertainty band [low, high] with its kind (fitErrorVsData is NOT a confidence bound).

basis.description: Only a model on this basis (never substituted).

condition.description: Condition fields the model must match, e.g. { rrr: 50 }.

direction.description: Orientation of the model to use.

outputUnit.description: Unit of the answer, e.g. 'W/(mm*K)'. Default: the model unit.

property.description: Catalogue property name, e.g. k, cp, E, cte, thermalStrain, density.

name: evaluate_property

description: Evaluate the limit surface of a subdivision solid exactly (independent of `levels`): the limit position and unit normal of cage `vertices` (default: all), and points at `samples` { face, u, v } (u, v in [0, 1] over a QUAD cage face, corner 0 at (0, 0), counter-clockwise). `curvature` adds the principal curvatures k1 >= k2 (1 / document unit, positive when convex). World coordinates. Each point carries its subdivision rule (smooth / crease / corner) and valence; data.extraordinary lists the cage vertices of valence other than 4 where continuity drops to G1. A point at an extraordinary vertex (curvature unbounded) or on an n-gon face is flagged `degenerate` with code DIR_EVAL_DEGENERATE. At most 10000 points. Next: check_subdivision, edit_subdivision_cage.

curvature.description: true: add principal curvatures k1, k2 (flagged degenerate where undefined).

id.description: Id of the subdivision solid.

samples.description: Surface samples on quad faces.

face.description: A cage face: element id ("f-1.2", stable across topology edits) or current index.

u.description: Parameter along the first edge of the face (0..1).

v.description: Parameter along the last edge of the face (0..1).

vertices.description: Cage vertices whose limit points are returned. Default (no samples either): all.

items.description: A cage vertex: element id ("v-1.7", stable across topology edits) or current index.

name: evaluate_subdivision

description: Health check of a solved explicit_dynamics case (PHY-19 §5.4): termination, energy error (E_kin + E_int + E_hg + E_wall - E_kin0 - W_ext) / (E_kin0 + W_ext), hourglass / internal energy ratio, added mass ratio. Limits: hourglassLimit has the named default 0.10 (rule of thumb); energyErrorLimit and addedMassLimit have NO default (a warning says so; the added-mass limit falls back to the case mass-scaling limit). Returns status pass | warn | fail and one item per check with code, value and the limit with its source.

addedMassLimit.description: Largest added mass / model mass. Default: the case maxAddedMassRatio when mass scaling is on.

analysisId.description: Id of the analysis (affected[0] of create_analysis, e.g. an-1.1).

contactLimit.description: Largest |contact energy| / internal energy (warning above). No default.

hourglassLimit.description: Largest hourglass / internal energy ratio, > 0. Default 0.10 (named).

name: explicit_energy_check

description: Replace an InstanceEntity with concrete copies of its component's entities baked into world space. Each produced entity receives a fresh id. The component definition is NOT removed. The instance entity is removed and its order position is filled with the produced entities. Returns the new entity ids in affected.

id.description: Id of an InstanceEntity to explode into its world-space component entities.

name: explode_instance

description: Explode a polyline entity into individual line segments. Each consecutive pair of vertices becomes a separate line entity. If the polyline is closed, a final segment is added from the last point back to the first. The original polyline is removed. No-op if the entity is not a polyline or has fewer than 2 points.

id.description: Id of the polyline entity to explode.

name: explode_polyline

description: Export the 3D bodies (all, or entityIds) as a 3MF package (.3mf, ZIP with 3D/3dmodel.model), the format slicers and print services read: one object per body carrying its name (set_entity_name, else the id) and its colour as a base material, one build item per object, units millimetre (document lengths are converted). Vertices are welded into an indexed mesh; data.objects[].manifold says whether each body is a closed, consistently oriented shell (printable). Returns data: { format:"3mf", fileName, base64, objectCount, triangleCount, objects[] (name, vertices, triangles, manifold; beams for a beam lattice, levelsetNodes for a level set), implicit?, beamLattice? }; the CLI writes it with --save PATH.3mf. Large meshes (over 250000 triangles) are streamed and compressed (their vertices are written as they are, not welded, so a mesh whose shells touch only by position reports manifold false), so multi-million-triangle implicit bodies export; the package is returned as one base64 string, which caps it near 8 million triangles (EXPORT_MESH_TOO_LARGE above: use implicit "levelset", beamLattice, a coarser voxel, decimate_mesh or export_stl). 2D shapes and unknown ids are skipped. Does NOT modify the document.

beamLattice.description: Write implicit strut / graph lattice bodies as a 3MF Beam Lattice (nodes + beams with end radii, the clipping region as clippingmesh, the realised mesh as representationmesh) instead of their triangles: small files, slicer-native struts. TPMS and other bodies stay meshes; data.beamLattice lists what was written and what was skipped with the reason.

beamRepresentation.description: With beamLattice: also write the realised mesh of each lattice as its representationmesh (for consumers that cannot build beams; the file then holds the mesh too). Default false.

confirmExportControlled.description: Human confirmation for a document that uses export-controlled (ITAR / EAR) material records: a signature object produced in the desktop app, with a nonce field, over the export act and the document hash. An agent cannot give it: true is refused with MAT_HUMAN_GATE. Without it a controlled document is refused with MAT_EXPORT_CONTROLLED.

entityIds.description: Array of entity ids to include in the export. Omit (or pass []) to export ALL 3D solid entities in the document. 2D and unknown ids are silently skipped.

implicit.description: levelset: write implicit bodies as a 3MF Volumetric & Implicit level set (the field itself as an implicit function of native nodes, bounded by a box mesh; no triangles), for printers that read the extension; strut / graph lattices and bodies built on them stay beam lattices or meshes (data.implicit lists written and skipped with the reason). The function is negative inside (the spec does not state the interior sign of a level set; llull uses the sign of its own mesh-distance node). Document units other than millimetres are refused for bodies built on solids. mesh (default): triangles.

maxBytes.description: Refuse with EXPORT_MESH_TOO_LARGE when the compressed model part of a streamed (large) export would exceed this many bytes. Default and maximum 375000000 (the package is returned as one base64 string). Bodies up to 250000 triangles are not limited by it.

name.description: File name without extension (default "model"); reduced to letters, digits, "." "_" "-".

description: Export a composite part to STEP AP242 (ISO 10303-21): the exact tool solid and, when create_ply_solids made them, the explicit per-ply solids ("<ply> piece <n>"; exact B-reps where the kernel builds the slab, triangles otherwise) go through export_step_ap242 (named products, flat, geometric validation properties); llull then appends the implicit laminate definition as the CAx-IF composite structure (Recommended Practices for Composite Materials v4.4): a ply_laminate_table with its ply_laminate_sequence_definitions in stacking order, one product per ply (category "ply") with its material (make_from_usage_option to a stock-material product), thickness, orientation (ply_orientation_angle against a reinforcement_orientation_basis rosette) and boundary curves, the ply solids as ply pieces under their ply, the base surface (plane, cylinder, cone, sphere; not a NURBS sheet) and the composite validation properties named as the CAx-IF validation practice names them (number of tables / sequences / plies / cores / materials / orientations / rosettes, total ply surface area, ordered orientation values, ordered sequences per laminate table, curve length and ply-piece count per ply, boundary length per rosette, area per material). llull also writes its own lossless records (part frame, chart polygons, lamina data, per-ply area, thickness, mass) as property records of the tool product. The written text is read back and everything is compared with the model (data.selfCheck). import_composite_ap242 reads it back. Returns data: { format, step, schema, part, tool, plies[{ ply, name, order, area, thickness, solids }], validation, selfCheck, solids: { exact, faceted }, records, policy, reviewRequired }. Ply pieces hang under their ply by next_assembly_usage_occurrence as the practice prescribes, so a reader built on OpenCascade sees only the tool solid in the raw file (import_composite_ap242 compensates). Cores are not written: data.notWritten.cores counts them and data.reviewRequired lists cores_not_written (and unverified_material_basis for lamina data of mean / unknown basis). Needs the OCC kernel. Does not modify the document.

description: Export the document (or a subset of entities) to glTF 2.0 format. Produces a triangle tessellation in world space for every exportable 3D solid entity. 2D shape entities are silently skipped. Revolution and instance entities are fully expanded. Returns the UNCHANGED document, affected:[], and a data object with:   format ("gltf" or "glb"), triangleCount, nodeCount, materialCount,   text (glTF 2.0 JSON string — when binary=false, default),   base64 (GLB binary blob base64-encoded — when binary=true). Structure: one glTF node per entity (node.name = the entity name from set_entity_name, else its id; each child of an instance is its own node), and entities that belong to a group (group_entities) are children of a node named after the group. Node extras carry the llull entity id and kind. Meshes are indexed and carry POSITION and creased smooth NORMAL attributes; parts with identical geometry and appearance (pattern copies: array_polar / array_linear bolts, blades) share ONE mesh placed by each node matrix. One PBR material per distinct appearance: the assigned document material (color, metalness, roughness) or else the entity color, converted to linear glTF factors — ready for Blender / Cycles or any viewer. A material finish (create_material finish) embeds procedural albedo / normal / roughness PNG maps with box-projected TEXCOORD_0 (plus KHR_materials_clearcoat); text decals (add_decal) are extra alpha-blended textured meshes. The BIN buffer is inlined as a data: URI in JSON mode. In GLB mode the 12-byte header + JSON chunk + BIN chunk are packed per the glTF 2.0 spec. entityIds: omit to export all 3D entities; provide an array to export a subset. binary: false (default) → data.text contains JSON; true → data.base64 contains GLB. Does NOT modify the document.

binary.description: Output format selector. false (default): data.text contains a glTF 2.0 JSON string with the binary buffer inlined as a data: URI. true: data.base64 contains a base64-encoded GLB binary container (12-byte header + JSON chunk + BIN chunk per glTF 2.0 spec). Most web viewers accept JSON glTF; most desktop importers accept GLB.

description: Laser-projection data of a composite part: for every ply piece the boundary polyline on the tool face as 3D points in the tool (document) frame, in millimetres, as a plain-text list (a neutral layout; vendor formats are not written). Consecutive points are at most `spacing` apart (default 75 mm) and every corner turning at least `cornerAngle` degrees (default 20) is included. `plies` selects plies by id or name (default all). description: Export 3D solids to STEP (ISO 10303-21) from the kernel exact B-rep through the XDE writer: AP242 by default (AP214 or AP203 on request), the document unit as the file length unit (numbers are not converted), real assembly structure (one PRODUCT per component, one placed NEXT_ASSEMBLY_USAGE_OCCURRENCE per instance, shared parts written once), entity names, colours, layers, materials, and the CAx-IF geometric validation properties (volume, surface area, centre of volume) of every product and of the root assembly. The written text is read back with an independent Part 21 reader and its validation properties are compared with the model (data.selfCheck, tolerance 1e-9 relative); a disagreement refuses the export with XCH_SELFCHECK_RED. Surface sheets (nurbs_surface) are written as B-spline face products. Returns data: { format, step, schema, schemaName, unit, solidCount, sheetCount, entityIds, skipped, assembly?, gvp[{ product, volume, area, centroid }], selfCheck, policy, provenance, reviewRequired }. Same document and same timestamp give identical bytes. Imported bodies whose sender validation properties were red or not checkable need acceptUnverified (a human signature). Needs the exact kernel (kernel_info); the mesh kernel refuses with XCH_WRITER_UNAVAILABLE. A kernel that only writes shapes directly (no XDE writer) exports through a simpler writer only when you pass includeValidationProperties:false (AP214 or AP242 header, no validation properties, PMI or self-check; data then has no gvp/selfCheck/policy); otherwise it refuses with XCH_WRITER_UNAVAILABLE. This is the in-process kernel export (needs ctx.kernel); the CLI tool export_step (llull export_step --save part.stp) is the file-writing entry point that calls it (or the Python bridge) and saves the result. Does not modify the document.

description: Export the document (or a subset of entities) to STL format — the standard triangle-mesh interchange format accepted by slicers, mesh editors, and 3D printers. Supported entity kinds: box, cylinder, sphere, cone, torus, wedge, pyramid, extrusion, mesh. entityIds: omit to export all 3D entities; provide an array to export a subset. format: "ascii" (default, human-readable) or "binary" (more compact, required by some importers). name: optional solid name embedded in the STL header (default: the entity name when exactly one named entity is exported, else "llull"). perEntity: one named solid block per entity (ASCII). description: Export the kinematic model as a URDF robot description (ROS, Gazebo, MuJoCo, PyBullet) with one STL mesh per link. source "dynamics" uses the rigid bodies and body joints (add_rigid_body, add_body_joint); "assembly" uses component instances connected by add_joint joints (revolute / prismatic; the child instance moves relative to the parent, axis through the parent origin); "auto" (default) uses dynamics when it has bodies, else the assembly. Each body is a link with visual and collision meshes (meshes/<link>.stl, metres, in the link frame) and an inertial block from mass_properties (mass, centre of mass, inertia about it). Link frames are aligned with the world axes and sit at their joint anchor; joint origins are the anchor offsets. Revolute joints are written "continuous" (the document stores no angle limits), prismatic joints get lower/upper = -/+ prismaticTravel, damping and friction come from dynamics joints. Bodies without a parent are attached to the "world" link (fixed when welded / assembly root, else floating). Spherical joints and loop-closing joints cannot be in a URDF tree and are listed in data.notes. Returns data: { format:"urdf", source, robot, files[] (first the .urdf, then meshes/*.stl; each { name, content }), linkCount, jointCount, notes[] }; the CLI writes them with --save DIR. Does NOT modify the document.

description: Extrude faces of a subdivision cage along their average normal (or `direction`) by `distance` in document units, creating side quads; the smooth surface grows a boss or handle. Faces are ids from select_cage_elements or data.faceIds ("f-1.2") or indices. Edge-connected faces extrude as one region (one shared normal) unless `individual`. Existing element ids are kept, new ones are minted; a symmetric cage extrudes the mirror faces too. Negative distance cuts inward. Refuses edges / vertices (DIR_ELEMENT_KIND), distance 0 (DIR_DISTANCE_ZERO). Returns data { vertexCount, faceCount, vertices, vertexIds, faceIds, capFaces, newFaces, newVertices }. Next: edit_subdivision_cage to shape the new faces, inset_cage_faces, check_subdivision.

direction.description: World-space direction of the extrusion (any non-zero length). Default: each region average face normal.

distance.description: Extrusion distance in document units along the direction (negative = into the solid). Not 0.

description: Extrude a closed 2D profile along +Z into an extrusion solid. Right-handed world frame, +Z up. Give EXACTLY ONE source: `profile` (inline array of [x, y] points, at least 3, implicitly closed, placed at `position`, default [0,0,0]); OR `id` of one closed drawn shape (circle, rectangle, ellipse, closed polyline, closed spline); OR `ids` of several coplanar open pieces (line, arc, open polyline, open spline) that join end to end into one closed loop, in any order and direction. A drawn sketch keeps its curved boundaries exact (true arcs and Bézier splines for the exact kernel and STEP export; the polygon is only the display tessellation), is placed at the (first) source entity position (override with `position`), inherits the source rotation (it extrudes along its work-plane normal) unless rotation, axis or plane is given (the profile keeps the source in-plane [x, y]; an explicit rotation / axis re-orients that plane), and stays in the document. The solid spans from the position along +Z for depth units (depth must be > 0). Orientation: pass EITHER rotation (Euler radians) OR axis [dx,dy,dz] = the extrusion direction (the profile plane normal; local +Z maps to it). axis wins when both are given; the derived Euler angles are stored. A text entity created with a font (add_text font=...) is accepted as `id`: its glyph outlines, holes included, are extruded into one mesh solid (any kernel; the text is kept). thin {thickness, side centre|inside|outside} extrudes only a wall instead of a solid prism: an open polyline (id, or inline profile with openPath true) becomes an offset band, a closed profile a ring (needs a geometry kernel; result is a mesh with an exact B-rep).

axis.description: Optional direction [dx, dy, dz] (any non-zero length, normalized) that is the extrusion direction (local +Z) points along in world space, e.g. [1, 0, 0] lays it along +X. When given it OVERRIDES rotation (the rotation param is ignored and the resolved Euler angles are stored). A zero-length or malformed axis is rejected as a no-op.

color.description: Hex color string #rrggbb, e.g. "#c8553d". Defaults to "#c8553d".

depth.description: Extrusion depth in document units along +Z from the position. Must be > 0.

id.description: Id of one closed 2D shape: circle, rectangle, ellipse, closed polyline or closed spline. Use ids instead for a loop made of several pieces.

ids.description: Ids of coplanar 2D pieces (line, arc, polyline, spline) that join end to end into one closed loop; order and direction do not matter. Alternative to id and profile.

openPath.description: Only with thin: true means the inline `profile` is an OPEN path (not implicitly closed). Default false.

plane.description: Sketch plane id (create_sketch_plane): extrude along the plane normal, the profile in the plane axes. Without it a drawn source already extrudes along its own work plane (its rotation). Excludes rotation and axis.

position.description: World-space origin of the profile plane [x, y, z] in document units. Defaults to [0, 0, 0] for an inline profile and to the (first) source entity position for id/ids. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

profile.description: Inline closed loop: array of [x, y] points in the XY plane of the profile (at least 3, do not repeat the first point). Omit when id or ids is given.

rotation.description: three.js intrinsic XYZ Euler angles in RADIANS [rx, ry, rz] (equivalent to rotating about world Z first, then world Y, then world X). Matches rotate_entity convention. Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. If non-finite or not length-3 the rotation is ignored and [0,0,0] is used.

thin.description: Thin-wall extrusion: instead of a solid prism, extrude only a wall of the given thickness along the profile. A closed profile gives a ring (outer minus inner outline, needs a geometry kernel), an open profile (open polyline id, or an inline profile with openPath true) gives an offset band (mitred corners). Volume = wall area x depth. Curved sketches are used through their display polygon.

side.description: "centre": the wall is centred on the profile (thickness/2 each side); "inside": the wall grows toward the inside of a closed profile (left of the travel direction of an open path); "outside": it grows outward (right of the travel direction of an open path).

thickness.description: Wall thickness in document units (> 0), measured in the profile plane.

With resultsId (a set made by import_qif_results for this revision) Form 3 rows also carry the imported measured value and the verdict of the measuring system (resultStatus) and Form 1 the serial number; llull does not judge them. description: Read-only fastener-fit helper (ASME Y14.5 fastener formulas): positional tolerance of a hole pattern from the hole and fastener MMC sizes. floating: both parts have clearance holes, T = H − F per part. fixed: the fastener is held in one part (threaded / press-fit), T1 + T2 = H − F, split by `split` (share of part 1, default 0.5). With statedPosition: the virtual condition H − T; with actualSize too: the MMC bonus (actual − H) and the allowed position (stated + bonus); with holeLmc too: the allowed position at LMC. statedWithinClearance says whether the stated position fits the clearance budget of its part (`part`, fixed fasteners). Sizes in document units.

actualSize.description: Actual (measured) hole size within [holeMmc, holeLmc]: MMC bonus and allowed position.

fastenerMmc.description: Fastener size at maximum material condition F (largest shank), > 0, < holeMmc.

holeLmc.description: Hole size at least material condition (largest hole); bounds actualSize.

holeMmc.description: Hole size at maximum material condition H (smallest hole), > 0.

part.description: fixed: which part statedPosition belongs to (1 or 2); its share of H − F bounds statedWithinClearance. Default 1.

split.description: fixed: share of H − F given to part 1, in (0, 1). Default 0.5 (equal split).

statedPosition.description: Stated position tolerance at MMC (diameter), >= 0: virtual condition and bonus.
