description: Quick fatigue life at ONE stress or strain amplitude (no FE, no document change). method stress_life: material record + modelId of an S-N model (sn_basquin, sn_power_law, sn_table) and a stress `amplitude` (+ `mean`, `meanStress` model, Marin `modifiers` that multiply the curve strength, e.g. surface 0.8). method strain_life: modelId of an en_coffin_manson model and EITHER `strainAmplitude` OR `nominal` { amplitude, mean } with an optional `notch` { kt, q, feIncludesKt } (needs cyclicModelId, a cyclic_ramberg_osgood model: Neuber local stress / strain, then CMB, Morrow or SWT life). Returns data { cyclesToFailure, reversalsToFailure, equivalentAmplitudeMPa, localStressMaxMPa, localStrainMax, transitionReversals, extrapolated, items[], unverified, reviewRequired }. An amplitude at or above Ftu returns item FAT_STATIC_FAILURE and no life. Results are not approved: a qualified engineer must review.

unit.description: Unit text of the 08 grammar, e.g. 'degC', 'K', 'W/(m^2*K)', 'W'.

cyclicModelId.description: strain_life with nominal stress or SWT: id of the cyclic_ramberg_osgood model.

material.description: Material record id (define_material_record / create_material name) holding the models.

unit.description: Unit text of the 08 grammar, e.g. 'degC', 'K', 'W/(m^2*K)', 'W'.

walker.description: Walker exponent gamma in (0, 1]; gamma 0.5 equals SWT.

meanStress.description: Mean-stress correction: none | goodman (needs Ftu on the record) | gerber (Ftu) | soderberg (Fty) | morrow (sn_basquin sigma_f) | swt | { walker: gamma }. A compressive mean gives no benefit for goodman / gerber / soderberg / morrow unless compressiveMean "formula". Default none.

modelId.description: Id of the S-N or en_coffin_manson model on that material (add_material_model).

modifiers.description: stress_life: Marin modifiers (surface, size, reliability ...), each with a justification.

justification.description: Mandatory reason / source of the factor.

name.description: Which Marin-type modifier this is.

value.description: Factor > 0 multiplying the curve strength (0.8 = 20 % weaker than the test specimen). Never defaulted.

nominal.description: strain_life: nominal stress amplitude and mean; local response by Neuber when a notch is given.

amplitude.description: A stress { value, unit } with a stress unit (MPa, ksi, psi, ...).

Unit text of the 08 grammar, e.g. 'degC', 'K', 'W/(m^2*K)', 'W'.

notch.description: Optional notch: the nominal stress is scaled by Kf = 1 + q (Kt - 1) (Neuber on the cyclic curve for strain-life).

feIncludesKt.description: true when the stress already contains the concentration (no extra Kf); false: Kf scales the nominal stress.

q.description: Notch sensitivity q in [0, 1]: Kf = 1 + q (Kt - 1).

strainAmplitude.description: strain_life: total strain amplitude (> 0), alternative to `nominal`.

description: Read one result field of a SOLVED analysis as numbers: von_mises, u_mag, u_x, u_y, u_z, s_xx, s_yy, s_zz (heat cases: temperature, heat_flux) for a load case (loadCase, default the first) or a mode (mode, 1-based, modal / buckling: displacement of the mode shape, whose amplitude is arbitrary). Returns data { field, unit, resultSet, count, min { value, node, at }, max { value, node, at }, mean, rows [{ node, at, value, entityId, distance? }] }; min / max / mean cover every node of the result set. rows are the `limit` (default 20, max 500) nodes with the largest (or smallest, order) value, OR the nodes you name (nodes: mesh node ids), OR the nearest node to each of `points` (document units), OR the nearest node to each result probe (probes: true); give at most one of them. Values are nodal (the solver averages stress at shared nodes) in the analysis unitSystem (N-mm-t-s: MPa, mm); `at` and distance are in the analysis length unit. Singular spots (point loads, supports, re-entrant corners) read high: judge them. Requires fea_mesh and fea_solve on this machine.

analysisId.description: Id of the analysis (affected[0] of create_analysis, e.g. an-1.1).

field.description: Field to read: von_mises | u_mag | u_x | u_y | u_z | s_xx | s_yy | s_zz | temperature | heat_flux.

limit.description: Extremes only: how many nodes to return (default 20, max 500).

loadCase.description: Load case name (static / thermo-mechanical). Default: the first load case.

mode.description: modal / buckling only: mode number, 1-based. Default 1.

nodes.description: Mesh node ids to read (see describe_analysis / analysis_report for positions). At most 500.

order.description: Extremes only: rank the nodes by largest (default) or smallest value.

points.description: Points in document units; the nearest node to each is read.

items.description: A point [x, y, z] in document units; the nearest mesh node is read.

probes.description: true = read the node nearest to each result probe of the analysis (add_result_probe).

name: fea_result_field

description: Turn an existing CLOSED 3D solid (box, cylinder, extrusion, boolean result, imported mesh...) into an implicit FIELD whose negative side is the solid, so it can be shelled, offset, blended or filled with a lattice. The distance is exact to the solid's stored triangles; for curved or B-rep sources it is reported as a distance bound (data.tessellationExact false). Refused for 2D shapes, curves, sheets and meshes with free edges (IMP_SOLID_NOT_CLOSED). The solid itself is left untouched; hide it with create_implicit_body hideSource when the realised body replaces it.

entityId.description: Id of the closed 3D solid entity.

name.description: Optional label for the field node.

name: field_from_solid

description: Close a hole of an open subdivision cage: `edge` (id "e:<idA>|<idB>" or [a, b] vertex indices) is any edge of the hole boundary. mode "ngon" (default) adds one face over the whole loop; "quads" adds a centre vertex and n/2 quads (the loop needs an even number of edges; the centre has valence n/2). When the last hole closes the cage is closed again and has a volume. A symmetric cage fills the mirror holes too. Refuses an edge that borders two faces (DIR_NOT_BOUNDARY) and "quads" on an odd loop (DIR_FILL_ODD). Returns data { vertexCount, faceCount, vertices, vertexIds, faceIds, newFaces, newVertices, loopSize }. Next: set_cage_crease, edit_subdivision_cage, check_subdivision.

edge.description: Any edge of the hole boundary: id "e:<idA>|<idB>" or [a, b] vertex indices.

id.description: Id of the subdivision solid.

mode.description: "ngon" (default): one face over the loop. "quads": a centre vertex and n/2 quads (even loops only).

name: fill_cage_hole

description: Close holes (boundary loops) of a mesh (or the triangles of any 3D solid) with the method of Liepa (2003): the loop is triangulated by dynamic programming (smallest dihedral angle to the neighbouring faces, then smallest area), the patch is refined to the edge length of its surroundings (centroid insertion with Delaunay edge swaps) and the inserted vertices are faired: fairing "none" keeps the plain triangulation, "tangent" minimises membrane area (flat), "curvature" (default) minimises thin-plate bending (smooth continuation of the surface). The first boundary loop of analyze_mesh is index 0. A patch with no inserted vertex (small holes) is the plain triangulation whatever the fairing; raise refinementFactor (default 1.414) for more patch vertices. Existing vertices never move. Reports per loop the edges, triangles added, vertices inserted and patch area (document units^2), and the loops skipped with their code; closed tells whether the result is watertight. Refusals: MESH_ENTITY_NOT_FOUND, MESH_NOT_A_MESH, MESH_HOLE_NOT_FOUND (explicit holes only), MESH_HOLE_TOO_LARGE, MESH_HOLE_NON_SIMPLE, MESH_HOLE_NO_TRIANGULATION. With holes "all" (default), loops over maxBoundaryEdges or that cannot be triangulated are skipped and listed instead of refused, and a mesh without any loop comes back unchanged with filled [] (totalLoops 0). Next: repair_mesh mode=orient, check_mesh.

near.description: A point [x, y, z] (document units, world) near the hole; the loop with the closest vertex is chosen.

holes.description: Which holes: "all" (default), a list of loop indices as numbered by analyze_mesh boundaryLoops (0-based), or a list of {near: [x, y, z]} points naming the closest loop.

id.description: Id of the mesh (or other 3D solid) to fill.

keepSource.description: true: keep the source and add the result as a new mesh. Default false: the source entity is rewritten in place (same id, name, layer, colour).

maxBoundaryEdges.description: Largest loop (edges) to fill. Default 1000. Loops up to 120 edges use the exact O(n^3) triangulation, larger ones a greedy one.

refine.description: Insert vertices so the patch matches the surrounding edge length. Default true.

refinementFactor.description: Liepa density factor alpha (1..10): a patch triangle is split when alpha x (centroid to corner distance) exceeds the local edge length. Default 1.414 (sqrt 2).

name: fill_mesh_holes

description: Fill a closed loop of 3 to 12 boundary curves (nurbs_curve ids, non-rational, in any order and orientation) with ONE surface sheet that contains every boundary curve exactly: the loop is grouped into the four sides of a bilinearly blended Coons patch (3 curves give a triangular patch with one collapsed side; with more than 4 curves neighbouring curves become one composite side, the groups chosen to balance side lengths). The curve ends must meet end to end within `tolerance`. By default the fill is position (G0) continuous only. `neighbours` makes it tangent (G1) or curvature (G2) continuous with existing sheets: each entry names a loop curve (`curveId`), the nurbs_surface (`surfaceId`) that has this curve as one of its four boundary edges, and `continuity` "G1" (the fill leaves the sheet perpendicular to the edge in its tangent plane) or "G2" (also the normal curvature across the edge). The match is made on the poles near each edge, so it is approximate between them: the result reports the MEASURED g0Gap and, over the middle 80 % of the edge, g1AngleRad and g2Gap per neighbour (data.boundaries; cornerG1AngleRad is the worst angle at the edge ends, where the adjacent boundary curves fix the surface) - read them, and run check_continuity for a full audit. The corner poles are never moved, so every boundary curve stays exact; at corners shared by two constrained sides the later one wins. Returns the surface id and the boundary deviation.

boundaryIds.description: 3 to 12 nurbs_curve ids forming a closed loop.

color.description: Hex color string #rrggbb, e.g. "#c8553d". Defaults to "#9fb4c7".

layerId.description: Layer id to assign the entity to. Defaults to the document default layer.

name.description: Optional display name for the entity (shown in the scene tree).

neighbours.description: Optional G1 / G2 conditions: one entry per loop curve that must continue an existing sheet.

continuity.description: "G1" tangent plane or "G2" tangent plane plus normal curvature across the edge.

curveId.description: One of boundaryIds: the loop curve that lies on an edge of `surfaceId`.

surfaceId.description: Id of the nurbs_surface whose boundary edge is that curve.

position.description: Origin [x, y, z] of the surface in document units; the poles are relative to it. Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

tolerance.description: Largest gap (document units) between consecutive curve ends. Default 1e-6 x the size of the curves.

name: fill_surface

description: Round a single vertex of a polyline with a tangent arc of the given radius. The polyline entity is updated: the vertex at vertexIndex is replaced by two tangent points (one on each adjacent segment), and a new arc entity is added tangent to both segments. vertexIndex is 0-based; for an open polyline valid range is 1 to N-2 (interior vertices only); for a closed polyline any vertex 0 to N-1 is valid. No-op if radius is too large for the adjacent segment lengths, or if the entity is not a polyline.

id.description: Id of the polyline entity to fillet.

radius.description: Fillet radius. Must be > 0.

vertexIndex.description: 0-based index of the polyline vertex to fillet. For open polylines: valid range is 1 to N-2 (interior vertices). For closed polylines: valid range is 0 to N-1.

name: fillet_2d

description: Round (fillet) exact B-rep edges of a 3D solid entity and replace it with a new mesh entity that keeps the exact construction (its brep recipe), so booleans, further fillets and STEP export still see true faces and edges. The source entity is consumed. Select edges with edgeIndices (indices from inspect_topology) and/or edgesNear (points near the edges, robust to parametric edits); with neither, ALL edges are filleted. To give each edge its own radius (optionally varying along the edge) pass edges: [{ index | near, size, sizeEnd?, sizes?, interpolation?, law? }] instead. A radius law runs from size at the start of the edge to sizeEnd at its end, through sizes control points ({ t in (0, 1) along the picked edge, size }): interpolation "smooth" (default) passes one smooth curve through them with zero slope at the ends, "linear" joins them with straight pieces; or law { expression of t in [0, 1] (pi, cos, ...), samples } sampled at uniform t. On a CLOSED edge (a cylinder rim) the law must close on itself (r(0) = r(1), BLD_LAW_NOT_PERIODIC otherwise). A bad value is BLD_LAW_INVALID with the param path; run check_blends afterwards to read the realised radius back. profile { type: "conic", rho } or { type: "curvature", shape } changes the cross-section (conic: rho 0.4142 is the circle at 90 degrees; curvature: zero curvature at both contacts, G2 to planar faces); size2 (+ side1Near | side1Name) makes the blend asymmetric: size and size2 are then the two LEGS (tangent distances from the edge on each face). These are built for straight edges between planar faces that end on flat square faces, with one constant size per edge, and not at a vertex shared by two selected edges (BLD_PROFILE_FAILED says which condition fails); rho / shape outside [0.05, 0.95] is BLD_RHO_RANGE / BLD_SHAPE_RANGE. mode "chord" reads every size as the chord between the two tangent points of the round (planar faces: closed form; any other pair, e.g. a cylinder rim against its cap: the wedge angle sampled along the edge; BLD_CHORD_UNDEFINED where the faces are tangent). Needs the exact kernel (check kernel_info): the OCC kernel (the desktop default; LLULL_KERNEL=occt-native or occt for the CLI and server). With the mesh kernel it no-ops (unchanged doc). Target must be a 3D solid (box, cylinder, sphere, cone, torus, wedge, pyramid, extrusion, revolution, or mesh — including boolean results).

edgeIndices.description: 0-based indices of the unique B-rep edges to fillet, as listed by inspect_topology on the same entity (each edge counted once). Pass [] or omit (with no edgesNear) to fillet ALL edges.

edgeNames.description: Persistent edge names (inspect_topology lists them on the native kernel): recorded automatically from the first pick and used on regeneration, so the same edge is rounded after an upstream edit; a name that is gone or split refuses the step (REF_LOST / REF_SPLIT). Wins over edgeIndices / edgesNear.

edges.description: Per-edge radii: each entry names ONE edge (index, or near = a point on it) and gives its own radius law (size, optional sizeEnd for a linear variation along the edge, optional sizes control points). Edges listed here are rounded in one operation; use it INSTEAD OF radius / radiusEnd / edgeIndices / edgesNear. Differing radii need a kernel that reads radius laws (native OCC); equal ones work everywhere exact.

items.description: One edge with its own radius law.

index.description: 0-based unique-edge index (inspect_topology). Give exactly one of index or near.

interpolation.description: How the radius runs between the control points: "smooth" (default: one smooth curve through them, the kernel interpolation) or "linear" (straight transitions between consecutive points).

law.description: Expression law r(t) instead of size / sizeEnd / sizes. On a closed edge (a rim) r(0) must equal r(1) (periodic law).

expression.description: Radius as an expression of t in [0, 1] (document units), e.g. "1 + 0.5*cos(2*pi*t)". Only t, pi, tau and the built-in functions are allowed; it must be > 0 at every sample.

samples.description: Number of uniform samples of t in [0, 1] the kernel receives (5..257). Default 33.

near.description: A point [x, y, z] in document units on or near the edge (the roundable edge nearest to it is taken). Give exactly one of index or near.

side1Name.description: With size2: persistent face name of side 1 (alternative to side1Near).

side1Near.description: With size2: a point [x, y, z] in document units on the face that carries size (side 1).

size.description: Radius at the START of the edge (document units, > 0); in mode "chord" the chord length instead. Give it unless law is given.

size2.description: Asymmetric blend: the leg on the face NOT named by side1Near / side1Name (document units, > 0); size is then the leg on side 1. Needs a straight edge between two planar faces (BLD_PROFILE_FAILED otherwise); the section is the elliptic quarter of the circle unless profile says otherwise.

sizeEnd.description: Optional radius at the END of the edge (> 0, document units); the radius goes from size to sizeEnd (kernel smooth transition, flattened at both ends; interpolation "linear" makes it straight). Omit for a constant radius.

sizes.description: Optional interior control points the radius passes through (variable-radius law); needs a kernel that reads radius laws.

t.description: Relative position along the picked edge (0 = its start, 1 = its end), strictly inside (0, 1), increasing.

edgesNear.description: Select edges by location: each point picks the roundable edge nearest to it (distance to the edge curve, so any point on an edge, e.g. its visible corner on a drawing, selects it). Prefer this in parametric models: the feature history keeps the points, so the same edge is re-selected after an upstream edit renumbers edges. Combines with edgeIndices.

items.description: A point [x, y, z] in document units near the edge to fillet (e.g. its mid point from inspect_topology).

id.description: Id of the 3D solid entity to fillet. Must exist and be a 3D solid kind.

mode.description: "radius" (default): sizes are radii. "chord": sizes (radius, radiusEnd, edges[].size...) are the CHORD length between the two tangent points of the round on the faces at the edge; converted per edge to r = c / (2 cos(theta / 2)) for planar faces meeting at wedge angle theta (a right-angle edge: r = c / sqrt 2); other face pairs use the wedge angle sampled along the edge. Needs an exact kernel.

profile.description: Cross-section of the blend. conic and curvature profiles are built for STRAIGHT edges between two PLANAR faces that end on flat faces square to them, with a constant size (BLD_PROFILE_FAILED says what else is not built); sizing is by radius (the contact lines of the circular fillet of that radius) or by legs (size2).

rho.description: conic: shoulder ratio in [0.05, 0.95], dimensionless: the section is the rational quadratic between the contact points and the corner with weight rho / (1 - rho). 0.4142 (sqrt 2 - 1) is a circle at a 90 degree edge, 0.5 a parabola, below it flatter, above it fuller.

shape.description: curvature: fraction in [0.05, 0.95], dimensionless, of the way from each contact point to the corner at which the section leaves the face; larger is fuller.

type.description: "circular" (default: the rolling ball, G1 to the faces), "conic" (needs rho) or "curvature" (needs shape: zero curvature at both contacts, G2 to planar faces).

radius.description: Fillet radius in document units. Must be > 0. Required unless edges is given (then each entry carries its own size).

radiusEnd.description: Variable fillet: radius at the END of each selected edge (> 0), document units; the radius varies from radius at the edge start to radiusEnd (the kernel smooth transition, flattened at both ends; use edges[] with interpolation "linear" for a straight one). Omit for a constant radius. Not allowed on a closed edge unless equal to radius (BLD_LAW_NOT_PERIODIC).

name: fillet_edge

description: Blend two sets of faces of a 3D solid that need not share an edge (a rolling ball of radius `radius` touching both, tangent to each) and replace the solid by the result; the faces between the contact lines (e.g. a chamfer between two walls) are consumed (data.consumedFaces lists them, data.blends the new blend face). facesA / facesB pick faces by points on them (near) and/or persistent names. Alternatively holdLine { id of a drawn line or polyline lying on one of the two faces, onFaces "A" | "B" } rounds the edge the two faces share with the radius that makes the blend leave that face on the drawn curve (radius = distance to the edge / tan(fold / 2), fold = angle between the outward normals); a conic / curvature profile with a hold line follows the profile rules (a varying radius is BLD_PROFILE_FAILED). profile { type: "conic", rho } or { type: "curvature", shape } changes the section. This kernel build blends ONE planar face per set that end on flat faces square to the blend; BLD_FACE_FILLET_NO_SOLUTION says when no ball of that radius stays in the material (and the smallest radius that does), BLD_FACE_BLEND_UNSUPPORTED what else is not built. Needs the exact native kernel (check kernel_info); with the mesh kernel it no-ops. Run check_blends afterwards.

facesA.description: First face set (one planar face in this build).

names.description: Persistent face names (inspect_topology): recorded automatically from the first pick and used on regeneration; a name that is gone or split refuses the step (REF_LOST / REF_SPLIT). Win over near.

near.description: Points on the faces of the set; each picks the face it lies on (inspect_faces lists faces and centres).

items.description: A point [x, y, z] in document units on the face (the face nearest to it is taken; it must be on the solid).

facesB.description: Second face set (one planar face in this build); must not share a face with facesA.

names.description: Persistent face names (inspect_topology): recorded automatically from the first pick and used on regeneration; a name that is gone or split refuses the step (REF_LOST / REF_SPLIT). Win over near.

near.description: Points on the faces of the set; each picks the face it lies on (inspect_faces lists faces and centres).

items.description: A point [x, y, z] in document units on the face (the face nearest to it is taken; it must be on the solid).

holdLine.description: Hold line: the blend leaves face set `onFaces` on this drawn curve. facesA and facesB must share an edge.

id.description: Id of a drawn line or polyline (draw_polyline) lying on the face; its points are in the plane of that face.

onFaces.description: Which set the curve lies on: "A" (facesA) or "B" (facesB).

id.description: Id of the 3D solid entity to blend. Must exist and be a 3D solid kind.

profile.description: Cross-section of the blend. conic and curvature profiles are built for STRAIGHT edges between two PLANAR faces that end on flat faces square to them, with a constant size (BLD_PROFILE_FAILED says what else is not built); sizing is by radius (the contact lines of the circular fillet of that radius) or by legs (size2).

rho.description: conic: shoulder ratio in [0.05, 0.95], dimensionless: the section is the rational quadratic between the contact points and the corner with weight rho / (1 - rho). 0.4142 (sqrt 2 - 1) is a circle at a 90 degree edge, 0.5 a parabola, below it flatter, above it fuller.

shape.description: curvature: fraction in [0.05, 0.95], dimensionless, of the way from each contact point to the corner at which the section leaves the face; larger is fuller.

type.description: "circular" (default: the rolling ball, G1 to the faces), "conic" (needs rho) or "curvature" (needs shape: zero curvature at both contacts, G2 to planar faces).

radius.description: Radius of the rolling ball in document units (> 0). Give exactly one of radius or holdLine.

name: fillet_faces

description: Full round of a rib or wall top: replace the center face by a half-cylinder tangent to the two side faces (radius = half the distance between them, document units) and to where the center face was, and replace the solid by the result. side1 / side2 are the two parallel faces facing away from each other, center the face between them (all picked by points on them and/or persistent names); the center face is consumed (data.consumedFaces). This kernel build rounds ONE planar face per set, the center exactly as wide as the gap between the sides and the rib ending on flat faces square to it; BLD_FULL_ROUND_NOT_OPPOSED / BLD_FULL_ROUND_NO_SOLUTION / BLD_FACE_BLEND_UNSUPPORTED say what is not met. Needs the exact native kernel (check kernel_info); with the mesh kernel it no-ops. Run check_blends afterwards (radius, tangency).

center.description: The face between the sides that the round consumes (one planar face, square to both sides).

names.description: Persistent face names (inspect_topology): recorded automatically from the first pick and used on regeneration; a name that is gone or split refuses the step (REF_LOST / REF_SPLIT). Win over near.

near.description: Points on the faces of the set; each picks the face it lies on (inspect_faces lists faces and centres).

items.description: A point [x, y, z] in document units on the face (the face nearest to it is taken; it must be on the solid).

id.description: Id of the 3D solid entity to round. Must exist and be a 3D solid kind.

names.description: Persistent face names (inspect_topology): recorded automatically from the first pick and used on regeneration; a name that is gone or split refuses the step (REF_LOST / REF_SPLIT). Win over near.

near.description: Points on the faces of the set; each picks the face it lies on (inspect_faces lists faces and centres).

items.description: A point [x, y, z] in document units on the face (the face nearest to it is taken; it must be on the solid).

side2.description: Second side face (one planar face), parallel to side1 and facing away from it.

names.description: Persistent face names (inspect_topology): recorded automatically from the first pick and used on regeneration; a name that is gone or split refuses the step (REF_LOST / REF_SPLIT). Win over near.

near.description: Points on the faces of the set; each picks the face it lies on (inspect_faces lists faces and centres).

items.description: A point [x, y, z] in document units on the face (the face nearest to it is taken; it must be on the solid).

name: fillet_full_round

description: Filter entities by any combination of: kind, layerId, name (exact or substring), tag (exact), bboxMin/bboxMax (legacy overlap), nearPoint (centroid within radius), insideBBox (AABB fully inside), overlapsBBox (AABB intersects), touchingId (bbox touches another entity), nameFuzzy (case-insensitive substring on name), tagFuzzy (case-insensitive substring on any tag). All supplied filters are AND-ed. Returns matched entity descriptors (id, kind, layerId, name, tags) in result.data. Does NOT modify the document.

bboxMax.description: World-space maximum corner [x, y, z] of a bounding box filter. Must be provided together with bboxMin. Only entities whose world-space AABB overlaps this box are returned.

bboxMin.description: World-space minimum corner [x, y, z] of a bounding box filter. Must be provided together with bboxMax. Only entities whose world-space AABB overlaps this box are returned.

insideBBox.description: Spatial filter: return only entities whose world-space AABB is FULLY inside the given box. Provide as [[minX,minY,minZ],[maxX,maxY,maxZ]]. min must be <= max on every axis.

kind.description: Filter by entity kind. One of: "box", "cylinder", "sphere", "extrusion", "mesh", "cone", "torus", "wedge", "pyramid", "revolution", "sweep", "loft", "subdivision", "line", "polyline", "arc", "circle", "rectangle", "point", "ellipse", "spline", "text", "dimension", "image", "nurbs_curve", "instance". Omit to match all kinds.

layerId.description: Filter by layer id. Only entities assigned to this layer are returned. Omit to match all layers.

name.description: Filter by entity name. By default performs a case-insensitive substring match. Set nameExact:true for a case-sensitive exact match. Omit to match all names.

nameExact.description: When true, the name filter requires an exact case-sensitive match instead of a substring match. Default: false.

nameFuzzy.description: Fuzzy name filter: case-insensitive substring match on entity name. Matches any entity whose name contains this string. Omit to skip this filter.

nearPoint.description: Spatial filter: return only entities whose bbox centroid is within `radius` units (3D euclidean) of `point`. Provide as { "point": [x, y, z], "radius": number }. radius must be > 0.

point.description: World-space origin [x, y, z] of the proximity search.

radius.description: Maximum distance from point to entity centroid. Must be > 0.

overlapsBBox.description: Spatial filter: return only entities whose world-space AABB INTERSECTS the given box. Provide as [[minX,minY,minZ],[maxX,maxY,maxZ]]. min must be <= max on every axis.

touchingId.description: Spatial filter: return entities whose world-space AABB overlaps the AABB of the entity with this id. The reference entity itself is excluded from results. The id must exist in the document.

description: Clearance of a hole/shaft fit at operating temperatures. Give explicit limits for the hole and the shaft (nominal diameter and upper/lower deviations in document units, valid at specTemperature) and each part's CTE: a document material (holeMaterial / shaftMaterial = create_material name; a thermalStrain model is preferred, a cte model needs cteBasis[material] = secant with a reference temperature, or instantaneous) or an explicit secant CTE (holeCte / shaftCte with its reference temperature). specTemperature is the temperature the limits apply at and has NO default. Temperatures: `temperatures` (both parts), `range` {min, max, steps}, or per-part `holeTemperatures` + `shaftTemperatures` (same length), each with a unit. D(T) = D_spec (1 + a_sec (T - T_spec)) is applied to every limit diameter. Returns per row min/max clearance in document length units (negative = interference), a status (clearance, interference, interference_possible, clearance_possible), code TMC_FIT_INTERFERENCE / TMC_FIT_LOOSE against the fit intent (derived from the limits at specTemperature unless given), `unverified`, and the formula and CTE sources; every row needs review by a qualified engineer (disposition pending_human on failing rows). Optional `lame` adds contact pressure and hub bore hoop stress (elastic, constant E and nu). Use before approving a mixed-material fit; next: change materials / tolerances, or hand a failing row to a human reviewer.

name: fit_at_temperature

description: Fit a constitutive law to test data and return the model, residuals per test, its stability and (non-linear fits) a convergence report. Linear in the parameters (deterministic exact QR): kind hyper_neo_hooke | hyper_mooney_rivlin | hyper_yeoh | hyper_polynomial | hyper_reduced_polynomial (order 1-3): tests with mode uniaxial | equibiaxial | planar, rows [stretch, nominal stress], xMeasure 'stretch', yMeasure 'nominal_stress', units { y: 'MPa' }; the Drucker stability scan is returned (MATL_HYPERELASTIC_UNSTABLE) and a single mode warns MATL_FIT_INSUFFICIENT_MODES. kind ramberg_osgood: one test mode 'uniaxial_plastic', rows [total strain, true stress], fixed { E, nu } (engineering form ε = σ/E + 0.002 (σ/σ0.2)^n). kind visco_prony with fixed { tau: [{value, unit}…] } (relaxation times fixed, weights g_i fitted): one test mode 'relaxation', rows [time, shear modulus]. Levenberg-Marquardt (damping 1e-3 ×10 / ÷10, stop at relative cost change < 1e-12 or 500 iterations, deterministic multi-start unless 'start' is given, 'bounds' per parameter): hyper_ogden (terms 1-3, canonical μ_i, α_i, positive μ_i by default) and hyper_arruda_boyce on the hyperelastic tests; visco_prony without fixed.tau (terms, free times); ramberg_osgood with form 'true_stress' (E ε = σ + α (|σ|/σ0)^(n−1) σ, fixed { E, nu, sigma0 }); j2_voce and j2_chaboche on rows [equivalent plastic strain, true stress] (chaboche: fixed.yieldStress, terms); creep_garofalo on mode 'creep_rate' rows [stress, temperature, rate] with units { x, T, y }. data.convergence = { converged, stop, iterations, evaluations, starts, cost, conditionNumber, parameters[] }. Refusals: MATL_FIT_DID_NOT_CONVERGE, MATL_FIT_ILL_CONDITIONED (Jacobian condition > 1e8), MATL_FIT_START_INVALID. Objective absolute (default, named) or relative. Nothing is added to the document: pass data.model with data.validity, basis and fit to add_material_model. Output is unverified until a data source is given and a reviewer accepts it.

bounds.description: Non-linear fits: [lower, upper] per parameter name (null keeps that side of the named default bound).

dataSource.description: Where the rows come from (absent ⇒ unverified).

fixed.description: Fixed values as {value, unit}: ramberg_osgood { E, nu } (+ sigma0 for true_stress); visco_prony { tau: [{value, unit}…] } fits g_i only, omit tau (and give terms) to fit the times too, G0? when the t = 0 row is absent; j2_chaboche { yieldStress }; creep_garofalo { activationEnergy? } (omit to fit it from several temperatures).

form.description: ramberg_osgood only: 'engineering' (default) ε = σ/E + 0.002 (σ/σ0.2)^n by linear regression; 'true_stress' E ε = σ + α (|σ|/σ0)^(n−1) σ by Levenberg-Marquardt (fixed.sigma0 required).

kind.description: Law to fit.

objective.description: Residual weighting: 'absolute' nominal-stress residual (default, named) or 'relative'.

positive.description: hyper_ogden: require every shear term μ_i ≥ 0 (default true, named); false allows negative terms.

start.description: Non-linear fits: starting values by parameter name in kernel units (MPa, s, 1/MPa, J/mol), all of them. Replaces the deterministic multi-start. Names: hyper_ogden mu1…, alpha1…; hyper_arruda_boyce mu, lambdaM; visco_prony g1…, tau1…; ramberg_osgood true_stress alpha, n; j2_voce sigmaY, Q, b; j2_chaboche C1…, gamma1…; creep_garofalo A, alpha, n, activationEnergy.

terms.description: Number of terms of the non-linear series: hyper_ogden 1-3, j2_chaboche 1-10, visco_prony with free relaxation times 1-20.

mode.description: uniaxial | equibiaxial | planar (hyperelastic), uniaxial_plastic (ramberg_osgood, j2_voce, j2_chaboche), relaxation (visco_prony), creep_rate (creep_garofalo).

rows.description: Rows [x, y] (creep_rate: [stress, temperature, rate]); at most 10 000 over all tests.

units.description: Units of the columns: { y: 'MPa' } (and x for time: { x: 's' }; creep_rate: { x: 'MPa', T: 'K', y: '1/s' }).

validity.description: Validity to attach (default: the stretch / strain / time range of the data).

data.description: [min, max] of the data the parameters were derived from.

equation.description: [min, max] the source allows (⊇ data; default = data).

unit.description: Unit of the bounds, e.g. 'K', '1/s', '1'.

variable.description: State variable the range applies to: T, strainRate, time, equivalentPlasticStrain, stretch …

name: fit_material_model

description: Read-only: fit a plane, cylinder or sphere to the cloud points of a region (native seeded RANSAC on PCA-oriented points, then Levenberg-Marquardt on the orthogonal distance, inliers re-selected until stable). data: the parameters in document units and frame, inliers, rms, coverageDeg (cylinder / sphere; below 60 deg: SCN_FIT_LOW_COVERAGE, unverified), covariance (SI), std and crlb, the named threshold, warnings, and for a cylinder an `extraction` ready for commit_asbuilt_extraction. Same seed = same result. For circles in a section use slice_cloud fit=circle.

cloudId.description: Id of an attached cloud (affected[0] of attach_point_cloud, e.g. "cloud-1.1").

distanceThreshold.description: Explicit inlier band in document units (default 3 x noiseSigma, else 2.5 x the median point spacing).

kind.description: Primitive to fit.

noiseSigma.description: Scanner noise sigma in document units, when known: inlier band 3 sigma and the CRLB at sigma.

normalThresholdDeg.description: Largest angle between a point normal and the model normal for an inlier, degrees (default 20).

kind.description: Every point of the cloud.
Axis-aligned box in document units.
Sphere around a seed point.

radius.description: Radius in document units, > 0.

kind.description: A crop box from set_scan_crop (keep "inside").

seed.description: RANSAC seed (default 1); same seed = same result (AF-13).

name: fit_primitive

description: Fit a property law to measured rows [x, y, weight?] (at most 10 000): polynomial (degree, y vs x), log10Polynomial (NIST form, log10 y vs log10 x), arrhenius (ln y vs 1/T, x must be an absolute temperature), powerLaw (ln y vs ln x) or table1d (interpolating table). Householder QR on a scaled basis; residuals on the original y (RMS, max |r|, max |r/y|, R²); PROP_FIT_POOR above maxRelResidual (default 0.05). Returns a model that define_property_model accepts unchanged (validity = the data range, basis default unspecified ⇒ unverified until a data source is given and a reviewer accepts it). Read-only.

dataSource.description: Where the rows come from (absent ⇒ unverified).

id.description: Id of the fitted model.

objective.description: Residual weighting (default: the one the form linearises).

property.description: Catalogue property of the fitted model.

temperatureExponent.description: Fixed exponent m of arrhenius y = A T^m exp(−Q/(R T)) (default 0).

name: fit_property_model

description: Frame the entire document in the camera so all entities are visible. direction presets the viewing angle: "front" (eye at -Y looking along +Y), "back" (looking along -Y), "right" (looking along -X), "left" (looking along +X), "top" (overhead +Z), "bottom" (below -Z), "iso" (isometric, default), "current" (keep existing azimuth/polar, only adjust distance and target). padding multiplies the computed distance so geometry has breathing room (default 1.2). When the document is empty a default view is applied with an explanatory summary. Does NOT add to feature history.

direction.description: Viewing direction preset. One of: front, back, left, right, top, bottom, iso, current. Defaults to "iso". "current" keeps the existing azimuth and polar; only target and distance change.

padding.description: Scale factor applied to the computed distance so geometry is not edge-clipped. Default 1.2. Values < 1 crop the view; > 2 shows it very small. Must be > 0.

name: fit_view

description: DATA form of the flat pattern (same pattern as materialize_flat_pattern = 2D entities and export_flat_pattern_dxf = DXF file): compute the analytic flat pattern of a sheet-metal part (BA = theta*(R+K*T) added at every bend, unfolded from the base flat) without changing the document. Returns data { extents [x, y], area, outline (vertices, bounded), bends[] with angleDeg, insideRadius, direction up/down, ba, bd, ossb and the K-factor used with its source, joggles[] with allowance/run/inclinedStraight, hems[] (add_hem: gap, returnLeg, developedLength = pi*(gap/2+K*T)+leg, unverified model; a hem bend has ossb/bd null), formingNotes[] (beads are excluded from the pattern; a flanged hole is developed to an approximate, unverified cut diameter), provenance (formulas, inputs, sources), unverified + unverifiedInputs, reviewRequired }. Lengths are in the document length unit, angles in degrees. The result is computed by llull, not approved: a qualified person must review it. Refusal: FTR_PART_NOT_FOUND, FTR_NON_DEVELOPABLE. Next: export_flat_pattern_dxf, materialize_flat_pattern, check_sheet_metal.

id.description: Sheet-metal part id (returned by add_sheet_metal_base).

name: flat_pattern

description: Lay a straight 3D solid or mesh along a NURBS curve: the body axis (frame z, default the longest bounding-box direction, starting at the body start) is mapped onto the curve by arc length, the cross-section follows the curve frame (N and B perpendicular to the tangent), so a straight bar becomes a bar running along the curve with its length kept (stretch true scales it to the curve length instead). The frame x and y of the body become the curve normal and binormal; orientation "minimal" (default) uses the twist-free rotation-minimising frame, "fixed_up" keeps the normal toward the up vector (world z by default). On a circular arc this equals bend_body. Beyond the end of a shorter curve the body continues straight. Use it for hoses, rails, handrails and trim along a path. targetId is a nurbs_curve entity (create_nurbs_curve, interpolate_curve, add_helix, ...). The result replaces the entity as a mesh entity that keeps the construction (brep recipe). Refuses a missing or non-curve targetId (DEF_CURVE_NOT_FOUND), a zero-length curve or an up vector parallel to the tangent (DEF_CURVE_INVALID), and a body wider than the radius of curvature on the inside of the path (DEF_FOLDOVER, with the sampled min det J). Then call analyze_deformation and check_deformation.

frame.description: Body frame; every field defaults from the body bounds and the defaults used are reported in data.frame.

axis.description: Direction of the body axis (the straight base), unitless (normalised). Default: the longest bounding-box direction.

origin.description: A point of the body axis, world document units. Default: the centre of the face where the body starts along the axis.

reference.description: Direction that becomes the curve normal, unitless; must not be parallel to axis. Default: the next longest direction.

id.description: Id of the 3D solid or mesh entity to deform (describe_scene lists ids). It is replaced by the deformed mesh entity (keepSource keeps it).

ids.description: Ids of several 3D solids or meshes to deform with the same parameters (one feature step; every body gets its own frame and region defaults from its own bounds). Use this or id.

keepSource.description: true: keep the original entity(ies) next to the deformed one(s) instead of replacing them. Default false.

orientation.description: Frame along the curve: "minimal" (default, rotation-minimising, no twist) or "fixed_up" (normal toward the up vector).

output.description: How the result is computed: kernel choice and mesh tolerance.

mode.description: "auto" (default): the exact kernel builds the result when it can evaluate this deformation (the native kernel does for every law: the faces become B-splines fitted within output.tolerance), else the mesh path runs and the summary says so; "exact": refuse (DEF_EXACT_UNAVAILABLE) unless the exact kernel built it; "mesh": force the faceted mesh path.

preserveAnalytic.description: Recognise cylinders, cones and planes in an exact result (needs the exact warp of a later milestone; true is refused today).

tolerance.description: Largest deviation of the result from the true deformed surface, document units, > 0: the chordal deviation of the mesh path, or the fit error of the B-spline faces and edges on the exact path (a smaller value costs control points, not accuracy). Default: 1e-5 times the body bounding-box diagonal, clamped to [1e-6, 0.01].

stretch.description: true: scale the body length to the curve length (arc length ratio = curve length / body length). Default false: the length is kept.

targetId.description: Id of the nurbs_curve entity the body flows along (describe_scene lists ids). The body axis starts at the curve start.

up.description: Up vector for orientation "fixed_up", unitless; must not be parallel to the curve tangent anywhere. Default [0, 0, 1].

name: flow_along_curve

description: Wrap a body designed flat (a plate, an embossed logo, a rib) onto a curved target surface. The base is a plane (origin, normal, uDirection): the body x axis is uDirection, y is normal x uDirection, w is the offset along the normal. The point (x, y, w) goes to S(u*, v*) + w N(u*, v*) on the target, where x and y are ARC LENGTHS on the target measured from targetOrigin along the surface direction closest to targetUDirection (x) and the perpendicular one (y), and N is the target normal (a face of a solid: pointing out of the solid; a sheet: S_u x S_v, reversed by flipNormal). Lengths are kept along both directions at the origin; the material is stretched or squeezed by (R + w) / R on a cylinder of radius R (a plate W x H x t laid outside a drum has volume W H (t + t^2 / (2 R)), about 4 percent more than flat for t 2, R 30). target is {sheetId} (a nurbs_surface, any kernel) or {entityId, faceNear} (the face of a solid nearest to the world point faceNear; needs the native exact kernel). The result replaces the entity as a mesh entity that keeps the construction (brep recipe). Refuses a missing or unusable target (DEF_FLOW_TARGET_INVALID), a face without the exact kernel (DEF_TARGET_FACE_NEEDS_KERNEL), a body that leaves the target (DEF_FLOW_OUTSIDE_BASE), a body longer than the closed circumference of the target (DEF_FLOW_OVERLAP) and a body reaching inside the radius of curvature (DEF_FOLDOVER). Then call analyze_deformation and check_deformation.

base.description: The flat reference the body is laid out on: a plane. (A curved base sheet is not supported.)

plane.description: The base plane: origin, normal and uDirection.

normal.description: Normal of the base plane, unitless (normalised): the direction of the offset w. The body sits on its positive side to be laid outside the target.

origin.description: A point of the base plane, world document units (the body x, y are measured from it).

uDirection.description: Direction of the body x axis in the plane, unitless; its component perpendicular to normal is used.

flipNormal.description: true: put the body on the other side of a sheet target (reverses N). Default false; a face target always uses the outward side.

id.description: Id of the 3D solid or mesh entity to deform (describe_scene lists ids). It is replaced by the deformed mesh entity (keepSource keeps it).

ids.description: Ids of several 3D solids or meshes to deform with the same parameters (one feature step; every body gets its own frame and region defaults from its own bounds). Use this or id.

keepSource.description: true: keep the original entity(ies) next to the deformed one(s) instead of replacing them. Default false.

output.description: How the result is computed: kernel choice and mesh tolerance.

mode.description: "auto" (default): the exact kernel builds the result when it can evaluate this deformation (the native kernel does for every law: the faces become B-splines fitted within output.tolerance), else the mesh path runs and the summary says so; "exact": refuse (DEF_EXACT_UNAVAILABLE) unless the exact kernel built it; "mesh": force the faceted mesh path.

preserveAnalytic.description: Recognise cylinders, cones and planes in an exact result (needs the exact warp of a later milestone; true is refused today).

tolerance.description: Largest deviation of the result from the true deformed surface, document units, > 0: the chordal deviation of the mesh path, or the fit error of the B-spline faces and edges on the exact path (a smaller value costs control points, not accuracy). Default: 1e-5 times the body bounding-box diagonal, clamped to [1e-6, 0.01].

target.description: The surface the body is wrapped onto: a sheet, or a face of a solid.

entityId.description: Id of a solid whose face is the target (needs the native exact kernel). Give with faceNear.

faceNear.description: World point near the wanted face of entityId; the nearest face is used.

sheetId.description: Id of a nurbs_surface entity to flow onto. Give this or entityId with faceNear.

targetOrigin.description: World point on the target that the base origin goes to (its projection onto the target is used). Default: the point of the target nearest to the base origin.

targetUDirection.description: World direction on the target that the body x axis follows (its tangent component picks the iso-direction). Default: the base uDirection.

name: flow_on_surface

description: Read-only frontal (projected) area of 3D solids seen along the flow direction — the reference area A of drag D = ½ρV²·Cd·A — plus the wetted (surface) area for skin friction and the body length along the flow. Overlapping parts count once (silhouette union by rasterisation; `uncertaintyM2` = half the boundary cells). Lengths are converted from the document units to metres. Default flow direction [1, 0, 0]. Use for a cyclist + bike model, a fuselage, a car or any assembly; then compute_aero_drag { cd, entityIds } or road_load_power.

entityIds.description: Ids of the 3D solids / instances to project.

flowDirection.description: Direction the air moves relative to the body [x, y, z] (any length, not zero). Default [1, 0, 0]: a body moving along -x.

resolution.description: Silhouette grid cells along its larger extent, 50..2000. Default 400 (area error ~ ±0.5 %).

name: frontal_area

description: Read-only cross-section of a fuselage made by loft_fuselage, cut by the plane FS = `fs` of the aircraft frame (set_aircraft_frame; default FS along +x). Measured on the exact skin, not on a mesh. Returns, in aircraft coordinates and document units: halfBreadth (half the BL extent), crownWl (highest WL), keelWl (lowest WL), wlMaxBreadth (WL where the section is widest), area (document units squared) and perimeter, plus a closed cubic `curve` (degree and poles [fs, bl, wl]) through 128 points of the section. At an apex (point station) the area is 0 and `curve` is null. Reference: a circle station of radius 2 gives area 12.566 and perimeter 12.566. `bodyId` is the id returned by loft_fuselage.

bodyId.description: Id of the fuselage (the nurbs_surface id returned by loft_fuselage).

fs.description: Fuselage station of the cutting plane, document units; within the first and last station of the body.

name: fuselage_section_at

description: Generate the plies of a composite part from its zones (define_zone). The thickest zone gives the master stack; every other zone stack must embed in it (same angles in the same order, symmetric halves matched from both ends): otherwise the command is refused and names the two zones (CMP_ZONES_NOT_BLENDABLE; equally thick zones must be identical). Each master ply covers the union of the zones that contain it, extended by a ramp: at every thickness step the k-th dropped ply ends k * max(plyThickness * rampRatio, minStagger) beyond the full-thickness boundary (set_ply_drop_rules; default ramp 20:1, inner plies end first). A ramp that does not fit before the next zone boundary is refused (CMP_RAMP_CONFLICT with needed vs available length). Where a thick zone overlaps a thinner one it must have the higher priority. Plies are named "<sequencePrefix><n>" (default "S", n = 1-based position from the tool side) and carry the same sequence label. Existing generated plies need replaceGenerated true. Ends with check_laminate_rules / check_layup.

material.description: Lamina material name used by every generated ply (its plyThickness drives the ramps).

replaceGenerated.description: Remove plies generated earlier (not manual ones) and generate again; default false.

sequencePrefix.description: Prefix of ply names and sequence labels; default "S".

name: generate_plies_from_zones

description: Compute the CAx-IF geometric validation properties of 3D solids: volume, surface area, centre of volume (centroid) and bounding box, in document units (volume in units^3, area in units^2). These are the values export_step_ap242 embeds in a STEP file and verify_exchange_file compares with what a sender embedded. method says how each was integrated: brep (exact kernel B-rep), closed-form (analytic primitive) or mesh (triangles; less exact). Use mass_properties for mass and inertia from a material density, measure_bounding_box for the bounding box alone. Instances are reported under assemblies (all their solids combined, world placement applied). Does not modify the document.

entityIds.description: Ids of the solids or instances to measure. Omit or pass [] for every 3D entity of the document.

includeAssemblies.description: Report component instances as combined assemblies (volume, area, centroid of all their solids). Default true.

name: geometric_validation_properties

description: Read a material: its record (designation, temper, form, specs, licence, export marking, superseded, library origin), every stored value (density, moduli, allowables) with unit, basis, direction, thickness / e/D / temperature condition, provenance and whether it is unverified, which value is preferred, and the density mass_properties would use. A material made with create_material is legacy: density basis unspecified, provenance legacy. A private-library record without values on this machine says unresolved. Next: get_material_allowable.

material.description: Material id (create_material name or record id).

name: get_material

description: Read one design value of a material for the EXACT key (property, basis, direction, thickness, e/D, temperature): e.g. Ftu, basis A, L, 0.050 in. A basis is never substituted: when none matches, data.available is false and data.candidates lists the values that exist (MAT_ALLOWABLE_NOT_AVAILABLE). Without temperature the room-temperature value is returned; with temperature the temperature table is interpolated linearly and refused outside its range (MAT_TEMPERATURE_OUT_OF_RANGE, no extrapolation). Every value carries basis, provenance, unverified / unverifiedReasons and reviewRequired: true: an engineer must review it. forCertification: true refuses superseded sources (MAT_SOURCE_SUPERSEDED) and typical / supplier_unstated / unspecified values (MAT_VALUE_UNVERIFIED). Add values with set_material_property.

basis.description: Required basis: A, B, S, typical, supplier_unstated, company, unspecified. Never substituted.

direction.description: Direction of the value (L, LT, ST, …); omit or isotropic for a direction-free value.

edOverD.description: Bearing edge-distance ratio e/D (1.5 or 2.0) for Fbru / Fbry.

forCertification.description: Refuse superseded sources and unverified values (default false).

property.description: Property: Ftu, Fty, Fcy, Fsu, Fbru, Fbry, E, Ec, G, nu, density, elongation, cte, k, cp.

temperature.description: Temperature for a temperature-dependent value; omit for the room-temperature value.

unit.description: Temperature: unit, e.g. 'in', 'mm', 'degF', 'degC', 'K'.

thickness.description: Thickness the value must cover; needed for a value tabulated per thickness range.

unit.description: Product thickness: unit, e.g. 'in', 'mm', 'degF', 'degC', 'K'.
Unit of the answer (default: the stored unit), e.g. 'MPa'.

name: get_material_allowable

description: Create a named group containing >= 2 existing entities. The group id is returned in affected. Entities are not moved or changed.

ids.description: Array of entity ids to include in the group. Must contain >= 2 ids that exist in the document.

name.description: Optional human-readable label for the group, e.g. "Wheel assembly". Defaults to "Group".

name: group_entities

description: Closed-form (hand-calculation) reference values to sanity-check a finite-element or explicit-dynamics result; pure, reads no document. STRUCTURAL checks (N-mm-t-s units: mm, N, MPa, tonne/mm^3, Hz): cantilever_frequency | cantilever | ss_beam | euler_column | ss_plate_buckling | kirsch_kt. cantilever: End-loaded cantilever of rectangular section (Euler-Bernoulli, optional Timoshenko shear term). Inputs: P_N [N], L_mm [mm], E_MPa [MPa], b_mm [mm], h_mm [mm]; optional: nu [1]. cantilever_frequency: Natural frequency of the n-th bending mode of a clamped-free beam of rectangular section (both principal planes). Inputs: E_MPa [MPa], rho_t_per_mm3 [t/mm^3], b_mm [mm], h_mm [mm], L_mm [mm]; optional: mode [1]. ss_beam: Simply supported beam of rectangular section under a central point load and / or a uniform load (maxima at mid-span). Inputs: L_mm [mm], E_MPa [MPa], b_mm [mm], h_mm [mm]; optional: P_N [N], w_N_per_mm [N/mm]; at least one of P_N / w_N_per_mm. euler_column: Euler critical load of a prismatic column of rectangular section for a stated effective-length factor. Inputs: L_mm [mm], E_MPa [MPa], b_mm [mm], h_mm [mm], K [1]; optional: none. ss_plate_buckling: Uniaxial compressive buckling stress of a simply supported rectangular plate. Inputs: E_MPa [MPa], nu [1], t_mm [mm], a_mm [mm], b_mm [mm]; optional: none. kirsch_kt: Kirsch solution: circular hole in an infinite plate under remote uniaxial tension (gross stress concentration Kt = 3). Inputs: none; optional: S_MPa [MPa], y_over_a [1], theta_deg [deg]. Returns data { check, inputs, results [{ name, value, unit, formula }], assumptions, sources, comparison }. Pass compare { quantity, value } with the FE number (quantity = one result name) to get the relative difference; with toleranceRel it also says withinTolerance. Typical use: compare analysis_report probe / frequency / buckling values with the matching closed form (an FE result more than a few percent off a beam formula usually means a mesh, constraint or unit problem). The formulas are idealised (see assumptions): they bound, they do not substantiate. EXPLICIT-DYNAMICS checks (SI, unit-suffixed keys; compare does not apply): wave_speed (E_Pa, nu, rho_kg_m3 -> c0, cd), critical_time_step (+ L_e_m -> dt = L_e/cd), mass_scaling (+ dt_target_s -> scaled density and added-mass ratio), bar_impact (E_Pa, rho_kg_m3, v_m_s, L_m, optional sigma_y_Pa -> wall stress rho c0 v, two-bar stress, contact duration 2L/c0, yield velocity), johnson_cook_flow (A_Pa, B_Pa, n, C, m, eps_p, rate_per_s, ref_rate_per_s, optional T_K, Tm_K, Tr_K; the rate term is clamped at the reference rate), johnson_cook_failure (D1..D5, triaxiality = mean stress / von Mises, rate_per_s, ref_rate_per_s, optional temperatures); returns data { check, values, formula, inputs }, screening only. Thermal and engine hand checks are separate tools: thermal_analytic_check, thermal_stress_check, engine_quick_check.

check.description: Which closed-form case to evaluate (structural or explicit-dynamics; see the description).

compare.description: Structural checks only: compare one FE number with the closed-form result.

quantity.description: Name of one result of the check, e.g. "tip_deflection_mm".

toleranceRel.description: Acceptable relative difference (e.g. 0.02 for 2 %); sets comparison.withinTolerance.

value.description: The finite-element value, in the unit of that result.

inputs.description: Named numeric inputs of the check; the unit is in the key suffix (structural e.g. { "P_N": 9, "L_mm": 8, "E_MPa": 210000, "b_mm": 1, "h_mm": 1 }; explicit e.g. { "E_Pa": 2.1e11, "nu": 0.3, "rho_kg_m3": 7800 }).

name: hand_check

description: List the holes of a part as a table for drawings: one row per hole with its label (H1, H2, ... in table order), position x, y from the top-left corner of its face (x along the face, y downwards, document length units), kind (simple, counterbore, countersink, counterdrill), diameter, countersink diameter / included angle in degrees / depth, counterbore diameter / depth, blind depth or through, drill point angle with its source (a drill point that was not given is reported as defaulted, 118 degrees, source R8) and tip height, and the cosmetic thread, and at = the hole centre [x, y, z] in world coordinates (to mark it on the model). Holes come from add_hole, or are recognised from the B-rep of an imported solid when the kernel is exact (without a kernel only authored holes are listed, otherwise FTR_NEEDS_EXACT_KERNEL). Rows are sorted by face, then y, then x. Pass origin to measure from another datum of the face frame. Lengths in the document length unit, angles in degrees. The table is returned in data = { origin, rows } plus the unit, provenance and reviewRequired (computed by llull, not approved).

id.description: Id of the 3D solid.

origin.description: Datum [u, v] in the face frame, in document length units, replacing the default top-left corner of each face.

name: hole_table

description: Turn the holes recognised on an exact 3D solid (an imported STEP part, see recognize_features) into a build_project plan of add_hole steps: data.actions, one step per group of identical holes (same kind, diameters, depth, drill point and entrance plane) with their world positions. The first step cuts into `stock`, the entity or "$alias" you will drill (a plain stock whose faces contain the hole entrances); each next step cuts into the previous result. Lengths are in the document length unit, angles in degrees; a blind hole always carries its drill point angle (0 = flat). Holes whose classification is ambiguous are included and listed in data.ambiguous. Needs an exact kernel: otherwise refused with FTR_NEEDS_EXACT_KERNEL (also FTR_PART_NOT_FOUND). Next: build_project with data.actions.

id.description: Id of the 3D solid (mesh with an exact B-rep) whose holes are read.

stock.description: Entity id (or "$alias" of an earlier plan step) of the solid the plan drills; the first add_hole step targets it.

name: holes_from_recognition

description: Hollow a closed mesh (or 3D solid) into a shell of constant wall thickness with a sealed internal cavity (print preparation: saves resin / filament). The cavity is the parallel body at -wallThickness from a signed-distance field, so inward corners stay sharp and the cavity is a clean manifold; the outer surface is kept from the input. Reports data.materialVolume and data.cavityVolume (document units^3). Needs the Manifold engine. A sealed cavity traps material in resin printing: give `drainHoles` ({near, diameter}): each is a cylinder 3 x the wall long along the outward surface normal at the surface point nearest to `near`, subtracted so the cavity opens to the outside (data.drainHoles lists the points; data.cavityOpen). Refusals: MESH_NOT_CLOSED, MESH_PARAM_INVALID, MESH_OFFSET_RESOLUTION, MESH_ENGINE_UNSUPPORTED, MESH_BOOLEAN_FAILED.

drainHoles.description: Drain holes that open the cavity to the outside (up to 16). Default none: the cavity stays sealed.

near.description: Point [x, y, z] (document units, world); the hole is centred on the surface point nearest to it.

id.description: Id of the closed mesh (or other 3D solid) to hollow.

keepSource.description: true: keep the source and add the result as a new mesh. Default false: the source entity is rewritten in place (same id, name, layer, colour).

maxCells.description: Level-set grid cell cap; a finer tolerance than the cap allows refuses with MESH_OFFSET_RESOLUTION. Default 40000.

tolerance.description: Target distance (document units) between a result vertex and the exact surface: the level-set grid edge is set to it. When that needs more cells than maxCells the grid is coarsened to fit and the result reports the weaker bound it really has (data.toleranceMet false, data.errorBound). Default 0.002 x bounding-box diagonal (named default).

wallThickness.description: Wall thickness in document units, measured inward from the outer surface.

name: hollow_mesh

description: Convert points read off an image underlay (pixel coordinates) into model coordinates. Returns `data.world` ([x, y, z] per point) and `data.xy` ([x, y] per point — ready for draw_polyline, extrude_profile or revolve_profile when the underlay lies on the XY plane), plus `data.unitsPerPixel`. Calibrate first (calibrate_underlay) so the numbers are true scale. Image pixel coordinates [px, py]: origin at the TOP-left corner of the picture, +px right, +py DOWN (as read off the image); fractional values are fine.

id.description: Id of the image underlay the pixel coordinates refer to.

points.description: Pixel points [[px, py], …] to convert (1..10000).

items.description: Image pixel coordinates [px, py]: origin at the TOP-left corner of the picture, +px right, +py DOWN (as read off the image); fractional values are fine.

name: image_to_world

description: Measure an implicit body (id from create_implicit_body) or field (id from add_field_primitive / add_tpms_lattice...): volume with an error estimate, mesh area, relative density (volume / region volume; the region defaults to the support box), bounds, number of solid components and enclosed voids (volume and a point inside each). region (a field id) restricts the volume and the density to that region, e.g. the box a lattice fills. Volumes are in document units cubed. Strut lattices use a low-discrepancy quadrature (an aligned grid would alias with the struts).

id.description: Id of an implicit body or of a field node.

region.description: Field id restricting the measure (volume, density). Default: no restriction.

voxel.description: Measure grid spacing in document units. Default: about 2^19 cells over the support box.

name: implicit_properties

description: Import an airfoil from the TEXT of a UIUC-style coordinate file (the CLI reads the file: pass its content as `text`): Selig (upper trailing edge -> leading edge -> lower trailing edge) or Lednicer (counts line, upper LE -> TE, lower LE -> TE); `format` "auto" detects it. The raw points are stored with their sha256 and a cubic NURBS curve is fitted through every point. `normalize` "chord" moves/rotates/scales the section so the leading edge (farthest point from the trailing edge) is at the origin and the trailing edge on +x at 1; "none" (default) keeps the file as is (some files, e.g. naca23012.dat, match their equations only when NOT normalised). `trailingEdge` "keep" (default) or "closed" (refuses a gap above 1e-4 chord). Imported airfoils are UNVERIFIED unless `expectedSha256` of the pinned file matches the text. At most 2000 points.

expectedSha256.description: sha256 (hex) of the pinned source file; when it equals the hash of `text` the airfoil is marked verified.

format.description: File layout. Default "auto" (Lednicer when the first data line holds two counts > 1).

normalize.description: "chord": place LE at the origin and TE midpoint at (1, 0); "none" (default): keep the coordinates.

position.description: Where to place the curve [x, y, z] in document units. Default [0, 0, 0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

source.description: Where the file comes from (URL, database name); stored as provenance.

text.description: Content of the airfoil file (name line, then "x y" pairs; Lednicer files have a counts line "n_upper n_lower").

trailingEdge.description: "closed" requires the trailing-edge gap <= 1e-4 chord; default "keep".

name: import_airfoil

description: Import minimum-bend-radius rows (material, temper, thickness -> minimum inside radius at a bend angle) that check_sheet_metal and sheet_metal_calc match against. Give `rows` (each row states its own units 'mm' or 'in') or `csv` text with the header material,temper,thickness,minInsideRadius,units,bendAngle,source,verification. Every row needs a source (standard/handbook and edition): a row without one refuses the whole import with FTR_TABLE_ROW_NO_SOURCE and the path rows.<i>.source. Rows are 'unverified' unless marked 'verified' (dual-review transcription); results computed from unverified rows are flagged. Rows with the same key replace the earlier ones. Next: create_sheet_metal_rule.

csv.description: CSV text with a header line: material,temper,thickness,minInsideRadius,units,bendAngle,source,verification. Give this OR rows.

rows.description: Radius rows; give this OR csv.

bendAngle.description: Bend angle in degrees the row applies to (AC 43.13-1B Table 4-6 rows apply at 90).

material.description: Material label matching the rule material (text).

minInsideRadius.description: Minimum inside bend radius, in the row's `units` (mm or in).

source.description: Mandatory provenance: standard/handbook and edition (a row without it is refused, FTR_TABLE_ROW_NO_SOURCE).

temper.description: Temper label matching the rule temper (text).

thickness.description: Sheet thickness the row applies to, in the row's `units` (mm or in).

units.description: Unit of thickness and minInsideRadius of this row: 'mm' or 'in'.

verification.description: 'verified' only after dual-review transcription from the cited source; default 'unverified'.

name: import_bend_radius_table

description: Import the composite laminate of a STEP AP242 file written by export_composite_ap242: a composite part (tool surface frame, laminate side, rules), its plies in stacking order with name, sequence, material, orientation (part frame, degrees), rosette and boundary polygons, the rosettes, and the lamina materials the document does not have yet (created with basis "unknown", so every result computed from them is unverified). With importSolids (default) the exact solids of the file (the tool solid and the ply solids) are imported first through import_step_exact and the part is attached to the imported tool solid. The validation properties embedded in the file (the CAx-IF composite validation properties: counts, total ply surface area, orientation values, sequence order, curve lengths, areas per material and rosette; and llull own area of each ply, summed thickness, mass) are recomputed from the rebuilt plies and compared, and the CAx-IF structure of the file (laminate table, sequences, plies, materials, orientation angles, ply pieces) is read back and compared with the plies (properties named "structure: ..."): data.validation lists property, subject, embedded, recomputed, relative difference and band green / yellow / red / not_checkable. Nothing imported is verified: data.reviewRequired is true. Files without llull composite records (from other systems, or the CAx-IF structure alone) are refused with CMP_AP242_NO_COMPOSITE. Give the file as `text` or `stepBase64`. Needs the OCC kernel only when importSolids is true. A ply solid the file lists but the import did not yield under its name, a tool solid that did not import, and a ply solid whose volume differs from ply area x thickness are red findings (reasons solids_unlinked, tool_not_imported, validation_red).

importSolids.description: Import the exact solids of the file (tool and ply solids) with import_step_exact; default true. false builds the part only, with the tool entity id of the file.

name.description: Name of the created part; default the part name in the file.

stepBase64.description: The file as base64 (or give text).

text.description: ISO 10303-21 text of the file (or give stepBase64).

name: import_composite_ap242

description: Import an ASCII DXF drawing (AutoCAD, Civil 3D, BricsCAD, QCAD, survey software exports) as editable 2D entities on their DXF layers: LINE, LWPOLYLINE (bulges as arcs), POLYLINE, ARC, CIRCLE, POINT, TEXT, MTEXT, block INSERTs (exploded) and 3DFACE (one mesh per layer). Elevations are kept as the entity plane height. Units come from $INSUNITS unless `sourceUnit` is given. Binary DXF and DWG are not supported (save as ASCII DXF). For terrain from survey DXFs use import_survey_dxf.

layers.description: Only import these DXF layers (case-insensitive). Default: every layer.

sourceUnit.description: Drawing unit when $INSUNITS is missing or wrong. Default: $INSUNITS, else the document unit.

name: import_dxf

description: Import a fastener catalogue file into the document (bolts, rivets, Hi-Lok pins, nuts and washers are all families). The file is { format: "llull-fastener-catalog", schemaVersion: 1, families: [...] }; each family has id, kind, standard, a part-number grammar (literal / code table / int fields; an int field named diameterDash selects the size), sizes (dash, nominalDiameter, thread, dims such as headDiameter, height, thickness with options), grip / length rules, licence and provenance. Every dimension needs provenance.citation or sourceId and a parsable length unit. Nothing is bundled: the user supplies the dimensions (licence flags travel with the family; licensed-no-redistribution families are refused: FAST_LICENCE_EMBED_FORBIDDEN). Next: list_fastener_families, select_fastener.

catalog.description: The catalogue file object: { format: "llull-fastener-catalog", schemaVersion: 1, title?, families: FastenerFamily[] }.

replace.description: Overwrite families whose id already exists with different content. Default false: such a clash is refused (FAST_CATALOG_CONFLICT).

name: import_fastener_catalog

description: Embed a TrueType (.ttf) or CFF-outline OpenType (.otf) font in the document so text can be turned into outlines (text_outline, extrude_profile, emboss_on_face). Give the file as `base64` (CLI: `file=PATH` or `path=PATH` reads the file and fills it). The font is parsed completely and stored with the document, so a reopened document needs no font file. Refused when the font forbids embedding (OS/2 fsType restricted), is larger than 4 MB, is CFF2 / WOFF / a collection (not supported) or is damaged. The result is `unverified` unless you pass the sha256 of the file as `sourceSha256` and it matches. Importing the same bytes twice returns the first record. Next: add_text with font=<id>, then text_outline. Refusals carry error.code WRP_FONT_PARSE, WRP_FONT_FORMAT_UNSUPPORTED, WRP_FONT_EMBEDDING_RESTRICTED, WRP_FONT_TOO_LARGE.

base64.description: The font file bytes, base64 encoded. The CLI fills it from file=PATH or path=PATH.

blob.description: Recorded by the command itself: the sha256 of the font blob already embedded in the document. Replay reads the bytes from there; give base64 instead.

licence.description: Licence text to record, e.g. "SIL OFL 1.1". Default: the licence string of the font name table, if any.

path.description: Original file path, kept only as provenance text; the CLI also reads the file from it when base64 is absent.

sourceSha256.description: sha256 (hex) you expect the font bytes to have. A match marks the font verified; a mismatch refuses the import.

name: import_font

description: Import an IGES file (<= 5.3, ANS US PRO/IPO-100) as exact B-rep solids: the 3D geometry (trimmed / bounded surfaces, solids, shells) is read, loose faces are sewn into closed shells at max(the file's resolution, 1e-6 x diagonal) and healed into solids, stored like import_step_exact (one mesh entity per solid, content-addressed blob). Lengths are converted from the file unit (Global section; exact factor in data.iges.unitFactor) to the document unit. data.iges lists the entity census, the types no translator reads (annotation, properties: untranslated), open shells that did not close and the sewing tolerance used. IGES has no validation properties, so the bodies are flagged unverified and the report asks for review. Needs the exact OCC kernel with the IGES translator. Give the file as text or igesBase64. Refusals carry error.code KRN_STEP_UNREADABLE, KRN_STEP_NO_SOLID, XCH_WRITER_UNAVAILABLE, KRN_NO_EXACT_KERNEL.

fileName.description: Original file name, kept in the report and provenance only.

heal.description: Run shape healing on every solid. Default true.

igesBase64.description: The IGES file bytes, base64 encoded (ASCII). Give exactly one of text or igesBase64.

name.description: Entity name; several solids get a numeric suffix. Default: none.

sew.description: Sew faces into closed shells. Default true; false keeps only solids the file already holds.

sha256.description: sha256 (hex) of the file bytes computed by the host; kept in the provenance. Default: sha256 of the text.

text.description: The IGES file as text. Give exactly one of text or igesBase64.

name: import_iges

description: Import a material library (format llull-material-library): records with PHY-01 values, each with basis, source, licence and export marking. Give the library object (inline, embedded libraries only), or { libraryId, version, sha256 } for a library file registered on this machine (register_material_library); a licensed library (licensed-no-redistribution) is storage private: it is read from the machine, never copied into the document file, and its records stay unresolved on a machine without the file until resolve_material_libraries. A sha256 that differs from the library content is refused (MAT_LIBRARY_HASH_MISMATCH). Imported records are read-only; assign them with assign_material. Another version of a known library needs replace: true (diff_material_libraries shows what changed).

confirmation.description: Human signature object (with a nonce), required only when replace would LOWER the export marking of the library or of a record (for example ITAR → none). An agent cannot give it: MAT_HUMAN_GATE.

library.description: The library object: { format: "llull-material-library", schemaVersion: 1, id, version, title, licence, exportMarking, storage: "embedded", sources, materials[] }.

libraryId.description: Id of a library file held on this machine (instead of library).

replace.description: Replace an already imported library of the same id (a new version); default false.

sha256.description: Expected content hash. Required with libraryId; optional check with an inline library.

name: import_material_library

description: Create mesh solids from world-space triangle data — the landing point for STEP import and for code-imported shapes that have no analytic llull primitive. Each body becomes one mesh entity (optionally named and coloured). Meshes render, measure and export but have no editable dimensions.

bodies.description: Bodies to create. Each: { positions: [x,y,z, ...] world-space numbers, indices?: [i0,i1,i2, ...] (omit for a triangle soup of 9 numbers per triangle), name?: string, color?: "#rrggbb" }.

name: import_mesh

description: Import a triangle mesh file as mesh entities: STL (ascii or binary), OBJ (polygons are fan-triangulated; groups become faceGroups), PLY (ascii / binary) or 3MF (units from the file). Vertices closer than weldTolerance are welded and the report lists triangles, welded vertices, dropped attributes, open and non-manifold edges and shells. STL, OBJ and PLY carry no unit, so `units` is REQUIRED for them (coordinates are converted once into the document unit). Give the file as `fileKey` (the sha256 of a file kept in the mesh asset store of this machine; the CLI stores `file=PATH` there so the document keeps 64 hex characters, not the file), `base64` or `text` (stored in the document step: small files only). A result over 100000 triangles is kept in the asset store with a display LOD. The result is `unverified` unless you pass the file sha256 as `sourceSha256` and it matches. Next: analyze_mesh, then check_mesh. Refusals carry error.code MESH_IMPORT_UNITS_REQUIRED, MESH_IMPORT_FORMAT_UNKNOWN, MESH_IMPORT_PARSE, MESH_IMPORT_EMPTY, MESH_IMPORT_SHA_MISMATCH, MESH_IMPORT_TOO_LARGE, MESH_ASSET_MISSING, MESH_ASSET_UNAVAILABLE.

base64.description: The file bytes, base64 encoded (STL, OBJ, PLY or 3MF); recorded in the document step. Give exactly one of fileKey, base64 or text.

color.description: Display colour "#rrggbb". Default: light grey.

fileKey.description: sha256 (64 hex) of a file kept in the mesh asset store (the CLI stores `file=PATH` and fills this). Give exactly one of fileKey, base64 or text.

fileName.description: Original file name, kept in the entity provenance only.

format.description: File format; default: sniffed from the content.

name.description: Entity name; several bodies get a numeric suffix. Default: the name in the file, else none.
