sourceSha256.description: sha256 (hex) you expect the file bytes to have. A match marks the mesh verified; a mismatch refuses the import (MESH_IMPORT_SHA_MISMATCH).

text.description: The file as text (ascii STL, OBJ, ascii PLY). Give exactly one of fileKey, base64 or text.

units.description: Unit of the file coordinates (mm, cm, m, in, ft). Required for STL, OBJ and PLY; for 3MF it overrides the file unit.

weldTolerance.description: Vertices closer than this (document units) are merged. Default: 1e-6 x the bounding-box diagonal (reported as a named default).

name: import_mesh_file

description: Import a wing from the text of an OpenVSP `.vsp3` file (XML; read the file and pass its text). The wing geometry is rebuilt with create_wing: each section of the file (`XSec_n` parameters Span, Root_Chord, Tip_Chord, Sweep at Sweep_Location, Dihedral, Twist at Twist_Location) becomes a span station with its chord, sweep, dihedral and twist, the position comes from X / Y / Z_Rel_Location and the XZ symmetry flag makes `mirror`. Airfoils: NACA 4-series section curves (Camber, CamberLoc, ThickChord) are recreated with airfoil_from_naca; any other section type (an AF / Selig file airfoil, a conic, ...) is REFUSED with the list of such sections unless `fallbackNaca` names the NACA designation to put there instead (the summary and `data.substituted` then say so and `unverified` is true). Values are used in the file's own length unit: set_units to match first, or give `lengthScale` (e.g. 25.4 for inches into mm). `geomName` picks one wing of a multi-wing file (default: the first). Notes: the OpenVSP `Span` of a section is used as its projected span; the real TR1208.vsp3 of the OpenVSP examples was not available when this was written (offline), so the XML layout is the documented one and untested on that file.

fallbackNaca.description: NACA designation ("0012", "2412", "23012") used for sections whose airfoil is not a NACA 4-series curve. Default: refuse such files.

geomName.description: Name of the wing geometry to import. Default: the first wing of the file.

lengthScale.description: Factor applied to every length of the file (> 0). Default 1: the file unit is the document unit.

mirror.description: Override the symmetry of the file: true adds the left half. Default: from the file (XZ symmetry flag, else true).

text.description: The full text of the .vsp3 file (OpenVSP XML).

name: import_openvsp_wing

description: Import a piping spec file into the document as a draft. The file is { format: "llull-pipe-spec", schemaVersion: 1, id, revision?, title?, service?, dimensionalStandard (ASME | EN | ISO | company: required, no default), rating { system, class | pn, materialGroup }, materials?, corrosionAllowance { value, unit: mm | in } (required), millTolerance?, designLimits { minTemperatureC, maxTemperatureC }?, sizeRange { fromNps, toNps } or { fromDn, toDn }, catalogs: [catalogue ids searched in order], components: [{ id, type, fromNps/toNps or fromDn/toDn, catalogRef, ends?, facing?, class?, radius?, schedule? | scheduleFromPipe?, wallMm?, priority?, branchFromNps/branchToNps? (olets, reducing tees), commodityCode? }], branchTable { cells: { "<header NPS>": { "<branch NPS>": T | RT | W | S | TH | SI | SIR } } }, status? }. The spec is always stored as draft: approval is a separate human-gated act. Importing identical content changes nothing; different content under an existing id needs replace:true (a draft is overwritten, an approved spec gets a new revision). Next: check_pipe_spec to validate it, resolve_spec_component / resolve_branch to use it, export_pipe_spec for the canonical file.

replace.description: Overwrite a spec with the same id but different content. Default false: such a clash is refused (PSC_SPEC_CONFLICT).

spec.description: The spec file object (format llull-pipe-spec, schemaVersion 1).

name: import_pipe_spec

description: Import a piping component catalogue file into the document. The file is { format: "llull-piping-catalog", schemaVersion: 1, id, version?, title?, licence, families: [...] }; a family is { id, type (pipe, elbow90, flangeWeldNeck …), standard ("ASME B16.9"), dimensionalStandard? (ASME | EN | ISO | company), radius? (LR | SR), ends?, unit? (mm | in, default mm), sizes: [...] }; a size is { nps or dn, smallNps? / smallDn?, schedule?, class?, pn?, facing?, <dimension>: number … (outsideDiameter, wall, centreToEnd, boltCircle, boltCount, …), provenance: { citation or sourceId }, dimProvenance?, verified? | verifiedDims? }. Every dimension needs provenance.citation or sourceId, and a value is unverified unless the file says verified (AF-32). Imported values are stored in millimetres. Licence licensed-no-redistribution is refused (PSC_LICENCE_EMBED_FORBIDDEN). Nothing is bundled for ASME B16.11, olets, EN 10253 or B16.47: import them here. The id llull-open-piping is reserved. Next: check_piping_catalog to validate the dimensions against the standards, lookup_piping_component to read rows.

catalog.description: The catalogue file object: { format: "llull-piping-catalog", schemaVersion: 1, id, licence, families: ComponentFamily[] }.

replace.description: Overwrite a catalogue with the same id but different content. Default false: such a clash is refused (PSC_CATALOG_CONFLICT).

name: import_piping_catalog

description: Create plies of a composite part from a CSV text in the export_ply_table layout (header row required): ply (name), material (lamina record name) and orientation (degrees) are required; sequence, order (sorts the rows; 0 = tool side) and rosette (name) are optional; area_mm2, zones and mass columns are ignored. Every ply covers the whole face; refine regions with edit_ply. A part that already has plies needs `replace` true (its plies are removed first). Refused with the row number on a bad row.

csv.description: CSV text with a header row (ply,sequence,order,material,orientation,rosette,...).

replace.description: Remove the part plies first; default false.

name: import_ply_table

description: Import the measured results of a QIF 3.0 file (MeasurementResults / MeasuredCharacteristics / CharacteristicMeasurements, ANSI/DMSC QIF 3.0) as the FAI results of one revision: each characteristic measurement is matched to a characteristic number of the register (assign_characteristic_ids) through the Name of its CharacteristicItem (the balloon number) or, when the file carries no items, its CharacteristicItemId; its Value, unit and Status (PASS, FAIL, ...) are stored as the measuring system wrote them (llull does not judge them). HUMAN GATE. The file is parsed safely: DOCTYPE and entities are refused, size (8 MB), nesting (48) and element count are limited. The result set keeps the SHA-256 of the exact file. Read it back with fai_report_skeleton { resultsId }. Matches and gaps are in the summary. Needs `confirmation` (plm_act_payload) over exactly these params, the file included: an agent gets PLM_HUMAN_GATE and hands over.

at.description: When the act happened: ISO-8601 UTC, e.g. 2026-11-02T09:30:00Z. The host (UI / llull CLI) fills it; commands never read a clock.

by.description: Ignored: the import is recorded under the signer of the confirmation.

confirmation.description: HUMAN SIGNATURE, required: { alg: "Ed25519", keyId, publicKey, signature, nonce } made by a human with a TRUSTED signing key over this exact act (get the bytes with plm_act_payload, sign them in the desktop app or `llull exec ... --confirm-key KEYID`). An agent has no trusted key: it prepares the act and hands over (PLM_HUMAN_GATE).

id.description: Result set id; omitted = 'FRS-<revision>-<n>'.

revision.description: Revision label of the managed item the results were measured against, e.g. "B".

serial.description: Serial number of the unit measured (A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ - /), recorded on the result set and Form 1.

xml.description: The QIF 3.0 file text (UTF-8, at most 8 MB), e.g. the contents of a CMM results .qif / .xml file.

name: import_qif_results

description: Import a STEP file as exact B-rep solids (not triangles): the file is read, every solid is checked and healed (BRepCheck, ShapeFix, sewing of loose shells), stored as a content-addressed document blob and shown as one mesh entity per solid that keeps its exact shape (volumes, fillets, booleans and STEP export stay exact). Names and colours of the file are kept. An assembly keeps its structure: one component per product, one instance per placed occurrence (assembly: false flattens it). The geometric validation properties the sender embedded (volume, surface area, centroid) are compared with the recomputed ones per product (verify): data.report.exchange lists product, band green / yellow / red / not-checkable, both values and the exact file-unit factor (25.4 for inch); a red or not-checkable body is flagged unverified and the report asks for review, but the import still completes. Needs the exact OCC kernel (kernel_info); otherwise use the CLI tool import_step for a mesh. Give the file as stepBase64 or text. Lengths are converted from millimetres into the document unit. data.report lists per solid validAsRead / validAfterHeal / actions / maxToleranceMm / freeEdges / faces / faceted, the root census, skipped items and warnings (KRN_IMPORT_TOLERANCE_HIGH above kernelSettings maxImportTolerance; XCH_GVP_YELLOW / XCH_GVP_RED / XCH_GVP_NOT_CHECKABLE). Refusals carry error.code: KRN_NO_EXACT_KERNEL, KRN_STEP_UNREADABLE, KRN_STEP_TESSELLATED_ONLY, KRN_STEP_NO_SOLID, KRN_HEAL_FAILED. format: "iges" reads an IGES file the same way (import_iges adds the IGES census, sewing report and unit handling).

assembly.description: Keep the assembly structure of the file: one component per product, one instance per placed occurrence (a part used twice is one component). Default true. False flattens everything into world-space solids.

fileName.description: Original file name, kept in the report and provenance only.

format.description: "step" (default, ISO 10303-21) or "iges" (IGES 5.3; same healing, report and refusal codes). The file goes in text / stepBase64 either way.

gvpPolicy.description: Band limits of the validation-property check; each omitted limit keeps its default.

greenCentroidPerDiag.description: Largest centroid distance still green, as a fraction of the bounding-box diagonal. Default 1e-3.

greenRel.description: Largest relative volume / area difference still green. Default 1e-3.

yellowCentroidMm.description: Largest centroid distance still yellow, in millimetres. Default 1.

yellowRel.description: Largest relative volume / area difference still yellow (red beyond). Default 1e-2.

heal.description: Run shape healing (ShapeFix) on every solid at the document linear tolerance. Default true.

importPmi.description: Attach the semantic PMI of an AP242 file (datums, feature control frames, size and location dimensions on faces) to the imported solids through apply_pmi_set: every item is review-required, an item whose face cannot be mapped is counted in data.report.pmi.unmapped, none is silently dropped. Default true; has no effect on a file without PMI or with assembly false.

keepOriginal.description: Also store the STEP text as a model/step document blob for audit (large). Default false.

name.description: Entity name overriding the names in the file; several solids get a numeric suffix. Default: the names of the file.

sew.description: Sew loose shells and faces into closed solids. Default true.

sha256.description: sha256 (hex) of the file bytes, computed by the host; kept in the provenance. Default: sha256 of the text.

stepBase64.description: The STEP file bytes, base64 encoded (ISO 10303-21 text, UTF-8/ASCII). Give exactly one of stepBase64 or text.

text.description: The STEP file as Part 21 text. Give exactly one of stepBase64 or text.

verify.description: Compare the geometric validation properties the sender embedded (volume, surface area, centroid) with what llull recomputes from the imported B-rep, per product, and flag the bodies unverified when they disagree or cannot be checked. Never blocks the import. Default true.

name: import_step_exact

description: Extract survey points from a topographic DXF into a point group, ready for create_surface: POINT entities, vertices of 3D polylines / elevated contours / lines (breaklines), 3DFACE corners and, optionally, numeric spot-height TEXT ("123.45" placed at the level). Filter by DXF `layers` (e.g. ["TOPO_PTS", "CONTOURS"]). Points at elevation 0 are ignored unless `keepZeroElevation`. Units from $INSUNITS unless `sourceUnit`.

keepZeroElevation.description: Keep points at z = 0. Default false.

layers.description: Only these DXF layers (case-insensitive). Default: every layer.

name.description: Point group name. Default "DXF survey <n>".

sourceUnit.description: Drawing unit when $INSUNITS is missing. Default: $INSUNITS, else m.

sources.description: What becomes a point: points, vertices, faces, text. Default points, vertices, faces.

name: import_survey_dxf

description: Import survey points (topographic survey, total station / GNSS export) as a named point group. Give `text` (CSV / TXT file content, one point per line; header and # comment lines skipped) in `format` PENZD (default: number, easting, northing, elevation, description), PNEZD, PENZ, PNEZ, ENZ or NEZ, and/or `points` [{ x, y, z }]. Coordinates are in `sourceUnit` (default m) and are converted to the document unit. Then build a terrain with create_surface.

coordinates.description: Coordinate frame of the input. "grid" (projected CRS) is converted to local with the site calibration (set_site_calibration) and is refused without one. Default "local".

name.description: Point group name. Default "Survey <n>".

points.description: Points given directly.

number.description: Point number / name. Default: running index.

sourceUnit.description: Unit of the coordinates in `text` / `points`. Default m.

text.description: Survey file content (comma, tab, ; or space separated).

name: import_survey_points

description: Lighten an existing closed 3D solid in one call: an inside skin of `wall` (document units) plus a lattice infill (TPMS or struts) clipped to the solid shrunk by the wall, realised as an implicit body at `voxel`. It runs field_from_solid, shell_field, offset_field, add_tpms_lattice / add_strut_lattice, combine_fields and create_implicit_body for you (their ids are in data.steps), hides the source solid, and reports the volumes. openBy (a field id) removes skin and infill where that field is negative (an opening to drain or inspect); drainHoles {diameter, count} subtracts vertical (z) through-holes: one on the axis, or `count` on a circle, so powder or resin can leave (run check_implicit and look for IMP_TRAPPED_VOID). Pick voxel at most wall / 2 (the check warns below that). Next: implicit_properties, check_implicit, export_3mf / export_stl.

color.description: Optional hex colour of the body.

drainHoles.description: Vertical (z) through-holes for powder / resin drainage.

count.description: Number of holes (integer 1..16): 1 on the axis of the solid, more on a circle.

entityId.description: Id of the closed 3D solid (box, extrusion, boolean result, mesh...) to lighten.

cellSize.description: Cell size in document units: a number or [x, y, z].

kind.description: TPMS family.

level.description: Network level (number or scalar field id).

origin.description: Lattice origin [x, y, z]. Default [0, 0, 0].

relativeDensity.description: Target solid fraction of the cell (0..1) instead of thickness / level.

thickness.description: Sheet wall thickness (number or scalar field id).

type.description: A TPMS infill (see add_tpms_lattice).

cellSize.description: Cell size in document units: a number or [x, y, z].

origin.description: Lattice origin [x, y, z]. Default [0, 0, 0].

radius.description: Strut radius in document units (number or scalar field id).

type.description: A strut infill (see add_strut_lattice).

lattice.description: The infill lattice, clipped to the inside of the skin.

maxTriangles.description: Refuse a body with more triangles than this (see create_implicit_body).

name.description: Optional name of the body.

openBy.description: Id of a field: skin and infill are removed where it is negative.

voxel.description: Grid spacing of the realised body in document units (> 0); halve it for 4x smaller error and 8x more samples.

name: infill_solid

description: Insert a straight row of identical fastener stacks (insert_fastener_stack at each position) along from -> to with either pitch {value, unit} or count. Rivet rows are checked against the minimum pitch 3 D and edge distance 2 D (AC 43.13-1B 4-57(c)); other families use minPitch / minEdgeDistance when given. edgeDistance is the distance from the row to the plate edge as the caller knows it. A violation refuses the row (FAST_PITCH / FAST_EDGE_DISTANCE, listed in data.violations) unless allowViolations is true, which places it with warnings. Selection params as in select_fastener; needs stackIds. With pitch, the pitch is adjusted (count = round(length/pitch)+1) so the last fastener lands on `to`. Returns data.rowId, data.stackIds, data.count, data.pitchIn (actual) and data.requestedPitchIn.

allowViolations.description: Place the row although pitch or edge distance is below the minimum, reporting warnings. Default false: refuse.

axis.description: Fastener axis direction [x, y, z] pointing from the head side to the nut side. Default [0, 0, 1].

codes.description: Part-number code choices by grammar field name, e.g. { "material": "AD" } for MS20470AD4. A missing choice takes the first catalogue code and is reported.

count.description: Number of fasteners, spread evenly from `from` to `to` (1..500). Give this OR pitch.

diameterDash.description: Size dash of the family as listed by list_fastener_families (e.g. "3" for NAS6203, "4" for MS20470AD4, "8" for HL19 1/4 in).

edgeDistance.description: Distance from the fastener axes to the nearest plate edge, as { value, unit }, known to the caller (it is checked against the minimum, not measured)

unit.description: Length unit of the value, e.g. 'in', 'mm', 'ft'.

family.description: Id of the fastener family in the document catalogue (e.g. "NAS6203-6220", "MS20470", "HL19"). Use list_fastener_families to see ids.

from.description: Axis point [x, y, z] (document units) of the first fastener.

holeDiameter.description: Hole diameter as { value, unit }; overrides the catalogue hole diameter. Required when the catalogue lists none

unit.description: Length unit of the value, e.g. 'in', 'mm', 'ft'.

holeMode.description: Hole cut through every plate of the stack with the geometry kernel: "cut_close_tolerance" (default, diameter from the catalogue size or holeDiameter), "cut_clearance" (clearance diameter from the catalogue or holeDiameter) or "none" (no cut).

maxWasherTotal.description: Largest combined washer thickness allowed as { value, unit }. Default 1/8 in (AC 43.13-1B 7-37), reported as a defaulted rule

unit.description: Length unit of the value, e.g. 'in', 'mm', 'ft'.

minEdgeDistance.description: Minimum edge distance for non-rivet families as { value, unit }. Rivets default to 2 D (AC 43.13-1B 4-57(c)).

unit.description: Length unit of the value, e.g. 'in', 'mm', 'ft'.

minPitch.description: Minimum pitch for non-rivet families as { value, unit }. Rivets default to 3 D (AC 43.13-1B 4-57(c)).

unit.description: Length unit of the value, e.g. 'in', 'mm', 'ft'.

nut.description: Optional nut family id (e.g. "MS21042") for the same diameter dash; enables the thread-protrusion check.

pitch.description: Requested spacing between fastener axes as { value, unit }; the row is divided into round(length / pitch) equal intervals so the last fastener lands on `to` (actual pitch in data.pitchIn). Give this OR count

unit.description: Length unit of the value, e.g. 'in', 'mm', 'ft'.

rivetRounding.description: Rivet length rounding to the catalogue step: "up" or "nearest". Default: the catalogue rule (up), reported as a defaulted rule.

stackIds.description: Ids of the 3D solids (plates) every fastener of the row passes through; measured at each position along axis.

to.description: Axis point [x, y, z] (document units) the row runs towards; the last fastener is exactly here.

washer.description: Optional washer family id (e.g. "NAS1149") used to shim the gap between grip and stack.

washerSide.description: Side of the stack the shim washers go on: "nut" (default) or "head".

name: insert_fastener_row

description: Insert one fastener stack through plates: runs the select_fastener rules, cuts the hole through every plate (exact boolean with the kernel), and places the bolt/pin/rivet, shim washers and nut as instances of one component per part number (created once; geometry from the catalogue dimensions, or flagged representative placeholders that are excluded from mass). Needs stackIds + axisPoint (+ axis, head to nut direction). holeMode picks the cut; holeDiameter {value, unit} overrides the catalogue. Records the stack in the document (id fst-<step>.<k>, returned in data.stackId); bill_of_materials then lists the standard parts. Refused selections change nothing. Next: check_fastener_layout, bill_of_materials. Delete with delete_fastener_stack (holes stay: undo to restore the plates).

axis.description: Fastener axis direction [x, y, z] pointing from the head side to the nut side. Default [0, 0, 1].

axisPoint.description: Point [x, y, z] in document units the fastener axis passes through (with stackIds). Not required with stack.

codes.description: Part-number code choices by grammar field name, e.g. { "material": "AD" } for MS20470AD4. A missing choice takes the first catalogue code and is reported.

diameterDash.description: Size dash of the family as listed by list_fastener_families (e.g. "3" for NAS6203, "4" for MS20470AD4, "8" for HL19 1/4 in).

family.description: Id of the fastener family in the document catalogue (e.g. "NAS6203-6220", "MS20470", "HL19"). Use list_fastener_families to see ids.

holeDiameter.description: Hole diameter as { value, unit }; overrides the catalogue hole diameter. Required when the catalogue lists none

unit.description: Length unit of the value, e.g. 'in', 'mm', 'ft'.

holeMode.description: Hole cut through every plate of the stack with the geometry kernel: "cut_close_tolerance" (default, diameter from the catalogue size or holeDiameter), "cut_clearance" (clearance diameter from the catalogue or holeDiameter) or "none" (no cut).

maxWasherTotal.description: Largest combined washer thickness allowed as { value, unit }. Default 1/8 in (AC 43.13-1B 7-37), reported as a defaulted rule

unit.description: Length unit of the value, e.g. 'in', 'mm', 'ft'.

nut.description: Optional nut family id (e.g. "MS21042") for the same diameter dash; enables the thread-protrusion check.

rivetRounding.description: Rivet length rounding to the catalogue step: "up" or "nearest". Default: the catalogue rule (up), reported as a defaulted rule.

stack.description: Stack thickness to fasten (total thickness of the joined layers) as { value, unit }. Give this OR stackIds

unit.description: Length unit of the value, e.g. 'in', 'mm', 'ft'.

stackIds.description: Ids of the 3D solids (plates) the fastener passes through; their thickness along the axis is measured. Give this OR stack. Needs axisPoint.

washer.description: Optional washer family id (e.g. "NAS1149") used to shim the gap between grip and stack.

washerSide.description: Side of the stack the shim washers go on: "nut" (default) or "head".

name: insert_fastener_stack

description: Insert a valve or a reducer (concentric or eccentric) into a routed pipe run (route_pipe / auto_route_pipe / add_branch), spec-driven. A flanged valve (the spec row says FL ends) splits the leg: face-to-face from the catalogue, a flange + gasket + bolt set on each face, pipe pieces shortened to fit (data.pipePieces, data.legCutLengthsMm); a butt-weld valve has no flanges; a socket-weld or threaded valve takes the pipe socketDepth - 1.6 mm / threadEngagement into each end; a reducer occupies its end-to-end length and the run continues at dn2 downstream. An eccentric reducer (reducerEccentric) needs flat ("top" = flat on top, +Z; "bottom", -Z; horizontal or sloped pipes) or flatDirection (any side, needed on vertical pipes): the outer surfaces of the two pipes line up on the flat side, so the smaller axis sits (OD big - OD small) / 2 toward it; the leg after the reducer must take that offset up along its own axis (turn the flat to it; within the angle tolerance the residual is a RTE_ECCENTRIC_OFFSET warning), else RTE_ECCENTRIC_OFFSET; a branch downstream of it on the same leg is refused. at: { leg, centreDistance } (leg index of route_pipe data.legs, distance of the centre from the leg start, mm) or { point: [x, y, z] } on the centreline. Valves: stemDirection points to the handwheel (default up, or +X on a vertical pipe); data.handwheelCentre = centre + stem x catalogue stemHeight (0 when the row has none, stemHeightFromCatalogue false); data.operator = { kind handwheel | gear | actuator, bodies [{ id, kind, from, axis, lengthMm, radiusMm }] } is the operator envelope from the row (handwheelDiameter, gearboxDiameter / gearboxHeight, actuatorDiameter / actuatorHeight along the stem direction), null when the row describes none; check_piping reports its clashes. Returns the component id (affected[0]) to pass to move_inline_component / remove_inline_component / check_piping; data = { componentId, runId, type, tag, leg, centreDistance, dn, dn2, lengthMm, centre, facePositions [[x,y,z],[x,y,z]] (upstream, downstream), partIds, stemDirection, handwheelCentre, legCutLengthsMm, pipePieces, counts, warnings, unverified }. Refusals: RTE_UNITS_UNSUPPORTED, RTE_UNKNOWN_RUN, RTE_INLINE_DOES_NOT_FIT (detail names the neighbours and the cut length), RTE_SPEC_NO_COMPONENT, RTE_SIZE_MISMATCH, RTE_NO_CONNECTION_RULE, RTE_RATING_MISMATCH, RTE_FACING_MISMATCH, RTE_ECCENTRIC_INVALID (flat missing / both given / on a concentric reducer / top or bottom on a vertical pipe), RTE_ECCENTRIC_OFFSET. Next: check_piping (maxHandwheelCentreHeight), piping_takeoff.

centreDistance.description: Distance of the component centre from the leg start point of intersection, document units.

leg.description: Leg index, 0 = the first leg (data.legs of route_pipe).

point.description: A point [x, y, z] on the run centreline, within 0.01 mm.

at.description: Position: { leg, centreDistance } or { point } on the centreline.

dn2.description: Reducers only: the outlet size DN the run continues at (the inlet is the run size at that point). Valves: omit.

flat.description: Eccentric reducers only: the flat side, "top" (flat on top, FOT: +Z) or "bottom" (FOB: -Z), on a horizontal or sloped pipe. The outer surfaces of the two pipes line up on the flat side, so the smaller pipe axis moves toward it by (OD big - OD small) / 2. Give this or flatDirection.

flatDirection.description: Eccentric reducers only: direction from the pipe axis toward the flat side [dx, dy, dz] (any side, needed on a vertical pipe); projected perpendicular to the pipe and normalised. Give this or flat.

runId.description: Pipe run id (affected[0] of route_pipe / auto_route_pipe / add_branch).

stemDirection.description: Valves: direction from the valve centre toward the handwheel [dx, dy, dz]; normalised. Default: up (+Z), or +X on a vertical pipe.

type.description: Catalogue type: a valve (valveGate, valveGlobe, valveCheck, valveBall, valveButterfly, valvePlug), reducerConcentric or reducerEccentric (needs flat or flatDirection).

name: insert_inline_component

description: Place a new InstanceEntity referencing an existing Component definition. The instance carries its own world-space transform (position, rotation, scale). Editing the component later automatically updates all its instances. componentId must exist in doc.components. Returns the new instance id in affected. Next: check_assembly finds overlapping, floating and too-thin parts.

componentId.description: Id of an existing Component in doc.components. Obtain via create_component.

position.description: World-space origin [x, y, z] for the instance. Default: [0, 0, 0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

rotation.description: Euler rotation [rx, ry, rz] in radians (XYZ order). Default: [0, 0, 0].

scale.description: Per-axis scale factors [sx, sy, sz]. Default: [1, 1, 1]. All components must be finite.

name: insert_instance

description: Splice a new feature history step into featureHistory immediately after the step with id afterStepId, then regenerate the document. If afterStepId is omitted the step is appended at the end. The new step is always active (suppressed=false).

afterStepId.description: Id of the existing FeatureStep after which to insert the new step. If omitted, the new step is appended at the end of featureHistory.

label.description: Optional human/AI-readable label for this step, e.g. "Base plate".

name.description: Registry command name (snake_case) for the new step, e.g. "add_box". Must be a known command name; unknown names are stored but skipped during replay.

params.description: Params object for the command named in `name`. Must be compatible with that command.

name: insert_step

description: Inset faces of a subdivision cage: the boundary of each region of selected faces moves `thickness` inward in the face plane (even offset: every new edge exactly `thickness` from its old edge) and `depth` along the region normal (positive = outward, negative = into the solid), joined to the old boundary by a ring of quads. Faces are ids or indices; edge-connected faces inset as one region unless `individual`. Element ids are kept, new ones minted; a symmetric cage insets the mirror faces too. Refuses a thickness that would collapse the inner loop (DIR_INSET_TOO_THICK, with the largest valid thickness). Returns data { vertexCount, faceCount, vertices, vertexIds, faceIds, innerFaces, newFaces, newVertices }. Next: extrude_cage_faces, edit_subdivision_cage, set_cage_crease.

depth.description: Signed offset of the inner faces along the region normal, document units (+ outward). Default 0.

evenOffset.description: true (default): keep the width exactly `thickness` at corners (scales the corner offset); false: move corners by `thickness` along the bisector.

faces.description: Faces to inset, as ids or indices.

items.description: A cage face: element id ("f-1.2", stable across topology edits) or current index.

id.description: Id of the subdivision solid.

individual.description: true: inset every face on its own. Default false (edge-connected faces inset together).

thickness.description: Inset width in the face plane, document units (> 0).

name: inset_cage_faces

description: List the physics model: every rigid body with its computed mass (kg), centre of mass (document units) and moment of inertia about its joint axis (kg·m², revolute joints; a prismatic joint reports translatingMassKg instead: the body plus the bodies it carries) and the densities used (densitySources, densityDefaulted: true when the steel default filled in, with a DYN_DENSITY_DEFAULTED warning; unverified), plus joints, gear couplings (ratio, teeth, efficiency), motors, propellers (with their Ct / Cp table), cylinder pressures and engine losses (losses, only when set), and any problem that would stop simulate_motion. With mobility true (default) it also reports the closed-loop structure: data.topology { tree: spanning-tree joints rooted at the ground, loops: joints that close loops, flipped: tree joints whose declared parent/child sense is reversed }, data.mobility { gruebler: 6·bodies − joint constraints; rank: numerical rank of the loop-constraint Jacobian at the start pose; dof: tree coordinates − rank = true degrees of freedom (a crank-driven slider-crank has 1); redundant: constraint rows that repeat what the tree already fixes (FPR_REDUNDANT_CONSTRAINT, with the joint to change; make one revolute loop joint spherical); treeCoordinates, constraintRows } and data.loopGapsM (distance in metres between the two pins of each loop at the start pose; above 1 µm simulate_motion refuses with FPR_LOOP_OPEN). Gear couplings are not counted in the degrees of freedom. Use it to check a setup before simulating. Read-only; needs no physics engine.

mobility.description: Report data.topology, data.mobility and data.loopGapsM (default true).

name: inspect_dynamics

description: List the faces of an exact 3D solid with located geometry: per face its index (the same index inspect_topology uses), surface type (plane, cylinder, cone, sphere, torus, bspline, …), area, centroid, outward unit normal (planes), axis and radius (cylinder, cone, sphere, torus: the torus minor radius; a cone reports its radius at the face centroid) and, on request, sample points inside the trimmed face. With graph=true it also returns the face adjacency graph: per face its surface parameters, whether it is stored reversed, its loops (edge indices, outer loop first) and uv box; per edge the faces it joins and whether the edge is convex, concave, smooth (tangent faces) or unknown. Use it to pick faces for holes, datums, tolerances or meshing: sample points and centroids are positions in the document frame. All lengths are document units and areas their square. Needs the exact kernel (check kernel_info): the OCC kernel (the desktop default; LLULL_KERNEL=occt-native or occt for the CLI and server); the mesh kernel has no B-rep and the command is refused with error.code KRN_NO_EXACT_KERNEL. For edges, edge indices and vertex counts (the fillet_edge / chamfer_edge selectors) use inspect_topology. Does not modify the document.

entityId.description: Id of the 3D solid entity to inspect (a primitive, or a boolean / fillet / chamfer / shell result).

faces.description: 0-based face indices to report (as listed by inspect_topology). Omit to report every face. An index out of range is refused.

graph.description: When true, also return the face adjacency graph (all faces, regardless of the faces filter). Default false.

samples.description: Number of sample points per face, placed inside the trimmed face on a regular uv grid (0-256). Default 0 (none).

name: inspect_faces

description: Read-only: report the exact NURBS definition of a nurbs_surface (degreeU / degreeV, pole grid size, knots per direction, domain, continuity at each interior knot, bounds) or of a nurbs_curve: degree, pole count, rational or not, knots with multiplicities, parameter domain, weights, the poles (when at most 200), the continuity class at each interior knot (C0 = corner, C1, C2 ...), whether it is closed, its arc length and the pole bounding box (all lengths in document units). Use it to check what create_nurbs_curve, interpolate_curve or create_conic produced, or before edit_nurbs.

id.description: Id of a nurbs_curve or nurbs_surface entity.

name: inspect_nurbs

description: Read-only: report frames and sizes of a sweep (sweep_profile, add_coil) along its path. At `samples` equally spaced arc-length fractions (default 21, 2..2000) or at explicit `at` fractions return the entity-local point, unit tangent, section axes (normal = section x, binormal = section y), twist (radians), scale, path curvature radius, the section extent toward the centre of curvature and the fold margin (curvature radius / extent; <= 1 means the swept surface folds onto itself, null on straight runs). Totals: pathLength and integralAreaDs (∫ section area ds, the volume of a section centred on the path), twistVsMinimalRad (net section rotation about the path relative to the twist-free frame), twistVsFrenetRad (net rotation of the Frenet frame relative to the twist-free frame, ∫ torsion ds; null where Frenet is undefined), analyticVolume when the section is round (else null; use mass_properties). Lengths in document units, areas in units squared, angles in radians. Use it to explain a frame mode or to find where a sweep is about to fold.

at.description: Explicit arc-length fractions in [0, 1] to measure (at most 2000).

id.description: Id of a sweep entity.

samples.description: Number of equally spaced arc-length fractions, integer 2..2000. Default 21. Ignored when `at` is given.

name: inspect_sweep

description: List the exact B-rep topology of a 3D solid as the geometry kernel holds it: its faces (surface type, area) and its unique edges (curve type, length, start/end/mid points). The edge indices are the ones fillet_edge and chamfer_edge take in edgeIndices — inspect first, then pick edges by position (e.g. the edge whose mid point is at the top front). Works on primitives and on boolean / fillet / chamfer / shell results (they keep their exact construction). Needs the exact kernel (check kernel_info): the OCC kernel (the desktop default; LLULL_KERNEL=occt-native or occt for the CLI and server); with the mesh kernel it no-ops. For located face geometry (normals, centroids, radii, sample points, adjacency graph) use inspect_faces. Does not modify the document.

id.description: Id of the 3D solid entity to inspect.

name: inspect_topology

description: Replay a named recipe's steps ADDITIVELY on top of the current document, assigning fresh entity ids each time. Existing entities are never removed or changed. Each call is independent — instantiating the same recipe twice produces two separate copies, each with their own unique ids. The recipe must already exist (call save_recipe first). The step is recorded in featureHistory so replaying the history re-expands the recipe.

name.description: Name of the recipe to instantiate. Must match an existing recipe created by save_recipe (case-sensitive). Example: "bracket_v1", "wheel_assembly".

name: instantiate_recipe

description: Create a 3D NURBS curve that passes exactly through every given point (global interpolation, knots by averaging). Typical use: an airfoil or hull section, a spine or a rail from measured points. `parameterization` sets how the points are spread along the curve: "chord" (default, chord-length), "centripetal" (best against overshoot at sharp turns) or "uniform". `degree` default 3 (needs at least degree + 1 points). Optional `startTangent` / `endTangent` fix the direction at the ends (direction only, any length; degree >= 2). Consecutive points must be distinct. Returns the curve id and the interpolation residual (should be ~1e-15 in document units).

color.description: Hex color string #rrggbb, e.g. "#c8553d". Defaults to "#2a7ab0".

endTangent.description: Optional direction [x, y, z] of the curve at the last point (any non-zero length).

layerId.description: Layer id to assign the entity to. Defaults to the document default layer.

name.description: Optional display name for the entity (shown in the scene tree).

parameterization.description: Parameter spacing of the points. Default "chord".

points.description: 2..10000 ordered through-points.

items.description: Point [x, y, z] in document units, relative to `position`.

position.description: Origin [x, y, z] of the curve in document units; the poles are relative to it. Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

startTangent.description: Optional direction [x, y, z] of the curve at the first point (any non-zero length).

name: interpolate_curve

description: Joint capacity of one placed fastener stack (read-only, V2 hook): single shear = fastener Fsu × π·D²/4 (one shear plane) and, for each sheet layer, bearing = sheet Fbru × D × layer thickness at edge ratio e/D. D is the catalogue nominal diameter; each sheet uses the material assigned to its entity (assign_material); the fastener material is fastenerMaterial. Values come from get_material_allowable with the EXACT basis you give (never substituted). The result basis follows MMPDS rules and is never upgraded: A only if every input is A; B if all are A or B; otherwise "mixed" with the per-input list in data.inputs. Typical / supplier values make the capacities unverified (data.unverified). The capacities are an input to a stress check, not a margin: reviewRequired is always true.

edOverD.description: Edge-distance ratio e/D of the bearing allowable (1.5 or 2.0): the Fbru value is keyed by it.

fastenerBasis.description: Basis of the fastener Fsu value to use (A, B, S, …); no other basis is substituted.

fastenerMaterial.description: Material id of the fastener (record carrying the shear allowable Fsu).

sheetBasis.description: Basis of the sheet Fbru value to use; no other basis is substituted.

sheetDirection.description: Grain direction of the sheet value (L, LT, …); omit for a direction-free value.

stackId.description: Id of a placed stack (fst-…); check_fastener_layout lists them.

name: joint_capacity

description: Report which geometry kernel is active for this session: "occt" (exact B-rep: STEP import, fillets, exact volumes) or "manifold" (mesh booleans only), its OCCT version / build, the optional capabilities it has (topology, analyze, distance, exportStep, importShapes, brepBlobs, ...), the isolation (worker, in-process or process) and, when the exact kernel failed to start, the fallback reason. Also returns the implicit field engine (data.fieldEngine: name "ts" or the native llull-field, with its sample and triangle limits) and the document modelingTolerance (linear mm, angular rad, maxImportTolerance mm) with its source, and warnings KRN_KERNEL_FALLBACK / KRN_KERNEL_MISMATCH (the document was written by another kernel or OCCT version). Call this before relying on exact results.
name: kernel_info

description: Laminate weight budget of a composite part (plies, prepreg, layup): for every ply the covered area (ramp extensions included) times its cured thickness gives volume, times the lamina density gives the ply weight. Returns ply area, laminate volume, total laminate weight, the centre of gravity [x, y, z] in the document frame (ply centroids mapped from the flat pattern onto the tool face and lifted to each ply mid-height) and per-material totals. Lengths are document units, volume is units^3, weight is in the density unit times units^3 (g when density is g/mm^3 in a mm document). Results from "mean" / "unknown" lamina data are flagged unverified. Refused when a used material has no density. Read-only.
name: laminate_mass

description: Describe a lattice field (from add_strut_lattice or add_tpms_lattice). Struts: cells, nodes, beams (exact for a region that is a block of whole cells on the lattice), total length, radius range (graded laws are ranged over the region), slenderness, node valence, rho1 = pi r^2 L / cell volume (no node overlap), rhoMeasured (quadrature of one cell, includes overlap), and the Maxwell count b - 3j + 6 with the class (octet stretch-dominated, the others bending-dominated). TPMS: control range, wall thickness (declared and measured by the distance transform, +-resolution), largest pore diameter, specific surface (table for gyroid / P / diamond, measured mesh area for the others), cell stretch of a cylindrical / spherical map. estimateMechanics adds the affine stretch-only stiffness of a strut cell (exact for the octet truss, an upper bound for bending-dominated cells) and the Gibson-Ashby law E/Es = C rho^n with the exponent of the class and the coefficient YOU give in scaling; baseMaterial {youngModulusMpa, source} turns the ratio into MPa. Always unverified and reviewRequired: never a design value.

baseMaterial.description: Solid material for the stiffness in MPa; without it only ratios E/Es are given.

source.description: Where Es comes from (data sheet, coupon test, ...). Required.

youngModulusMpa.description: Young modulus Es of the solid material in MPa (> 0).

estimateMechanics.description: Add the stiffness estimate (opt-in; unverified, needs review).

id.description: Id of a lattice field (struts or tpms node).

resolution.description: Samples along the smallest cell axis (integer 16..128, default 64) for rhoMeasured and the TPMS thickness analysis (nodes are capped by the engine: 2^21 for the TS engine); the error falls roughly with 1/resolution.

scaling.description: Your Gibson-Ashby scaling law; without a coefficient no E is computed. Required for TPMS lattices (no verified law is built in).

coefficient.description: Coefficient C (from coupon tests or a cited source; llull ships no table).

exponent.description: Exponent n of E/Es = C rho^n (1 stretch-dominated, 2 bending-dominated for strut lattices).

name: lattice_properties

description: Query: steady-state heat loss per metre of a pipe line (create_pipeline) through its steel wall and its insulation (set by create_pipeline / update_pipeline insulation) to the ambient, Q' = (Ti - Ta) / [ 1/(hi pi D0) + ln(D1/D0)/(2 pi ks) + ln(D2/D1)/(2 pi kins) + 1/(ho pi D2) ] (Incropera; ISO 12241), with D0 the bore, D1 the outside diameter from the spec pipe row at the line DN, D2 = D1 + 2 x insulation thickness (D2 = D1 for a bare line). Give the fluid and ambient temperatures (degC), the outside film coefficient (W/m2K) and the steel conductivity (W/mK); the inside film is neglected when insideFilmWm2K is omitted; the insulation conductivity is read from the spec insulation table row when omitted. Returns data = { heatLossWPerM (positive = the line loses heat), surfaceTempC (outer surface), steelOuterTempC, resistances (K m/W), diametersMm, lengthM and totalHeatLossW over the routed runs of the line that derive, tracing (when set_heat_tracing recorded a maintain temperature: the heat loss at that temperature, i.e. the heat the tracing must supply), defaults (each input that was not given and what was assumed), provenance, reviewRequired: true }. No radiation and no temperature-dependent conductivity: a screening figure, not a thermal design. Refusals: RTE_UNKNOWN_LINE, RTE_SPEC_NO_COMPONENT, RTE_HEAT_LOSS_INPUT. Does not modify the document. Next: set_heat_tracing, piping_takeoff.

fluidTempC.description: Temperature of the content, degC (the design temperature of the line is a reasonable choice).

insideFilmWm2K.description: Inside film coefficient, W/m2K, > 0. Omit to neglect the inside film (a conservative upper bound of the loss).

insulationConductivityWmK.description: Insulation conductivity at its mean temperature, W/mK, > 0. Omit to read the conductivity column of the spec insulation table row.

outsideFilmWm2K.description: Outside film coefficient (convection plus radiation lumped), W/m2K, > 0, e.g. 10 still air, 25 wind.

steelConductivityWmK.description: Conductivity of the pipe steel, W/mK, > 0 (carbon steel about 50).

name: line_heat_loss

description: List the access-structure rules check_access evaluates: id, ruleset, clause, quantity, limits in mm / N / degrees (with the imperial original), grade and source. Grade A rows gate (fail), grade B rows only warn with STA_RULE_UNVERIFIED, grade C rows are listed with loaded: false and never evaluated. Rows with an open caveat carry a `flag` (the OSHA 2036 ladder retrofit date is under a proposed repeal, status unknown). Filter by ruleset and/or grade; without a grade filter only the loaded rows (A and B) are returned. Read-only.

grade.description: Only rows of this grade. Default: A and B (the loaded rows); "C" lists the rows that are not loaded.

ruleset.description: Ruleset to list: "iso_14122" or "osha_1910". Default: both.

name: list_access_rules

description: List every load of the physics model at its design values: each body weight at its centre of mass (gravity layer), every joint axis and gear coupling (joints), motor drive torque (drives) and propeller thrust at the governed speed (thrust). Each load has a short SI value, the setup behind it (detail), an origin and unit direction in document units and a magnitude (N or N·m; null when it is not a quantity). Filter with layers. Read-only; needs no physics engine. For the values during a run use simulate_motion.

layers.description: Keep only these layers (default: all of them).

name: list_dynamics_loads

description: List the fastener families in the document catalogue: id, kind, standard, licence, grip mode, part-number pattern and every size dash with its diameter in inches. Use it to find the family id and diameterDash that select_fastener and insert_fastener_stack need. Returns data.families; the document is unchanged.

kind.description: Optional filter: only families of this kind (bolt, hi_lok_pin, solid_rivet, nut, washer, ...).

name: list_fastener_families

description: List the fonts text can use: the fonts bundled with llull (usable by family name in add_text font=..., embedded in the document on first use) and the fonts already embedded in this document by import_font. Each entry gives id, family, style, format, licence, sha256, source ("bundled" or "document") and `verified` (the bytes match a pinned sha256). Next: add_text with font=<id or family>.
name: list_fonts

description: List the piping specs in the document: id, title, latest revision and status (draft, approved, superseded), every revision, dimensional standard (ASME or EN), rating basis, size range, catalogues searched, number of components, component types and whether a branch table exists. Filter by specId or by the status of the latest revision. Next: resolve_spec_component or resolve_branch to pick components, check_pipe_spec to validate, import_pipe_spec / create_pipe_spec to add one.

status.description: Only specs whose latest revision has this status.

name: list_pipe_specs

description: List the piping component catalogues available: the bundled open catalogue llull-open-piping (ASME B36.10M / B36.19M pipe by NPS and schedule, B16.9 elbows / tees / reducers, B16.5 weld-neck flanges, B16.20 spiral-wound gaskets, B16.10 gate valves, EN 1092-1 PN16 flanges; every value carries its source and a verified flag = two sources agree) and the catalogues imported into this document. Per family: component type, standard, sizes (NPS inch designation or DN), schedules, classes, row count and how many values are verified. Also lists the rating tables and the standards that are import-only (no free source). Filter by catalogId, type or standard. Next: lookup_piping_component for one row, import_piping_catalog to add your own.

catalogId.description: Only this catalogue (id, or id@version). Default: all.

standard.description: Only families whose standard contains this text, case-insensitive (e.g. "B16.9", "EN 1092").

type.description: Only families of this component type (pipe, elbow90, flangeWeldNeck, gasketSpiralWound, valveGate …).

name: list_piping_catalogs

description: List the PMI items of the document (read-only): per item its id, kind, text rendering (e.g. "⌖ | Ø0.3 Ⓜ | A | B | C", "4X Ø6.6–6.9"), the solid and B-rep faces it is attached to (indices and surface type, as last resolved), review state (review.required true until a qualified engineer accepts it), unverified reason, and its annotation plane { origin, normal, xDir } and position in document units. Also the governing standard, general tolerance note and saved views. Filter by entityId or kind. ascii: true replaces Unicode symbols with plain text. Use it to inspect, plan inspection or check what an agent created; check_pmi validates the items.

ascii.description: true = plain ASCII text instead of Unicode GD&T symbols. Default false.

entityId.description: Only items of this solid.

kind.description: Only items of this kind.

name: list_pmi

description: List the pipe-content colour schemes llull can apply with apply_service_colour_scheme: asme_a13_1 (ASME A13.1 marker colours: fire_quenching, toxic_corrosive, flammable_oxidizing, combustible, water, compressed_air, user_defined_1..4) and iso_14726 (ISO 14726 main colours by medium: fresh water, sea water, fuel, steam, ...). Each row has its category, named colours (fieldColour + letterColour, or mainColour), source ids, grade (A = two or more extracts agree) and any conflict between sources, plus displayHex from the default palette (approximate: a display choice, never a standard value). Standards are paywalled: transcribed from public extracts, not authoritative. Read-only. Error: VIS_SCHEME_UNKNOWN.
name: list_service_colour_schemes

description: Read-only steel section catalogue: IPE, HEA, HEB, UPN, cold-formed C purlins, SHS, RHS, CHS and equal angles L, with depth h, width b, web / flange thickness (mm), mass (kg/m), area (mm²) and paint perimeter (mm). Optionally filter by family.
name: list_steel_profiles

description: List the saved review viewpoints in creation order: data.viewpoints [{ id, guid, name, camera }]. Read-only.

limit.description: Return at most this many (default all).

name: list_viewpoints

description: Replace the current document with one parsed from a serialized JSON string produced by serializeDocument (envelope format: llull-document v3; v1 and v2 are still read). On parse or validation failure the document is left unchanged.

json.description: A JSON string produced by serializeDocument — the full llull-document envelope ({ format: "llull-document", version: 3, document: { ... } }; versions 1 and 2 are also read). Must contain a valid CadDocument with entities, order, layers, layerOrder, selection, and camera.

name: load_document

description: Loft a fuselage outer skin from a station table in the aircraft frame (document units; FS along +x aft, BL along +y right, WL along +z up unless set_aircraft_frame changed it, then stations are mapped through that frame; control curves are always in document coordinates). `stations` is a list of { fs, section } with fs strictly increasing; a section is "point" (the nose / tail tip, allowed only first or last), "circle" { radius, wl }, "superellipse" { halfBreadth, halfHeight, exponent, wl } or "conic" { halfBreadth, wlMaxBreadth, upper { wlExtreme, rho }, lower { wlExtreme, rho } } (Liming conic halves: rho 0.4142 is circular, 0.5 parabolic; conic and circle sections are exact rational NURBS, a superellipse an approximation). The skin is the exact skin through the sections (cubic across stations by default). `controlCurveIds` (nurbs_curve ids such as the crown, keel or max-breadth lines made with interpolate_curve) must cross every station and turn the skin into a Gordon surface (periodic around the closed sections); the distance from the curves to the skin is reported as controlCurveDeviation and a skin farther than 1e-3 of the size from them is refused. The result is one closed nurbs_surface sheet (no volume entity: use thicken_surface for a shell); the summary and data report the enclosed volume when both ends are points. Reference: Sears-Haack body L 10, R 0.5 has volume 3 pi^2 R^2 L / 16 = 4.6264. Next: analyze_surface_curvature, check_continuity.

controlCurveIds.description: Optional nurbs_curve ids (crown, keel, max-breadth lines) crossing every station; they must meet each section within `controlTolerance`.

controlTolerance.description: Largest distance (document units) between a control curve and a section. Default 1e-4 x the fuselage length.

degreeV.description: Degree of the skin along the fuselage, integer 1..5. Default 3 (capped by stations - 1); 1 gives straight lofting between stations.

stations.description: 2..60 stations in order of increasing fs.

fs.description: Fuselage station (x), document units; strictly increasing along the list.

bl.description: Buttock line of the section centre (default 0 = the centre plane).

exponent.description: superellipse: exponent n in (1, 50], 2 = ellipse, larger = boxier.

halfBreadth.description: conic / superellipse: half of the maximum breadth (distance from the centre to the max-breadth points) > 0.

lower.description: conic: the lower (keel) arcs.

rho.description: Liming rho in (0, 1) of the lower arcs.

wlExtreme.description: Water line of the keel (below wlMaxBreadth).

radius.description: circle: radius > 0.

type.description: "point" = an apex (nose / tail tip, first or last station only); "conic" = four rho-conic arcs; "circle"; "superellipse" (|y/a|^n + |z/b|^n = 1, approximated by four conics: exact for n = 2, max radial error about 0.4 % of the radius at n = 2.5 and 1 % at n = 6, reported as superellipseDeviation).

upper.description: conic: the upper (crown) arcs.

rho.description: Liming rho in (0, 1) of the upper arcs; 0.4142 = circular, 0.5 = parabola.

wlExtreme.description: Water line of the crown (above wlMaxBreadth).

wl.description: point / circle / superellipse: water line of the point or of the section centre, document units.

wlMaxBreadth.description: conic: water line of the max-breadth points.

name: loft_fuselage

description: Fuselage from Liming master lines: three longitudinal nurbs_curve lines in the aircraft frame (FS = x by default) define the conic sections at ANY station - `crownId` (the crown, WL of the top of the section along FS), `keelId` (the keel, WL of the bottom) and `breadthId` (the maximum-breadth line: its BL is the half breadth and its WL the water line of the widest point). `stations` lists the FS values to cut (2..60, strictly increasing, each inside the extent of all three lines); the conic shoulder `rho` follows `rhoUpper` / `rhoLower` laws (default the circular 0.4142). A station where crown, keel and breadth coincide becomes an apex (nose or tail, first or last station only). The sections are then lofted exactly like loft_fuselage (same result, definition stored in doc.aero.bodies). Make the master lines with interpolate_curve through points [fs, 0, wl] (crown, keel) and [fs, halfBreadth, wl] (breadth). Reference: crown z = r(x), keel z = -r(x), breadth y = r(x) at wl 0 with r the Sears-Haack radius gives the Sears-Haack body.

breadthId.description: nurbs_curve id of the max-breadth line (points [fs, halfBreadth, wl]; the BL is the half breadth).

crownId.description: nurbs_curve id of the crown line (points [fs, 0, wl]).

degreeV.description: Degree of the skin along the fuselage, integer 1..5. Default 3.

keelId.description: nurbs_curve id of the keel line (points [fs, 0, wl]).

rhoLower.description: Rho law as [fs, rho] pairs sorted by increasing fs, each rho in (0, 1); linear between the pairs, constant outside.

rhoUpper.description: Rho law as [fs, rho] pairs sorted by increasing fs, each rho in (0, 1); linear between the pairs, constant outside.

stations.description: 2..60 strictly increasing FS values (aircraft frame, document units) where sections are derived.

name: loft_fuselage_from_master_lines

description: Loft a solid through 2+ cross-sections placed in 3D, in order: transitions such as round-to-square ducts, tapered and flattened bike tubes, bottle and nozzle bodies, boat hulls, aero fairings. Right-handed world frame, +Z up. Give either `sectionIds` (closed 2D sketches: circle, ellipse, rectangle, closed polyline or spline; each placed by its own work-plane position and rotation) or inline `sections` (each a center [x, y, z], optional plane rotation (Euler XYZ radians, [0,0,0] = an XY-plane section), and one of radius, radiusX+radiusY, section points or sectionId). Sections are resampled to the same point count and aligned so the surface does not twist; ruled: false (default) blends smoothly through all sections, ruled: true joins neighbours with straight lines. Kept exact for the OCC kernel and STEP export (B-spline skin through the sections). EXACT SECTIONS: when sectionIds are all nurbs_curve entities (create_nurbs_curve, interpolate_curve, airfoil_from_naca ...) every section is lofted as the curve it is - not resampled to 24 points, a sharp trailing edge stays sharp - and a straight edge closes an open curve; all curves need degree 1..3, no weights, the same number of knot spans and the same start point/orientation convention.

alignment.description: Seam alignment of closed sections (exact re-seaming, shapes unchanged): auto moves each section start to the point nearest the previous start so rulings do not twist; none keeps the starts as built (a seam one corner apart twists a square loft to 2/3 of its volume).

centerlineId.description: Two sections only: id of a curve (arc, spline, nurbs_curve) from the first to the last section centre; `sectionCount` blended sections are placed normal to it.

closed.description: Join the last section back to the first (a ring such as a torus or a duct loop; >= 3 sections, smooth, no end caps).

color.description: Hex color string #rrggbb, e.g. "#c8553d". Defaults to "#6b8f9c".

coupling.description: How the points of neighbouring sections pair up: arc_length (equal fractions of arc length; the sections are cut at every corner so corners stay edges), vertices (cut at the fractions of `vertexPairs`; one face per segment).

endAngleRad.description: Largest allowed angle (radians) between a loft end and its target before the end section is refined. Default 0.01.

endCondition.description: How the loft arrives at the LAST section: { type: free | normal | direction | tangent_to_face | curvature_to_face | point, magnitude, direction, draftDeg, faceId, at }. Needs a smooth loft (not ruled).

at.description: point only: [x, y, z] of the tip. Only valid at the first or last section.

direction.description: direction only: [x, y, z] world direction (non-zero).

draftDeg.description: normal only: tilt of the departure toward the section centre in degrees (positive narrows the loft).

faceId.description: tangent_to_face / curvature_to_face: id of the nurbs_surface the end section lies on.

magnitude.description: Speed of the departure, > 0, default 1 = the natural speed (the distance to the next section per unit of parameter). Larger bulges the loft out along the condition.

type.description: free: no condition (default); normal: leave perpendicular to the section plane; direction: leave along `direction`; tangent_to_face: tangent to the sheet `faceId` (G1); curvature_to_face: tangent and curvature continuous with the sheet (G2); point: add the single point `at` beyond that end section as a tip (a nose or cone apex); every given section is kept.

fitTolerance.description: Largest refit deviation (document units) of arc_length coupling. Default 1e-6 x the loft size.

guideIds.description: Guide curves (nurbs_curve ids) crossing every section: the loft becomes a Gordon surface that contains them.

guideTolerance.description: Largest gap (document units) between a guide and a section still counted as meeting. Default 1e-4 x the loft size.

id.description: Optional explicit entity id. If omitted a unique id is generated.

layerId.description: Layer id to assign the entity to. Defaults to the document default layer.

ruled.description: true: straight lines between neighbouring sections; false (default): smooth blend.

seams.description: One curve-parameter fraction 0..1 per section where its seam goes (overrides alignment).

sectionCount.description: With centerlineId: number of intermediate sections, integer 1..64 (default 8).

sectionIds.description: Ids of closed 2D sketches, in loft order, each in its own (parallel or tilted) plane.

sections.description: Inline sections in loft order (alternative to sectionIds).

center.description: Section plane origin [x, y, z] in world coordinates.

radius.description: Round section radius (> 0).

radiusX.description: Elliptical section: half-width along section x (> 0); give with radiusY.

radiusY.description: Elliptical section: half-height along section y (> 0); give with radiusX.

rotation.description: Section plane rotation, Euler XYZ radians; [0, 0, 0] lays the section in the XY plane.

vertexPairs.description: coupling vertices: per section the ascending curve-parameter fractions 0..1 of its vertices (same count per section; the first is the seam of a closed section).

name: loft_sections

description: Skin a NURBS surface sheet through ordered section curves (nurbs_curve ids, e.g. from interpolate_curve, create_conic or airfoil_from_naca): u runs along each section, v across the sections in the order given. The sections are not resampled: they are made compatible (common degree and knots, exact) and the v poles interpolate them, so rational sections such as circles stay exact. Sections must start at corresponding points and run the same way. Optional `guideIds` (curves crossing every section within `guideTolerance`) turn it into a Gordon surface: the result contains the guides as well as the sections (fitted bicubic; the section deviation is reported). `degreeV` is the degree across the sections (1..5, default 3 capped by sections - 1; 1 gives a ruled skin). This is the sheet counterpart of loft_sections (which makes a solid). Next: analyze_surface_curvature, check_continuity, thicken_surface.

alignment.description: Seam alignment of closed sections (exact re-seaming, shapes unchanged): auto moves each section start to the point nearest the previous start so rulings do not twist; none keeps the starts as built (a seam one corner apart twists a square loft to 2/3 of its volume).

closed.description: Join the last section back to the first (a ring such as a torus or a duct loop; >= 3 sections, smooth, no end caps).

color.description: Hex color string #rrggbb, e.g. "#c8553d". Defaults to "#9fb4c7".

coupling.description: How the points of neighbouring sections pair up: arc_length (equal fractions of arc length; the sections are cut at every corner so corners stay edges), vertices (cut at the fractions of `vertexPairs`; one face per segment).

degreeV.description: Degree across the sections, integer 1..5. Default 3 (capped by the number of sections - 1).

endAngleRad.description: Largest allowed angle (radians) between a loft end and its target before the end section is refined. Default 0.01.

endCondition.description: How the loft arrives at the LAST section: { type: free | normal | direction | tangent_to_face | curvature_to_face | point, magnitude, direction, draftDeg, faceId, at }. Needs a smooth loft (not ruled).

at.description: point only: [x, y, z] of the tip. Only valid at the first or last section.

direction.description: direction only: [x, y, z] world direction (non-zero).

faceId.description: tangent_to_face / curvature_to_face: id of the nurbs_surface the end section lies on.

magnitude.description: Speed of the departure, > 0, default 1 = the natural speed (the distance to the next section per unit of parameter). Larger bulges the loft out along the condition.

type.description: free: no condition (default); normal: leave perpendicular to the section plane; direction: leave along `direction`; tangent_to_face: tangent to the sheet `faceId` (G1); curvature_to_face: tangent and curvature continuous with the sheet (G2); point: add the single point `at` beyond that end section as a tip (a nose or cone apex); every given section is kept.

fitTolerance.description: Largest refit deviation (document units) of arc_length coupling. Default 1e-6 x the loft size.

guideIds.description: Optional nurbs_curve ids of guide curves that cross every section, listed across the sections.

guideTolerance.description: Largest distance (document units) between a guide and a section still counted as meeting. Default 1e-4 x the size of the curves.

layerId.description: Layer id to assign the entity to. Defaults to the document default layer.

name.description: Optional display name for the entity (shown in the scene tree).

position.description: Origin [x, y, z] of the surface in document units; the poles are relative to it. Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

seams.description: One curve-parameter fraction 0..1 per section where its seam goes (overrides alignment).

sectionIds.description: 2..60 ordered nurbs_curve ids to skin through.

startCondition.description: How the loft leaves the FIRST section: { type: free | normal | direction | tangent_to_face | curvature_to_face | point, magnitude, direction, draftDeg, faceId, at }. Needs a smooth loft (not ruled).

description: Look up ONE component size row in a piping catalogue and return its dimensions in millimetres, each with verified (two sources agree) and its source. Give the component type and a nominal size: nps (inch designation "2-1/2" or number 2.5) or dn (integer). Pipe rows are keyed by standard + NPS + schedule: schedule "10" is ASME B36.10M, "10S" is B36.19M, "STD"/"XS"/"XXS" and "40"/"80" also exist; give schedule for a pipe or the answer is ambiguous. Reducers take smallNps; flanges take class (150/300/600 …) and facing, EN flanges take dn and pn. Answers use flat keys such as outsideDiameterMm, wallMm, insideDiameterMm (derived), centreToEndMm, boltCircleMm, boltCount, boltDiameterIn ("5/8"), boltHoleMm (derived), faceToFaceMm, innerRingIdMm, centeringRingOdMm, lengthMm. A missing B16.9 long-radius / short-radius 90 degree elbow size is derived from the standard rule (1.5 x NPS / 1.0 x NPS) and flagged derived. Unverified values are listed with PSC_DATA_UNVERIFIED. Refuses unknown catalogues, sizes and schedules with a code. Next: pipe_section_properties for mass, check_piping_catalog to validate a catalogue.

catalogId.description: Catalogue id, or id@version. Default: the bundled llull-open-piping.

class.description: ASME pressure class of a flange, gasket or valve: 150, 300, 600 …

dn.description: Nominal diameter DN, integer (e.g. 100). Converted to NPS through the fixed DN <-> NPS map when the row is NPS-keyed.

ends.description: Restrict to families offering this end type (BW, FL, SW …).

facing.description: Flange face: RF, FF, RTJ, TG, MF.

nps.description: Nominal pipe size, inch designation: "2-1/2", "6" or the number 2.5, 6 (multiples of 1/8). Give nps or dn.

pn.description: EN pressure nominal PN of a flange: 16, 40 …

radius.description: Elbow bend radius: LR (long, 1.5 x NPS) or SR (short).

smallDn.description: Branch / small-end DN of a reducer, reducing tee or olet.

smallNps.description: Branch / small-end NPS of a reducer, reducing tee or olet.

standard.description: Restrict to families whose standard contains this text (e.g. "B36.19M", "EN 1092-1").

type.description: Component type: pipe, elbow90, elbow45, tee, reducerConcentric, flangeWeldNeck, gasketSpiralWound, valveGate …

name: lookup_piping_component

description: Insert edge loops into a subdivision cage: `edge` (id "e:<idA>|<idB>" or [a, b] vertex indices) is an edge CROSSING the loop; the cut follows the strip of quads across it until it closes, adding `cuts` evenly spaced loops (default 1), or one loop at `factor` (0..1 from the first vertex of the pair) when cuts is 1. More resolution to shape with; new vertices lie on the old edges, so the cage outline is unchanged. Refuses a strip that meets an n-gon (DIR_LOOP_NOT_QUAD): cut from another edge. A symmetric cage cuts the mirror loops too. Returns data { vertexCount, faceCount, vertices, vertexIds, faceIds, newVertices, newFaces, stripFaces }. Next: edit_subdivision_cage, set_cage_crease { loopFrom }.

cuts.description: Number of loops to insert, 1..32 (default 1), evenly spaced along the crossed edges.

edge.description: An edge crossing the loop (each loop edge it crosses is split); id or [a, b] vertex indices.

factor.description: Position of a single loop along the crossed edges, 0..1 exclusive, from the first vertex of the picked edge (default 0.5). Only with cuts 1.

id.description: Id of the subdivision solid.

name: loop_cut_cage

description: The validation properties of one revision as a LOTAR-style archive (modelled on EN 9300, not conformant to it) stores them: per 3D entity the volume, area and centroid with the method that computed them (mass_properties), and counts of entities, solids, components, drawing sheets and PMI items. A frozen revision (released, superseded, obsolete) is measured from its release snapshot, the open current revision from the live definition. An archive keeps these figures so a later re-derivation from the archived content can be compared (llull lotar verify). Returns data { revision, definitionHash, source, validation }. Read-only.

revision.description: Revision label; default = the current revision.

name: lotar_validation_properties

description: Read a manufacturing BOM made by create_mbom (the as-built, sealed variant of the engineering_bom; not the building quantity_takeoff): data { id, name, baseline, lines, omitted, differences: { omitted, quantityChanged: [{ partNumber, ebom, mbom }], manufacturingOnly }, totalQuantity, sealOk }. Without id: the list of MBOM ids with their baseline and line count. Read-only.

id.description: MBOM id; omitted = list every MBOM.

name: manufacturing_bom

description: The SHA-256 a human signs to authorize dispose_margin on one FAIL or MARGINAL row of compute_margins: pass the same analysisId / rowId / decision / justification and the same criterion / allowable / groupBy / loadCases / marginalBand you will send to dispose_margin. The signature (Ed25519 over the UTF-8 hex hash) goes in dispose_margin as signature. Valid only for the current results. An agent cannot sign. Read-only.

against.description: Which check the explicit allowable is used for: ultimate (default) or yield (limit load cases only).

unit.description: Stress unit, e.g. "MPa", "psi", "ksi".

allowable.description: "ftu" (ultimate check), "fty" (yield check), or { value, unit, against? }. Omit for both checks from the material models.

analysisId.description: Id of the analysis (affected[0] of create_analysis, e.g. an-1.1).

criterion.description: Applied stress: von_mises (default) or the largest magnitude of the normal component s_xx, s_yy or s_zz.

groupBy.description: part (default): one row per part; target: per constraint / load node set and part.

justification.description: The engineering justification that will be recorded.

loadCases.description: Load case names to include (default: all load cases of the analysis).

marginalBand.description: MS value below which a passing row is MARGINAL (>= 0, in MS units). No default: without it no row is marginal.

rowId.description: Row id of compute_margins, e.g. "r4" (a FAIL or MARGINAL row).

singularityNote.description: Mandatory (non-empty) engineering justification when singularityRadius is given; echoed in the result data.

singularityRadius.description: Override of the singularity exclusion radius, in DOCUMENT length units (>= 0; 0 = exclude nothing). Default: 2 x the mesh globalSize (llull default, reported as defaulted). REQUIRES singularityNote.

name: margin_disposition_payload

description: Record that a cloud arrived pre-registered (contractor data) without a llull registration: a record of method "supplied", status "unverified", so everything derived from the cloud carries unverified until a reviewer accepts it (accept_registration).

cloudId.description: Id of an attached cloud (affected[0] of attach_point_cloud, e.g. "cloud-1.1").

reportRef.description: Reference of the contractor registration report.

name: mark_registration_supplied

description: Measure the volume, area, centroid, inertia and (when a density is known) the mass of a 3D solid, in the document unit. Use measure_bounding_box for the bounding box alone and geometric_validation_properties for the unit-density values a STEP file embeds. Supported entity kinds: 'box', 'cylinder', 'sphere' (closed forms), 'extrusion', 'cone', 'torus', 'wedge', 'pyramid', 'revolution' (Pappus's centroid theorem; a profile crossing the axis falls back to the bounding-box volume), 'sweep' (round section: section area × exact path length), 'loft' (the exact skinned B-rep with the OCC kernel, else its display triangles), 'subdivision', 'mesh' (a kernel result with the OCC kernel: the exact B-rep; otherwise its display triangles), and 'instance' (assembly: the combined mass, centroid and inertia of its component solids, each with its own material, else the instance material, else the density param). 2D shape entities are rejected. Density resolution, in order: the assigned material's density property model (define_property_model property "density"; the preferred one, read at 20 degC), else the material's plain density (create_material, g/(document-unit)³), else the density param. A material always wins over the param. With none, mass is not given and the inertia is per unit density. If a material has density models that cannot be used (several and none preferred, or not valid at 20 degC), the command refuses with that code instead of falling back. Method order: exact (OCC kernel B-rep integration) > closed-form (primitives; volume of cone, torus, revolution, ... with inertia from the triangles scaled to it) > mesh (display triangles, integrated in a part frame so a part far from the origin keeps its precision). Returns data: { volume, volumeUnit (e.g. "mm³"), method ("exact" | "closed-form" | "mesh"), centroid (document unit, in the chosen frame), area and areaUnit when known, frame, inertia: { atCentroid, atOrigin (about `about`, default the frame origin), about, principal: { moments (ascending), axes (unit vectors, right-handed) }, radiiOfGyration, unit ("g·mm²" with a density, else "mm⁵ (per unit density)") } (3x3 matrices, row-major, off-diagonals are -∫xy dm), provenance: { method, kernel: { name, ... }, inputs: { entityIds, recipeKey?, densitySource } }, reviewRequired: { value, reasons[] }, warnings? (KRN_PRECISION_ENVELOPE when the part is beyond ±1e5 mm), relErrorEstimate? } and, when a density is known, { density (g/(document-unit)³), densityKgPerM3, mass (in massUnit), massUnit, massG, massKg, massLb, densitySource (which value was used), densityDefaulted, unverified, unverifiedReasons } (plus unit: "g" when massUnit is g). A plain material density or a param is always unverified (no basis or source); a density model is unverified when its basis is typical / supplier_unstated / unspecified (unverified is about the density only). reviewRequired.value is true for purpose weight-and-balance, any unverified density, a mesh-integrated figure ('method_mesh'), a mesh body without a B-rep ('faceted_body'), a body imported from STEP / IGES whose sender validation properties were red or not checkable (data.importUnverified = { value, reasons } with import_gvp_red / import_gvp_not_checkable / verify_skipped, also in reviewRequired.reasons), or a part outside the precision envelope; the summary then says the figure is computed by llull, not approved, and needs a qualified engineer. A composite part id (create_composite_part) is not an entity: it is delegated to laminate_mass (ply and core mass of the laminate; its data shape applies). Does not modify the document.

about.description: Optional point [x, y, z] in document length units, expressed in the chosen frame, about which data.inertia.atOrigin is taken (parallel-axis theorem). Default: the frame origin [0, 0, 0].

unit.description: Density unit, e.g. "g/cm^3", "kg/m^3", "lb/in^3".

density.description: Optional fallback density, used only for solids without an assigned material; omit it to measure the volume alone. Either { value, unit } (e.g. { "value": 0.101, "unit": "lb/in^3" }) or a bare number in g/(document-unit)³ (for a mm document: steel ≈ 0.00785, aluminium ≈ 0.0027). Must be > 0.

entityId.description: Id of the 3D solid entity to measure. Supported kinds: 'box', 'cylinder', 'sphere', 'extrusion', 'mesh', 'cone', 'torus', 'wedge', 'pyramid', 'revolution', 'sweep', 'loft', 'subdivision', 'instance'.

frame.description: Frame of data.centroid and data.inertia: 'document' (default; world axes, origin at the document origin) or 'entity' (axes and origin of the entity's own position / rotation).

massUnit.description: Unit of data.mass and of the summary: g (default), kg or lb. massG / massKg / massLb are always given.
