purpose.description: 'general' (default) or 'weight-and-balance'. weight-and-balance marks the result reviewRequired (data.reviewRequired.value true): the figure is computed by llull and not approved; a qualified engineer must review it before it is used for flight or certification.

surfaceModel.description: subdivision solids only: which surface the volume (and mass) measures. Default 'level_mesh': the refined `levels` mesh (what the viewport shows, identical with and without a kernel). 'limit_patches': the exact limit-surface patch solid when the native kernel is installed (volume, centroid, inertia and method all exact, from that solid); without the kernel it falls back to the level mesh. data.surfaceModel says which model was used.

name: mass_properties

description: Drive one material point of a constitutive set along a path and return stress-strain history without a mesh. Each step imposes strain (dimensionless; engineering shear for xy, xz, yz) or stress ({ value, unit }) per component xx, yy, zz, xy, xz, yz, reached linearly over its increments; uncontrolled components stay stress-free. Presets fill components a step leaves out: uniaxial_strain, plane_strain (zz, xz, yz held at zero strain, NAFEMS NL1), equibiaxial (yy follows xx), pure_shear (yy held), simple_shear, uniaxial_stress. Give increments per step (default 100, named). Small strain for elasticity, J2 plasticity, Ramberg-Osgood, Prony viscoelasticity and creep; finite for hyperelastic laws (incompressible, D = 0: modes uniaxial_stress / equibiaxial / pure_shear with xx = nominal strain λ − 1 or nominal stress; compressible, D1 > 0: general paths on any of the six components, shear by the simple-shear gradient, uncontrolled components stress-free and solved by Newton, so uniaxial stress contracts laterally; rows carry Hencky strain, Cauchy stress, principal stretches, nominal stress and volumeRatio J). Stress in MPa, time in s, T in K; step and increment are 1-based; at most 100 000 increments per call.  Next: compare with test data, then check_material_models.

forCertification.description: Refuse a result built on unverified data (MAT_VALUE_UNVERIFIED) and flag reviewRequired.

kinematics.description: 'small' strain, or 'finite' for hyperelastic homogeneous modes.

model.description: Ad-hoc law in add_material_model input form, not stored; it fills the slot of its behaviour (alone when no set is given).

output.description: 'steps' (default): one row per step end; 'increments': every increment (at most 10 000 rows).

preset.description: State preset filling the components a step does not control.

set.description: Constitutive set id (default: the material default set).

strain.description: Strain target at the end of the step.

stress.description: Stress target at the end of the step.

unit.description: Unit, e.g. 'MPa', 's', 'K'.

control.description: Per component xx, yy, zz, xy, xz, yz: exactly one of strain or stress. Absolute targets at the end of the step.

duration.description: Step duration (default 1 s; read by rate, time and creep laws).

unit.description: Unit, e.g. 'MPa', 's', 'K'.

temperature.description: Temperature of the step; referenced property models are evaluated there.

unit.description: Unit, e.g. 'MPa', 's', 'K'.

name: material_point_response

description: ENTITIES form of the flat pattern (same pattern as flat_pattern = data and export_flat_pattern_dxf = DXF file): draw the flat pattern of a sheet-metal part as plain 2D entities (outline polyline, cutouts, bend lines) on layers FLAT-<id>, FLAT-<id>-CUT, FLAT-<id>-BEND-UP and FLAT-<id>-BEND-DOWN, so it can be seen (render_view view=top) and drafted on. It is a snapshot: re-running replaces the previous snapshot of the same part. Lengths are in the document length unit. Refusal: FTR_PART_NOT_FOUND, FTR_NON_DEVELOPABLE. Use flat_pattern for the numbers and export_flat_pattern_dxf for the file.

id.description: Sheet-metal part id (returned by add_sheet_metal_base).

origin.description: Optional plane position [x, y] in the document length unit where the lower-left corner of the pattern is placed. Default: beside the folded part, right of its bounding box.

name: materialize_flat_pattern

description: Measure an angle. Provide either: (a) three world-space points as [[vx,vy,vz],[a1x,a1y,a1z],[a2x,a2y,a2z]] where the first point is the vertex and the angle is between the two rays vertex→arm1 and vertex→arm2; or (b) two line entity ids (lineId1, lineId2) to measure the angle between their direction vectors. Returns data: { degrees, radians }. Does not modify the document.

lineId1.description: Id of the first 'line' entity. Used together with lineId2 to measure the angle between two lines.

points.description: Three world-space points [[vx,vy,vz],[a1x,a1y,a1z],[a2x,a2y,a2z]]. First is the vertex; angle is measured between rays vertex→point[1] and vertex→point[2].

name: measure_angle

description: Compute the area of a closed 2D shape or of a surface sheet. Provide either: (a) an entityId for a closed polyline, rectangle, circle, or ellipse entity, or for a nurbs_surface sheet (its surface area, after any trim_surface by curves); or (b) an explicit polygon as points ([[x,y],...], >= 3 points). Returns data: { area, unit } where unit is the squared document unit (e.g. "mm²"). Open polylines are rejected with an explanatory message. Does not modify the document.

entityId.description: Id of a closed 2D shape entity: 'polyline' (must have closed:true), 'rectangle', 'circle', or 'ellipse'.

points.description: Explicit polygon vertices [[x,y],...] in the local 2D plane. Must have at least 3 points. The polygon is implicitly closed (last → first).

name: measure_area

description: Compute the world-space axis-aligned bounding box (AABB) only; use mass_properties for mass, centroid and inertia. Three modes: (a) entityId — AABB of one entity; (b) useSelection:true — combined AABB of the current document selection; (c) no params (or useSelection:false) — combined AABB of the entire document. Returns data: { min:[x,y,z], max:[x,y,z], size:[w,h,d] }. Does not modify the document. Entity rotation and the sweep angle of a partly turned profile are applied (the AABB wraps the actual geometry). A kernel result (mesh with its B-rep) under the exact OCC kernel uses the B-rep bounds, not the display triangles.

entityId.description: Id of the entity whose bounding box to compute. Takes precedence over useSelection.

useSelection.description: When true and entityId is not provided, compute the AABB of the current selection. Falls back to the whole document if the selection is empty.

name: measure_bounding_box

description: Read-only point-to-point measure on a cloud: each end is a point or {nearest: point} snapped to the closest scan point within snapRadius. Returns the distance, the delta [dx, dy, dz] and the snapped points (document units).

cloudId.description: Id of an attached cloud (affected[0] of attach_point_cloud, e.g. "cloud-1.1").

nearest.description: [x, y, z] seed: snaps to the nearest scan point within snapRadius.

from.description: A point [x, y, z] or {nearest: [x, y, z]} snapped to the cloud (document units).

snapRadius.description: Snap radius for {nearest} ends in document units (default 50 mm).

nearest.description: [x, y, z] seed: snaps to the nearest scan point within snapRadius.

to.description: A point [x, y, z] or {nearest: [x, y, z]} snapped to the cloud (document units).

name: measure_cloud

description: Read-only deviation of measured points, or of another entity, from a target shape. `id` is the TARGET: a nurbs_surface, a nurbs_curve or a 3D solid (its tessellation). The source is either `points` (a measured cloud, document units, world coordinates) or `referenceId` (a nurbs_surface sampled on `samples` x `samples` points, a nurbs_curve sampled `samples` times, or a solid: its vertices). Every source point is projected on the target (Newton foot point on NURBS; closest triangle on a solid): returns max, mean, rms, the 95th percentile, the worst point and its foot, a 10-bin histogram, and for a surface target the distance signed along its normal. Reference: a sphere of radius 10 against points on radius 10.5 gives max = mean = rms = 0.5. With `tolerance`, `pass` is true when max <= tolerance. One-way: swap the roles to measure the other direction, or set `symmetric` for two meshes / 3D solids (Hausdorff both ways).

id.description: Id of the target: a nurbs_surface, a nurbs_curve or a 3D solid.

points.description: Measured points to compare with the target (1..20000). Give this or `referenceId`.

items.description: Measured point [x, y, z] in document units (world coordinates).

referenceId.description: Id of the entity whose samples are compared with the target (nurbs_surface, nurbs_curve or 3D solid). Give this or `points`.

samples.description: Samples per direction (surface) or along a curve for `referenceId`, integer 2..200. Default 25.

symmetric.description: true: measure BOTH ways between two meshes / 3D solids (`id` and `referenceId`, no `points`): forwardMax reference -> target, backwardMax target -> reference, hausdorff = the larger, with mean, rms, a 10-bin histogram and the worst point, from vertices and triangle centroids (`samples` is ignored; `tolerance` is checked against hausdorff). Default false (one-way).

tolerance.description: Largest acceptable maximum deviation, document units (> 0). Adds a `pass` verdict.

name: measure_deviation

description: Measure the straight-line distance between two locations. Each location may be a world-space point [x,y,z] (point1/point2) or an entity id (entityId1/entityId2, centroid used). Mix point and entity freely (e.g. point1 + entityId2). Returns data: { distance, unit } and a factual summary. Does not modify the document.

entityId1.description: Id of the first entity. Its bounding-box centroid is used as the first location when point1 is not provided.

entityId2.description: Id of the second entity. Its bounding-box centroid is used as the second location when point2 is not provided.

point1.description: First world-space point [x, y, z]. Omit to use entityId1 centroid instead.

point2.description: Second world-space point [x, y, z]. Omit to use entityId2 centroid instead.

name: measure_distance

description: Compute the perimeter or total length of a 2D shape. Supported entity kinds: 'line' (segment length), 'polyline' (sum of segment lengths; closed polyline adds last→first segment), 'rectangle' (2*(width+height)), 'circle' (circumference 2πr), 'arc' (arc length r*|angle|). Returns data: { perimeter, unit }. Does not modify the document.

entityId.description: Id of the 2D shape entity to measure. Supported kinds: 'line', 'polyline', 'rectangle', 'circle', 'arc'.

name: measure_perimeter

description: Convert a closed triangle mesh (or any 3D solid's triangles) into an exact B-rep solid on the native OCC kernel, so mass_properties is exact (method exact) and export_step writes real faces. mode "faceted": one planar face per triangle (the polyhedron the mesh is), up to `maxFaces`. mode "prismatic": segment_mesh first (same featureAngleDeg / fitTolerance), then each region fitted by a plane, cylinder, cone or sphere becomes ONE face on that exact surface, bounded by the exact intersection curves with its neighbours, and the faces are sewn into a solid (a plate with a tessellated hole gives 6 planes and a cylinder of the fitted radius; volume = the analytic value). Freeform regions, and regions whose boundary cannot be followed within fitTolerance, stay triangles (listed in data.facetedGroups with the warning MESH_BREP_GROUP_FACETED). Reports data.faces {plane, cylinder, ..., faceted}, volumeExact against volumeMesh, the largest fit residual (document units) and the kernel sewing report. The mesh must be closed, manifold and consistently wound. Refusals: MESH_ENTITY_NOT_FOUND, MESH_NOT_A_MESH, MESH_NOT_CLOSED, MESH_PARAM_INVALID, MESH_NON_MANIFOLD, MESH_ORIENTATION_INCONSISTENT, MESH_DEGENERATE, MESH_BREP_SEW_FAILED, MESH_KERNEL_UNSUPPORTED, MESH_ASSET_MISSING.

featureAngleDeg.description: prismatic: edges whose faces meet at more than this angle (degrees) separate regions. Default 30.

fitTolerance.description: prismatic: largest distance (document units) of a region vertex to its primitive, and the sewing tolerance. Default 0.001 x bounding-box diagonal (named default).

id.description: Id of the closed mesh (or other 3D solid) to convert.

keepSource.description: true: keep the source and add the result as a new mesh. Default false: the source entity is rewritten in place (same id, name, layer, colour).

maxFaces.description: Refuse meshes with more triangles than this. Default 50000, at most 200000.

mode.description: "faceted": one planar face per triangle. "prismatic": one exact face per fitted plane / cylinder / cone / sphere region.

name: mesh_to_brep

description: Rebuild a mesh solid (from import_mesh / the CLI tool import_step) that is a constant-section prism as an editable extrusion: it looks for an axis along which every vertex lies on two parallel planes and all side faces are parallel to the axis, extracts the outline polygon of the section (outer loop and holes) and recreates it as an extrude_profile solid (plus a boolean subtract of an extruded tool per hole, which needs the geometry kernel). The mesh is replaced by the new solid, which keeps its colour; use keepSource to keep the mesh too. Refuses, leaving the document unchanged, when the mesh is not a closed constant section (spheres, tapers, stepped or curved-profile parts: the outline is read from mesh edges, so arcs come back as polygons), has several separate regions or islands inside holes.

id.description: Id of the mesh entity (kind "mesh") to rebuild.

keepSource.description: Keep the source mesh next to the new solid. Default false (the mesh is replaced).

name: mesh_to_solid

description: Minkowski sum (dilation: grow `a` by the shape of `b`) or difference (erosion: the positions where `b` still fits inside `a`) of two closed meshes / solids. Sum with a small ball rounds every edge and corner of `a`; sum with a box grows it anisotropically; difference with a cutter gives the cutter-centre region. Convex x convex sums are exact in the TypeScript engine; non-convex operands and every difference use the Manifold engine (desktop app / CLI host). `b` is placed as modelled, so centre it on the origin for a symmetric result. Reports the result volume and area (document units). Refusals: MESH_NOT_CLOSED, MESH_ENTITY_NOT_FOUND, MESH_NOT_A_MESH, MESH_PARAM_INVALID, MESH_ENGINE_UNSUPPORTED.

a.description: Id of the closed mesh / solid to dilate or erode; rewritten with the result unless keepSources.

b.description: Id of the closed mesh / solid used as the structuring element (centre it on the origin).

keepSources.description: true: keep `a` and add the result as a new mesh. Default false: `a` is rewritten in place.

name: minkowski_sum

description: Mirror an entity across the origin plane normal to a world axis by negating that axis component of its position ONLY: the entity's shape, size and rotation are not reflected (a handed part keeps its handedness; only its location moves to the other side). axis must be 'x', 'y', or 'z'.

axis.description: World axis to mirror across: 'x' negates the X position component, 'y' negates Y, 'z' negates Z.

id.description: Id of the entity to mirror.

name: mirror_entity

description: Create the shape a fraction t of the way between two entities with the same structure: two nurbs_curve entities with the same degree, knot vector and pole count, two nurbs_surface sheets with the same degrees, knot vectors and pole grid, or two mesh entities with the same vertices count and triangle connectivity. Poles (or vertices) are interpolated linearly in world coordinates, so t 0 reproduces fromId, t 1 reproduces toId, and two planes z 0 and z 10 morph at t 0.3 into the plane z 3. Both inputs are kept; the result is one new entity of the same kind. Use it for blending design variants and for animation frames. Refuses ids that do not exist (DEF_ENTITY_NOT_FOUND), entities of different structure (DEF_MORPH_INCOMPATIBLE, with the first difference found: a topology change needs implicit modelling) and t outside 0..1 (DEF_MORPH_PARAMETER).

fromId.description: Id of the entity at t = 0 (nurbs_curve, nurbs_surface or mesh).

t.description: Fraction of the way from fromId to toId, unitless, 0..1.

toId.description: Id of the entity at t = 1; must have the same structure as fromId.

name: morph_bodies

description: Evaluate the mechanism across a value sweep and return per-step instance transforms plus interference flags. mode="joint": sweep a single joint (by jointId) through a value range (radians for revolute, units for prismatic). mode="parameter": sweep a named doc.parameters entry through a value range, propagating to any joints that reference it. "target" is the joint id or parameter name to sweep. "start" and "end" define the sweep range (inclusive). "steps" is the number of samples (default 24; clamped to [2, 360]; non-integers rounded). "interferenceCheck" (default false): when true, runs a lightweight overlap test (axis-aligned box of each instance in its rotated pose; faces that merely touch are not interference) on every instance pair at each step. Returns the input document unchanged (affected:[]) with data: { steps: MotionStep[], interferences: InterferencePair[],   summary: { totalSteps: number, framesWithInterference: number } }. Failure cases (unknown target, start===end, steps<2) return an explanatory summary with empty data.

contactSetId.description: Id of a contact set (create_contact_set). The sweep ends at the first value where a pair of the set touches (bisected to 1e-9 of the range) or an unsolved loop stops closing; data.contact reports { stopped, stopValue, reason, pair }.

end.description: End value of the sweep range (inclusive). For revolute joints: radians. For prismatic joints: document units. For parameters: the parameter's unit.

interferenceCheck.description: When true, run a lightweight AABB overlap pass on every pair of InstanceEntity objects at each step. Colliding pairs are recorded in the returned interferences array. Default: false.

mode.description: Sweep mode. "joint": vary a specific joint value directly. "parameter": vary a named doc.parameters entry; downstream joints that reference it are re-evaluated.

start.description: Start value of the sweep range (inclusive). For revolute joints: radians. For prismatic joints: document units. For parameters: the parameter's unit.

steps.description: Number of samples across the range (default 24, minimum 2, maximum 360). Must be an integer. Step k = start + (end - start) * k / (steps - 1).

target.description: What to sweep. For mode="joint": the joint id (must exist in doc.joints). For mode="parameter": the parameter name (must exist in doc.parameters and resolve to a number).

name: motion_study

description: Move building elements in plan by delta [dx, dy]; use this instead of move_entities for building elements, because hosted elements and supports follow and joins are recomputed (move_entities would desync the building model). Doors/windows travel with their wall (to slide an opening along its wall use update_opening). Corner joins are recomputed. A moved pipe takes its pipe supports along and a moved steel member makes its supports re-check their reach: they re-attach to the steel at the new position or become unattached (the summary says which). A support alone is refused: it rests on its pipe or on its spec-driven run (the refusal names it; a run moves with the equipment it connects to or by edit_route).
name: move_building_element

description: Translate several entities by the same delta in one step (one undo). Ids that do not exist are skipped and listed in the summary; if none exist nothing changes.

delta.description: Translation [dx, dy, dz] in document units applied to every entity.

ids.description: Entity ids to move (non-empty, at most 10000). Missing ids are skipped.

name: move_entities

description: Move faces of an imported or built B-rep directly, without its history (direct editing). Pick the faces by faceIndices, facesNear or faceNames. mode "offset" (`distance`, document units): every picked face moves along its surface normal - a plane along its outward normal (positive adds material), a cylinder / cone / sphere / torus AWAY from its axis or centre (a bore widens, a boss thickens); the neighbouring faces extend or shrink to meet the moved ones (drafted and obtuse neighbours, adjacent picked faces) (BRepOffset_MakeOffset, intersection join). mode "translate" (`vector` [x, y, z]): one planar face moves by the component of the vector along its normal (the in-plane part changes nothing), any other pick is a FEATURE (a hole, a boss, a pocket: pick all its faces) that is moved rigidly to the new place. mode "rotate" (`axis` { origin, direction } and `angleDeg`, |angle| < 85 for a planar face): a planar face tilts to its rotated plane with the neighbours extending; any other pick is a feature rotated rigidly. Exact B-rep only (native OCC kernel); the source is consumed and the result must be one valid solid. Returns data { volumeBefore, volumeAfter, volumeUnit, faces }. Refuses missing mode parameters (DIR_FACE_MOVE_PARAMS), a cylinder or sphere that would vanish (DIR_FACE_MOVE_TOPOLOGY) and a move OCC cannot rebuild (DIR_FACE_MOVE_FAILED). Next: mass_properties, inspect_topology, delete_faces.

angleDeg.description: rotate: angle in degrees, positive counter-clockwise about the axis direction (non-zero, below 180).

axis.description: rotate: the rotation axis.

direction.description: Axis direction [x, y, z] (any length > 0).

origin.description: A point [x, y, z] on the rotation axis.

distance.description: offset: signed distance in document units along the surface normal (non-zero).

faceNames.description: Persistent face names (inspect_topology on the native kernel): recorded automatically from the first pick and used on regeneration; a name that is gone or split refuses the step (REF_LOST / REF_SPLIT).

facesNear.description: Faces picked by location: each point takes the face nearest to it.

items.description: A point [x, y, z] on the face (its nearest face is taken).

id.description: Id of the 3D solid.

mode.description: How the faces move: "offset" along the surface normal, "translate" by a vector, "rotate" about an axis.

vector.description: translate: displacement [x, y, z] in document units (non-zero).

name: move_faces

description: Slide a valve or reducer along its leg: give the new centreDistance (from the leg start, mm) or a delta (mm along the leg direction, negative toward the start). The cut lengths of the neighbouring pipe pieces are re-derived; nothing else changes. Refused when the component would overlap an elbow, flange set, tee or another component, or leave the leg (RTE_INLINE_DOES_NOT_FIT, document unchanged). Same data as insert_inline_component. Refusals: RTE_UNKNOWN_RUN, RTE_UNKNOWN_COMPONENT, RTE_INLINE_DOES_NOT_FIT.

centreDistance.description: New distance of the centre from the leg start, mm. Give this or delta.

delta.description: Shift along the leg direction, mm. Give this or centreDistance.

name: move_inline_component

description: Read-only snap to a scan point: the cloud point nearest to `point` (document units) within maxDistance, with its source record index and the distance of the second-nearest point (ambiguity check: when both are close, pick a better seed). data.found is false when no point is within maxDistance.

cloudId.description: Id of an attached cloud (affected[0] of attach_point_cloud, e.g. "cloud-1.1").

name: nearest_cloud_point

description: Surface through a network of crossing curves given in ANY order (nurbs_curve ids, 6 to 120): two families of curves, every curve of one meeting every curve of the other and none meeting its own family (a curve net, e.g. 3 + 3 curves of a panel). The families are found by their crossings (curves within `tolerance` of each other), ordered along each other and oriented consistently, then a Gordon surface is fitted: u runs along the family of the FIRST id, v across it. Refused with SWG_NETWORK_UNSORTABLE when the crossing graph is not two families (a curve crosses its own family, or is isolated) and SWG_NETWORK_NOT_INTERSECTING naming a pair that does not meet. `edgeMatch` makes an edge of the result (u0, u1, v0, v1) continue an existing sheet: [{ boundary, neighbourId (a nurbs_surface whose boundary edge the edge lies on), continuity G0 | G1 | G2 }]; the measured gaps and angles are returned (data.boundaries). Returns data { families, crossingGap, deviation, guideDeviation, seamGap, boundaries }. Next: check_continuity, analyze_surface_curvature, check_sweep_loft.

color.description: Hex color string #rrggbb, e.g. "#c8553d". Defaults to "#9fb4c7".

curveIds.description: 6 to 120 nurbs_curve ids forming the network, in any order and direction.

edgeMatch.description: Optional edge matching to neighbouring sheets, one entry per edge.

boundary.description: Edge of the result to match: u0 / u1 the first / last u isoline, v0 / v1 the first / last v isoline.

continuity.description: G0 position only (measured), G1 tangent plane, G2 tangent plane and normal curvature across the edge.

neighbourId.description: Id of the nurbs_surface the edge continues; the edge must lie on one of its four boundary edges.

layerId.description: Layer id to assign the entity to. Defaults to the document default layer.

name.description: Optional display name for the entity (shown in the scene tree).

position.description: Origin [x, y, z] of the surface in document units; the poles are relative to it. Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

tolerance.description: Largest gap (document units) between two curves still counted as crossing. Default 1e-4 x the size of the network.

name: network_surface

description: Read-only ideal rocket engine (thrust chamber + nozzle) performance by 1D isentropic flow of a perfect gas (Sutton & Biblarz ch. 3, NASA SP-125): characteristic velocity c*, exit Mach / pressure / temperature / velocity, thrust coefficient C_F and specific impulse Isp in vacuum and at the ambient pressure, mass flow and thrust. Chamber: `chamberPressure` (+ required `pressureUnit`), `chamberTemperatureK`, `gamma` and `molarMass` (kg/kmol) of the combustion gas — take the chamber values of a NASA CEA run, e.g. LOX/LH2 MR 6 at 206 bar: Tc 3599 K, γ 1.1475, M 13.61 (c* then matches CEA to 0.1 %, Isp the shifting-equilibrium value to ~3 %). Nozzle: `expansionRatio` Ae/At or `exitPressure`; `divergence` ideal (λ 1, default), conical (`halfAngleDeg`, λ = (1+cos α)/2) or factor (`divergenceFactor`, e.g. 0.99 for an 80 % bell). Ambient: `ambientPressure` or `altitudeM` (standard atmosphere); default vacuum. Size by `throatDiameterM`, `throatAreaM2` or a `thrustN` target (in vacuum or at ambient, `thrustAt`). `cStarEfficiency` (default 1) models combustion losses. Warns on over-expansion and on likely flow separation (p_e < 0.4 p_a, Summerfield). Next: design_nozzle for the CAD contour.

altitudeM.description: Ambient pressure of the U.S. Standard Atmosphere 1976 at this geometric altitude in m (-5000..86000).

ambientPressure.description: Ambient pressure in pressureUnit, >= 0 (0 = vacuum). Or altitudeM.

divergence.description: Exit-flow divergence loss: ideal (default, λ 1), conical (halfAngleDeg) or factor.

exitPressure.description: Design exit pressure in pressureUnit (0 < p_e < p_c). Give this or expansionRatio.

expansionRatio.description: Nozzle area ratio Ae/At > 1. Give this or exitPressure.

gamma.description: Ratio of specific heats of the gas, 1 < γ < 2 (≈ 1.13-1.25 for combustion products).

halfAngleDeg.description: conical: nozzle half-angle in degrees, 0 < α < 45 (15 typical).

molarMass.description: Molar mass of the gas in kg/kmol (g/mol), > 0.

pressureUnit.description: Unit of every pressure parameter: Pa, kPa, MPa, bar, atm (101325 Pa) or psi (6894.757 Pa). Required.

throatDiameterM.description: Throat diameter in m, > 0 (sizing; give at most one of the three sizing inputs).

thrustAt.description: Condition of thrustN: vacuum (default) or ambient.

thrustN.description: Target thrust in N, > 0: the throat is sized for it.

name: nozzle_performance

description: Create a parallel-offset copy of a 2D shape at the given distance. Supported kinds: line (offset perpendicular to direction, positive=left of start→end), polyline (each segment offset then joined at miter intersections), circle (concentric: positive=larger, negative=smaller), rectangle (all sides expand/shrink: positive=outward, negative=inward). The original entity is unchanged; a new entity is added. No-op for unsupported kinds or if the resulting shape would be degenerate (e.g. negative circle radius).

distance.description: Offset distance in work-plane units. Positive = left of direction (line/polyline) or outward (circle/rectangle). Negative reverses the direction.

id.description: Id of the source entity to offset.

name: offset_2d

description: Grow (distance > 0) or shrink (distance < 0) an implicit FIELD by a distance in document units: the iso-surface moves outward by `distance`. Exact when the source field is exact (primitive, transform or field_from_solid of one); on blended / booleaned / lattice sources the surface is not the true offset and the reply carries warning IMP_OFFSET_NOT_EXACT.

distance.description: Offset distance in document units; positive grows the body, negative shrinks it. A number or a scalar field id (graded offset, create_scalar_field).

field.description: Id of the field to offset.

name.description: Optional label for the result node.

name: offset_field

description: Offset the surface of a mesh (or any 3D solid) by a signed distance: positive grows it, negative shrinks it. method "level_set" (default) builds the parallel body from a signed-distance field: robust on any closed mesh, outward corners become round, inward corners stay sharp, and the result is a clean manifold; it needs a closed mesh and the Manifold engine (desktop app / CLI host). The grid edge is the `tolerance`; a result vertex lies within one edge of the exact offset surface, so the volume is within area x edge (data.errorBound, data.toleranceMet says whether the tolerance itself was reached within maxCells; smooth surfaces are usually far better than the bound). method "normal" moves each vertex along its angle-weighted normal: works on open meshes and anywhere, but may self-intersect for large distances (data.selfIntersectionsCreated). Lengths in document units. Refusals: MESH_ENTITY_NOT_FOUND, MESH_NOT_A_MESH, MESH_NOT_CLOSED, MESH_PARAM_INVALID, MESH_OFFSET_RESOLUTION, MESH_ENGINE_UNSUPPORTED.

distance.description: Signed offset in document units: > 0 outward, < 0 inward. Must not be 0.

id.description: Id of the mesh (or other 3D solid) to offset.

keepSource.description: true: keep the source and add the result as a new mesh. Default false: the source entity is rewritten in place (same id, name, layer, colour).

maxCells.description: Level-set grid cell cap; a finer tolerance than the cap allows refuses with MESH_OFFSET_RESOLUTION. Default 40000.

method.description: "level_set" (default, closed meshes, needs Manifold) or "normal" (vertex normals, open meshes allowed).

tolerance.description: Target distance (document units) between a result vertex and the exact surface: the level-set grid edge is set to it. When that needs more cells than maxCells the grid is coarsened to fit and the result reports the weaker bound it really has (data.toleranceMet false, data.errorBound). Default 0.002 x bounding-box diagonal (named default).

name: offset_mesh

description: Lay copies of an entity along a curve: chain links round a chainring and cassette loop, tyre tread blocks round a tyre, sprocket / gear teeth, cable clips, rivets, fence posts, parts fanned on an arc. By default each copy is ORIENTED by the curve: model the source at the world origin in its "along the path" pose: its local +X follows the path tangent, +Y the path normal, +Z the binormal (≈ world up on a horizontal path); copies rotate about their position. orient:false keeps the source rotation instead (plain spacing along a path). rollStep adds an extra roll about the tangent per copy (π/2 alternates chain plates). Source: `sourceId` (an entity to copy) or `componentId` (fresh instances of a component from create_component). Path, give exactly one: `pathId` (a 2D sketch curve: line, arc, polyline, spline, circle, ellipse, rectangle; open or closed), `path` points (straight runs, or smooth: true for a spline; closed: true loops back) or `arc` (centre, normal, radius and angle sweep in radians; a full 2π sweep is a closed loop). Open paths put copies at both ends (a single copy sits at the start); closed loops space count copies evenly all round. startOffset / endOffset trim the open path from both ends (on a closed loop startOffset shifts the pattern). The source entity is kept.

arc.description: Alternative to pathId / path: a circular arc to follow.

center.description: World-space [x, y, z] centre of the arc.

endAngle.description: Sweep end in radians (counter-clockwise about normal).

normal.description: Normal of the arc plane (non-zero), e.g. [0, 0, 1] for an XY arc.

radius.description: Arc radius, > 0.

startAngle.description: Sweep start in radians from the plane's local +X axis.

closed.description: With path points: loop back from the last point to the first.

componentId.description: Alternative to sourceId: id of a component; each copy is a new instance of it.

endOffset.description: Path length skipped at the end (default 0, >= 0). Ignored on closed loops.

orient.description: Rotate each copy to the path frame (default true); false keeps the source rotation.

path.description: World [x, y, z] points of the path (>= 2). Alternative to pathId.

pathId.description: Id of a 2D sketch curve to follow (placed by its own work plane).

rollStep.description: Extra roll about the tangent added per copy, in radians (default 0).

smooth.description: With path points: a smooth spline through them (default: straight runs).

sourceId.description: Id of the entity to copy (2D or 3D).

startOffset.description: Path length skipped at the start (default 0, >= 0). On a closed loop: pattern shift.

name: pattern_along_path

description: Repeat seed profiles on a rectangular lattice and emboss, deboss or scribe all copies on a face in ONE exact operation (a perforation grid, a row of dimples, studs on a grip). `seedProfileIds` are closed 2D shapes (or texts with a font) in the sketch; `grid` { countX, countY, pitchX, pitchY } gives the number of copies along the sketch x and y axes and the distance between copy origins, in sketch (chart) document units (on a cylinder x runs round the circumference, y along the axis; lengths are kept). `placement` puts the seed (copy 0, 0) on the face like emboss_on_face. Copy (i, j) is the seed moved by (i pitchX, j pitchY). Everything else is emboss_on_face: mode emboss | deboss | scribe, depth, maxLengthStrain, fitTolerance, the closed forms, the data (plus data.instances and data.grid). A pitch smaller than the seed extent refuses with WRP_PATTERN_OVERLAP, a copy leaving the face with WRP_OUTSIDE_FACE (nothing is cut). Needs the exact (native) kernel. Next: check_wrap, mass_properties.

depth.description: Height of the emboss or depth of the deboss, document units, > 0. Not used by scribe.

face.description: The face to work on: give faceNear (a point on the face), or faceIndex, or faceName. The command records the face name so a later edit of the model finds the same face (REF_LOST when it is gone).

faceIndex.description: Unique face index of the solid (inspect_faces / inspect_topology list them).

faceName.description: Persistent face name recorded by an earlier run of this command; wins over faceIndex and faceNear.

faceNear.description: A point on or near the intended face [x, y, z] in world document units; the face nearest to it is taken.

fitTolerance.description: Largest deviation of a fitted pcurve from its exact image, document units. Default: 1e-6 x the solid diagonal.

grid.description: The lattice: counts and pitches in the sketch frame. At most 2000 copies in all.

countX.description: Copies along the sketch x axis (1..200).

countY.description: Copies along the sketch y axis (1..200).

pitchX.description: Distance between copy origins along x, sketch document units (> the seed width when countX > 1).

pitchY.description: Distance between copy origins along y, sketch document units (> the seed height when countY > 1).

id.description: Id of the solid.

maxLengthStrain.description: Largest accepted relative length change of the wrap (1 = 100 %). Default 0.02 (named default).

mode.description: emboss: material added; deboss: material removed; scribe: the face is split along every copy, no material change.

placement.description: Sketch-to-face placement. Chart axes: x follows the circumference (cylinder / cone: +azimuth about the axis from the face x direction; plane: the face x direction), y follows the axis (cone: away from the apex along the generator; plane: normal x x direction). Lengths and angles are kept (develop).

anchor.description: Where the sketch sits on the face: sketch point `chart` lands on face point `on`.

chart.description: Sketch point [x, y] (sketch plane document units) that lands on `on`. Default [0, 0].

on.description: Point [x, y, z] on the face where the sketch point lands. Default: the point of the face nearest to faceNear (else the face centroid).

angleDeg.description: Turn of the sketch in degrees, counter-clockwise seen from outside the face, from the face reference direction (cylinder / cone: around the axis, +azimuth; plane: the face x direction). Default 0.

method.description: How the sketch is carried onto the face. develop (default) keeps every length and angle and works on plane, cylinder and cone faces (Gaussian curvature 0). geodesic, parametric and project are not built yet (WRP_METHOD_UNAVAILABLE); a sphere or freeform face is WRP_FACE_NOT_DEVELOPABLE with develop.

mirror.description: Flip the sketch y axis (a wrap seen from inside). Default false.

seedProfileIds.description: Ids of the closed 2D profiles (or font texts) repeated by the pattern.

name: pattern_on_face

description: Read-only pressure drop of one pipe run (add_pipe_run), flowing from its first to its last point. Give the run id (`pipeId`, e.g. "pipe-1") and exactly one flow: `flowM3h` (m³/h) or `massFlowKgS` (kg/s). Fluid is water at `temperatureC` (default 20 °C; density and viscosity from Kell / Vogel fits) unless `density` (kg/m³) and `viscosity` (Pa·s) are given for another liquid. Inner diameter = outside diameter minus twice the standard wall (Sch 40 / STD table of add_pipe_run, e.g. DN100 -> 102.26 mm). Roughness defaults by the pipe material (steel 0.045 mm, stainless 0.015, galvanised 0.15, cast iron 0.26, copper / plastic 0.0015). Friction: laminar 64/Re below Re 2300, else Colebrook-White solved iteratively. Straight loss = f (L/D) ρ v²/2 along the 3D centreline; fittings = ΣK ρ v²/2 with one K per interior bend from its deflection angle (K90 by `bendType`: long_radius 0.30, standard 0.40, mitre 1.10; K = K90 · sin(θ/2)/sin 45°) plus `extraK` (valves, entrance / exit); static = ρ g Δz (end minus start elevation, a riser adds head, a drop gives back). Returns data { diameter, velocity, reynolds, friction, losses (kPa), bends, pressureDrop { kPa, bar, headM }, warnings }; warns when velocity is outside 0.5-3 m/s (liquids) or the flow is laminar / transitional. Incompressible single-phase only (not for gas, steam or slurries).

bendType.description: Bend construction for K: long_radius (r/D 1.5, K90 0.30, default), standard (r/D 1, 0.40) or mitre (1.10).

density.description: Fluid density in kg/m³, > 0. Default: water at temperatureC.

extraK.description: Extra loss coefficient ΣK of valves, strainers, entrance / exit, ≥ 0. Default 0.

flowM3h.description: Volumetric flow in m³/h, > 0. Give this or massFlowKgS.

massFlowKgS.description: Mass flow in kg/s, > 0 (converted with the fluid density). Give this or flowM3h.

pipeId.description: Id of the pipe run from add_pipe_run, e.g. "pipe-1".

roughnessMm.description: Absolute pipe roughness ε in mm, > 0. Default by the pipe material (steel 0.045).

temperatureC.description: Water temperature in °C, 0..100. Default 20. Ignored for the property it overrides.

viscosity.description: Fluid dynamic viscosity in Pa·s (e.g. 0.001 for water), > 0. Default: water at temperatureC.

name: pipe_hydraulics

description: Section properties and mass per metre of a round steel pipe: inside diameter, metal and flow area (mm2), second moment I and section modulus Z (mm4, mm3), and mass per metre of the metal (plain-end, 7850 kg/m3 by default), contents and insulation, plus weight in kN/m. Give a pipeId (pipe element: uses its spec OD / wall, else the legacy wall table, flagged unverified), or nps / dn with schedule (ASME B36.10M / B36.19M row from the catalogue), or odMm with wallMm. Lengths are mm in and out (a pipe element diameter is read in document units). Example: NPS 6 Sch 40, water: 28.264 + 18.646 = 46.909 kg/m. Refuses unknown pipes / sizes / schedules and non-physical walls (wall >= OD / 2). Next: use weightKnPerM for support and rack loads (check_pipe_supports, pipe_hydraulics).

dn.description: Nominal diameter DN (integer). Converted to NPS for the catalogue lookup.

insulation.description: Insulation layer around the pipe (mass only; cladding is not included).

materialDensityKgM3.description: Pipe metal density in kg/m3. Default 7850 (carbon steel).

nps.description: Nominal pipe size, inch designation ("6", "2-1/2" or 2.5). With schedule: OD and wall come from the catalogue. Give nps or dn.

odMm.description: Outside diameter in mm, when no size is given.

pipeId.description: Id of a pipe element (building category pipe). Its spec binding (OD, wall) is used, else the legacy wall table (flagged unverified).

schedule.description: Pipe schedule ("40", "80", "STD", "10S" …); with nps / dn selects the catalogue wall.

standard.description: Pipe standard, "ASME B36.10M" (default), "ASME B36.19M" or "EN 10220" (OD only: give wallMm).

wallMm.description: Nominal wall in mm (with nps / dn / odMm, instead of a schedule).

name: pipe_section_properties

description: Query: the connectivity graph of routed pipe: nodes (every derived part, and the tie-ins / equipment nozzles that runs attach to), edges (joints between parts, attachments of a part to a port, olets welded to their header piece), openEnds (part ports connected to nothing: free run ends, unused tee outlets), components (connected groups of node ids), and mismatches (connected ports that disagree in size, rating, facing or end type). Give lineIds to limit it (attached branch and continuation runs are included); from + to (a port id such as "P-101:N2" or a tie-in id, or a part id) adds data.path, the shortest chain of node ids between them or null when they are not connected. data = { nodes, edges, openEnds, components, mismatches, path?, brokenRuns }; a run that no longer derives is listed in brokenRuns and left out. Does not modify the document. Refusals: RTE_UNKNOWN_LINE, RTE_UNKNOWN_PORT. Next: check_piping for the issues, route_pipe to connect an open end.

from.description: Path start: port id (tie-in id, "<tag>:<mark>") or part id. Give with `to`.

lineIds.description: Line ids to include (affected[0] of create_pipeline). Omit for every line.

to.description: Path end: port id or part id. Give with `from`.

name: piping_connectivity

description: Query: bill of materials and cut list of routed pipe, derived from the stored runs and their spec: part counts by key (elbow90LR, elbow90LRTrimmed = a 90 elbow cut to the turn, pipeBend, flangeWeldNeck / flangeSocketWeld / flangeThreaded, gasketSpiralWound, boltSet, valveGate, reducerConcentric, reducerEccentric, tee, reducingTee, weldolet, sockolet, threadolet, stubIn ...), pipePieces (cutLengthMm per straight piece, leg index), joints (buttWeld, branchWeld = the set-on weld of an olet or stub-in to the header, socketWeld, threaded, flanged, fittingToFitting, with position, gap and, for socketWeld / threaded, engagementMm = how far the pipe goes into the fitting, which the cut lengths include), counts also hold buttWelds, branchWelds, socketWelds, threadedJoints, flangedJoints and fittingToFitting, studs, totalPipeMm, centrelineLengthMm (legs - 2 x centre-to-end + arcs), legs and turns (angle, nominal angle, deviationDeg, centreToEnd, kind standard | trimmed | bend; a bend part lists radiusMm and developedLengthMm = the pipe in its arc, not counted in totalPipeMm), inline (valves and reducers: faces, part ids, size; valves: operator envelope; eccentric reducers: flat side, offset, invertStepMm), branches (tee / olet / stub-in per branch point), insulation (per insulated line: code, thickness, material, pipeLengthMm of the straight pieces and the outer area of the insulation round them in m2; fittings are not counted), tracing (per line with set_heat_tracing: tracers, centrelineM, valves, flanges, supports on its runs, allowances, tracerLengthM), supports (pipe supports per run, add_pipe_support runId), warnings and unverified (spec not approved or catalogue rows not grade A, with reasons). Lengths in mm. Give runId or lineId; with neither, every run is counted. A run that no longer derives (its equipment or tie-in moved or was removed, the spec lost a part: marked broken) is skipped and listed in data.brokenRuns [{ runId, code, message }]; asked for by runId it is refused with its RTE_* code. Refusals: RTE_UNKNOWN_RUN, RTE_UNKNOWN_LINE. Does not modify the document. Next: check_piping for the issues; route_pipe / insert_inline_component / add_branch to change the route.

lineId.description: Every run of one line (affected[0] of create_pipeline).

name: piping_takeoff

description: Put 2D entities (sketches drawn in local coordinates) on a sketch plane: each entity's local plane becomes the sketch plane, its local origin at the plane origin plus at (plane-local [x, y]). Extrude / revolve them afterwards as usual. Regeneration re-places them, so a sketch on a face plane follows the face.

at.description: Plane-local [x, y] of the entities' local origin. Default [0, 0].

ids.description: Ids of the 2D entities to place.

name: place_on_sketch_plane

description: Earthworks report of a graded platform by the grid method: cut and fill volumes (m³), net (cut - fill, positive = surplus to export), cut / fill plan areas (m²), pad area, maximum cut / fill depth, grid spacing and the number of samples outside the TIN, plus the daylight line vertices. Read-only; data { platformId, cutM3, fillM3, netM3, cutAreaM2, fillAreaM2, padAreaM2, maxCutDepthM, maxFillDepthM, gridSpacingM, samples, samplesOutsideTin, daylight }.

gridSpacing.description: Grid cell size (document units). Default: about 2500 cells over the pad.

name: platform_earthworks

description: The SHA-256 a human signs to authorize one human-only PLM act (set_item_identity with policy, set_item_marking, record_approval, release_item, create_change_order with a classification, classify_change_order, set_change_state, set_lifecycle_state to obsolete, attach_release_package, bind_component_item, unbind_component_item, record_as_built, import_qif_results): pass the command, the params you will send (without confirmation) and a fresh nonce. The signature (Ed25519 over the UTF-8 hex hash, prefixed by the context string the signing host applies) goes in the command as confirmation { alg, keyId, publicKey, signature, nonce }. It is valid only for the current PLM state of this document. An agent cannot sign. Read-only.

nonce.description: A fresh random string chosen by the signer (at least 8 characters).

params.description: The params the command will be called with (confirmation, at and by are not part of the payload; the host sets at).

name: plm_act_payload

description: What changed between two revisions of the managed item (or against "WORKING", the live document): parameters (expression from -> to), feature steps (added / removed / edited / suppressed counts and ids), entities, materials, sheet title blocks and effectivity. Revisions without a snapshot (in_work, never released) can only be compared as the current revision. Read-only; volume / mass deltas are not computed yet.

from.description: Revision label, or "WORKING".

to.description: Revision label, or "WORKING".

name: plm_diff

description: Report the configuration-management status of this document: managed item, revisions (state, iterations, content hash, effectivity), open ECR / ECO, whether the definition is dirty since the last checkpoint, integrity of released revisions (recomputed hashes: ok / mismatch), policy with defaults named, unverified inputs and `nextHumanAction` in plain language. Read-only.
name: plm_status

description: Run the physics simulation (same engine and parameters as simulate_motion) and draw the result as an SVG time-series chart, so a motion can be inspected without a screen. Returns data.svg (stacked panels sharing the time axis; each has a title, y axis with unit, grid, legend), data.width, data.panels (per series: min, max, final value, in the panel unit) and a one-line summary. `quantities` picks the panels: "joint_angle" (deg for revolute joints, mm for prismatic ones, from the start pose), "joint_velocity" (rpm / m/s), "motor_torque" (N·m), "motor_power" (kW), "reaction_force" (magnitude per tree joint and loop, N; runs the reaction pass, slower), "energy" (J: kinetic, potential = gravity + joint springs relative to the start pose, total, and cumulative energy dissipated by damping / friction: a flat total = conservation, a falling one = decay). `joints` restricts the series to those joint (or motor) ids. Default: joint_velocity of every joint. Closed loops and cylinders use the same timestep rules as simulate_motion. With the CLI, `llull plot_simulation … --save plot.png` rasterizes data.svg. Read-only; needs the physics engine like simulate_motion.

joints.description: Only these joint / motor ids (reaction_force: joint or loop ids). Default every one (at most 12 joint series).

quantities.description: Panels to draw: joint_angle, joint_velocity, motor_torque, motor_power, reaction_force, energy. Default ["joint_velocity"].

sampleRate.description: Samples per second drawn. Default about 600 points over the run (never below 50 Hz).

timestep.description: Integration step in seconds; default as simulate_motion.

width.description: Chart width in px. Default 900.

name: plot_simulation

description: NUMBERS form of the ply book (the SVG sheets of the same plies come from export_ply_book): numeric content of the ply book of a composite part: plies grouped by sequence label (one sheet per sequence), each with its id, name, material, orientation in degrees, covered area in mm^2, the ids of its flat pieces (the pieces export_ply_flat_patterns_dxf writes) and the boundary length in mm. The result is flagged reviewRequired (a ply book is a release document) and unverified when a lamina record is mean / unknown data. Read-only.
name: ply_book_data

description: Read-only preparation report of a flow case, before any solve. Unions the bodies into one surface (through the kernel when installed), checks it is watertight and not self-intersecting (open / non-manifold edge counts with positions), finds features smaller than two cells of the target grid (thin walls, gaps, small holes and bosses), sizes the flow domain (buildings: COST 732 / AIJ; external aero: named llull defaults) and the blockage, estimates cells, device memory and run time, and picks the solver from the Mach number. `data.checks` is a pass / warn / fail / not_run list with stable CFD_* codes; `data.status` is the worst of them. Nothing is changed or solved. Pass `deviceMemoryBytes` to also check the memory against a device.

deviceMemoryBytes.description: Device memory in bytes (> 0) to check the estimate against, e.g. 8e9. Absent: the memory check is not run.

quality.description: Check at this grid quality (64 / 128 / 256 cells per reference length) instead of the case value.

name: prepare_cfd_case

description: Largest constant fillet radius each edge of a 3D solid accepts, measured by bisection on exact kernel evaluations (each edge probed alone with fillet_edge semantics, results cached by the kernel). Use it BEFORE fillet_edge: pick a radius below maxRadius. Select edges like fillet_edge (edgeIndices from inspect_topology, edgesNear points, or edgeNames); with none, every roundable edge up to 32. Returns per edge: maxRadius (largest radius that builds, document units), upperBound (first guess: mean width of the adjacent faces across the edge; the search grows beyond it while it builds, up to the bounding-box diagonal), limitingCode (the BLD_* code of the first refused radius, e.g. BLD_RADIUS_TOO_LARGE, or null when nothing up to the diagonal was refused) and the number of exact evaluations. Interactions between several rounded edges are not probed: round them together and read the refusal code. Needs the exact kernel (check kernel_info). Does not modify the document.

edgeIndices.description: 0-based unique-edge indices from inspect_topology. Omit (with no edgesNear / edgeNames) to probe every roundable edge.

edgeNames.description: Persistent edge names (inspect_topology lists them on the native kernel); win over edgeIndices / edgesNear.

edgesNear.description: Select edges by location, as in fillet_edge.

items.description: A point [x, y, z] in document units on or near the edge (the roundable edge nearest to it is probed).

id.description: Id of the 3D solid entity to probe.

maxEvaluations.description: Exact fillet evaluations per edge (>= 1). Default 12.

tolerance.description: Stop the bisection when the bracket is smaller than this, in document units (> 0). Default 1e-3 x the bounding-box diagonal (1e-3 x the first guess when the diagonal is unknown).

name: probe_fillet

description: Read how result probes change over time: for every stored increment of a solved analysis (heat_transient: each written time; a static or steady case has one) return the probe value, so heating curves and settling can be checked without a screen. data { analysisId, series [{ probeId, name, quantity, unit, nodeId, nodeDistance, points [{ time (s), value }], missing (increments without a value), start, end, min, max (each { time, value } | null) }], svg (time-series chart, one panel per unit, or null when no probe has two increments), width, height }. The summary lists start / end / min / max per probe. Probes come from add_result_probe; values are read at the nearest mesh node, in the analysis unit system (temperature in the case scale). Needs state solved (fea_mesh then fea_solve); analysis_report gives the same values inline per load case or time. With the CLI, `--save plot.png` rasterizes data.svg.

analysisId.description: Id of the analysis (affected[0] of create_analysis, e.g. an-1.1).

plot.description: Draw data.svg. Default true; false returns the numbers only.

probeIds.description: Only these probe ids (affected[0] of add_result_probe). Default every probe of the analysis.

width.description: Chart width in px. Default 900.

name: probe_history

description: Bring edges of a 3D solid into a sketch plane as LINKED 2D geometry: mode "project" draws each edge projected onto the plane (an open polyline), mode "intersect" puts a point where each edge crosses the plane. Pick edges by edgeIndices / edgesNear / edgeNames (none = all). The link follows the edges by their persistent names on regeneration; a lost edge fails the step (REF_LOST) and check_model reports sketch_link_lost. break_sketch_link freezes the geometry. Needs the native kernel.

edgesNear.description: Edges picked by location.

items.description: A point [x, y, z] near the edge.

frozen.description: Set by break_sketch_link: plane-local geometry drawn as is, with no link to a solid.

id.description: Id of the 3D solid whose edges are used.

mode.description: "project" (default): edges projected onto the plane; "intersect": their crossing points.

name: project_edges_to_sketch

description: Project 2D sketch entities (or font text) onto the faces of a solid: along `direction` (default: the sketch normal, turned to point at the solid) each point lands on the nearest face ahead of it; with `closest: true` each point goes to its closest point on the faces within `maxDistance`. The result is one nurbs_curve per run of a sketch piece on a face (data.curves[i]: id, faceIndex, faceName, length3d and chartLength in document units, lengthStrain = length3d / chartLength - 1). Projection stretches (a 30 mm chord projected onto a radius 20 cylinder is a 33.92 mm arc); wrap_to_face keeps lengths. `faces` limits the target faces (default: all). Parts of the sketch that miss every face are reported in data.missed [{ entityId, fraction }]; nothing landing at all refuses with WRP_PROJECTION_MISSES_FACE. Needs the exact (native) kernel. Next: check_wrap, wrap_to_face, emboss_on_face.

closest.description: Project every point to its closest point on the faces instead of along a direction. Default false.

direction.description: Projection direction [x, y, z] (world). Default: the sketch plane normal, turned toward the solid.

entityIds.description: Ids of the 2D sketch entities (or font texts) to project.

faces.description: Faces to project onto, each picked like `face` of wrap_to_face. Default: every face of the solid.

items.description: The face to work on: give faceNear (a point on the face), or faceIndex, or faceName. The command records the face name so a later edit of the model finds the same face (REF_LOST when it is gone).

faceIndex.description: Unique face index of the solid (inspect_faces / inspect_topology list them).

faceName.description: Persistent face name recorded by an earlier run of this command; wins over faceIndex and faceNear.

faceNear.description: A point on or near the intended face [x, y, z] in world document units; the face nearest to it is taken.

fitTolerance.description: Largest deviation of a projected curve from its sampled points, document units. Default: 1e-6 x the solid diagonal (named default).

id.description: Id of the solid receiving the curves.

maxDistance.description: Closest mode only: farthest distance a point may travel to land, document units. Default: the solid diagonal.

requireAll.description: Refuse with WRP_PROJECTION_MISSES_FACE when any part of the sketch misses every face (default false: partial results are returned and listed in data.missed).

name: project_to_face

description: Propagate the scatter of the random variables through ALL (or one) limit states to get the distribution of g itself (not a design point; for one limit state with FORM/SORM and a method comparison use run_reliability_study). method "mc" (seeded Monte Carlo), "lhs" (Latin hypercube, default, lower variance) or "lhs_centred" sample `samples` points (default 10000, at most 2000000 in total over all limit states; needs an integer `seed` in [0, 4294967295]) and return for each limit state g: mean, sd, min, max, quantiles, a 20-bin histogram, Pf = P(g < 0) with standard error and Wilson 95 % interval, the equivalent beta, and PRB_PF_BELOW_RESOLUTION when nothing failed. method "fosm" (first-order second-moment, no seed) returns mean, sd, Cornell beta, Pf (g assumed normal) and the share of variance per variable. Correlation set with set_correlation is honoured. Limit states default to all defined ones. Computed by llull, not approved: a qualified engineer must review before any certification decision.

limitState.description: Only this limit state; default all limit states of the model.

samples.description: Number of samples (default 10000, at most 2000000). Ignored by fosm.

seed.description: Integer seed in [0, 4294967295] of the PRNG (xoshiro128**); the same model, method, samples and seed give bit-identical results.

name: propagate_uncertainty

description: Overall rms of an acceleration spectral density: spectrum (name) or points [[fHz, g2/Hz], ...], optionally within bandHz. Returns grms (g), the segments (f1Hz, f2Hz, slope dB/oct, area g^2) integrated exactly on log-log axes, and the source grade / unverified flag.

bandHz.description: Integration band [fLowHz, fHighHz]; default: the whole spectrum.

points.description: Inline breakpoints [[fHz, g2/Hz], ...].

name: psd_rms

description: Pressure-temperature rating of a flange class: the maximum working pressure in bar gauge (or psig) at a temperature, from the bundled ASME B16.5 table for material group 1.1 (carbon steel A105 / A216 WCB / A515-70 / A516-70) classes 150 to 2500. Linear interpolation between tabulated temperatures (permitted by B16.5); at or below the first row (38 degC) the first value applies; above the last row or below -29 degC the command refuses (PSC_PT_TEMPERATURE_OUT_OF_TABLE). Class 150 is tabulated to 200 degC, class 300 and up only to 50 degC (other points have no agreeing source). Give temperatureC, or temperature { value, unit: "C" | "F" }. unit "psi" returns the tabulated psig at or below 100 degF (285 for class 150) and otherwise converts bar at 0.0689475729 bar/psi, stating it. verified is true only when every row used is grade A. Ratings are for a qualified engineer to confirm. Next: check_pipe_spec compares design pressure with this rating.

standard.description: Rating standard, "ASME B16.5" (the only bundled table).

temperature.description: Design temperature with its unit. Give this or temperatureC.

unit.description: C or F.

temperatureC.description: Design temperature in degC. Give this or temperature.

unit.description: Pressure unit of the answer: bar (gauge, default) or psi (psig).

name: pt_rating

description: Push or pull ONE planar face of a 3D solid along its outward normal: distance > 0 adds material (the face moves out, its side faces follow), distance < 0 removes it. Pick the face by faceIndex, faceNear or faceName. Exact B-rep only (native OCC kernel); the source is consumed.

distance.description: Offset along the outward face normal in document units (non-zero; negative cuts into the solid).

faceName.description: Persistent face name (recorded automatically; see faceNames of draft_faces).

faceNear.description: A point [x, y, z] on the face.

id.description: Id of the 3D solid.

name: push_pull_face

description: Read-only bill of QUANTITIES (m, m2, m3 of construction) of the building model; for the parts list of a mechanical assembly use bill_of_materials (or plm engineering_bom / manufacturing_bom), metric: wall length / net face area / volume, slab area / volume, column and beam volume, stair volume, door and window counts and areas, room floor area — grouped by category and material. Each line has a key like "wall.concrete.m3" used by estimate_cost. data.csv is spreadsheet-ready. Column and beam volumes are NET (measured once where members meet: slab > column > beam — columns run to the slab soffit, beams are measured below the slab soffit and between column faces; beam length stays centre-to-centre); data.gross maps the key of each line whose raw modelled volume differs to that gross quantity.
name: quantity_takeoff

description: Read-only: points of a cloud in a region, in document units and frame, as a flat [x, y, z, …] array in canonical order (deterministic). lod "full" (default) returns every point in the region up to maxPoints (≤ 200000); lod "budget" returns a level-of-detail subset of at most `budget` points (whole octree levels, coarse first). data.truncated says when maxPoints cut the answer (SCN_QUERY_LIMIT warning): narrow the region. indices are the source record numbers.

cloudId.description: Id of an attached cloud (affected[0] of attach_point_cloud, e.g. "cloud-1.1").

maxPoints.description: Hard cap on returned points (default 10000, at most 200000).

kind.description: Every point of the cloud.
Axis-aligned box in document units.
Sphere around a seed point.

radius.description: Radius in document units, > 0.

kind.description: A crop box from set_scan_crop (keep "inside").

name: query_cloud_points

description: Recognise the manufacturing features of an exact 3D solid from its B-rep: holes (simple, counterbore, countersink, through or blind with a drill point; per hole the axis point at the entrance, the axis pointing into the material, diameter, countersink diameter / included angle in degrees / depth, counterbore diameter / depth, blind depth, drill point angle, face indices and confidence exact | ambiguous), pockets (floor height, depth, corner radius, floor fillet, open or closed), fillets, chamfers and sheet-metal bends. Faces of one surface that the kernel split in two (periodic cylinders and cones) are merged first. All lengths are in the document length unit, angles in degrees; results are deterministic and listed in data (counts, holes, pockets, bends, fillets, chamfers, unclassified face indices). Works on imported STEP solids (import_step_exact) and on parts built with add_hole / add_pocket. Needs an exact kernel: otherwise refused with FTR_NEEDS_EXACT_KERNEL (also FTR_PART_NOT_FOUND). Result computed by llull, not approved: reviewRequired is true.

angularTolerance.description: Angle tolerance in degrees for parallel axes and equal cone angles. Default 0.0001 degrees.

id.description: Id of the 3D solid (mesh with an exact B-rep) to analyse.

kinds.description: Feature kinds to report: hole, pocket, fillet, chamfer, bend. Omit for all.

lengthTolerance.description: Length tolerance in document length units for coaxial axes, equal radii and coplanar faces. Default 1e-6 of the model diagonal.

mergeSplitFaces.description: Merge faces on one analytic surface (split periodic faces) before recognising. Default true.

name: recognize_features

description: Record a role's approval of the in_review revision (roles: policy.requiredApprovalRoles, default design-authority and checker). HUMAN GATE. One approval per (role, user). An agent caller gets PLM_HUMAN_GATE: hand over to the responsible person in the desktop app.

at.description: When the act happened: ISO-8601 UTC, e.g. 2026-11-02T09:30:00Z. The host (UI / llull CLI) fills it; commands never read a clock.

confirmation.description: HUMAN SIGNATURE, required: { alg: "Ed25519", keyId, publicKey, signature, nonce } made by a human with a TRUSTED signing key over this exact act (get the bytes with plm_act_payload, sign them in the desktop app or `llull exec ... --confirm-key KEYID`). An agent has no trusted key: it prepares the act and hands over (PLM_HUMAN_GATE).

userId.description: Ignored: the approval is recorded under the signer of the confirmation (the trusted key record).

name: record_approval

description: Record what was built for one serial number: the product baseline it was designed to (create_baseline) and the deviations from it, each { partNumber (a member of the baseline), installedRevision (a revision label different from the baselined one), authority (the request for variance / waiver that allowed it, non-empty) }. HUMAN GATE. An empty deviations list records a unit built exactly to the baseline. Optionally names the manufacturing BOM it was built from (create_mbom, same baseline). The record is sealed with a SHA-256 and never edited. Needs `confirmation` (plm_act_payload) over exactly these params: an agent prepares the data and hands over (PLM_HUMAN_GATE). Compare with as_built_vs_as_designed.

asDesignedBaseline.description: Id of the product baseline (create_baseline) the unit was designed to, e.g. "BL-PBL-0003".

at.description: When the act happened: ISO-8601 UTC, e.g. 2026-11-02T09:30:00Z. The host (UI / llull CLI) fills it; commands never read a clock.

by.description: Ignored: the record is kept under the signer of the confirmation.

confirmation.description: HUMAN SIGNATURE, required: { alg: "Ed25519", keyId, publicKey, signature, nonce } made by a human with a TRUSTED signing key over this exact act (get the bytes with plm_act_payload, sign them in the desktop app or `llull exec ... --confirm-key KEYID`). An agent has no trusted key: it prepares the act and hands over (PLM_HUMAN_GATE).

deviations.description: Deviations from the baseline; [] = built to the baseline.

authority.description: The authority that allowed the deviation, e.g. "RFV-0012 (request for variance, use-as-is)".

installedRevision.description: Revision label actually installed (1-16 of A-Z, 0-9, -); must differ from the baselined revision.

partNumber.description: Part number of a member of the baseline that was installed differently.

mbom.description: Id of the manufacturing BOM (create_mbom) the unit was built from; its baseline must be asDesignedBaseline.

partNumber.description: Part number of the unit's end item: this document's managed item.

serial.description: Serial number of the unit (A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ - /, at most 64 characters), e.g. "SN-0007".

name: record_as_built

description: Record the result of a flow solve run by the host (cfd_solve transport) on a case. Not for hand use: the summary is re-derived from the stored result bundle (forces, peaks, provenance; the coefficients from the forces and the case reference), so numbers cannot be invented. `summary` is optional; when given it must equal the recomputed one exactly (the transport passes it so a replay without the result store keeps the record as unverified — only a complete summary of this case and hash is kept). Refused with CFD_RESULT_MISSING (bundle absent), CFD_RESULT_HASH_MISMATCH (hash, case or summary differ), CFD_INPUT_STALE (the case or the geometry changed while solving: solve again). Then: cfd_report caseId=ID.

resultsHash.description: sha256 of the canonical result bundle JSON, as returned by the cfd_solve transport.

summary.description: Exactly the summary returned by the transport (never hand-written): it is recomputed from the bundle and compared.

name: record_cfd_results

description: Record the result of an explicit dynamics run made by the host (explicit_run transport) on an explicit_dynamics case. Not for hand use: the summary is re-derived from the stored fe_explicit artifact, so numbers cannot be invented. `summary` is optional; when given it must equal the recomputed one (the transport passes it so a replay without the artifact store keeps the record as unverified, state missing). Refused with EXP_ARTIFACT_NOT_FOUND, EXP_SUMMARY_MISMATCH or EXP_RESULT_STALE (the set-up changed since the run: re-run explicit_run).

analysisId.description: Id of the analysis (affected[0] of create_analysis, e.g. an-1.1).

artifactHash.description: sha256 of the canonical fe_explicit artifact JSON, as returned by explicit_run.

Not for hand use: the summary is re-derived from the stored mesh artifact and refused unless it matches exactly, so numbers cannot be invented. Clears recorded results. Refused with FEA_ARTIFACT_NOT_FOUND when the artifact store does not hold the mesh, FEA_SUMMARY_MISMATCH when the summary differs, A mesh built for other inputs (the analysis or geometry changed since, e.g. on regeneration) is recorded STALE, not refused.

analysisId.description: Id of the analysis (affected[0] of create_analysis, e.g. an-1.1).

summary.description: Exactly the summary returned by the host transport (never hand-written): it is recomputed from the artifact and compared.

meshHash.description: sha256 of the canonical mesh artifact JSON.

Not for hand use: the summary is re-derived from the stored results artifact and refused unless it matches exactly. Refused with FEA_ARTIFACT_NOT_FOUND (artifact absent), FEA_SUMMARY_MISMATCH, FEA_MESH_MISMATCH (results not computed on the recorded mesh, or no mesh recorded); results computed for other inputs are recorded STALE (re-run fea_mesh then fea_solve).

analysisId.description: Id of the analysis (affected[0] of create_analysis, e.g. an-1.1).

description: Record an Ed25519 signature made by a human with the host key store (desktop "Approve & sign") over the canonical manifest of a target: { kind: "iteration", ref: "A.2" } (what an approver signs before release; the bytes are release_manifest with kind "iteration") or { kind: "release", ref: "A" } (a released revision). HUMAN GATE. The signature is verified with the host verifier and the key must be registered; it never signs. An agent caller gets PLM_HUMAN_GATE for approval / release meanings.

at.description: When it was signed (ISO-8601 UTC).

keyId.description: Ignored: the key id and signer are taken from the trusted key record of `publicKey`.

publicKey.description: Ed25519 public key, 64 lowercase hex characters.

signature.description: Ed25519 signature, 128 lowercase hex characters, over the UTF-8 canonical manifest bytes.

signer.description: Ignored: the signer is taken from the trusted key record, never from a request.

name.description: Signer display name.

target.description: What was signed.

kind.description: 'iteration' (before release, ref '<revision>.<n>') or 'release' (ref '<revision>').

ref.description: Iteration ref like 'A.2', or a revision label like 'A'.

name: record_signature

description: Record the result of a topology optimization run by the host (topology_solve transport) on a study and derive its iso-surface solid. Not for hand use: the summary is re-derived from the stored density field artifact, so numbers cannot be invented. `summary` is optional; when given it must equal the recomputed one exactly (the transport passes it so a replay without the artifact store keeps the record as unverified, state missing). Refused with TOP_ARTIFACT_NOT_FOUND (artifact absent), TOP_SUMMARY_MISMATCH (hash, field or summary differ), TOP_RESULT_STALE (the study, the analysis or the settings changed since the run: re-run topology_solve). The derived solid is a read-only concept shape on layer layer-topology; rebuild the part with suggest_rebuild and ordinary modelling commands.

fieldHash.description: sha256 of the canonical topology artifact JSON, as returned by the topology_solve transport.

studyId.description: Id of the topology study (affected[0] of create_topology_study, e.g. ts-3.1).

summary.description: Exactly the summary returned by the transport (never hand-written): it is recomputed from the artifact and compared.

name: record_topology_result

description: Re-derive implicit bodies from their field recipes: the meshes of bodies whose content hash no longer matches what the current engine would produce (e.g. after loading a document on another machine or engine, or after the source solids changed), or of the bodies you list. Bodies that are up to date are left alone. Replayable: the result depends only on the recipe, voxel and engine. Reports which bodies changed.

ids.description: Ids of the bodies to re-derive regardless of staleness. Default: every stale body.

name: regenerate_implicit_bodies

description: Send the in_review revision back to in_work (unfreezes the definition) with a mandatory comment explaining why. Recorded approvals are dropped.

at.description: When the act happened: ISO-8601 UTC, e.g. 2026-11-02T09:30:00Z. The host (UI / llull CLI) fills it; commands never read a clock.

by.description: User id doing the act (the host fills it from the authenticated user; an agent cannot override it where the server has named users).

name: reject_review

description: Release the in_review revision: freezes its content (SHA-256 of the canonical definition + an inline snapshot), uses the approvals recorded with record_approval, change order and effectivity, supersedes the previously released revision (its open effectivity closes the day / serial before this one starts) and implements the ECO. HUMAN GATE. Needs submit_for_review first, the policy roles approved (checker different from the author), an open ECO listing the item (after the first release) and, by default, a human approval signature (record_signature). check_release_readiness lists every blocker without changing anything. Needs `confirmation`, a trusted human signature over this exact act (plm_act_payload): an agent gets PLM_HUMAN_GATE; prepare with check_release_readiness and hand over to the humans.

at.description: When the act happened: ISO-8601 UTC, e.g. 2026-11-02T09:30:00Z. The host (UI / llull CLI) fills it; commands never read a clock.

by.description: Ignored: the release is recorded under the signer of the confirmation.

changeOrder.description: The open ECO that authorizes this release (lists this item).

confirmation.description: HUMAN SIGNATURE, required: { alg: "Ed25519", keyId, publicKey, signature, nonce } made by a human with a TRUSTED signing key over this exact act (get the bytes with plm_act_payload, sign them in the desktop app or `llull exec ... --confirm-key KEYID`). An agent has no trusted key: it prepares the act and hands over (PLM_HUMAN_GATE).

effectivity.description: Effectivity of this revision; default: the ECO's planned effectivity.

items.description: One effectivity range.

from.description: First unit covered (inclusive), of the kind.

kind.description: serial / msn: positive integers; date: YYYY-MM-DD; lot: an id string.

to.description: Last unit covered (inclusive). Absent = open-ended.

name: release_item

description: The canonical manifest of a frozen revision (kind "release": released / superseded / obsolete) or of an iteration of the revision (kind "iteration": what an approver signs before release). Returns data { body, canonical, sha256 }: `canonical` is the exact UTF-8 text a human signs (Ed25519) with the host key store, then record_signature. Read-only; deterministic.

kind.description: 'release' (default) or 'iteration' (the revision's current iteration).

meaning.description: What the signer will attest; it is part of the signed bytes. Default 'release' (kind release) or 'approval' (kind iteration).

name: release_manifest

description: Remesh a mesh (or the triangles of any 3D solid) into a regular, well-shaped triangulation of the same surface. Give EITHER `targetEdgeLength` (isotropic: every edge aims at that length) OR `minEdge`, `maxEdge` and `approxError` (adaptive: edge length follows the curvature, short where the surface bends, so the chord error stays near approxError). Per iteration (Botsch and Kobbelt 2004): split edges longer than 4/3 of the target, collapse edges shorter than 4/5, flip edges toward valence 6 (4 on constraints), relax vertices tangentially and project them back onto the input surface; a closing pass splits until no edge exceeds 4/3 of the target. Edges where the faces meet at more than preserveFeatureAngleDeg stay as feature lines (vertices slide along them, corners are fixed); boundary vertices are fixed unless preserveBoundary is false; `region` restricts the edit to a sphere. Needs a manifold, consistently wound mesh without degenerate faces (repair_mesh first). Reports data.edgeLength {min, max, mean, p5, p95}, fractionInBand (edges within 4/5..4/3 of the target) and the symmetric deviation from the input (document units). Reference: an icosphere of radius 10 remeshed to 1 gives edges <= 1.3333 and a surface deviation of a few hundredths. Refusals: MESH_ENTITY_NOT_FOUND, MESH_NOT_A_MESH, MESH_PARAM_INVALID, MESH_REMESH_EDGE_TOO_LARGE, MESH_NON_MANIFOLD, MESH_ORIENTATION_INCONSISTENT, MESH_DEGENERATE.
