approxError.description: Adaptive: allowed chord error (document units); edge length L = sqrt(6 e / k - 3 e^2) from the local curvature k, clamped to minEdge..maxEdge.

id.description: Id of the mesh (or other 3D solid) to remesh.

keepSource.description: true: keep the source and add the result as a new mesh. Default false: the source entity is rewritten in place (same id, name, layer, colour).

maxEdge.description: Adaptive: longest edge (document units), used on flat regions.

minEdge.description: Adaptive: shortest edge (document units), used where curvature is high.

preserveBoundary.description: true (default): boundary vertices of open meshes stay. false: they slide along the boundary.

preserveFeatureAngleDeg.description: Edges between faces turned by more than this (degrees) are kept as feature lines. Default 40.

project.description: Project vertices back onto the input surface after relaxation. Default true.

region.description: Only vertices inside this sphere are edited; the rest of the mesh stays as it is.

center.description: Centre [x, y, z] of the sphere (document units, world).

radius.description: Radius of the sphere (document units).

targetEdgeLength.description: Isotropic target edge length (document units). Not with minEdge / maxEdge / approxError.

name: remesh_mesh

description: Remove a valve or reducer from a pipe run: the leg is cut again without it (the pipe pieces around it merge into one) and the downstream size returns to the upstream size for a reducer. Refused with the RTE_* code when the run then no longer derives (e.g. RTE_SIZE_MISMATCH: the end port has the reduced size, RTE_BRANCH_NO_TABLE_ROW for a branch that took the reduced header size) and nothing changes. Refusals: RTE_UNKNOWN_RUN, RTE_UNKNOWN_COMPONENT.
name: remove_inline_component

description: Render the solved results of an analysis as a contour plot an engineer (or you) can LOOK at: an SVG image (embedded z-buffered raster, parts hide each other correctly) of the outer skin of the meshed parts coloured by a field in 12 crisp bands (blue = low, red = high) with a colour legend in the analysis units, the MAX / MIN locations, supports (cyan dots), loads (magenta dots + arrow) and thermal BCs (orange dots; dots are drawn only where visible), on the deformed shape (structural fields; the scale is printed in the subtitle) over a faint silhouette of the undeformed part. field: von_mises (default for static / thermo-mechanical), u_mag, u_x, u_y, u_z, s_xx, s_yy, s_zz, temperature (default for heat_*), heat_flux, and cylindrical components about an axis (axisPoint + axisDirection, default: the z axis through the centre of the plotted parts bounding box; a quarter / half model needs the real axis point): s_hoop, s_radial, s_axial, u_radial. modal / buckling cases: field mode (default) colours the displacement magnitude of the mode shape normalised to 1 (it has no unit; mode = which mode, 1-based, default 1; the subtitle gives its frequency in Hz or its buckling factor; the shape is drawn deformed with the automatic scale because mode amplitudes are arbitrary); stress fields do not exist for them. To see an interior peak (e.g. under a PCB): cut = { normal, offset } removes the half-space dot(normal, p) > offset of the undeformed model and colours the section face by the field; entityIds plots only those parts (min / max and the colour range then refer to the plotted parts). With surface: true also data.surface { positions (flat xyz per triangle corner, deformed, document units), values (one per corner), triangles, truncated }. Returns data { svg, field, unit, resultSet, min { value, at }, max { value, at }, deformationScale, levels, trianglesDrawn, entityIds, cut, axis }; save it as PNG with the CLI (--save plot.png). Requires a solved analysis on this machine (fea_mesh then fea_solve). min.at / max.at / axis / target are in the analysis length unit; data.surface is in document units.

analysisId.description: Id of the analysis (affected[0] of create_analysis, e.g. an-1.1).

axisDirection.description: s_hoop / s_radial / s_axial / u_radial: axis direction [x, y, z] (any non-zero length). Default [0, 0, 1].

axisPoint.description: s_hoop / s_radial / s_axial / u_radial: a point [x, y, z] (analysis length unit) on the axis. Default: centre of the plotted bounding box.

cut.description: One section plane, e.g. { normal: [0, 1, 0], offset: 0 } keeps y <= 0 and shows the field on the cut face.

normal.description: Plane normal [x, y, z] (any non-zero length); the side it points to is removed.

offset.description: Plane position: points with dot(unit normal, p) > offset are removed. Analysis length unit, undeformed mesh.

deformationScale.description: Displacement magnification of the drawn shape; 0 draws the undeformed shape. Default: automatic (structural fields).

direction.description: Custom viewing direction [x, y, z] from the part toward the viewer (overrides view), e.g. [0, -1, 0.3].

entityIds.description: Plot only these parts (entity ids of the analysis; the other parts are hidden). Default: every meshed part.

field.description: Field to colour by. Default: temperature for heat_steady / heat_transient, mode for modal / buckling, else von_mises.

height.description: Image height in pixels (240-2000). Default 640.

loadCase.description: Load case name of a static / thermo-mechanical case. Default: the first load case.

mode.description: modal / buckling only: mode number to plot (1 = lowest frequency / smallest buckling factor). Default 1.

range.description: Fixed colour range [min, max] (e.g. [0, 250] MPa) to compare plots; values outside fall in the end bands. Default: data range.

showMesh.description: Draw the element edges of the skin. Default false.

surface.description: Also return data.surface { positions, values, triangles, truncated }: the plotted triangles as flat xyz per corner (deformed, in DOCUMENT units) with one field value per corner, so a viewer can paint the contour on the model. Capped at 150000 corners. Default false.

target.description: Point [x, y, z] (analysis length unit, as data.max.at) kept at the centre when zoomed. Default: the part centre.

time.description: heat_transient: plot the result set nearest this time (s). Default: the last result set.

width.description: Image width in pixels (320-2000). Default 960.

zoom.description: Magnification (1-50) about `target` to inspect a detail such as a hole edge. Default 1.

name: render_fea_results

description: SEE a simulated mechanism: runs the physics simulation (same engine and parameters as simulate_motion / plot_simulation) and renders the rigid bodies at chosen instants as a grid of frames, each labelled "t = 0.25 s", so crank rotation, piston travel or a pendulum swing can be checked without a screen. Pick instants with `times` (seconds, at most 12) or `frames` (N evenly spaced instants from 0 to the duration, both included; default 4). Every frame uses the same camera, so motion reads directly. `trace` draws the centre-of-mass path of the named rigid bodies (e.g. the coupler or the end-effector) over all samples, with a dot at the current position. Camera as render_view: `view` or `direction`. Returns data.svg (the grid), data.width/height, and data.frames[{ time, bodies{ bodyId: { position (centre of mass, document units), rotationDeg (Euler XYZ degrees from the start pose) } } }] to read numbers. Frames show the nearest recorded sample (data.frames[].time is that sample's time). With the CLI, `llull render_motion … --save m.png` writes a PNG rasterized from data.svg (--save m.svg writes the SVG itself; if rasterizing fails the .svg is saved instead and the CLI reply shows data.svg as a short placeholder). Point springs (add_spring) are drawn as green zig-zag coils between their attachment points, which ride on their bodies (data.frames[].springs gives the end points and length). Read-only; needs the physics engine like simulate_motion.

direction.description: Custom viewing direction [x, y, z] from the scene toward the camera (Z-up); overrides `view`.

duration.description: Simulated seconds. Default: the largest of `times`, else 5.

frames.description: Number of evenly spaced instants from 0 to the duration, both included (1..12). Default 4. Ignored when `times` is given.

height.description: Height of ONE frame in pixels, clamped to [64, 2000]. Default 320.

sampleRate.description: Recorded samples per second (the frames and the trace snap to these). Default as simulate_motion; raise it for a smoother trace.

times.description: Instants to draw, in seconds from the start (1 to 12 values, each within 0..duration). Overrides `frames`.

timestep.description: Integration step in seconds; default as simulate_motion.

trace.description: Rigid body id (or ids, at most 4) whose centre-of-mass path is drawn across all samples, e.g. the coupler or the piston.

view.description: Camera as render_view: "iso" (default), "top", "bottom", "front", "back", "left", "right". Planar mechanisms read best face-on.

width.description: Width of ONE frame in pixels, clamped to [64, 2000]. Default 420.

name: render_motion

description: Render the document to a self-contained SVG image string so an AI agent can SEE the scene and self-correct. Returns the unchanged document plus a `data` object containing: `svg` (complete SVG string), `view` (resolved view name), `width`, `height`, `entityCount`, `bounds` (world AABB or null), and `camera` ({position, target, up}). Choose `view` to orient the render: "iso" (default isometric), "top", "bottom", "front", "back", "left", or "right" (all orthographic). Adjust `width`/`height` (pixels, clamped to [64, 2000], default 800×600) for resolution. Solids are flat-Lambert shaded and depth-buffered per pixel (mode "raster", default: a PNG inside the SVG, outlines at creases and part boundaries) or drawn as sorted SVG polygons (mode "vector"); 2D shapes are stroked paths. Camera: `zoom` (>1 magnifies), `direction` ([x,y,z] vector from the scene toward the camera, overrides `view`), `target` (point to look at). `title` draws text top-left, `background` sets the image color. Cutaway: `cut` clips solids (triangles are split, not dropped) and draws the section as a hatched cap, e.g. remove the quadrant x>0,y<0 with planes [{normal:[1,0,0],offset:0},{normal:[0,-1,0],offset:0}] and mode "intersection". Large scenes are never silently truncated: the polygon budget (`maxPolygons`) is shared fairly between entities, and `data.simplifiedEntityIds` / `data.skippedEntityIds` / `data.polygonCount` report what was reduced. Enrichments: turntable (multi-frame strip), isolate (highlight entities), section (cut-plane view), showDimensions (bbox labels), showAxes (world triad, default on), showGrid (ground grid, default on), showLabels (entity id/name labels + key-point markers, default off). The active exploded view (set_active_exploded_view) is drawn like the viewport: parts at their exploded positions. Does NOT modify the document; `affected` is always [].

background.description: Background CSS color: "#rrggbb", "#rgb", a color name ("white") or rgb()/hsl(). Default "#1a1a2e" (dark navy).

cut.description: Cutaway: clips the selected 3D solids against the planes (triangles are split exactly) and draws the exposed section as a light, hatched, outlined cap so solids do not look hollow. Rendered together with isolate/section/turntable.

entityIds.description: Entity ids to cut. Omit to cut every solid; other entities stay whole.

mode.description: "intersection" (default): remove only the region on the cut side of ALL planes (e.g. a quadrant or octant notch). "union": remove everything on the cut side of ANY plane.

planes.description: 1 to 6 cut planes. Each removes the half-space dot(unitNormal, p) > offset.

normal.description: Plane normal [x, y, z] (any non-zero length). It points to the REMOVED side.

offset.description: Plane position: points p with dot(unitNormal, p) = offset lie on the plane.

direction.description: Custom viewing direction: a non-zero [x, y, z] vector pointing from the scene center toward the camera (Z-up). Overrides `view`; e.g. [1,-1,0.5] looks from +X/-Y above. Result `view` is "custom".

fovDeg.description: Perspective vertical field of view in degrees, (0, 180). Default 45 (the viewport).

height.description: Output image height in pixels. Clamped to [64, 2000]. Default: 600.

hide2D.description: When true, 2D sketch entities (lines, arcs, circles, polylines, rectangles, text, dimensions...) are neither drawn nor counted in the framing/bounds, so leftover construction sketches used for extrusions do not shrink the 3D part in the frame. Default: false (2D shapes are drawn and framed).

isolate.description: Entity id (or array of ids) to highlight. All other entities are rendered dimmed/desaturated; the specified id(s) are shown at full color.

maxPolygons.description: Polygon budget of vector mode, clamped to [500, 100000], default 20000 (raster mode allows at least 400000). Entities over their fair share are decimated (see data.simplifiedEntityIds); raise it for finer detail at the cost of a larger SVG.

mode.description: "raster" (default): solids are depth-buffered per pixel (always correct occlusion, crisp outlines) and embedded as a PNG in the SVG; "vector": every face is an SVG polygon sorted back to front (editable, but faces can draw through each other in dense scenes).

projection.description: "orthographic" (default) or "perspective" (raster mode only; the eye is placed on the view direction so the scene fits fovDeg). Perspective draws no grid / axes / labels / dimensions and cannot be combined with turntable, isolate or section.

renderer.description: "reference" (default): the TypeScript raster, deterministic, data.svgSha256 + rendererVersion (use it for anything reproducible). "native": the same scene drawn on the GPU by llull-compute raster (CLI / desktop app only): a picture, no svgSha256, data.deterministic false, data.device / version / engine. Raster mode only. No binary in this host: NATIVE_TOOL_MISSING.

section.description: Render a section-plane view: entities on the negative side of the cut plane are dimmed; a colored dashed line marks the cut. axis: "x"|"y"|"z"; offset: world-space position of the plane.

axis.description: Axis normal to the cut plane: "x", "y", or "z".

offset.description: World-space position of the cut plane along the axis.

showAxes.description: When true (default), overlay a world-frame X/Y/Z axis triad anchored at the world origin. X=red, Y=green, Z=blue. A scale label (e.g. "1 mm = 42 px") is also shown. Set to false to suppress.

showDimensions.description: When true, overlay the bounding-box dimensions (W × D × H) as text labels on the image. Labels are placed near the bounding box edges in screen space.

showGrid.description: When true (default), overlay a faint ground grid on the Z=0 plane so you can judge object placement relative to the world origin. Set to false to suppress.

showLabels.description: When true, overlay per-entity id/name labels and key-point markers on the image. Each entity shows its name (or id) at the centroid of its key points (endpoints, center, corners, AABB corners for solids). Markers are color-coded by category: orange=point, cyan=2D curve, purple=3D solid, yellow=annotation. A legend appears in the top-right corner. Default: false (opt in to avoid clutter).

target.description: World point the camera looks at (default: center of the scene bounds). Combine with `zoom` to inspect a detail.

title.description: Text drawn top-left of the image (max 120 characters, longer is truncated).

turntable.description: Produce a horizontal strip of N evenly-spaced rotation frames around the Z (up) axis. frames: integer 1..12. When omitted, behavior is unchanged (single frame).

frames.description: Number of frames (1..12). Each frame is a separate rotated view stitched into one wide strip.

view.description: Camera direction. One of: "iso" (isometric — default, good for orienting in 3D), "top" (looking down the +Z axis), "bottom" (looking up the -Z axis), "front" (looking along the +Y axis), "back" (looking along the -Y axis), "left" (looking along the +X axis), "right" (looking along the -X axis). Omit for the default "iso" view.

viewpointId.description: Render from a saved viewpoint (save_viewpoint): its camera replaces view / direction / target / zoom / projection.

width.description: Output image width in pixels. Clamped to [64, 2000]. Default: 800.

zoom.description: Magnification of the framed scene, clamped to [0.1, 50]. 1 (default) fits the whole scene; 3 shows a third of it.

name: render_view

description: Render a walkthrough (create_walkthrough) to PNG frames: the camera glides between the saved viewpoints (eye linear, direction spherical) at `fps` frames per second; frames = floor(duration × fps) + 1. Solids and sketches only (no grid / axes). data: { frames, fps, durationS, width, height, files: [{ fileName: "frame-0001.png", base64 }] } — save them with `--save dir/`. renderer "reference" (default) adds frameSha256[] (deterministic per rendererVersion); "native" draws each frame on the GPU with llull-compute (CLI / desktop only): GPU frames without digests, data.deterministic false. Errors: VIS_WALKTHROUGH_NOT_FOUND, VIS_WALKTHROUGH_INVALID (more frames than maxFrames), VIS_RENDER_BUDGET, NATIVE_TOOL_MISSING.

height.description: Frame height in pixels, clamped to [64, 2000]. Default 360.

id.description: Walkthrough id (wt-<n>).

maxFrames.description: Refuse when the walkthrough needs more frames than this (1..600). Default 600.

width.description: Frame width in pixels, clamped to [64, 2000]. Default 640.

name: render_walkthrough

description: Set the stacking order of a part: `order` lists every ply id or name from the tool side (first) to the top (last), each exactly once. Sequence labels are not renamed.

order.description: All plies of the part, tool side first.

items.description: Ply id or name.

name: reorder_plies

description: Move a feature history step to a new position (0-based index) in the featureHistory list, then regenerate the document. Use to change the order in which operations are applied.

newIndex.description: Zero-based target index in featureHistory. Must be an integer; clamped to [0, history.length-1]. Moving to the same index is a no-op.

stepId.description: Id of the FeatureStep to move (from doc.featureHistory[*].id).

name: reorder_step

description: Repair a mesh (or the triangles of any 3D solid). Modes, least to most intrusive: "weld" merges vertices closer than weldTolerance and drops faces that collapse; "clean" also removes degenerate (repeated vertex or zero area) and duplicate faces; "orient" makes every shell consistently wound (outward for closed shells; reports faces flipped); "stitch" closes gaps by merging boundary vertices closer than maxGap, then cleans; "close_holes" is stitch followed by a plain fill of every boundary loop up to maxBoundaryEdges (use fill_mesh_holes for faired patches); "wrap" rebuilds a closed manifold envelope from a signed-distance field (Manifold engine; destroys inner structures, reports innerStructuresDestroyed). removeSmallComponents deletes noise shells (at most maxFaces faces, or a closed shell of volume at most maxVolume) in any non-wrap mode; the largest shell is never removed. Typical order: analyze_mesh -> repair_mesh mode=stitch -> fill_mesh_holes -> repair_mesh mode=orient -> check_mesh. Reports data.changes {welded, duplicatesRemoved, degenerateRemoved, flipped, stitched, holesFilled, componentsRemoved}, closed, volume and the symmetric deviation from the input (document units). Lengths in document units. Refusals: MESH_ENTITY_NOT_FOUND, MESH_NOT_A_MESH, MESH_OFFSET_RESOLUTION and MESH_ENGINE_UNSUPPORTED (wrap).

id.description: Id of the mesh (or other 3D solid) to repair.

keepSource.description: true: keep the source and add the result as a new mesh. Default false: the source entity is rewritten in place (same id, name, layer, colour).

maxBoundaryEdges.description: close_holes: loops with more edges than this stay open (reported). Default 1000.

maxCells.description: Level-set grid cell cap; a finer tolerance than the cap allows refuses with MESH_OFFSET_RESOLUTION. Default 40000.

maxGap.description: stitch / close_holes: boundary vertices closer than this (document units) are merged. Default 100 x the weld tolerance (named default).

mode.description: Repair mode, least to most intrusive: weld, clean, orient, stitch, close_holes, wrap.

removeSmallComponents.description: Delete small noise shells (not for wrap). Give maxFaces and / or maxVolume. The largest shell always stays.

maxFaces.description: Remove shells with at most this many faces.

maxVolume.description: Remove closed shells whose absolute volume is at most this (document units^3).

tolerance.description: Target distance (document units) between a result vertex and the exact surface: the level-set grid edge is set to it. When that needs more cells than maxCells the grid is coarsened to fit and the result reports the weaker bound it really has (data.toleranceMet false, data.errorBound). Default 0.002 x bounding-box diagonal (named default).

weldTolerance.description: Vertices closer than this (document units) are merged before repair. Default 1e-6 x bounding-box diagonal (named default).

name: repair_mesh

description: Replace a planar face of a 3D solid by a parallel target plane: the face moves onto the plane and its side faces follow (e.g. bring a boss up to a datum, or flush a face with another part). The target is a plane { origin, normal } parallel to the face (copy it from inspect_faces of the other part). Pick the face by faceIndex, faceNear or faceName. Exact B-rep only (native OCC kernel).

faceNear.description: A point [x, y, z] on the face.

id.description: Id of the 3D solid.

target.description: A plane by a point and its normal.

normal.description: Plane normal [x, y, z] (any length > 0).

origin.description: A point [x, y, z] on the plane.

name: replace_face

description: Recompute the document from scratch by replaying all non-suppressed steps in featureHistory in order. Use after manually editing the history list or to verify the document is consistent with its feature recipe.
name: replay_history

description: Request a waiver for a failing finding of check_layup (a rule violation, a strength ratio below 1, a disabled rule for release): give its `code` and the `ids` it lists, and a `reason`. The waiver is recorded as PENDING; it does not change the verdict: only a qualified human approval makes it effective, and an agent cannot grant it. Refused (CMP_WAIVER_NO_FINDING) when check_layup (purpose release) has no current finding with that code on those ids.

code.description: Finding code from check_layup, e.g. CMP_FPF_RATIO_BELOW_ONE.

ids.description: Ids the finding lists (zone ids, ply ids); every one must belong to the finding.

loads.description: The load cases of the check_layup run that produced the finding (needed for strength findings).

name.description: Load case name.

reason.description: Why the finding is acceptable (for the reviewer).

name: request_layup_waiver

description: Resolve a branch connection from the spec branch table: the fitting kind for a header size x branch size (T equal tee, RT reducing tee, W weldolet, S sockolet, TH threadolet, SI stub-in, SIR reinforced stub-in) and the spec component that makes it (a tee at the header size, a reducing tee, an olet whose header and branch ranges cover the sizes); a stub-in returns no component (the reinforcement check is pipe stress, pack 07). Sizes are NPS (inch designation or number) or DN. An empty cell, such as a branch larger than its header, is refused with PSC_BRANCH_UNDEFINED and the branches defined for that header. Next: resolve_spec_component for the other parts, edit_pipe_spec setBranchCell to fill a cell.

branchNps.description: Branch NPS, inch designation or number. Give branchNps or branchDn.

headerNps.description: Header (run) NPS, inch designation or number. Give headerNps or headerDn.

name: resolve_branch

description: Which released revision applies to a unit: `kind` serial | msn (positive integer unit), date (YYYY-MM-DD) or lot (id). Returns data { revision | null, state }. Obsolete and cancelled revisions never resolve. Read-only.

kind.description: Effectivity kind.

partNumber.description: Part number; default and only supported: this document's item.

unit.description: The unit: serial / MSN integer, date string, lot id.

name: resolve_effectivity

description: Fill the records of private (licensed) material libraries from the library files held on this machine. A saved document keeps only { libraryId, version, sha256 } for them; run this after load_document. A record is filled only when the file has exactly the pinned sha256; otherwise it stays unresolved (provider missing, library missing or hash mismatch) and mass_properties / get_material_allowable answer available: false with MAT_LIBRARY_UNRESOLVED. This is a session command: it is not recorded in the feature history and never saved. Register a file first with register_material_library; import a new version explicitly with import_material_library.
name: resolve_material_libraries

description: Pick the one component a pipe spec allows for a component type and nominal size (NPS inch designation such as "2-1/2" or 2.5, or DN) and return its catalogue dimensions in millimetres with verified flags, the schedule and wall (a butt-weld fitting takes the spec pipe schedule), the ends, the commodity code and the source. Reducing tees, olets and reducers need branchNps / branchDn. Refuses sizes outside the spec range (PSC_SIZE_OUT_OF_RANGE), types the spec does not define at that size (PSC_NO_COMPONENT) and equal-priority matches (PSC_AMBIGUOUS_COMPONENT). When the spec names a standard the catalogue does not hold (B16.11, olets) the component is still selected but verified is false (PSC_DATA_UNVERIFIED). Next: resolve_branch for branch connections, check_pipe_spec to validate the spec; routing commands consume this.

branchNps.description: Branch / small-end NPS (reducing tee, olet, reducer).

class.description: Only components of this pressure class (150, 3000 …).

dn.description: Nominal diameter DN (integer). Converted through the fixed DN <-> NPS map when needed.

ends.description: Only components with this end type (BW, SW, FL …).

facing.description: Only components with this flange face.

nps.description: Nominal pipe size, inch designation ("6", "2-1/2") or number (2.5). Give nps or dn.

pn.description: Only components of this EN PN.

radius.description: Only elbows of this bend radius (LR, SR).

type.description: Component type: pipe, elbow90, elbow45, tee, reducingTee, reducerConcentric, flangeWeldNeck, gasketSpiralWound, valveGate, weldolet …

name: resolve_spec_component

description: Repair a document whose released definition no longer matches its recorded content hash (tampered file, integrity mismatch reported by load_document or plm_status): replace the definition with the revision snapshot. Refused while the integrity is ok. Camera, selection and the PLM record are kept.

revision.description: The current released revision to restore, e.g. "A".

name: restore_revision_snapshot

description: Open the next revision (B after A, per the scheme) of a RELEASED item under an open change order that lists it (policy.requireChangeOrder; with exactly one such ECO it is picked automatically). The new revision is in_work at iteration 1 and based on the current one, which stays released and unchanged. Then edit the model, submit_for_review and release_item. An agent may do this step.

at.description: When the act happened: ISO-8601 UTC, e.g. 2026-11-02T09:30:00Z. The host (UI / llull CLI) fills it; commands never read a clock.

by.description: User id doing the act (the host fills it from the authenticated user; an agent cannot override it where the server has named users).

changeOrder.description: Open ECO listing this item. Default: the single open ECO listing it.

name: revise_item

description: Create a surface of revolution by rotating a closed 2D profile around an axis. Right-handed world frame, +Z up. Either pass profile, an array of [x, y] points where x is the radial offset from the axis and y is the axial offset (at least 3 points, implicitly closed), or profileIds: drawn 2D sketch entities (spline, arc, line, polyline, circle, ellipse) that form one closed loop, read in their sketch-plane coordinates (x = radial, y = axial). A sketched profile keeps its exact curves (smooth bell nozzles, domes, fillets) for the exact kernel and STEP export. axis controls the revolution axis: "x", "y", or "z" (shorthand), or a [dx,dy,dz] direction vector. Default axis is "z" (+Z up, the natural axis for a Z-up document). angle is the sweep in radians (default 2π for a full revolution; must be > 0). segments is the number of radial subdivisions (default 32, minimum 3). Stores a parametric revolution entity; tessellated as triangles in render_view and export_stl.

angle.description: Sweep angle in radians. Must be > 0. Default: 2π (full 360° revolution). Use π for a half-revolution, π/2 for a quarter, etc.

axis.description: Revolution axis. Use "x", "y", or "z" for the principal axes, or pass a [dx, dy, dz] array for an arbitrary direction (it will be normalised). Default: "z" (natural +Z-up axis).

color.description: Hex color string #rrggbb, e.g. "#c8553d". Defaults to "#6b8f9c".

id.description: Optional explicit entity id. If omitted a unique id is generated.

layerId.description: Layer id to assign the entity to. Defaults to the document default layer.

position.description: World-space origin of the revolution axis [x, y, z] in document units. Default: [0, 0, 0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

profile.description: Closed polygon cross-section: array of [x, y] points. x = radial offset from the axis (≥ 0 for outward), y = axial offset along the axis. Minimum 3 points. The polygon is implicitly closed — do NOT repeat the first point at the end. Omit when profileIds is given.

profileIds.description: Ids of coplanar 2D sketch entities forming one closed loop (one closed shape, or open pieces such as a spline plus lines that join end to end in any order). Their sketch-plane x is the radial offset, y the axial offset; curves are kept exact. Alternative to profile.

rotation.description: three.js intrinsic XYZ Euler angles in RADIANS [rx, ry, rz] (equivalent to rotating about world Z first, then world Y, then world X) applied after revolution. Default: [0, 0, 0]. Malformed or non-length-3 values are ignored and [0,0,0] is used.

segments.description: Number of radial subdivisions for tessellation. Integer; higher = smoother surface. Default: 32. Minimum: 3 (smaller values are raised to 3).

name: revolve_profile

description: Read-only power <-> steady speed of any road vehicle (bicycle, e-bike, car, truck): aerodynamic drag ½ρ(CdA+Fw)V_A²V, rolling resistance Crr·m·g·cos θ·V, climbing m·g·sin θ·V, wind and drivetrain efficiency. Give exactly one of `speed` (+ speedUnit) or `powerW` (drivetrain input power; the steady speed is solved). `vehicle` generic (default: `crr` required, no wheel / bearing terms, efficiency 1 = power at the wheels) or bicycle (Martin et al. 1998 road-cycling preset, validated R² 0.97, SE 2.7 W: Crr 0.0032, wheel drag Fw 0.0044 m², bearing loss V(91 + 8.7·V) mW, chain 0.976; rider + bike CdA upright ≈ 0.27, drops ≈ 0.24, time trial ≈ 0.21 m², Defraeye 2010). `massKg` total moving mass; drag area `cdA` m² or `cd` + `entityIds` (frontal area of the model); `gradePercent`; `headwindMS` (+ head / - tail); air from altitudeM (standard atmosphere) or densityKgM3. model `bassett_1999`: track-cycling hour records (Bassett et al. 1999 eq. 8, velodrome, no wind): `riderHeightM`, `riderMassKg`, bike 10 kg, aerodynamic factor `k1` (or the density ratio of `altitudeM` (or `densityKgM3` / 1.225) × position / bike / clothing / helmet factors). Returns the power breakdown (aero, rolling, bearings, gravity, drivetrain), speed and the 1-hour distance; every defaulted input is flagged.

altitudeM.description: Geometric altitude in m for the U.S. Standard Atmosphere 1976 (-5000..86000). Default 0 (sea level) unless densityKgM3 is given.

bearingLosses.description: road_load: add the bicycle wheel-bearing loss V(91 + 8.7·V) mW (bicycle default true, generic false).

bikeFactor.description: bassett: Kb (0.93 aero bike, 1.07 drop bars + spoked wheels). Default 1.

bikeMassKg.description: bassett: bicycle mass in kg (default 10, the paper value).

cd.description: road_load: drag coefficient on the frontal area of entityIds.

cdA.description: road_load: drag area CdA in m² (> 0). Or cd + entityIds.

crr.description: road_load: rolling resistance coefficient, 0..0.1. Required for generic; bicycle default 0.0032 (Martin 1998 road tyres).

densityKgM3.description: Air density in kg/m³ (> 0) instead of the standard atmosphere, e.g. a measured value.

drivetrainEfficiency.description: road_load: drivetrain efficiency in (0, 1] (bicycle default 0.976; generic default 1 = power at the wheels).

entityIds.description: road_load: vehicle (+ rider) solids; frontal area along flowDirection (default [1, 0, 0]).

flowDirection.description: Direction the air moves relative to the body [x, y, z] (any length, not zero). Default [1, 0, 0]: a body moving along -x.

gradePercent.description: road_load: road grade in % (rise / run × 100, -25..25). Default 0.

headwindMS.description: road_load: wind along the road in m/s, + headwind / - tailwind. Default 0.

helmetFactor.description: bassett: Kh (1.025-1.04 no aero helmet). Default 1.

k1.description: bassett: aerodynamic factor K1 = Kd·Kpo·Kb·Kc·Kh (overrides the factors below).

massKg.description: road_load: total moving mass in kg (vehicle + rider / payload, > 0). Required.

model.description: road_load (default: any road vehicle, Martin et al. 1998 terms) or bassett_1999 (track cycling hour record, Bassett et al. 1999).

positionFactor.description: bassett: Kpo (e.g. 1.0 aero bars, 0.95 Superman, 0.96 Obree, 1.08 drop bars). Default 1.

powerW.description: Power at the drivetrain input in W (crank, motor shaft; > 0); the command solves the steady speed. Give this or speed.

resolution.description: Silhouette grid cells along its larger extent, 50..2000. Default 400 (area error ~ ±0.5 %).

riderHeightM.description: bassett: rider height in m (1.4..2.2). Required.

riderMassKg.description: bassett: rider mass in kg (40..120). Required.

speed.description: Speed (air speed for aircraft, ground speed for road vehicles) in speedUnit, >= 0.

speedUnit.description: Unit of speed: m/s (default), km/h, kn (knot, 1852 m/h) or mph.

temperatureOffsetK.description: ISA temperature deviation ΔT in K at the standard pressure (e.g. 15 for ISA+15). Default 0.

trackFactor.description: bassett: K, external conditions (track roughness). Default 1.

vehicle.description: road_load: generic (default: crr required, no wheel / bearing terms, drivetrain 1) or bicycle (Martin 1998 preset: crr 0.0032, Fw 0.0044 m², bearing loss, drivetrain 0.976).

viscosityPaS.description: Dynamic viscosity in Pa·s with densityKgM3; default Sutherland at 288.15 K + temperatureOffsetK (1.7894e-5 Pa·s).

wheelAreaM2.description: road_load: wheel rotation drag area Fw in m², added to CdA (bicycle default 0.0044, generic 0).

name: road_load_power

description: Read-only ideal velocity change of a rocket stage by the Tsiolkovsky equation Δv = Isp·g0·ln(m0/mf) (no gravity or drag losses), from `ispS` (s, e.g. nozzle_performance vacuum Isp) and the masses: `initialMassKg` with `propellantMassKg` (or `finalMassKg`). Optional `thrustN` gives the mass flow and burn time. Or give `targetDeltaVMS` instead of the propellant / final mass to get the propellant needed.

finalMassKg.description: Final (burn-out) mass in kg, 0 < mf < m0.

propellantMassKg.description: Propellant burned in kg, 0 < m_p < m0.

targetDeltaVMS.description: Wanted Δv in m/s (> 0): returns the propellant mass needed.

thrustN.description: Thrust in N (> 0) for mass flow and burn time.

name: rocket_delta_v

description: Rotate an entity. Without pivot: add Euler-angle deltas (radians) to its rotation field; it turns about its own origin (position), which for a solid built off-origin (revolve, sweep, mesh) may not be its middle. With pivot: rigidly turn the entity by the rotation R(delta) (XYZ Euler, world frame) about the pivot point — a world [x, y, z] or "center" (its bounding-box center) — so position moves too and the pivot stays fixed.

delta.description: Euler-angle increments [dRx, dRy, dRz] in radians to add to the current rotation.

id.description: Id of the entity to rotate.

pivot.description: Optional world point [x, y, z] to rotate about, or "center" for the entity bounding-box center. Omit to rotate in place about the entity origin.

name: rotate_entity

description: Say in which order auto_route_lines would route several lines, without routing: lines promoted by earlier failures first, then DN descending (wide lines claim space first), then straight-line (Manhattan) distance between the two ends descending, then the request position. promote lists line ids moved to the front (the latest first), as the retry of auto_route_lines does. data = { order: [lineId], rule, lines: [{ lineId, dn, distanceMm }] }. Read-only; the native transport (llull auto_route with lines) uses it to plan.

common.description: Settings applied to every line that does not set its own (grid, bendCost, clearance, gridMargin, preferElevations, ...).

bendCost.description: Cost of one bend in mm of pipe (default 1000): higher = fewer bends, longer pipe.

clearance.description: Gap kept to every obstacle beyond the pipe (or insulation) surface, mm (default 50).

elevationPenalty.description: Extra cost per mm of horizontal pipe off every preferred elevation (default 0.5).

grid.description: Lattice cell, mm (default 50). Both port stubs must land on one lattice.

gridMargin.description: How far the search box extends beyond the two port stubs, mm (default 2000).

keepOut.description: Entity ids the route must avoid even when a port sits on them (maintenance space, access).

keepOutBoxes.description: Extra keep-out boxes (world, mm) the route must avoid.

preferElevations.description: Preferred centreline elevations z (e.g. rack levels), mm: horizontal pipe elsewhere pays elevationPenalty.

lines.description: The lines to route (1 to 64), each as for auto_route_pipe: { lineId, from, to, ...settings }.

bendCost.description: Cost of one bend in mm of pipe (default 1000): higher = fewer bends, longer pipe.

clearance.description: Gap kept to every obstacle beyond the pipe (or insulation) surface, mm (default 50).

elevationPenalty.description: Extra cost per mm of horizontal pipe off every preferred elevation (default 0.5).

portId.description: Port id: tie-in point id (add_tie_in_point), "<tag>:<mark>" of an equipment nozzle (add_nozzle) or "<runId>:start|end".

direction.description: Face direction at the open end, pointing toward the pipe (an axis direction).

from.description: Start end: { portId } or an open end { point, direction }.

grid.description: Lattice cell, mm (default 50). Both port stubs must land on one lattice.

gridMargin.description: How far the search box extends beyond the two port stubs, mm (default 2000).

keepOut.description: Entity ids the route must avoid even when a port sits on them (maintenance space, access).

keepOutBoxes.description: Extra keep-out boxes (world, mm) the route must avoid.

maxExpansions.description: In-process search cap per first-move candidate for this line (default the request value, maximum 200000).

preferElevations.description: Preferred centreline elevations z (e.g. rack levels), mm: horizontal pipe elsewhere pays elevationPenalty.

solution.description: A solution of route_problem (from llull auto_route); validated before it is committed.

cost.description: Integer µm cost: lattice length + bends x bendCost + elevation penalties.

engine.description: Caller-asserted source (recorded as given): 'llull-route' (set by llull auto_route), 'ts' or a name for a hand-written route.

expansions.description: Caller-asserted (recorded as given): states the search expanded.

optimal.description: Caller-asserted (recorded as given): true when the search proved the route minimal.

pis.description: Interior points of intersection in route order.

items.description: Point of intersection [x, y, z], mm.

problemHash.description: route_problem data.problemHash the solution was computed for.

portId.description: Port id: tie-in point id (add_tie_in_point), "<tag>:<mark>" of an equipment nozzle (add_nozzle) or "<runId>:start|end".

direction.description: Face direction at the open end, pointing toward the pipe (an axis direction).

to.description: End end: { portId } or an open end { point, direction }.

promote.description: Line ids moved to the front, the latest promoted first.

name: route_lines_order

description: Route a pipe line by compass legs from a start port, spec-driven: every turn gets the elbow of the line spec (angle within the spec tolerance, catalogue centre-to-end, never a formula), a flanged (FL) port gets a flange (weld neck, socket-weld or threaded as the spec pipe asks) + gasket + bolt set, and every straight piece gets its cut length (leg length minus the centre-to-ends, flange sets and weld gaps at its ends; on a socket-weld spec (plain-end pipe, SW fittings) the pipe goes socketDepth - 1.6 mm gap into each socket, on a threaded spec threadEngagement into each fitting, so those cuts are longer; a SW or SC tie-in takes the depth of the spec own socket fittings). A turn no spec angle fits is a trimmed 90 elbow (spec elbowAngles.trimmedAllowed, turns up to 90 deg) or, with bendRadius or the spec bendRadiusD, a pipe bend (butt-weld pipe, R tan(turn/2) tangents), both flagged RTE_NONSTANDARD_FITTING. Lengths in document units (mm; the document must be in mm). from/to: { portId } (tie-in id from add_tie_in_point, "<tag>:<mark>" of an equipment nozzle such as "V-101:N1" from add_nozzle / equipment_ports, or "<runId>:start|end" to continue a run) or an open { point, direction? }. legs: [{ direction "+X"|"-X"|"+Y"|"-Y"|"+Z"|"-Z" or [dx,dy,dz], length }] from the start; the first leg must leave along the start port direction (within the tolerance). A SLOPED leg gives planLength (its horizontal length) and slope { value, unit percent|ratio|deg, fall } instead of length, along a horizontal direction: it falls (or rises) by planLength x s, so a 1 % fall over 8000 is 80 mm lower and 8000.39999 long; the elbow after it turns by the real angle (89.427 degrees into a vertical leg) and is the standard 90 elbow within the spec tolerance; a sloped first / last leg is judged on its plan direction against the port; the declared slope is stored per leg (check_piping RTE_ADVERSE_SLOPE / RTE_POCKET) and sloped legs report planLengthMm, dropMm (positive = descends along the flow) and slopeDeg in data.legs. via: extra points of intersection after the legs. When `to` is a port, a straight closing leg to it is added if the last point is on its axis (the last leg may omit length to run straight to it). inline: [{ type (valve, reducerConcentric or reducerEccentric), at: { leg, centreDistance }, dn2 (reducers), tag, stemDirection (valves), flat "top" | "bottom" or flatDirection (eccentric reducers) }] places valves and reducers while routing (leg = index in data.legs, the closing leg included); a reducer is how the run meets a `to` port of another size; an eccentric reducer moves the smaller axis toward its flat side by (OD big - OD small) / 2 and the leg after it must take that offset up (RTE_ECCENTRIC_OFFSET). Add them later with insert_inline_component. Open-end directions are normalised (zero is refused). Returns the run id (affected[0]); data = { runId, lineId, lineNumber, pis, closingLeg, mergedPoints, portDeviationDeg, legs (index, direction, lengthMm, cutLengthsMm, planLengthMm / dropMm / slopeDeg on sloped legs), turns (turnDeg, nominalDeg, deviationDeg, centreToEnd, fitting, kind standard | trimmed | bend), insulation, envelopeDiameterMm (OD + 2 x the line insulation, null without), counts, pipePieces (id, leg, cutLengthMm), totalPipeMm, centrelineLengthMm, studs, warnings (RTE_WELD_SPACING, RTE_FITTING_TO_FITTING, RTE_NONSTANDARD_FITTING, RTE_ECCENTRIC_OFFSET), unverified, unverifiedReasons, partIds, inlineIds, dn (start, end), spec, angleTolerance, weldGap, weldSpacing, pipe }; parts and joints are listed by piping_takeoff. A spec that is not approved or has non-grade-A rows reports unverified. Refusals: RTE_UNITS_UNSUPPORTED, RTE_UNKNOWN_LINE, RTE_UNKNOWN_PORT, RTE_PORT_IN_USE, RTE_SLOPE_INVALID (slope on a vertical leg, no planLength, over 100 %), RTE_INVALID_PORT (zero open-end direction), RTE_SIZE_MISMATCH (also a reducer without dn2), RTE_RATING_MISMATCH, RTE_FACING_MISMATCH, RTE_NO_CONNECTION_RULE (an end type the spec pipe does not take: BE pipe BW, PE pipe SW, THD pipe SC), RTE_ECCENTRIC_INVALID, RTE_ECCENTRIC_OFFSET, RTE_PORT_DIRECTION, RTE_CLOSING_LEG_IMPOSSIBLE (detail.offset), RTE_ZERO_LEG, RTE_NO_FITTING_FOR_ANGLE (detail.anglesDeg, trimmedAllowed, bendRadiusD; also a bend tighter than one outside diameter), RTE_SEGMENT_TOO_SHORT (detail.cutLengthMm), RTE_INLINE_DOES_NOT_FIT, RTE_SPEC_UNKNOWN, RTE_SPEC_NO_COMPONENT, RTE_SPEC_AMBIGUOUS. Next: piping_takeoff for the cut list; check_piping; add_branch / insert_inline_component; delete_pipe_run to redo.

angleToleranceDeg.description: Overrides the spec tolerance for port directions and elbow angles, degrees, 22.5 at most (named in the result).

bendRadius.description: Pipe bends: centreline radius in mm (for example 5 x the outside diameter) of the bend each turn that no spec elbow angle fits becomes, instead of a trimmed elbow. Butt-weld pipe only; the bend is flagged RTE_NONSTANDARD_FITTING. Omit to use the spec (trimmedAllowed / bendRadiusD).

portId.description: Port id: a tie-in id, "<tag>:<mark>" of an equipment nozzle, or "<runId>:start|end".

direction.description: Direction the pipe leaves (start) or arrives along reversed (end) [dx, dy, dz]; optional.

point.description: Open end [x, y, z], document units (mm).

from.description: Start: { portId } or an open { point, direction? }.

inline.description: Valves and concentric reducers placed while routing (see insert_inline_component for the rules).

at.description: Where the centre sits: { leg, centreDistance }.

centreDistance.description: Distance of the component centre from the leg start point of intersection, document units.

leg.description: Leg index, 0 = the first leg (data.legs of route_pipe).

dn2.description: Reducers only: the outlet size DN the run continues at (the inlet is the run size at that point). Valves: omit.

flat.description: Eccentric reducers only: the flat side, "top" (flat on top, FOT: +Z) or "bottom" (FOB: -Z), on a horizontal or sloped pipe. The outer surfaces of the two pipes line up on the flat side, so the smaller pipe axis moves toward it by (OD big - OD small) / 2. Give this or flatDirection.

flatDirection.description: Eccentric reducers only: direction from the pipe axis toward the flat side [dx, dy, dz] (any side, needed on a vertical pipe); projected perpendicular to the pipe and normalised. Give this or flat.

stemDirection.description: Valves: direction from the valve centre toward the handwheel [dx, dy, dz]; normalised. Default: up (+Z), or +X on a vertical pipe.

type.description: Catalogue type: a valve (valveGate, valveGlobe, valveCheck, valveBall, valveButterfly, valvePlug), reducerConcentric or reducerEccentric (needs flat or flatDirection).

legs.description: Legs from the start point, in order.

length.description: Length along the direction, document units, > 0. May be omitted on the last leg when `to` is a port.

planLength.description: Sloped leg: the HORIZONTAL length, document units, > 0 (give it with slope and without length). The leg runs along the horizontal direction and falls / rises by slope: drop = planLength x s, length = planLength x sqrt(1 + s^2) (1 % over 8000: drop 80, length 8000.39999).

slope.description: Slope of this leg (needs planLength; the direction must be horizontal, a compass +X..-Y or a horizontal vector). The following elbow turns by the real angle (89.427 degrees for a 1 % leg into a vertical one), which is a standard 90 elbow within the spec tolerance.

fall.description: true = the pipe descends along the flow (a drain); false = it rises along the flow.

unit.description: "percent" (1 = 1 %), "ratio" (drop / plan length, 0.01) or "deg".

value.description: Slope size, > 0: percent of the plan length (1 = 1 %), a ratio (0.01) or degrees, per unit. At most 45 degrees (100 %).

portId.description: Port id: a tie-in id, "<tag>:<mark>" of an equipment nozzle, or "<runId>:start|end".

direction.description: Direction the pipe leaves (start) or arrives along reversed (end) [dx, dy, dz]; optional.

point.description: Open end [x, y, z], document units (mm).

to.description: End: { portId } (a closing leg is added) or an open { point }. Omit to end at the last leg.

via.description: Points of intersection added after the legs.

items.description: Point of intersection [x, y, z].

name: route_pipe

description: Build the canonical auto-routing problem of a pipe line between two ports without routing it: lattice (cell, origin, box), port stubs, integer-micrometre costs (bend cost, rack-elevation penalty) and every obstacle box inflated by pipe radius + insulation + clearance (3D entities, the clash bodies of existing runs, keep-outs). The elbow centre-to-end and the flange sets of flanged ports come from the line spec (catalogue rows, not formulas). Ports are tie-in ids, equipment nozzles "<tag>:<mark>" or run ends. data = { problem, problemHash, defaults, elbowCentreToEnd, flangeSetLengths, portOwners, unverified, unverifiedReasons }; the native router (llull auto_route, llull-compute route) solves it and auto_route_pipe checks the solution against the same hash. Refusals: RTE_UNITS_UNSUPPORTED (non-mm document), RTE_UNKNOWN_LINE, RTE_UNKNOWN_PORT, RTE_PORT_IN_USE, RTE_SIZE_MISMATCH, RTE_PORT_DIRECTION, RTE_RATING_MISMATCH, RTE_FACING_MISMATCH, RTE_SPEC_UNKNOWN, RTE_SPEC_NO_COMPONENT, RTE_UNKNOWN_KEEPOUT, RTE_AUTOROUTE_NO_PATH. Next: auto_route_pipe (or llull auto_route for large boxes).

bendCost.description: Cost of one bend in mm of pipe (default 1000): higher = fewer bends, longer pipe.

clearance.description: Gap kept to every obstacle beyond the pipe (or insulation) surface, mm (default 50).

elevationPenalty.description: Extra cost per mm of horizontal pipe off every preferred elevation (default 0.5).

portId.description: Port id: tie-in point id (add_tie_in_point), "<tag>:<mark>" of an equipment nozzle (add_nozzle) or "<runId>:start|end".

direction.description: Face direction at the open end, pointing toward the pipe (an axis direction).

from.description: Start end: { portId } or an open end { point, direction }.

grid.description: Lattice cell, mm (default 50). Both port stubs must land on one lattice.

gridMargin.description: How far the search box extends beyond the two port stubs, mm (default 2000).

keepOut.description: Entity ids the route must avoid even when a port sits on them (maintenance space, access).

keepOutBoxes.description: Extra keep-out boxes (world, mm) the route must avoid.

preferElevations.description: Preferred centreline elevations z (e.g. rack levels), mm: horizontal pipe elsewhere pays elevationPenalty.

portId.description: Port id: tie-in point id (add_tie_in_point), "<tag>:<mark>" of an equipment nozzle (add_nozzle) or "<runId>:start|end".

direction.description: Face direction at the open end, pointing toward the pipe (an axis direction).

to.description: End end: { portId } or an open end { point, direction }.

name: route_problem

description: Ruled sheet: straight lines joining two curves (nurbs_curve ids; hypar from two skew lines, frustum sheet from two circles, hull strakes) or a curve and a point (a cone). u runs along the curves, v from the first curve (0) to the second (1). `coupling` decides which points are joined: parameter (default; curves are made compatible, exact), arc_length (equal fractions of arc length, curves refitted within fitTolerance), developable (rulings whose tangent planes coincide so the sheet can be unrolled flat: Gaussian curvature 0; exact for coaxial circles of equal basis, else paired by Newton and refitted). `reverse` flips the second curve. Returns data { area (units squared), maxAbsGaussianCurvature (1/units squared), scaledGaussianCurvature (K x diagonal^2, dimensionless), developable (boolean: scaled K <= 1e-6, unit independent), rulingTwistMaxRad, coupling, fitDeviation }. Next: measure_area, analyze_surface_curvature, thicken_surface, check_sweep_loft.

color.description: Hex color string #rrggbb, e.g. "#c8553d". Defaults to "#9fb4c7".

coupling.description: Pairing of the two curves: parameter (default), arc_length (equal arc-length fractions) or developable (rulings with a common tangent plane; refused with SWG_NOT_DEVELOPABLE if none exists).

curveId.description: One nurbs_curve id, joined to `point` (a cone over the curve).

curveIds.description: Exactly two nurbs_curve ids to join. Alternative to curveId + point.

fitTolerance.description: Largest allowed refit deviation in document units for arc_length pairing (> 0). Default 1e-6 x the size of the curves.

layerId.description: Layer id to assign the entity to. Defaults to the document default layer.

name.description: Optional display name for the entity (shown in the scene tree).

point.description: World [x, y, z] apex for curveId (a cone).

position.description: Origin [x, y, z] of the surface in document units; the poles are relative to it. Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

reverse.description: Run the second curve backwards before pairing (default false).

name: ruled_surface

description: Reliability analysis of ONE limit state g(x) (failure when g < 0) with one or several methods, compared: "form" (Hasofer-Lind / Rackwitz-Fiessler iteration in standard normal space, Nataf transform for distributions and correlation), "sorm" (FORM + Breitung curvature correction, needs a converged design point with beta > 0), "mc" (seeded Monte Carlo or Latin hypercube, needs `seed`) and "fosm" (first-order second-moment). Default methods: form, mc, fosm; methods ["form"] is the plain FORM run. data.form (and data.sorm) = { beta, pfForm = Φ(-beta), designPointX { variable: { value, unit } } (most probable failure point), importance { variable: alpha^2 } (sums to 1: which variable drives failure), iterations, converged, items[] } (beta is negative when all variables at their medians already fail; exact for linear g in normal variables: (muR - muS) / sqrt(sR^2 + sS^2); gradients by central differences); data.monteCarlo and data.fosm as in propagate_uncertainty; comparison { pf: { method: Pf }, formInsideMonteCarloInterval } and the item PRB_FORM_MC_DISAGREE when the FORM Pf falls outside the Monte Carlo Wilson 95 % interval (report the Monte Carlo value, consider SORM). For several limit states or the distribution of g itself use propagate_uncertainty. Computed by llull, not approved: a qualified engineer must review before any certification decision.

methods.description: Methods to run, any of form, sorm, mc, fosm. Default ["form", "mc", "fosm"]. ["form"] = FORM only; add "sorm" for the Breitung correction.

samples.description: Monte Carlo samples (default 10000, at most 2000000).

sampling.description: Sampling scheme of the "mc" method. Default "lhs".

seed.description: Integer seed in [0, 4294967295] of the PRNG (xoshiro128**); the same model, method, samples and seed give bit-identical results.

tolerance.description: FORM stops when no u component changes by more than this (default 1e-8).

name: run_reliability_study

description: Sample a material property along one variable (e.g. k from 4 K to 300 K): `count` points (default 101, at most 1000), linear or log spacing; optionally the integral ∫ y dx (e.g. the conductivity integral in W/m, adaptive Gauss-Kronrod) and a piecewise-linear solver table whose linear interpolation stays within relTol (default 1e-3) of the model, for solver decks. Same range rules as evaluate_property: from / to must lie in the valid range (PROP_OUT_OF_RANGE). Read-only; numbers behind a property chart.

count.description: Number of samples, endpoints included (default 101, max 1000).

unit.description: Unit, e.g. 'K', 'degC', 'degF', '1/s'.

fixed.description: Values of the other variables, each with its unit.

from.description: Start of the sweep with its unit.

unit.description: Unit, e.g. 'K', 'degC', 'degF', '1/s'.

integrate.description: Also return ∫ y d(variable) over [from, to].

outputUnit.description: Unit of y. Default: the model unit.

solverTable.description: Also return a piecewise-linear solver table (for solver decks).

solverTableRelTol.description: Max relative linear-interpolation error of the solver table (default 1e-3).

spacing.description: Sample spacing (log needs from > 0). Default linear.

to.description: End of the sweep with its unit (> from).

unit.description: Unit, e.g. 'K', 'degC', 'degF', '1/s'.

name: sample_property

description: Snapshot the current featureHistory into a named recipe stored in the document. A recipe is a saved constructive sequence that can be re-instantiated any number of times (on this or any document) via instantiate_recipe, each time producing independent entities with fresh ids. Saving does NOT change any geometry. If a recipe with the same name already exists it is replaced.

label.description: Optional human/AI note describing the recipe's purpose, e.g. "L-bracket with 3 holes".

name.description: Unique lookup key for the recipe, e.g. "bracket_v1", "wheel_assembly". Must be a non-empty, non-whitespace-only string. Used as both the display name and the key for instantiate_recipe.

name: save_recipe

description: Save a named review viewpoint (a BCF viewpoint camera, for review issues, walkthroughs and render_view; for a drawing view that also shows chosen PMI items or a section use create_saved_view instead) in the document: give `camera` (perspective eye / direction / up / fovDeg or orthographic eye / direction / up / viewHeight), or omit it to save the current document camera (set_camera / fit_view, 45° perspective). Direction and up are normalised and made orthogonal. Returns the id (vp-<n>) in affected[0] and data { id, guid, camera }. Viewpoints feed render_view (viewpointId), create_walkthrough and export_bcf. Does not add a feature step. Error: VIS_CAMERA_INVALID.

camera.description: Camera of the viewpoint (BCF PerspectiveCamera / OrthogonalCamera).

direction.description: View direction [x, y, z] (any non-zero length; normalised on save).

eye.description: Camera position [x, y, z] in document units (Z-up).

fovDeg.description: Perspective: vertical field of view in degrees, (0, 180). Default 45 (the viewport).

up.description: Up vector [x, y, z]; made orthogonal to direction on save. Default [0, 0, 1].

viewHeight.description: Orthographic: visible height of the view in document units, > 0.

fromDocumentCamera.description: true: save the current document camera (the same as omitting camera). Not together with camera.

name.description: Viewpoint name, e.g. "Pump skid from the walkway".

name: save_viewpoint

description: Uniformly scale an entity by a positive factor. Scales geometry in-place for all kinds — 3D: box size, cylinder radius & height, sphere radius, extrusion profile & depth; 2D: line/polyline points, arc/circle/ellipse radii, rectangle width & height, spline points (about the local origin). Position is unchanged.

factor.description: Uniform scale factor. Must be greater than 0. A value of 2 doubles the size; 0.5 halves it.

id.description: Id of the entity to scale.

name: scale_entity

description: Scale a 3D solid or mesh by a different factor on each axis (a sphere becomes an ellipsoid, a cylinder an elliptic cylinder). factors are unitless multipliers along the frame x, y, z axes (default: world x, y, z) about center (default: the body bounding-box centre). A negative factor mirrors the body about that axis plane (a true mirror: the faces stay outward). Volume is multiplied by |sx sy sz|. Exact on the native kernel (no approximation: curved faces become B-splines); on the mesh kernel or without a kernel the triangles are scaled. The entity is replaced by a mesh entity that keeps the construction (brep recipe). Refuses a zero factor (DEF_SCALE_SINGULAR) and factors all equal to 1 (DEF_NO_EFFECT). For one factor on all axes use scale_entity. Then call analyze_deformation and check_deformation.

center.description: Fixed point of the scale, a world point in document units. Default: the body bounding-box centre.

factors.description: Scale factors [sx, sy, sz], unitless, along the frame x, y, z axes. Negative mirrors that axis; 0 is refused.

frame.description: Axes the factors act along; default the world axes.

axis.description: Direction of the frame z axis, unitless (normalised). Default [0, 0, 1].

reference.description: Direction giving the frame x axis, unitless; must not be parallel to axis. Default: the first world axis not parallel to axis ([1, 0, 0] for the default axis).

id.description: Id of the 3D solid or mesh entity to deform (describe_scene lists ids). It is replaced by the deformed mesh entity (keepSource keeps it).

ids.description: Ids of several 3D solids or meshes to deform with the same parameters (one feature step; every body gets its own frame and region defaults from its own bounds). Use this or id.

keepSource.description: true: keep the original entity(ies) next to the deformed one(s) instead of replacing them. Default false.

output.description: How the result is computed: kernel choice and mesh tolerance.

mode.description: "auto" (default): the exact kernel builds the result when it can evaluate this deformation (the native kernel does for every law: the faces become B-splines fitted within output.tolerance), else the mesh path runs and the summary says so; "exact": refuse (DEF_EXACT_UNAVAILABLE) unless the exact kernel built it; "mesh": force the faceted mesh path.

preserveAnalytic.description: Recognise cylinders, cones and planes in an exact result (needs the exact warp of a later milestone; true is refused today).

tolerance.description: Largest deviation of the result from the true deformed surface, document units, > 0: the chordal deviation of the mesh path, or the fit error of the B-spline faces and edges on the exact path (a smaller value costs control points, not accuracy). Default: 1e-5 times the body bounding-box diagonal, clamped to [1e-6, 0.01].

name: scale_nonuniform

description: Sculpt a triangle mesh (or the triangles of any 3D solid) with a brush stroke: each stamp centre is projected onto the surface, then every vertex closer than `radius` (euclidean distance, t = distance / radius < 1) moves by strength x falloff(t). Brushes: "draw" along the area-weighted normal of the brush region (direction "area_normal", default) or each vertex normal ("normal") or a fixed vector; "inflate" along vertex normals; "grab" by the `direction` vector times falloff (strength ignored); "smooth" toward the neighbour mean (strength <= 1, `taubin` adds the inflating step); "flatten" onto the plane through the brush region centroid (or `planePoint`) with the region normal; "pinch" tangentially toward the stamp centre; "crease" = draw with -strength plus pinch with strength / 2; "layer" raises to min(strength x falloff, maxHeight) above the surface at stroke start without accumulating. Falloffs: constant 1, linear 1 - t, smooth (1 - t^2)^2 (default), sphere sqrt(1 - t^2). `symmetry` {plane yz|xz|xy through the origin} stamps the mirror image in the same pass. `refineEdge` first splits edges longer than that inside the brush so detail is possible. Reports movedVertices, maxDisplacement (document units), displacedVolume (closed mesh: volume after - before; open height field: sum of triangle area x mean vertex displacement along the face normal) and symmetryError (largest distance between mirror vertex pairs). Connectivity is unchanged without refineEdge. Refusals: MESH_ENTITY_NOT_FOUND, MESH_NOT_A_MESH, MESH_PARAM_INVALID, MESH_SCULPT_STAMP_OFF_SURFACE.

brush.description: Brush: draw, inflate, grab, smooth, flatten, pinch, crease or layer.

anyOf.description: Vector [x, y, z]: the displacement of grab, the direction of draw / layer.

direction.description: "area_normal" (default) region normal, "normal" per-vertex normals, or a vector (required by grab).

falloff.description: Falloff curve of t = distance / radius. Default "smooth".

id.description: Id of the mesh (or other 3D solid) to sculpt.

keepSource.description: true: keep the source and add the result as a new mesh. Default false: the source entity is rewritten in place (same id, name, layer, colour).

maskRegion.description: Only vertices inside this sphere may move.

center.description: Centre [x, y, z] of the sphere (document units, world).

radius.description: Radius of the sphere (document units).

maxHeight.description: layer only: largest layer height (document units). Default unlimited.

planePoint.description: A point [x, y, z] of the flatten plane (document units). Default the brush region centroid.

radius.description: Brush radius (document units).

refineEdge.description: Split edges longer than this (document units) inside the brush before sculpting.

center.description: Stamp centre [x, y, z] (world, document units); projected onto the surface.

strength.description: Strength: displacement per stamp at the centre (document units); a fraction 0..1 for smooth / flatten / pinch.

symmetry.description: Also stamp the mirror image of every stamp (a stamp on the plane is applied once).

plane.description: Mirror plane through the origin: yz mirrors x, xz mirrors y, xy mirrors z.

taubin.description: smooth only: add the inflating Taubin step to avoid shrinkage. Default false.

name: sculpt_mesh

description: Single-degree-of-freedom quick check. Give the natural frequency fnHz (Hz) and damping as zeta (fraction of critical) or Q (= 1/(2 zeta)); there is no default damping. input.kind 'harmonic': amplification Q at fn, receptance peak, half-power points and Q estimate, base transmissibility. input.kind 'random' with asdG2PerHz (white base ASD, g^2/Hz), spectrum (name) or points [[fHz, g2/Hz], ...]: absolute acceleration rms in g and relative displacement rms in mm, integrated EXACTLY (closed form for white noise, adaptive grid otherwise) - the answer of record - with Miles' equation sqrt(pi/2 fn Q W(fn)) beside it for comparison, and the named 3-sigma peak. Use before and after a random_response analysis; it never replaces one.

Q.description: Amplification factor Q = 1 / (2 zeta). Give zeta or Q.

bandHz.description: Integration band [fLowHz, fHighHz]; default: the whole spectrum.

asdG2PerHz.description: random: white base ASD level in g^2/Hz.

kind.description: harmonic (unit force / base) or random base acceleration.

points.description: random: inline ASD breakpoints [[fHz, g2/Hz], ...].

zeta.description: Viscous damping ratio (fraction of critical, 0 < zeta < 1). Give zeta or Q; there is no default.

name: sdof_response

description: Cut an implicit field or body by a plane and report the section as numbers: closed boundary loops (outer loops positive area, holes negative), their perimeters, the solid area, and the solid fraction of the sampled square (the numeric version of a section view; use it to see the inside of a lattice). The plane is given by a point and a normal; the sampled square has side `size` (document units), is centred on the point and uses a resolution x resolution grid (resolution 8..400; the area error falls with its square). Loops are decimated to 2000 points each; svg true adds an SVG drawing of the section in data.svg (save it with --save).

id.description: Id of a field node or of an implicit body.

normal.description: Plane normal [x, y, z] (non-zero).

origin.description: A point on the plane [x, y, z] in document units: the centre of the sampled square.

resolution.description: Samples along each side of the square (integer 8..400, default 200).

size.description: Side of the sampled square in document units (> 0).

svg.description: Also return an SVG drawing of the loops in data.svg.

name: section_field

description: Segment a mesh (or the triangles of any 3D solid) into regions and fit each one with the analytic surface it follows: "plane", "cylinder" (axis, radius), "cone" (apex, axis, half angle), "sphere" (centre, radius) or "freeform" when none is within `fitTolerance`. A region is a set of faces joined across edges whose dihedral angle is at most `featureAngleDeg`, so a tessellated hole wall is ONE cylinder while the sharp edges around it separate it from the planes (a plate with a hole gives 6 planes and 1 cylinder). The fit of a region is the plane when every vertex is within `fitTolerance` of it, else the primitive with the lowest Bayesian information criterion among those within the tolerance (least squares + Levenberg-Marquardt on the region vertices), else freeform with the residual of the best attempt. Reports per group the face count, area (document units^2) and fit with rms and max residual (document units), the adjacency of the regions (shared edges and length) and the count by type. Next: mesh_to_brep (faceted or prismatic) turns the groups into B-rep faces. Needs a manifold, consistently wound mesh without degenerate faces (repair_mesh first). The torus is not fitted. Refusals: MESH_ENTITY_NOT_FOUND, MESH_NOT_A_MESH, MESH_PARAM_INVALID, MESH_NON_MANIFOLD, MESH_ORIENTATION_INCONSISTENT, MESH_DEGENERATE, MESH_ENGINE_CAP_EXCEEDED.

featureAngleDeg.description: Edges whose faces meet at more than this angle (degrees) separate regions. Default 30.

fitTolerance.description: Largest distance (document units) of a region vertex to its primitive. Default 0.001 x bounding-box diagonal (named default).

id.description: Id of the mesh (or other 3D solid) to segment.

kinds.description: Primitives to try. Default all four (the torus is not fitted).

maxListed.description: Longest group / adjacency list returned; totals are exact. Default 50.

name: segment_mesh

description: Find cage elements of a subdivision solid and return their stable ids for the editing commands. Give exactly ONE selector: `nearest` (world point -> nearest vertex, edge or face per `kind`, default vertex); `loopFrom` (edge: the edge loop through it, ordered, continuing straight through valence-4 vertices); `ringFrom` (edge: the quad strip across it, the edges a loop cut would split plus the strip faces); `region` (world box: vertices inside, edges and faces entirely inside); `within` ({ point, radius } world sphere, same rule); `faces` ({ normal, within }: faces whose outward normal is within the cone, dot(n, normal) >= 1 - within). `grow` widens the result by n rings of neighbours; `kind` keeps only vertices, edges or faces. Returns data { vertices, edges, faces } (ids), vertexIndices, faceIndices. Next: extrude_cage_faces, inset_cage_faces, loop_cut_cage, set_cage_crease, edit_subdivision_cage.

faces.description: Faces whose outward normal lies in a cone around `normal`.

normal.description: World direction (any non-zero length) the faces should face.

within.description: Cone width as 1 - cos(angle): 0 exact, 0.05 about 18 degrees, 1 a half space. Default 0.05.

grow.description: Rings of neighbours added around the result (default 0).

id.description: Id of the subdivision solid.

kind.description: For `nearest`: which element to find (default vertex). Otherwise: keep only this kind in the result.

loopFrom.description: Edge whose edge loop is selected (id or [a, b]).

nearest.description: World point; selects the cage element of `kind` closest to it.

region.description: World box: elements entirely inside it.

ringFrom.description: Edge whose quad strip (face ring) is selected (id or [a, b]).

within.description: World sphere: elements entirely inside it.

radius.description: Sphere radius, document units.

name: select_cage_elements

description: Select the fastener for a stack (read-only): grip dash, part number, shim washers, length and thread protrusion. Give family and diameterDash (list_fastener_families), and the stack either as stack { value, unit } or as stackIds + axisPoint (+ axis) measured along the axis. Optional nut and washer family ids (same diameter dash) enable the protrusion check and shimming. Bolts use the smallest grip >= stack (washers fill the gap, total <= 1/8 in by default, at most 3); Hi-Lok pins use the grip whose range contains the stack; rivets use stack + 1.5 D rounded to the catalogue step. Every rule left at its default is listed in data.rules with source and defaulted: true. Failures return data.ok = false with reasons[] (FAST_STACK_OUT_OF_RANGE, FAST_WASHER_GAP, FAST_PROTRUSION_SHORT, ...). All lengths in data are inches (…In). Next: insert_fastener_stack.

axis.description: Fastener axis direction [x, y, z] pointing from the head side to the nut side. Default [0, 0, 1].

axisPoint.description: Point [x, y, z] in document units the fastener axis passes through (with stackIds). Not required with stack.

codes.description: Part-number code choices by grammar field name, e.g. { "material": "AD" } for MS20470AD4. A missing choice takes the first catalogue code and is reported.

diameterDash.description: Size dash of the family as listed by list_fastener_families (e.g. "3" for NAS6203, "4" for MS20470AD4, "8" for HL19 1/4 in).

family.description: Id of the fastener family in the document catalogue (e.g. "NAS6203-6220", "MS20470", "HL19"). Use list_fastener_families to see ids.

maxWasherTotal.description: Largest combined washer thickness allowed as { value, unit }. Default 1/8 in (AC 43.13-1B 7-37), reported as a defaulted rule

unit.description: Length unit of the value, e.g. 'in', 'mm', 'ft'.

nut.description: Optional nut family id (e.g. "MS21042") for the same diameter dash; enables the thread-protrusion check.

rivetRounding.description: Rivet length rounding to the catalogue step: "up" or "nearest". Default: the catalogue rule (up), reported as a defaulted rule.

stack.description: Stack thickness to fasten (total thickness of the joined layers) as { value, unit }. Give this OR stackIds

unit.description: Length unit of the value, e.g. 'in', 'mm', 'ft'.

stackIds.description: Ids of the 3D solids (plates) the fastener passes through; their thickness along the axis is measured. Give this OR stack. Needs axisPoint.

washer.description: Optional washer family id (e.g. "NAS1149") used to shim the gap between grip and stack.

washerSide.description: Side of the stack the shim washers go on: "nut" (default) or "head".

name: select_fastener

description: Make a colour profile the active display profile (colour_by_rule_report and check_display default to it), or pass profileId null to show entity colours again. Geometry is untouched. Error: VIS_PROFILE_NOT_FOUND. Does not add a feature step.

profileId.description: Profile id, or null to deactivate.

name: set_active_colour_profile

description: Show an exploded view in the viewport (and exploded drawings), or none. Omit "id" to switch the explosion off. "step" limits the explosion to steps 1..step (progressive reveal); omit it for the full explosion. Real part placements are never modified.

id.description: Exploded view id; omit to show the assembled model.

step.description: Show only offsets with step <= this. Default: all.

name: set_active_exploded_view

description: Set the active level: new building elements go there when no levelId is given.

levelId.description: Level id, e.g. "level-1".

name: set_active_level

description: Turn on adiabatic heating for a Johnson-Cook material of an explicit_dynamics case: the plastic work heats the material, dT = beta * sigma_y * d(eps_p) / (rho * c_p), and the flow stress softens by (1 - T*^m), T* = (T - T_transition) / (T_melt - T_transition); the D5 term of the Johnson-Cook failure strain uses the same T*. beta = Taylor-Quinney coefficient (default 0.9, LS-DYNA). The specific heat c_p comes from the material's cp property model (define_property_model property cp), read when the job is built; the run starts at the Johnson-Cook transition temperature. enabled false removes the heating (isothermal).

analysisId.description: Id of the analysis (affected[0] of create_analysis, e.g. an-1.1).

enabled.description: false removes the heating of this material. Default true.

material.description: Document material id (create_material name) used by a part of the case.

taylorQuinney.description: Fraction beta of the plastic work turned into heat, 0..1. Default 0.9 (named).

name: set_adiabatic_heating

description: Define the aircraft coordinate frame used by fuselage stations (FS, BL, WL): a document position is datum + fs * fsAxis + bl * blAxis + wl * wlAxis. `datum` is the document position of FS = BL = WL = 0; the three axes are unit vectors, mutually perpendicular and right-handed (fsAxis x blAxis = wlAxis). Default frame when never set: datum [0, 0, 0], FS along +x (aft), BL along +y (right), WL along +z (up). Applies to fuselages lofted AFTER this call (loft_fuselage) and to fuselage_section_at; existing geometry is not moved. `units` must equal the document units (set_units first); it documents the unit of the datum and of every station value.

blAxis.description: Unit direction [x, y, z] of increasing buttock line (usually to the right). Default use [0, 1, 0].

datum.description: Document position [x, y, z] of FS = 0, BL = 0, WL = 0, in document units.

fsAxis.description: Unit direction [x, y, z] of increasing fuselage station (usually aft). Default use [1, 0, 0].

units.description: Length unit of datum and stations: "mm", "cm", "m", "in" or "ft"; must equal the document units.

wlAxis.description: Unit direction [x, y, z] of increasing water line (up). Must equal fsAxis x blAxis. Default use [0, 0, 1].

name: set_aircraft_frame

description: Set the vertical design profile of an alignment from PVIs [{ station, elevation, curveLength? }] (document units). Grades are straight between PVIs; an interior PVI with `curveLength` > 0 gets a symmetric parabolic vertical curve centred on it (first / last PVI cannot). The first and last PVI stations must lie within the alignment stations. The summary lists grades and K values.

pvis.description: At least 2 PVIs; sorted by station automatically.

elevation.description: Design elevation at the PVI, document units.

name: set_alignment_profile

description: Shake the base of a frequency_response / random_response case: a uniform base ACCELERATION along direction x | y | z applied by CalculiX *BASE MOTION to every node with a homogeneous constraint on that DOF (add a fixed / pinned / zero-displacement constraint on the base faces first). random_response: spectrum = name of a define_vibration_spectrum ASD (g^2/Hz; single input, fully correlated). frequency_response: amplitudeG = harmonic amplitude in g (9.80665 m/s^2). Replaces any earlier base excitation of the case.

amplitudeG.description: frequency_response only: harmonic base acceleration amplitude in g (> 0).
