projection.description: Heaviside projection of the filtered density (filter.kind must be density): crisper 0/1 layouts, lower grey. Give {} for the defaults, values to override them, null to remove it.

beta.description: Final sharpness beta of the Heaviside projection, >= 1 (larger = crisper 0/1 layout). Default 16.

betaEvery.description: Iterations per continuation level: beta doubles after each level, or when the design converged at the current beta. Default 50.

betaStart.description: beta of the first continuation level, > 0 and <= beta. Default 1.

eta.description: Threshold density eta, in (0, 1). Default 0.5 (volume preserving).

protectLoadSupport.description: Keep the voxel layer at every load and support solid. Default true; false reproduces top88.

studyId.description: Id of the topology study (affected[0] of create_topology_study, e.g. ts-3.1).

threshold.description: Density at or above which a voxel counts as solid in the derived geometry, in (0, 1). Default 0.5.

name: set_topology_settings

description: Change an image underlay's display: `opacity` in [0, 1] and/or `locked` (a locked underlay is never picked in the viewport, so tracing over it cannot select it by accident).

id.description: Id of the image underlay.

locked.description: Lock (true) or unlock (false). Omit to keep.

opacity.description: Opacity in [0, 1] (0 = invisible, 1 = opaque). Omit to keep the current value.

name: set_underlay

description: Set the document unit of length and/or the display precision (decimal places). Affects how all geometry values are displayed and labelled. At least one of units or displayPrecision should be provided.

displayPrecision.description: Number of decimal places to show when formatting length values (e.g. 2 → "12.50 mm"). Must be an integer in [0, 20].

units.description: Unit of length for the document. Allowed values: 'mm' (millimetres), 'cm' (centimetres), 'm' (metres), 'in' (inches), 'ft' (feet).

name: set_units

description: Give walls a build-up (wall type), like Revit / ArchiCAD composite walls: layers listed from the right-hand face (looking from start to end — the exterior of a counter-clockwise perimeter) to the left-hand face, each { material, thickness, function: structure | insulation | membrane | air | finish }. Wall thickness becomes the sum; quantities are reported per layer material; plans show the layer lines; IFC gets a material layer set. layers: null removes the build-up.

thickness.description: Layer thickness in document units (> 0).

wallIds.description: Ids of existing straight walls (e.g. ["wall-1"]); curved walls are not accepted.

name: set_wall_layers

description: Sew nurbs_surface sheets together. (1) Exactly two sheets that share one whole boundary edge and `makeSolid` false (default): they become a single multi-span nurbs_surface; the edges must coincide within `tolerance` (document units), the sides, their orientation and the knot vectors are matched automatically, the joint is a C0 crease (check_continuity on the pair first if tangency matters). (2) `makeSolid` true, or three and more sheets: the sheets are meshed with identical boundary samples along shared edges and welded within `tolerance`; when the result has no free edge it becomes ONE closed, outward-oriented triangle-mesh solid (volume and mass_properties work; there is no exact B-rep, which needs the native kernel) and the summary / data give the volume. A single closed sheet (a sphere, a tube) can be sewn on its own (`ids` of 1 with makeSolid true) to close its seam. If free edges remain nothing changes and the refusal says how many and where: raise `tolerance`, or fill / blend the gap first. The inputs are removed and the result has position [0, 0, 0].

ids.description: 2 or more nurbs_surface ids (1 only with makeSolid true).

makeSolid.description: Sew into a closed mesh solid (default false for exactly two sheets; implied for three or more).

resolution.description: Solid only: mesh resolution, integer 8..96 (grid lines per sheet direction and boundary samples across the longest extent). Curved sheets lose volume as it drops (a sphere is 1.6 % low at 24, 0.4 % at 48). Default 24.

tolerance.description: Largest distance (document units) between matching edge poles / welded vertices. Default 1e-6 x the size of the surfaces.

name: sew_surfaces

description: Compute sheet-metal bend quantities for one bend with no part needed: bend allowance BA = theta*(R+K*T), outside setback OSSB = tan(theta/2)*(R+T), inside setback, bend deduction BD = 2*OSSB-BA (flat length = sum of mold-line legs - BD) and the AC 43.13-1B K-chart value tan(theta/2). All lengths are in `units` ('mm' or 'in', required). The angle is the angle bent THROUGH in degrees (a closed 45-degree angle is a 135-degree bend). Mode k_factor needs kFactor (never defaulted; refusal FTR_K_FACTOR_MISSING); mode faa_empirical uses BA = (0.01743*R+0.0078*T)*theta_deg. Other refusals: FTR_K_FACTOR_OUT_OF_RANGE, FTR_BEND_ANGLE_OUT_OF_RANGE (0 < angle < 180), FTR_PARAM_INVALID. Give material and temper to also return the minimum inside radius of a matching imported radius-table row (import_bend_radius_table). The result carries provenance (formulas, inputs, sources), unverified flags and reviewRequired. Next: create_sheet_metal_rule, then add_sheet_metal_base.

angle.description: Bend angle in degrees: the angle bent THROUGH (0 = flat, 90 = right angle, closed 45-degree angle = 135). Must satisfy 0 < angle < 180.

kFactor.description: K-factor (dimensionless, neutral-axis offset / T). Required in mode k_factor and never defaulted. ANSI 0 < K <= 0.5; DIN 0 < K <= 1 (DIN K = 2 x ANSI K).

kStandard.description: Convention of kFactor (dimensionless K): 'ansi' (default, reported as defaulted) or 'din' (converted to ANSI by halving).

material.description: Material label (e.g. 2024) used with temper to look up the minimum radius row; text, no unit.

mode.description: 'k_factor' (default) uses BA = theta*(R+K*T); 'faa_empirical' uses the FAA/EAA formula BA = (0.01743*R+0.0078*T)*theta_deg and ignores kFactor.

temper.description: Temper label (e.g. T3) used with material to look up the minimum radius row; text, no unit.

thickness.description: Sheet thickness T in `units`; must be > 0.

units.description: Unit of thickness, insideRadius and of every returned length: 'mm' or 'in'. Required.

name: sheet_metal_calc

description: Hollow an implicit FIELD into a wall of constant thickness (document units): inside keeps the wall within the surface, outside builds it around, centred straddles the surface. Never fails for thin features (unlike shell_solid). Exact on exact sources; otherwise warning IMP_OFFSET_NOT_EXACT. Combine with a lattice for infill (union of skin and lattice).

field.description: Id of the field to hollow.

name.description: Optional label for the result node.

side.description: Which side of the original surface the wall occupies. Default inside.

thickness.description: Wall thickness in document units (> 0): a number or a scalar field id (graded wall, create_scalar_field; its known range must stay > 0).

name: shell_field

description: Hollow out a closed 3D solid, leaving walls of the given thickness (grown inward), and replace it with a new mesh entity. The source entity is consumed. By default the result has a sealed internal cavity; pass openFacesNear (points on the faces to remove) for an open-topped shell. Requires a geometry kernel that supports shellSolid; a kernel without it (or a solid that is too thin for the thickness) makes this a graceful no-op that leaves the document unchanged. Target must be a 3D solid (box, cylinder, sphere, cone, torus, wedge, pyramid, extrusion, revolution or mesh).

id.description: Id of the closed 3D solid entity to hollow. Must exist and be a 3D solid.

openFacesNear.description: Faces to leave OPEN (removed), picked by location: each point removes the face nearest to it, giving an open-topped box / pocket instead of a sealed internal cavity. Omit or pass [] for a sealed cavity. Needs the OCC kernel.

items.description: A point [x, y, z] on or near the face to remove (e.g. its centre from inspect_topology).

thickness.description: Wall thickness in document units. Must be > 0 and smaller than half the solid's thinnest dimension.

name: shell_solid

description: Shock response spectrum (maximax, positive and negative absolute acceleration in the input unit, e.g. g) of a base acceleration pulse by the Smallwood ramp-invariant recursive filter. input.kind 'half_sine' { peakG, durationS } (sampled finely per frequency) or 'history' { timeS[], accelG[] } or { history: name of define_time_history with unit g }, uniformly sampled with dt <= 1/(10 fMax) (else DYN_SAMPLING_TOO_COARSE). Q (amplification, commonly 10) is required. Frequencies: frequenciesHz, or fMinHz..fMaxHz every 1/octaveFraction octave (default 6, i.e. 1/6 octave). A zero tail of 1.5 periods of each frequency captures the residual response.

Q.description: Amplification factor Q = 1 / (2 zeta) of the SDOF oscillators (> 0.5).

fMinHz.description: Lowest frequency in Hz (with fMaxHz, instead of frequenciesHz).

history.description: history: name of a define_time_history entry in g (instead of timeS / accelG).

kind.description: Pulse kind.

octaveFraction.description: Points per octave between fMinHz and fMaxHz; default 6.

name: shock_response_spectrum

description: Run the rigid-body physics of the mechanism (bodies, joints, gears, motors, propellers) forward in time with a real physics engine (MuJoCo) and report what happens: final speed of every joint (rpm), when it settled, engine torque and power, propeller thrust / torque / absorbed power, and measured gear ratios (a self-check). Gravity applies (set_gravity). Read-only. For kinematic poses of component instances without mass or forces (add_joint) use evaluate_motion instead; plot_simulation charts and render_motion animates the result of this run. detail "summary" (default) = numbers only; "series" adds per-sample time series (speeds, positions, torques, thrust, power) for plotting; `energy: true` adds the kinetic / potential / total / dissipated energy balance (J; automatic when a joint or add_spring has a spring) with the work put in by motors / governors / gas pressure (inputWorkJ), the work absorbed by propellers and balanceErrorJ (initial + input - dissipated - propellers - final, ~0), and data.springs (length range and force per add_spring); "poses" also adds every body's pose per sample (for playback). Warnings flag a run that has not settled. Typical: duration 10 s, timestep 0.001 s (use 0.0002 s for fast, light parts). Closed loops (slider-crank, four-bar): before integrating, the start pose is checked and a loop open by more than 1 µm is refused (FPR_LOOP_OPEN, nothing is run or snapped); with loops the default timestep is the "auto" rule min(1 ms, 0.5 deg of crank at the top speed) unless set_dynamics_solver or `timestep` says otherwise, and data.loops reports the largest constraint violation (metres), its tier (pass <= 1 µm, warn <= 10 µm = FPR_LOOP_DRIFT warn, reactions approximate; fail above, reactions unreliable) and the solver settings used. `reactions`: "off", "peaks" (default when the mechanism has loops) or "series": data.reactions gives, per tree joint, the force (N) and moment (N·m) on the child body at the joint anchor in world axes, and per loop closure the resultant force (N) on the child (no moment), each with peak magnitude, time and crank angle (the crank angle axis is the cycle angle of the first cylinder, or the joint named by `crankAxis`); along the axis of a driven joint the reported component includes the drive force itself. With cylinder pressures (add_cylinder_pressure) the sampling defaults to one sample per crank degree and data.engineReport gives, over the last full cycle: torque against crank angle per cylinder and total (detail series), mean torque (N·m), indicated power (kW), IMEP and peak pressure per cylinder, cycle-energy closure (gate 0.5 %, FPR_ENERGY_CLOSURE), speed ripple against the analytic ΔE/(I·ω²), and the peak wrist-pin, rod, side-thrust, crank-pin and main-bearing forces. Simulate at least one full cycle (two crank turns for a four-stroke) after the speed has settled. data.engineReport.realism (FR-FPR-70 / 71 / 73 / 76): with set_engine_losses, BRAKE torque and power (indicated minus friction), BMEP = IMEP - FMEP and mechanical efficiency (losses{}, with a governor-torque cross-check); per cylinder the reciprocating mass and primary / secondary inertia-force amplitudes against the gas peak (reciprocating[]); an accuracy{} statement for every scalar (band or null = "± ?", basis, origin input / calibrated / predicted / verification, validationLevel 0-4, warnings; a value at a speed the heat release was calibrated at is "calibrated", not validation evidence); plausibility[] (FPR_UNREALISTIC: peak-pressure angle and CA50 vs MBT, mechanical efficiency, Rotax-class propeller inertia / torque, reciprocating mass on the default density). A gear with efficiency (add_gear_coupling) loses (1 - efficiency) of its torque on the driven shaft; a propeller with a Ct / Cp table and airspeed follows J = V/(nD). Next: read data.loops.tier first, then data.engineReport and data.reactions.

crankAxis.description: Id of the revolute tree joint whose angle (deg, 0-360) labels the peaks of reactions; default none (time only).

energy.description: Add the energy balance: data.energy (kinetic, potential = gravity + joint springs relative to the start pose, total, energy dissipated by joint damping / friction, largest departure of the total from its initial value as a fraction of the peak energy) and, with detail "series", data.series.energy per sample. Also inputWorkJ (work of motors, speed governors and cylinder gas pressure), propellerWorkJ (absorbed by propellers) and balanceErrorJ = initial total + input - dissipated - propellers - final total (zero when every energy flow is counted). Default false, except true when a joint or an add_spring has a spring. A lossless mechanism keeps its total constant (conservation check); damping makes it decay by data.energy.dissipatedJ.

reactions.description: Joint / loop reaction forces: "off", "peaks" (default when the mechanism has loops), "series" (adds every sample).

sampleRate.description: Recorded samples per second. Default 50, raised for loop mechanisms to 36 per turn of the crank so periodic motion is not aliased; engines: one per crank degree. At most 6001 samples per run.

timestep.description: Integration step in seconds, at least 5e-6 (half of the smallest auto step, so a timestep-halving check can always run). Default 0.001 (loops or cylinders: the "auto" rule or the stored solver setting).

name: simulate_motion

description: Automatic pipe sizing: sets each pipe diameter to the smallest commercial size that carries its accumulated design flow at its current slope within `maxDepthRatio` (and `minVelocity` when given). Flows follow the modified rational method of check_drainage_network (entry times, travel times, optional `idf` curve, diverging manholes split by capacity share); sizing and velocities are iterated to convergence (max 10 passes). Only diameters change: inverts stay, so a larger outgoing pipe may end up with its crown above the incoming one - these manholes are reported as WARNING / data.crownWarnings (fix with update_drainage_pipe invertFrom for soffit matching). Pipes that fail even at the largest size, or have no downhill slope, are reported and left unchanged.

idf.description: Intensity-duration-frequency curve i = a / (t + b)^c (mm/h, t = time of concentration in minutes) replacing the constant intensity: each pipe uses i at its own Tc (modified rational method). Do not combine with `rainfallIntensityMmH`.

a.description: IDF coefficient a (> 0): i = a / (t + b)^c in mm/h.

b.description: IDF offset b in minutes (>= 0).

maxDepthRatio.description: Maximum flow depth / diameter, 0 to 1. Default 0.8.

minVelocity.description: Minimum velocity in m/s. Default: not enforced.

rainfallIntensityMmH.description: Constant design rainfall intensity in mm/h (> 0). Default 50. Do not combine with `idf`.

name: size_drainage_pipes

Use it to find the header at rack level before extract_pipes, or to draw sections.

cloudId.description: Id of an attached cloud (affected[0] of attach_point_cloud, e.g. "cloud-1.1").

fit.description: Primitives to fit in the slab (default none).

maxRadius.description: Largest circle radius in document units (default 2 m).

minRadius.description: Smallest circle radius in document units (default 5 mm).

noiseSigma.description: Scanner noise sigma in document units (inlier band 3 sigma; default 2.5 x the section spacing).

normal.description: [x, y, z] plane normal (any length > 0).

origin.description: [x, y, z] point on the cutting plane (document units).

kind.description: Every point of the cloud.
Axis-aligned box in document units.
Sphere around a seed point.

radius.description: Radius in document units, > 0.

kind.description: A crop box from set_scan_crop (keep "inside").

seed.description: RANSAC seed (default 1); same seed = same result (AF-13).

description: Slide an edge loop of a quad subdivision cage along the cage without changing its topology: `edges` ({ loopFrom: edge } or a list; an edge is an id "e:<idA>|<idB>" or [a, b] vertex indices) names any edge of the loop (it continues straight through valence-4 vertices, as select_cage_elements loopFrom shows). Every loop vertex moves along the edge that crosses the loop at it by |factor| of that edge's length: factor 0.5 halfway to the neighbour, 1 onto it. A positive factor slides towards the LEFT of the direction a -> b seen from outside the solid, a negative one towards the right. Use it to shift a loop cut sideways. A symmetric cage keeps its symmetry. Refuses a factor outside -1..1 or 0 (DIR_SLIDE_RANGE) and a loop with a vertex that has no face on the sliding side (DIR_SLIDE_LOOP_INVALID). Returns data { vertexCount, faceCount, vertices, vertexIds, faceIds, slid }. Next: edit_subdivision_cage, check_subdivision.

loopFrom.description: Any edge of the loop, directed first -> second vertex as written.

items.description: A cage edge: id "e:<vertexIdA>|<vertexIdB>" (stable) or a [vertexIndex, vertexIndex] pair.

edges.description: The loop to slide: { loopFrom: edge } or a list of edges (the loop through the FIRST one). An edge is an id "e:<idA>|<idB>" or [a, b] vertex indices.

factor.description: Fraction -1..1 of the rung edge length: positive = towards the left of a -> b seen from outside, negative = towards the right. Not 0.

id.description: Id of the subdivision solid.

name: slide_cage_edges

description: Smooth the vertices of a mesh (or the triangles of any 3D solid) with the umbrella operator, connectivity unchanged. method "taubin" (default) alternates a shrinking step lambda and an inflating step mu = 1 / (passBand - 1 / lambda) (Taubin 1995), which removes noise above the pass-band frequency without the shrinkage of plain "laplacian" smoothing (which loses about 1.8 % of the radius of a sphere in 10 iterations at lambda 0.6307). Taubin with the paper values still grows a clean sphere slightly (+0.12 % in 10 iterations), so volumeCorrection (default true for closed meshes) rescales about the volume centroid to the input volume. weights "uniform" (default) or "cotangent". Boundary vertices stay unless fixBoundary is false; `region` restricts smoothing to a sphere. Reports data.mu, volumeBefore / volumeAfter (document units^3), meanDisplacement and maxDisplacement (document units) and the symmetric deviation from the input. Refusals: MESH_ENTITY_NOT_FOUND, MESH_NOT_A_MESH, MESH_PARAM_INVALID.

fixBoundary.description: Keep boundary vertices of open meshes in place. Default true.

id.description: Id of the mesh (or other 3D solid) to smooth.

keepSource.description: true: keep the source and add the result as a new mesh. Default false: the source entity is rewritten in place (same id, name, layer, colour).

passBand.description: Taubin pass-band frequency kPB: 1 / lambda + 1 / mu. Must be below 1 / lambda. Default 0.1 (Taubin 1995: 0.01..0.1).

region.description: Only vertices inside this sphere are smoothed.

center.description: Centre [x, y, z] of the sphere (document units, world).

radius.description: Radius of the sphere (document units).

volumeCorrection.description: Rescale a closed result to the input volume. Default true.

weights.description: Neighbour weights: "uniform" (default) or "cotangent" (follows the triangle shapes).

name: smooth_mesh

description: Run the constraint solver (constructive pass on fixed points and dimension chains, then damped Levenberg-Marquardt) and update entity geometry so that all declared constraints are satisfied, keeping the branch the sketch already has. The solver works on the 2D XY plane (position Z is unchanged); lines, circles and arcs move by their own endpoints/centers/radii/angles, other entities by position. Returns in data: { residual, iterations, converged, dof, fullyConstrained, isFullyConstrained, skipped } where dof = unknowns minus rank of the constraint Jacobian over every line/arc/circle (a free line has 4), fullyConstrained lists the entity ids that no constraint leaves free to move, and skipped lists constraints that could not be evaluated (wrong entity kinds, unknown parameter). Non-convergent results are returned with the best-effort positions and converged:false. No parameters required.
name: solve_constraints

description: Split a 3D solid in two along a plane: the source is replaced by two mesh entities, the half on the normal side first, then the other. Works on every kernel with booleans (exact B-rep halves on the native kernel). Refused when the plane misses the solid.

id.description: Id of the 3D solid to split.

normal.description: Plane normal [x, y, z] (any length > 0).

origin.description: A point [x, y, z] on the plane.

name: split_body

description: Split faces of a 3D solid along a plane (the body stays one solid; each picked face crossing the plane becomes two faces, e.g. to draft or push-pull only part of a face). Pick faces by faceIndices, facesNear or faceNames. Exact B-rep only (native OCC kernel).

faceNames.description: Persistent face names (inspect_topology on the native kernel): recorded automatically from the first pick and used on regeneration; a name that is gone or split refuses the step (REF_LOST / REF_SPLIT).

facesNear.description: Faces picked by location: each point takes the face nearest to it.

items.description: A point [x, y, z] on the face (its nearest face is taken).

id.description: Id of the 3D solid.

plane.description: A plane by a point and its normal.

name: split_face

description: Divide the faces of a solid along curves lying on them (nurbs_curves made by wrap_to_face, project_to_face or create_curve_on_face on this solid): a closed curve cuts out a patch (faces + 1), an open one that runs from edge to edge divides the face in two. The volume does not change; the divided faces get new persistent names, so later commands (colour, draft, PMI, emboss_on_face) can address the patches. Each curve must lie on one face of the solid within `tolerance` (default 1e-5 x the solid diagonal, a named default): its samples are projected into the face parameters, fitted and checked back against the curve. Returns data { facesBefore, facesAfter, faces[{ index, name, area }] (the new faces; area in document units squared), volumeBefore, volumeAfter }. Refuses with WRP_SPLIT_CURVE_NOT_ON_FACE (the curve is no curve-on-face of this solid), WRP_SPLIT_FIT_FAILED, WRP_SPLIT_NO_EFFECT (the curves divide nothing, e.g. an open curve ending inside the face). Needs the exact (native) kernel. Next: inspect_faces, emboss_on_face, mass_properties.

curveIds.description: Ids of the nurbs_curve entities (with onFace) to divide along; each must lie on a face of this solid.

id.description: Id of the solid to divide.

tolerance.description: Largest distance a curve may lie from its face, and the fit tolerance of its face-parameter curve, document units. Default: 1e-5 x the solid diagonal (named default).

name: split_face_by_curves

description: Cut a composite ply with a dart or a splice so that each resulting piece is draped and flattened on its own (FR-CMP-42). The cut is a polyline in the part frame (`path`, chart coordinates as in add_ply polygons) or a line / polyline / nurbs_curve entity (`curveId`) projected on the tool face. A "splice" must cross the ply boundary at both ends and divides a piece in two; `overlap` (document length units, default 0) grows the piece on the LEFT of the path direction over the other one. A "dart" is a slit from the boundary toward the interior: it divides the ply when it meets another dart (e.g. several darts meeting at a pole cut a hemisphere ply into wedges) or runs boundary to boundary; a lone dart stays recorded as a slit and does not change the pieces. Each piece is draped from the ply seed (the piece bisector when the seed is a vertex of the piece). Run check_producibility afterwards. Several cuts accumulate on the ply.

curveId.description: Alternative to `path`: id of a line, polyline or nurbs_curve entity projected on the tool face.

kind.description: "dart" (slit from the boundary) or "splice" (cut across the ply).

overlap.description: Splice overlap, document length units, >= 0; the piece on the left of the path direction grows by this.

part.description: Part id or name; needed only when `ply` is a name.

path.description: Cut polyline in the part frame, at least 2 vertices (ends past the boundary are clipped).

items.description: A vertex [x, y] in the part frame (document units).

name: split_ply

description: Merge the consecutive feature history steps fromStepId..toStepId (inclusive) into ONE step, so a long run of small edits (dozens of cage drags, pole moves, nudges of one entity) becomes a single history entry that undoes, edits and replays as a unit. The merged step re-runs the same commands in the same order. It is refused unless replaying the new history gives exactly the current document, so squash steps that EDIT existing elements; steps that create entities or cage elements (add_*, extrude, loop cut...) mint ids from their step number and are refused. Suppressed steps in the range are refused. Returns the new step id in the summary. Next: edit_step_params on the merged step, replay_history.

fromStepId.description: Id of the first step to merge (from doc.featureHistory[*].id).

label.description: Optional human-readable label for the merged step.

toStepId.description: Id of the last step to merge; it must come after fromStepId.

name: squash_steps

description: Translate movingId so that its bounding-box minimum face along axis exactly meets the bounding-box maximum face of baseId. Default axis is "z" (+Z up, W5A convention). Use this to stack objects on top of each other without overlapping.

movingId.description: Id of the entity to move.

name: stack_on

description: Worst-case and RSS gap of a one-dimensional dimension chain at operating temperatures, every contributor expanding with its own CTE. Give contributors { name, nominal, upper, lower, sensitivity (+1 / -1), material (create_material name) or cte (explicit secant alpha with its reference temperature) } in document length units valid at specTemperature, specTemperature (NO default) and temperatures. D(T) = D_spec (1 + a_sec (T - T_spec)) is applied to the nominal and to both limits of each contributor; the gap is sum(sensitivity x dimension). Returns per temperature the mean gap, worst-case min/max, RSS sigma and range (half tolerance / sigmaPerHalfTolerance, default 3), the shift against specTemperature, each contributor's share, and with lowerSpecLimit / upperSpecLimit a status (within_worst_case, within_rss_only, outside) and code TMC_STACKUP_WC_EXCEEDED / TMC_STACKUP_OUT_OF_SPEC. Typed limits are unverified unless verified is true; every row needs review by a qualified engineer. Use it for gap, float or preload stack-ups of mixed materials; for a two-part hole/shaft fit use fit_at_temperature.

alpha.description: Secant CTE in 1/K, e.g. { value: 23e-6, unit: '1/K' }. 0 is allowed for a dimension that does not expand.

unit.description: Unit, e.g. 'degC', 'K', 'degF', '1/K'.

referenceTemperature.description: Temperature the secant CTE is referenced to (the datasheet statement).

unit.description: Unit, e.g. 'degC', 'K', 'degF', '1/K'.

source.description: Where the value comes from (recorded; it stays unverified without a material record).

lower.description: Lower deviation from nominal, document units, at specTemperature; must not exceed upper. Required unless pmiId is given.

material.description: create_material name whose thermalStrain / cte property model gives the CTE (cte models need cteBasis[material]).

name.description: Unique contributor name, e.g. "bore depth".

nominal.description: Nominal dimension in document length units at specTemperature (> 0). Required unless pmiId is given (then measured from the PMI item).

pmiId.description: Id of a 03 GDT size or location dimension (list_pmi): its measured nominal and tolerance become nominal / upper / lower (at specTemperature), and the contributor is verified unless verified: false.

sensitivity.description: Coefficient of this dimension in the gap: +1 (default) when growing it increases the gap, -1 when it decreases it. Any non-zero real.

upper.description: Upper deviation from nominal, document units, at specTemperature (e.g. +0.05). Required unless pmiId is given.

verified.description: true when the limits are confirmed against their source. Default true for a pmiId-linked contributor, false for typed limits (unverified).

kind.description: secant: alpha(T) is referenced to referenceTemperature; instantaneous: d(strain)/dT.

unit.description: Unit, e.g. 'degC', 'K', 'degF', '1/K'.

cteBasis.description: Basis of the cte model per material name (PHY-01 models carry no basis field).

sigmaPerHalfTolerance.description: Sigmas in a tolerance half-range for the RSS combination. Default 3 (named in the result).

specTemperature.description: REQUIRED, never defaulted: temperature the limits apply at, e.g. { value: 20, unit: "degC" }.

unit.description: Unit, e.g. 'degC', 'K', 'degF', '1/K'.

temperatures.description: Operating temperatures (every contributor at the same temperature), 1 to 50.

unit.description: Unit, e.g. 'degC', 'K', 'degF', '1/K'.

description: Stretch a 3D solid or mesh along an axis: inside the region the length is multiplied by factor (unitless, > 0; 1.5 lengthens by half, 0.5 halves); the part past region.end is translated rigidly, the part before region.start is unchanged, so features outside the region keep their shape. Volume grows by (factor - 1) times the volume inside the region. With preserveVolume true the whole body is stretched along the axis and shrunk across it by 1/sqrt(factor) so its volume is unchanged (no region allowed). The frame and region default from the body (axis = longest direction, region = the whole body). region.start and region.end are document units from the frame origin, which defaults to the body centre (so a 100-long body spans -50..50 by default). The result replaces the entity as a mesh entity that keeps the construction (brep recipe). Refuses factor <= 0 (DEF_STRETCH_FACTOR) and factor 1 (DEF_NO_EFFECT). Then call analyze_deformation and check_deformation.

factor.description: Length multiplier inside the region, unitless, > 0 (1 = no change).

frame.description: Stretch frame; every field defaults from the body bounds and the defaults used are reported in data.frame.

axis.description: Stretch direction, unitless (normalised). Default: the longest bounding-box direction.

origin.description: Frame origin, a world point in document units. Default: the body bounding-box centre.

reference.description: Direction giving the frame x axis, unitless; must not be parallel to axis. Default: the next longest direction.

id.description: Id of the 3D solid or mesh entity to deform (describe_scene lists ids). It is replaced by the deformed mesh entity (keepSource keeps it).

ids.description: Ids of several 3D solids or meshes to deform with the same parameters (one feature step; every body gets its own frame and region defaults from its own bounds). Use this or id.

keepSource.description: true: keep the original entity(ies) next to the deformed one(s) instead of replacing them. Default false.

output.description: How the result is computed: kernel choice and mesh tolerance.

mode.description: "auto" (default): the exact kernel builds the result when it can evaluate this deformation (the native kernel does for every law: the faces become B-splines fitted within output.tolerance), else the mesh path runs and the summary says so; "exact": refuse (DEF_EXACT_UNAVAILABLE) unless the exact kernel built it; "mesh": force the faceted mesh path.

preserveAnalytic.description: Recognise cylinders, cones and planes in an exact result (needs the exact warp of a later milestone; true is refused today).

tolerance.description: Largest deviation of the result from the true deformed surface, document units, > 0: the chordal deviation of the mesh path, or the fit error of the B-spline faces and edges on the exact path (a smaller value costs control points, not accuracy). Default: 1e-5 times the body bounding-box diagonal, clamped to [1e-6, 0.01].

preserveVolume.description: true: stretch the whole body along the axis by factor and scale it across by 1/sqrt(factor) (volume unchanged); not allowed with region.

region.description: Part of the body along the axis that is stretched (a step: full stretch inside, none outside). Default: the whole body.

end.description: Region end along the axis, document units from the frame origin; must exceed start. Default: where the body ends.

start.description: Region start along the axis, document units from the frame origin. Default: where the body starts.

name: stretch_body

description: Refine a mesh (or the triangles of any 3D solid) so later operations have enough resolution. method "midpoint" splits every triangle into 4 at the edge midpoints and keeps the geometry exactly (area and volume unchanged); "loop" is Loop subdivision (4x the faces, the surface relaxes toward a smooth limit and a convex shape shrinks slightly); "smooth" (Manifold engine) refines toward a curved tangent surface, keeping creases sharper than featureAngleDeg, until edges are shorter than maxEdgeLength or `levels` is reached. Faces x 4 per level for midpoint / loop. Reports faces before / after, area and volume (document units). Refusals: MESH_ENTITY_NOT_FOUND, MESH_NOT_A_MESH, MESH_PARAM_INVALID, MESH_ENGINE_UNSUPPORTED, MESH_NON_MANIFOLD.

featureAngleDeg.description: method "smooth" only: dihedral angles above this stay sharp, in degrees. Default 30.

id.description: Id of the mesh (or other 3D solid) to subdivide.

keepSource.description: true: keep the source and add the result as a new mesh. Default false: the source is rewritten in place.

maxEdgeLength.description: method "smooth" only: refine until no edge is longer than this (document units). Default: use `levels`.

name: subdivide_mesh

description: Convert a subdivision solid to exact NURBS geometry for STEP, CAM and booleans. output "sheets" (default, no kernel needed): one bicubic nurbs_surface per patch of the once-refined cage (`faces` "unpacked") or one B-spline surface per maximal block of regular quads (`faces` "packed", fewer entities); regular quads are the exact Catmull-Clark limit surface, quads next to extraordinary vertices are geometry patches that meet G0 (no gaps) with a measured tangent break, which `extraordinary` "G1" reduces below `tangentToleranceDeg` by refining the cage further (more, smaller patches). output "solid": one exact B-rep solid (patches sewn by the native kernel; needs it, always the G0 patches). The SubD is removed unless `keep`. Returns data { patchCount, sheets[] or solid, maxDeviation (document units, from the limit surface at `samples` x `samples` points per patch), evEdges[] { patches, valence, g0, g1Deg }, maxEvG0, maxEvG1Deg, starPoints[] (extraordinary vertices and n-gon faces) }. Refuses a zero-area face (DIR_CONVERT_DEGENERATE) and a solid without the exact kernel (DIR_CONVERT_KERNEL). Next: sew_surfaces, export_step_ap242, check_surface_quality.

extraordinary.description: Treatment of patches around extraordinary vertices: "G0" (default, geometry patches) or "G1" (refine further until the tangent break is below tangentToleranceDeg; sheets only).

faces.description: sheets: "unpacked" (default) = one patch per refined quad; "packed" = one surface per maximal block of regular quads.

id.description: Id of the subdivision solid.

keep.description: true: keep the subdivision solid next to the result. Default false (it is replaced).

output.description: "sheets": nurbs_surface entities (default). "solid": one exact B-rep solid (needs the native kernel).

samples.description: Deviation samples per patch side (a samples x samples grid per patch), 1..16, default 2.

tangentToleranceDeg.description: extraordinary "G1": largest accepted normal angle in degrees along the edges next to an extraordinary vertex (default 0.5); the cage is refined until met.

name: subdivision_to_nurbs

description: Submit the current in_work revision for review: checkpoints it when dirty, moves it to in_review and freezes the definition. Refused while parameters have unresolved errors, or (policy.requireMarking) while the export marking is undetermined. Next: humans approve (record_approval), then release_item. An agent may do this step.

at.description: When the act happened: ISO-8601 UTC, e.g. 2026-11-02T09:30:00Z. The host (UI / llull CLI) fills it; commands never read a clock.

by.description: User id doing the act (the host fills it from the authenticated user; an agent cannot override it where the server has named users).

name: submit_for_review

description: Closed 2D loops that outline the optimized layout of a solved topology study, ready for the rebuild: model the outer loop with extrude_profile (profile = its points, depth = thickness, position / rotation from `placement`), each hole loop with extrude_profile + boolean subtract, round sharp re-entrant corners with fillet_edge, analyse the rebuilt part (05), then compare_to_topology. A 2D study uses its own plane; for a 3D study give `plane` (XY | XZ | YZ) and `offset`, the coordinate of the section along the plane normal (default the middle of the grid). Loops are in document units; `tolerance` (default one voxel) is the largest deviation of the simplification, `minLoopArea` (default 4 voxel^2, document units^2) drops specks (counted in droppedLoops). widthSamples lists member widths on the medial axis of the section: { at: plane-local [x, y], width (document units), widthMm }, widest first, from an exact distance transform. The loops are a suggestion from a concept result, to be reviewed.

minLoopArea.description: Loops with a smaller area are dropped, document units squared, >= 0. Default 4 voxel^2.

offset.description: 3D only: coordinate of the section plane along its normal, document units. Default the middle of the grid.

plane.description: Section plane of a 3D study (default XY). A 2D study uses its own plane.

studyId.description: Id of the topology study (affected[0] of create_topology_study, e.g. ts-3.1).

tolerance.description: Largest deviation of the simplified loops from the field contour, document units, > 0. Default one voxel.

name: suggest_rebuild

description: Spot elevations and slopes of a terrain surface at plan points. data.points lists { at, elevation (document units, null outside the TIN), slopePercent }.

points.description: Plan points to sample.

items.description: Plan point [x, y].

name: surface_elevation

description: Create a freeform shell part from boundary curves — hoods, fairings, fenders, panels, saddle tops, aero covers. Give 4 curves that close a loop (any order or direction; ends must meet) for a Coons patch spanning them, or 2 opposite curves for a surface ruled between them. Curves are `curves` (each 2+ world points; 3+ points pass a smooth curve through them) or `curveIds` (2D sketch curves — line, arc, polyline, spline — each in its own plane). The surface is thickened by `thickness` behind its front side (flip: in front) into a closed solid with a sharp rim, stored as a subdivision solid: reshape it with edit_subdivision_cage; with the OCC kernel it is an exact B-spline solid (STEP). The smooth surface follows the curves within the smoothing of a `cells` grid (more cells = closer). Returns data { vertexCount, faceCount, vertices }.

cells.description: Cage cells [along the first curve, across] (1..24 each; default [8, 8]).

color.description: Hex color string #rrggbb, e.g. "#c8553d". Defaults to "#6b8f9c".

curveIds.description: 2 or 4 ids of 2D sketch curves bounding the patch (alternative to curves).

curves.description: 2 or 4 boundary curves as world point lists (alternative to curveIds).

items.description: Curve point [x, y, z] in world coordinates.

id.description: Optional explicit entity id. If omitted a unique id is generated.

layerId.description: Layer id to assign the entity to. Defaults to the document default layer.

levels.description: Subdivision levels 0..4 (0 = the faceted cage itself; 2-3 is smooth; each level quadruples the face count).

name.description: Optional display name for the entity (shown in the scene tree).

thickness.description: Wall thickness in document units (> 0).

description: Create a NURBS surface sheet that passes exactly through a grid of points (global bicubic interpolation by default). `grid[i][j]` are points with i along u (outer array) and j along v, all rows the same length, at least degree + 1 in each direction; neighbouring points must be distinct. `degreeU` / `degreeV` default 3 (lowered automatically when the grid is smaller; 1..5). `mode` "interpolate" (default) fits the surface through the points; "control_net" uses the points as the control net instead (the surface then approximates them). Approximation to a tolerance is not available. Returns the surface id and the interpolation residual (round-off level). Next: analyze_surface_curvature, measure_deviation.

color.description: Hex color string #rrggbb, e.g. "#c8553d". Defaults to "#9fb4c7".

degreeU.description: Degree along u, integer 1..5. Default 3 (capped by the number of rows - 1).

degreeV.description: Degree along v, integer 1..5. Default 3 (capped by the number of columns - 1).

grid.description: Point grid grid[i][j], i along u, j along v; at most 200 x 200.

items.description: Point [x, y, z] in document units, relative to `position`.

layerId.description: Layer id to assign the entity to. Defaults to the document default layer.

mode.description: "interpolate" (default): pass through the points. "control_net": use them as poles.

name.description: Optional display name for the entity (shown in the scene tree).

position.description: Origin [x, y, z] of the surface in document units; the poles are relative to it. Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

name: surface_report

description: Sweep a closed cross-section along a 3D path into a solid: pipes, tubes, hoses, handrails, ducts, cable runs, coils. Right-handed world frame, +Z up. Path: either `path`, world [x, y, z] points — joined by straight runs whose corners are rounded with circular bends of bendRadius (pipe elbows), or with smooth: true a smooth spline through the points — or `pathId`, a 2D sketch curve (line, arc, polyline, spline, circle, ellipse, rectangle) placed by its work plane. Paths may be open or closed loops (closed: true, or a closed sketch); a loop has no end caps. Section (exactly one): `radius` for a round tube (+ innerRadius for a hollow pipe), `section` as [x, y] polygon points, or `sectionId` of a closed 2D sketch (circle, ellipse, rectangle, closed polyline/spline). The section is centred on the path; its +y axis points toward world +Z (toward +Y when the path starts vertical) and it is carried along with a rotation-minimizing (twist-free) frame. Paths, bends and sketched sections stay exact for the exact kernel and STEP export. Laws over the path arc-length fraction t (0..1): `twist` (radians; or `twistTurns`), `scale` or `area` (exclusive; area is the section area in document units squared), `stretch` {x, y}, and for stations `stationBlend` (smooth | linear). Volume of a section centred on the path is the integral of its area along the path whatever the twist. `orientation`: minimal (default, for pipes and anything round), fixed (the section keeps its plane, normal = direction, default +Z; extrusion-like oblique sweeps), frenet (curvature normal; only on paths that bend everywhere), binormal (section y follows `direction`). Rails: `guideIds` (1 or 2 nurbs_curves) pull the section onto the rails at every station: `anchors` are the section points that follow each rail (default: the outline points nearest the rails at the start), `guideMode` scale | orient | stretch, `maintainHeight` for two rails; two rails without a path use their midline as the spine (handles, grips, tapered hoses). `orientation` surface (+ `surfaceId`) keeps the section y axis along the sheet normal (bands and ribs standing on a surface). Refusals carry stable SWG_* codes (SWG_LAW_NONPOSITIVE, SWG_CLOSED_TWIST_NOT_PERIODIC on a closed path whose total twist is not a whole number of turns, SWG_FRAME_DEGENERATE, SWG_SELF_INTERSECTION_LOCAL). Next: inspect_sweep for the frames, check_sweep_loft for the checks, mass_properties for the volume. Booleans with other solids work like any primitive (e.g. boolean op union to weld pipes to a flange).

anchors.description: One [x, y] point per rail in section coordinates (the section point the rail passes through). Default: the section outline point nearest each rail at the path start, which must lie within railTolerance of the rail.

area.description: Section area (> 0, document units squared; the section scales by sqrt(area / start area)). A law over t in [0, 1] (the arc-length fraction along the path): { type: "linear", start, end } | "s_curve" (smoothstep) | "constant" { value } | "table" { points } | "expression" { expression }.

end.description: linear / s_curve: value at the path end (t = 1).

endSlope.description: table: optional derivative at t = 1 (default: a shape-preserving one-sided estimate from the last points).

expression.description: expression: formula of t (0..1 along the path), s (arc length from the start) and L (path length); radians, e.g. "1 + 0.25*sin(2*pi*t)".

points.description: table: [t, value] pairs (t a fraction of the path 0..1, or arc length in document units with lawParameter arc_length; value in the unit of the law (radians for twist, a factor for scale)), t strictly increasing from 0 to the end; a smooth shape-preserving cubic (no overshoot) passes through them.

start.description: linear / s_curve: value at the path start (t = 0).

startSlope.description: table: optional derivative at t = 0 (default: a shape-preserving one-sided estimate from the first points).

type.description: Law kind: constant, linear, s_curve (smoothstep), table or expression.

value.description: constant: the value, in the unit of the law (radians for twist, a factor for scale).

bendRadius.description: Centre-line radius of the bend at each corner of a straight-run path, in document units. Default: 3 × the section radius (a long-radius elbow). Must exceed the section radius.

closed.description: With path points: also join the last point back to the first, making a closed loop (rings, chains, tyre treads, gaskets); the closing corner is bent or smoothed like the others. A closed sketch pathId (circle, ellipse, closed spline/polyline, rectangle) is a loop already.

color.description: Hex color string #rrggbb, e.g. "#c8553d". Defaults to "#6b8f9c".

corners.description: Corners of a `path` of points: round (default) joins the straight runs with circular bends of bendRadius; miter keeps them sharp, the section ring lying in the bisector plane of each joint (square-cut duct and frame corners, volume A x total length). Mitre needs an open path of straight runs, turns below 150 degrees, legs longer than the section reach; not with smooth.

fitTolerance.description: Largest distance (document units, > 0) between the exact fitted faces and the sweep evaluator. Default 1e-7 x the model size (at least 1e-9). Checked now: a tolerance the fit cannot reach is refused with SWG_FIT_TOLERANCE.

guideIds.description: 1 or 2 rail curve ids (nurbs_curve). At every path station the section is pulled so its anchor points lie on the points where each rail crosses the section plane. With two rails and no path/pathId the spine is the midline of the rails (coupled by arc length). Not combined with twist / scale / area / stretch laws or stations.

guideMode.description: What the rails drive: scale (default: uniform scale + rotation; with two rails also placement), orient (rotation only, the section keeps its size), stretch (scale only along the anchor direction).

id.description: Optional explicit entity id. If omitted a unique id is generated.

innerRadius.description: Round section only: bore radius for a hollow pipe (0 < innerRadius < radius).

lawParameter.description: What t of a `table` law is: fraction (default) = the arc-length fraction 0..1, or arc_length = the arc length in document units (the table must run from 0 to the path length). Linear / s_curve / constant laws and expressions are unaffected (expressions already see s and L).

layerId.description: Layer id to assign the entity to. Defaults to the document default layer.

maintainHeight.description: Two rails: keep the section height and stretch it only along the line between the two anchors (elliptic sections from a circle). Default false.

path.description: World-space [x, y, z] points the section follows (>= 2). Without smooth, consecutive points are joined by straight runs and every corner gets a circular bend of bendRadius.

name: sweep_profile

description: Sweep an open or closed section CURVE along a path into a NURBS surface sheet (no caps): helicoids, ribbons, fins, hull skins, bands standing on a surface. Same path, laws, frames and rails as sweep_profile, but the section is a curve: `section` { line: [[x,y],[x,y]] } or { points: [[x,y], ...] } (section coordinates: x along the frame normal, y along the binormal, centred on the path), or `sectionId` of a nurbs_curve lying in its XY plane (rational conics stay exact). Path: `path` world points (straight runs with bends of bendRadius, or smooth: true), `pathId` (curve), or two rails `guideIds` whose midline is the spine. Laws over the arc-length fraction: twist (radians) / twistTurns, scale, stretch {x, y}; `orientation` minimal | frenet | fixed | binormal | axis_plane | surface (+ surfaceId: the section y axis follows that sheet's normal). Rails (`guideIds`, `anchors`, `guideMode`, `maintainHeight`) pull the section anchors onto the rails at every station: with two helical rails and a diameter section this is a helicoid. flip.description: surface only: true puts the section y axis on the opposite side of the sheet (against its normal). Default false.

mode.description: minimal (default): twist-free frame, for pipes and anything round; frenet: section follows the curvature normal, only on paths that bend everywhere; fixed: the section keeps its plane (normal = direction), oblique to the path; binormal: the section y axis tracks `direction`; axis_plane: the section lies in the plane through an axis (threads, springs and screws with a non-round section: x = radial, y = along the axis); surface: the section y axis follows the normal (S_u x S_v) of the sheet `surfaceId` at the foot of the path point (a band standing on a surface, a rib along a hull).

path.description: World-space [x, y, z] path points (>= 2), straight runs with circular bends of bendRadius. Alternative to pathId / two rails.

start.description: linear / s_curve: value at the path start (t = 0).

twist.description: Rotation of the section about the path tangent, in radians. A law over t in [0, 1] (the arc-length fraction along the path): { type: "linear", start, end } | "s_curve" (smoothstep) | "constant" { value } | "table" { points } | "expression" { expression }.

name: sweep_surface

description: Taper a 3D solid or mesh along an axis: each cross-section is scaled about the axis by 1 + (scaleEnd - 1) times a ramp that goes from 0 at region.start to 1 at region.end; past the end the body keeps scale scaleEnd. scaleEnd is unitless and > 0 (0.5 halves the end section, 2 doubles it). With flat true only the frame x direction is scaled (a wedge-like taper). Use it for tapered handles, pins, nozzles, columns. The frame, region and tolerance default from the body (axis = longest direction, region = the whole body, falloff "smooth"); the defaults used are reported in data.frame. The result replaces the entity as a mesh entity that keeps the construction (brep recipe). Refuses scaleEnd <= 0 (DEF_TAPER_DEGENERATE) and scaleEnd 1 (DEF_NO_EFFECT). Then call analyze_deformation and check_deformation.

flat.description: true: scale only along the frame x direction (flat taper); default false scales x and y.

frame.description: Deformation frame: local z = axis, x = reference projected perpendicular to the axis, y = z cross x; regions and radii are measured from the origin along it. Every field is optional and defaults from the body bounds; the defaults used are reported in data.frame.defaulted.

axis.description: Deformation axis, any non-zero direction (unitless; normalised). Default: the longest bounding-box direction (a world axis, ties: x before y before z).

origin.description: Frame origin, a world point in document units. Default: the body bounding-box centre (the bend uses the centre of the face at the start of the body).

reference.description: Direction giving the frame x axis, unitless: its component perpendicular to the axis is used; it must not be parallel to the axis. Default: the next longest bounding-box direction.

id.description: Id of the 3D solid or mesh entity to deform (describe_scene lists ids). It is replaced by the deformed mesh entity (keepSource keeps it).

ids.description: Ids of several 3D solids or meshes to deform with the same parameters (one feature step; every body gets its own frame and region defaults from its own bounds). Use this or id.

keepSource.description: true: keep the original entity(ies) next to the deformed one(s) instead of replacing them. Default false.

output.description: How the result is computed: kernel choice and mesh tolerance.

mode.description: "auto" (default): the exact kernel builds the result when it can evaluate this deformation (the native kernel does for every law: the faces become B-splines fitted within output.tolerance), else the mesh path runs and the summary says so; "exact": refuse (DEF_EXACT_UNAVAILABLE) unless the exact kernel built it; "mesh": force the faceted mesh path.

preserveAnalytic.description: Recognise cylinders, cones and planes in an exact result (needs the exact warp of a later milestone; true is refused today).

tolerance.description: Largest deviation of the result from the true deformed surface, document units, > 0: the chordal deviation of the mesh path, or the fit error of the B-spline faces and edges on the exact path (a smaller value costs control points, not accuracy). Default: 1e-5 times the body bounding-box diagonal, clamped to [1e-6, 0.01].

region.description: Part of the body along the frame axis where the effect ramps in. Past the end the body follows rigidly (carries the end transform); before the start it is unchanged. Default: the whole body.

end.description: Region end along the frame axis, document units from the frame origin; must exceed start. Default: where the body ends.

falloff.description: How the effect ramps from none at start to full at end: "smooth" (default, 3t^2 - 2t^3, no crease at the region ends) or "linear" (straight ramp; leaves a visible crease at both ends).

start.description: Region start along the frame axis, document units from the frame origin (may be negative). Default: where the body starts.

scaleEnd.description: Section scale reached at region.end, unitless, > 0 (1 = no change).

description: Outline of a text entity that has a font (add_text with font=...): the closed glyph loops that extrude_profile and emboss_on_face use. Returns `data` with loops (every contour), outerLoops, holes, area (document units squared, exact), outlineLength, advanceWidth (widest line, document units), bbox in the text plane relative to the text position, font {family, sha256}, `unverified` (the font bytes are not pinned), and provenance. Lengths follow the document unit (lengthUnit in the result). `output: "glyphs"` adds per-character topology (contours, holes, area in font units squared) paged by `offset` / `limit`; `output: "loops"` adds each region as flattened polylines (at most 2000 points per loop). `kerning: false` ignores the font kern pairs (advance widths only). Next: emboss_on_face, extrude_profile, wrap_to_face. Unmapped characters are listed in data.missingCharacters and the summary (WRP_GLYPH_MISSING, a warning). Refusals carry error.code WRP_TEXT_NO_FONT, WRP_ENTITY_NOT_FOUND.

id.description: Id of a text entity created with a font (add_text font=...).

kerning.description: Apply the font kern pairs. Default: the text entity setting (true).

limit.description: Most glyph records returned with output "glyphs". Default 200.

offset.description: First glyph record returned with output "glyphs". Default 0.

output.description: summary (default): totals only; glyphs: also one record per character; loops: also the region polylines.

name: text_outline

description: Evaluate a textbook closed-form heat-transfer solution, used as the reference a thermal model must reproduce. Pure and read-only. check: plane_wall (flux q in W/m^2, surface temperatures, heat-balance residual), slab_generation (centre temperature), semi_infinite (erf profile after a surface step), lumped (any body via V and As, or sphere d; returns validity { Bi, ok } with Bi < 0.1), fin (efficiency; with Tb and Tinf also heat rate Q adiabatic / convective-tip / corrected-length and tip temperature), parallel_plates (grey infinite plates, W/m^2), view_factor (needs configuration), stefan (Neumann one-phase melting: root lambda, front position, Stefan number), stefan_boltzmann (sigma from the exact SI constants, no inputs), interface (two slabs with a contact conductance). inputs maps each input name (names marked ? are optional) to { value, unit }; dimensionless inputs use unit "1". Inputs per check: plane_wall: L (wall thickness; length), k (thermal conductivity; conductivity), h1 (film coefficient on face 1; film), Tinf1 (fluid temperature on face 1; temperature), h2 (film coefficient on face 2; film), Tinf2 (fluid temperature on face 2; temperature) · slab_generation: half_thickness (half thickness of the slab; length), k (thermal conductivity; conductivity), qgen (volumetric heat generation (positive = source); generation), Ts (face temperature; temperature) · semi_infinite: Ti (initial uniform temperature; temperature), Ts (surface temperature applied at t = 0; temperature), alpha (thermal diffusivity k/(rho cp); diffusivity), x (depth below the surface; length), t (time since the step; time) · lumped: V? (body volume (with As: any shape); volume), As? (convecting surface area (with V); area), d? (sphere diameter (shorthand for V and As of a sphere; give V and As or d); length), rho (density; density), c (specific heat; specificHeat), k (thermal conductivity; conductivity), h (film coefficient; film), Ti (initial temperature; temperature), Tinf (fluid temperature; temperature), t (time; time) · fin: h (film coefficient; film), k (thermal conductivity; conductivity), d? (pin diameter (gives P = pi d, A = pi d^2/4; or give P and A); length), P? (section perimeter (with A, for any uniform section); length), A? (section cross-sectional area (with P); area), L (fin length; length), Tb? (base temperature (with Tinf: adds heat rates and tip temperatures); temperature), Tinf? (fluid temperature (with Tb); temperature) · parallel_plates: T1 (temperature of plate 1 (degC or K; converted to absolute); temperature), T2 (temperature of plate 2; temperature), eps1 (emissivity of plate 1, 0 < eps <= 1 (unit "1"); ratio), eps2 (emissivity of plate 2, 0 < eps <= 1 (unit "1"); ratio) · view_factor / parallel_rectangles: a (rectangle side a; length), b (rectangle side b; length), c (spacing between the identical, directly opposed rectangles; length) · view_factor / perpendicular_rectangles: l (length of the common edge; length), w (width of surface 1 (normal to the common edge); length), h (height of surface 2 (normal to the common edge); length) · view_factor / coaxial_discs: r1 (radius of disc 1; length), r2 (radius of disc 2; length), L (distance between the coaxial parallel discs; length) · view_factor / cube_summation: a (cube side; length) · stefan: k (conductivity of the liquid; conductivity), rho (density; density), cp (specific heat of the liquid; specificHeat), latent (latent heat of fusion; latentHeat), dT (wall temperature minus melting temperature (unit K); temperatureDifference), t (time since the wall was raised; time) · stefan_boltzmann: no inputs · interface: L1 (thickness of slab 1; length), k1 (conductivity of slab 1; conductivity), hc (interface (gap) conductance; film), L2 (thickness of slab 2; length), k2 (conductivity of slab 2; conductivity), T_hot (outer face temperature of slab 1; temperature), T_cold (outer face temperature of slab 2; temperature). Returns data { value, unit, outputs{name:{value,unit}}, formula, inputs, validity?, physicalConstants? }; temperature results use the unit of the first temperature input; radiation checks report sigma and absolute zero as named defaults. unitSystem (N-m-kg-s, N-mm-t-s, lbf-in-slinch-s) adds data.deckValue: the primary result expressed for a CalculiX deck in that system. Refuses a wrong dimension (THM_UNITS_MISMATCH), emissivity outside (0, 1] (THM_EMISSIVITY_INVALID), film coefficient <= 0 (THM_FILM_INVALID) or other non-physical inputs (THM_INPUT_INVALID). Next: compare a solved model against value with compare_to_expected.

configuration.description: Required when check is view_factor: parallel_rectangles (a, b, c), perpendicular_rectangles (l, w, h), coaxial_discs (r1, r2, L) or cube_summation (a).

unit.description: Unit, e.g. 'W/(m*K)', 'mm', 'degC', '1'.

inputs.description: Input name -> { value, unit }. Names per check are listed in the tool description.

unitSystem.description: Optional FEA unit system: adds data.deckValue, the primary result converted to it (not for temperatures).

description: Report the distortion of a solved analysis (typically thermo_static): for each face, the flatness (max - min signed distance of its nodes to their least-squares plane) before and after the displacement and the change, optionally against a flatness tolerance; for each named point, the displacement of the nearest node. A face is a mesh node set (targetKey of an existing constraint / load / probe target) or the nodes of a solid lying on a plane (onPlane). Lengths are in document units. Reads the stored results artifact; refused when the results are stale or missing. reviewRequired is always true: it is an engineering number for a qualified reviewer, not a drawing verdict.

analysisId.description: Id of the analysis (affected[0] of create_analysis, e.g. an-1.1).

name.description: Name of the face in the report, e.g. "mounting face".

onPlane.description: Alternative to targetKey: the nodes of an entity lying on a plane.

distance.description: Select nodes whose distance to the plane is <= this value, in document units (> 0, e.g. 1e-3).

entityId.description: Id of the analysed solid whose mesh nodes are selected.

normal.description: Face normal [x, y, z] (need not be unit length).

point.description: A point [x, y, z] in document units on the face plane.

targetKey.description: Key of a mesh node set: C_<constraintId>, L_<loadId>, P_<probeId> ... of a target already in the analysis (use its face as the face).

tolerance.description: Flatness tolerance in document units; when given, the report states whether the deformed face is within it.

points.description: Points whose displacement to report (nearest mesh node).

name.description: Name of the point.

point.description: Location [x, y, z] in document units (undeformed).

description: Closed-form thermo-mechanical hand calculations with units, for sanity checks and benchmarks (no FE). `check` selects the formula and `inputs` is a record of { value, unit } (any unit of the right dimension; temperature DIFFERENCES in K or degC). restrained: E (MPa: Young's modulus); alpha (1/K: secant CTE); dT (K: temperature rise from the stress-free state); nu (1: Poisson's ratio, in (-1, 0.5)) -> uniaxial, biaxial, triaxial stress in MPa. inclusion: E (MPa: Young's modulus); alpha (1/K: CTE of the inclusion minus CTE of the matrix); dT (K: temperature rise of the inclusion); a (mm: inclusion radius); r? (mm: radius of the outside point (>= a); default a (just outside the disc)) -> stresses inside and outside a hot disc in an infinite plate (NAFEMS T1). bimetal: t1 (mm: thickness of layer 1 (low expansion)); t2 (mm: thickness of layer 2 (high expansion)); E1 (MPa: Young's modulus of layer 1); E2 (MPa: Young's modulus of layer 2); alpha1 (1/K: CTE of layer 1); alpha2 (1/K: CTE of layer 2); dT (K: uniform temperature rise); L? (mm: cantilever length for the tip deflection) -> Timoshenko curvature (1/mm) with an equilibrium cross-check. thick_cylinder: E (MPa: Young's modulus); nu (1: Poisson's ratio, in (-1, 0.5)); alpha (1/K: secant CTE); a (mm: bore radius); b (mm: outer radius (> a)); dT (K: bore minus outer-surface temperature; T(r) = dT ln(b/r)/ln(b/a)); r? (mm: one radius in [a, b]; or use points; default both a and b); optional `points` = radii -> radial/hoop/axial stress rows in MPa. gradient_beam: alpha (1/K: secant CTE); dT (K: temperature difference between the two faces); h (mm: beam depth); L (mm: span (simply supported) or length (cantilever)) -> curvature, mid-span bow, cantilever tip; stress 0. shrink_fit: b (mm: solid shaft radius); c (mm: hub outer radius (> b)); E_hub (MPa: hub Young's modulus); nu_hub (1: hub Poisson's ratio); E_shaft (MPa: shaft Young's modulus); nu_shaft (1: shaft Poisson's ratio); interferenceMax (mm: maximum DIAMETRAL interference at the specification temperature); interferenceMin? (mm: minimum diametral interference at the specification temperature); alpha_hub? (1/K: hub secant CTE (with alpha_shaft, temperature, specTemperature)); alpha_shaft? (1/K: shaft secant CTE); temperature? (K: operating temperature (both parts)); specTemperature? (K: temperature the interferences apply at) -> Lame contact pressure and hub bore hoop stress (MPa); the thermal group adds the interference at temperature. cte_secant: referenceTemperature (K: stress-free temperature the secant CTE is referenced to); alpha0? (1/K: linear law: instantaneous CTE at lawTemperature); alpha1? (1/K^2: linear law: d(alpha)/dT); lawTemperature? (K: linear law: temperature alpha0 is given at); rereferenceTo? (K: also report the secant re-referenced to this temperature), plus `points` = temperatures, and either alpha0/alpha1/lawTemperature or `table` = instantaneous [{T, alpha}] rows -> instantaneous and secant CTE, thermal strain and optional re-referencing. Returns the formulas, inputs and assumptions. Compressive stress is negative; a fit across temperatures is fit_at_temperature.

unit.description: Unit, e.g. 'MPa', 'mm', '1/K', 'K', 'degC', '1' (dimensionless).

inputs.description: Named inputs of the check, each { value, unit } (names listed in the command description).

points.description: thick_cylinder: radii (length) to evaluate; cte_secant: temperatures (K, degC, degF).

unit.description: Unit, e.g. 'MPa', 'mm', '1/K', 'K', 'degC', '1' (dimensionless).

table.description: cte_secant: instantaneous CTE table (piecewise linear, strictly increasing T) instead of alpha0 / alpha1.

description: Make a solid from a nurbs_surface sheet by giving it thickness along its normal (S_u x S_v). `side` "normal" (default) offsets towards the normal, "reverse" against it, "both" half the thickness each way. The result is a closed triangle mesh solid (a tessellation with `quality` quads per knot span: volume and mass work, booleans work on the mesh, but it has no exact B-rep). Refused when the offset reaches a centre of curvature (thickness above the local radius). The sheet is kept; thicken then boolean / mass_properties.

id.description: Id of a nurbs_surface entity.

quality.description: Quads per knot span and direction of the tessellation, integer 2..24. Default 8.

description: Read-only report of a topology study: state (unsolved | solved | stale | missing | untrusted), the study definition, the named settings, the optimizer, the projection and the rules it runs under (manufacturing constraints, minimum member rule, objective), and - when solved - the verified result: compliance and its unit, iterations, status (converged | max_iterations), volume fraction, grey level (share of intermediate densities), solid volume, per-load-case compliance, the objective value and each constraint (value, limit, satisfied), the last `historyRows` iteration rows, the solver and its provenance. A stale result (study or analysis changed since the run) shows no numbers: re-run topology_solve. The result is a concept shape that must be rebuilt with ordinary modelling commands (suggest_rebuild) and reviewed by an engineer; it is never releasable.

historyRows.description: How many of the last iteration history rows to return, 0 to 1000. Default 20.

description: Cut a nurbs_surface sheet, in one of two ways. (1) Rectangle: `u` [from, to] and `v` [from, to] inside the surface domain (see inspect_nurbs `domain`): exact, the sheet keeps its id and its parameter values. (2) Curves: `curveIds` (nurbs_curve ids, chained end to end) are projected onto the sheet - to the closest point, or along `projectAlong` when given - and trim it. A CLOSED curve keeps its inside (`keep` "inside", default) or its outside (a hole); an OPEN curve must run from the sheet boundary across to the boundary (extend it past the edges) and needs `keepPoint`, a point near the side to keep. The sheet keeps its patch and stores the trim loops, so it renders and measures as the trimmed region: the result reports the exact trimmed `area` (also measure_area on the sheet id). A trimmed sheet accepts further trims only as holes inside the kept region; sewing, thickening and the analysis queries (curvature, draft, deviation) still use the whole underlying patch. Reference: a 10 x 10 plane trimmed by a circle of radius 3 keeping the inside has area 28.274334.

id.description: Id of a nurbs_surface entity.

keep.description: Curve mode, closed curve: keep the region "inside" the curve (default) or "outside" it (the curve becomes a hole).

keepPoint.description: Curve mode: a point [x, y, z] on the side to keep (projected onto the sheet). Required for an open curve; overrides `keep` for a closed one.

projectAlong.description: Curve mode: direction [x, y, z] (any non-zero length) along which the curves are carried onto the sheet. Omit for the closest-point projection.

tolerance.description: Curve mode: largest gap (document units, > 0) between chained curve ends, and the ray-hit tolerance. Default 1e-6 x the size.

description: Twist a 3D solid or mesh about an axis: each cross-section perpendicular to the axis is rotated by angleDeg times a ramp that goes from 0 at region.start to 1 at region.end (past the end the body keeps the full rotation). Volume is unchanged. Use it for twisted bars, drill flutes, blades, balusters. angleDeg is in degrees (positive = counter-clockwise looking down the axis toward the origin). The frame, region and tolerance default from the body (axis = longest direction, region = the whole body, falloff "smooth"); the defaults used are reported in data.frame. The result replaces the entity as a mesh entity that keeps the construction (brep recipe); the mesh is refined until the chordal deviation is within output.tolerance. Refuses angle 0 (DEF_NO_EFFECT) and regions that miss the body (DEF_REGION_MISSES_BODY). Then call analyze_deformation and check_deformation.

angleDeg.description: Total rotation reached at region.end, degrees; any non-zero value (360 and more are allowed).

frame.description: Deformation frame: local z = axis, x = reference projected perpendicular to the axis, y = z cross x; regions and radii are measured from the origin along it. Every field is optional and defaults from the body bounds; the defaults used are reported in data.frame.defaulted.

axis.description: Deformation axis, any non-zero direction (unitless; normalised). Default: the longest bounding-box direction (a world axis, ties: x before y before z).

origin.description: Frame origin, a world point in document units. Default: the body bounding-box centre (the bend uses the centre of the face at the start of the body).

reference.description: Direction giving the frame x axis, unitless: its component perpendicular to the axis is used; it must not be parallel to the axis. Default: the next longest bounding-box direction.

id.description: Id of the 3D solid or mesh entity to deform (describe_scene lists ids). It is replaced by the deformed mesh entity (keepSource keeps it).

ids.description: Ids of several 3D solids or meshes to deform with the same parameters (one feature step; every body gets its own frame and region defaults from its own bounds). Use this or id.

keepSource.description: true: keep the original entity(ies) next to the deformed one(s) instead of replacing them. Default false.

output.description: How the result is computed: kernel choice and mesh tolerance.

mode.description: "auto" (default): the exact kernel builds the result when it can evaluate this deformation (the native kernel does for every law: the faces become B-splines fitted within output.tolerance), else the mesh path runs and the summary says so; "exact": refuse (DEF_EXACT_UNAVAILABLE) unless the exact kernel built it; "mesh": force the faceted mesh path.

preserveAnalytic.description: Recognise cylinders, cones and planes in an exact result (needs the exact warp of a later milestone; true is refused today).

tolerance.description: Largest deviation of the result from the true deformed surface, document units, > 0: the chordal deviation of the mesh path, or the fit error of the B-spline faces and edges on the exact path (a smaller value costs control points, not accuracy). Default: 1e-5 times the body bounding-box diagonal, clamped to [1e-6, 0.01].

region.description: Part of the body along the frame axis where the effect ramps in. Past the end the body follows rigidly (carries the end transform); before the start it is unchanged. Default: the whole body.

end.description: Region end along the frame axis, document units from the frame origin; must exceed start. Default: where the body ends.

falloff.description: How the effect ramps from none at start to full at end: "smooth" (default, 3t^2 - 2t^3, no crease at the region ends) or "linear" (straight ramp; leaves a visible crease at both ends).

start.description: Region start along the frame axis, document units from the frame origin (may be negative). Default: where the body starts.

description: Change a fatigue case: any field of create_fatigue_case (omitted fields keep their value; `factors` merges like set_fatigue_factors). The merged case is validated like a new one.

analysisId.description: FE analysis whose STRESS results drive the case. After fea_solve, run the fatigue_field transport (llull-compute, every node) so compute_fatigue can rank the hot spots; without it compute_fatigue refuses with FAT_RESULTS_MISSING.

gate.description: Optional hysteresis gate (>= 0) in history units.

residue.description: half_cycles: residue counted as half cycles; repeat: close the history as a repeating block.

compressiveMean.description: Compressive mean-stress rule: no_benefit (default, conservative) or formula.

damageLimit.description: Miner damage limit D (> 0). Default 1 (Palmgren-Miner rule), reported as defaulted.

marginalBand.description: Margin band (>= 0): 0 <= margin < band is MARGINAL. No default.

modifiers.description: REPLACES the Marin modifier list (surface, size, reliability, ...). Each needs value > 0 and a justification.

justification.description: Mandatory reason / source of the factor.

name.description: Which Marin-type modifier this is.

value.description: Factor > 0 multiplying the curve strength (0.8 = 20 % weaker than the test specimen). Never defaulted.

scatter.description: Scatter factor SF on life. There is NO default: without it compute_fatigue refuses with FAT_SCATTER_FACTOR_UNSET.

source.description: Mandatory source of the factor (regulation, company rule, case input).

mode.description: hotspots

mapping.description: Histories driving the case. History-only: stress-kind histories whose scaled series are summed (same length). FE: one load_factor history per load case (loadCase; may be omitted when the analysis has one load case), superposed per node. Needs >= 1 entry.

loadCase.description: FE load case name this history drives (FE input; not used by history-only cases).

scale.description: Multiplier on the history values (history-only: stress = scale x value; FE: scale x load-case stress).

material.description: Curve to use: material record + model ids.

cyclicModelId.description: strain_life: id of the cyclic_ramberg_osgood model.

modelId.description: S-N model id (stress_life) or en_coffin_manson model id (strain_life).

recordId.description: Material record id holding the curve.

walker.description: Walker exponent gamma in (0, 1]; gamma 0.5 equals SWT.

meanStress.description: Mean-stress correction: none | goodman (needs Ftu on the record) | gerber (Ftu) | soderberg (Fty) | morrow (sn_basquin sigma_f) | swt | { walker: gamma }. A compressive mean gives no benefit for goodman / gerber / soderberg / morrow unless compressiveMean "formula". Default none.

method.description: stress_life (S-N, Miner) or strain_life (epsilon-N with Neuber on nominal stress histories).

name.description: New display name.

notch.description: Optional notch: the nominal stress is scaled by Kf = 1 + q (Kt - 1) (Neuber on the cyclic curve for strain-life).

feIncludesKt.description: true when the stress already contains the concentration (no extra Kf); false: Kf scales the nominal stress.

q.description: Notch sensitivity q in [0, 1]: Kf = 1 + q (Kt - 1).

blocksPerUnit.description: Blocks of the history per flight or hour (flights / hours only).

unit.description: Unit of the required life; flights / hours need blocksPerUnit.

name: update_fatigue_case

name.description: New display name.

target.description: New target (replaces the old one entirely).

edgesNear.description: Points identifying edges: each resolves to the nearest edge.

items.description: A point [x, y, z] in document units lying on (or very near) the intended edge.

facesNear.description: Points identifying faces: each resolves to the NEAREST face of the entity at meshing time.
